synergy.reason: Can safely dish out massive AoE damage while Lian Po knocks up multiple enemies.
Creates openings for the marksman to safely deal damage through strong teamfight initiation.

counters.reason: Kites the tank with high mobility while slowly whittling them down with true damage.
Easily bypasses Lian Po's durability and passive with long-range poke and percentage-based damage.

passive.description:
Lian Po has crowd control immunity while using his skills.
When in combat, Lian Po gains Battle Spirit continuously, and his Basic Attacks and skills grant more Battle Spirit on hit. Battle Spirit provides 0-20% damage reduction (based on the value of Battle Spirit). At max Battle Spirit, his Attack Speed is increased by 30%.
When out of combat, Battle Spirit diminishes over time, and is converted to 70(70 + 1.5% Health)Health recovery each time it diminishes, for up to 10 times in total.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Warrior's Soul

skill1.description:
Lian Po dashes in the target direction, dealing 55 (55 + 15% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and launching them for 0.5s. He also deals 5% of the target's Health as physical damage to heroes and 183 (5% of his Health) as physical damage to non-hero units.
Passive: Lian Po's every third Basic Attack is a heavy strike that deals 250 (250 + 100% extra physical attack) extra physical damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Burst Ram

skill2.description:
Lian Po charges up and slams the ground, gaining a shield that negates 360 (360 + 8.5% extra Health) damage for 5s. While charging, he slows enemies within range by 15% and pulls non-hero enemies toward him.
After 1s, the ground splits, dealing 350 (350 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies. Enemies closer to the epicenter take more damage, up to an extra 100%. If any enemies are within range when charging begins, Skill 1's Cooldown is reset.
He can use other skills while using Skill 2.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Magma Slam

skill3.description:
Lian Po leaps to the target location and hammers the ground 3 times. The direction of each strike can be adjusted using the movement wheel.
Strike 1: He deals 220 (220 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and slows them by 15% for 1s. Enemies in the center take an extra (60% extra physical attack) physical damage.
Strike 2: He deals 440 (440 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and slows them by 30% for 1s. Enemies in the center take an extra (90% extra physical attack) physical damage.
Strike 3: He deals 660 (660 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and launches them for 1s. He also deals 10% of the target's Health as physical damage to heroes and 10% of his Health as physical damage to non-hero units. Enemies in the center take an extra (150% extra physical attack) physical damage.
He can use Skill 1 while his Ultimate is in effect.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Tremor Smash

strategy.earlyGame: Lian Po starts the clash lane weaker than he looks. His Fury gauge is empty at level 1, so the damage reduction from his Passive isn't online yet — don't force extended trades before level 3. Instead, take short exchanges with the Skill 1 dash and the third-hit heavy strike from its passive, and soak waves behind the Skill 2 shield. Here's the trick: if an enemy is standing inside your Skill 2 charge zone, Skill 1's cooldown resets instantly, so you win trades on sheer number of touches. Once you hit level 4, rotate to the river for the 4:00 Tyrant and play knock-up bot next to your jungler.
strategy.midGame: Around the eight-minute mark, with two defensive items done, Lian Po gets to start fights on his own terms. You have super armor for the entire duration of your skill animations, so enemy stuns and knock-ups simply don't matter mid-cast — that's your license to dive. Drop out of a mid-lane brush with your Ultimate, use the first two slams to cut off the escape route, and land the third-slam knock-up on your real target. Win or lose the skirmish, leaving combat converts your Fury into HP, so you arrive at the next objective healthy. When teams start shadowboxing before Shadow Tyrant, volunteer to be the one who face-checks brushes.
strategy.lateGame: Past ten minutes, when Shadow Tyrant and Overlord decide games, your entire job comes down to one decision: who eats the first hit. Before the fight breaks out, smack a nearby minion or jungle camp to pre-stack Fury, so you enter with the damage reduction and attack speed already rolling. Your Ultimate lets you adjust the slam position through the first two hits — aim the third slam where the enemy is running to, not where they are, and it stops missing. You don't need kills; peeling two enemy backliners out of the fight is a full day's work. The one true loss condition is overchasing and dying alone.
strategy.teamfight: The dream engage is an Ultimate that clips two or three members of the enemy midline. On landing, charge Skill 2 in the middle of them — the pull and the blast keep them clumped while handing you a fresh Skill 1. Dash in, charge, dash again: that loop draws enemy fire onto you while carving their formation in half. You're there to split the fight, not to secure kills — leave those to your carries. When your HP dips, disengage for a moment, let Fury convert back into HP, then walk right back in. From the enemy's side, the tank they thought they killed just keeps coming back.

combos.title: Tremor Smash Full Engage
combos.sequence: Ultimate (first and second slams) → Skill 1 (weave it mid-animation) → Ultimate (third-slam knock-up) → Skill 2
combos.description: Your Ultimate lets you cast Skill 1 between slams — use the dash to chase a fleeing target back into range, then guarantee the third-slam knock-up. Finishing with Skill 2 adds follow-up damage and a shield in one button.

combos.title: Skill 1 Reset Loop
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Basic Attack (third-hit heavy strike) → Skill 2 (charge with the enemy inside the zone) → Skill 1
combos.description: Catching an enemy inside the Skill 2 charge zone refunds Skill 1 on the spot. This loop is Lian Po's bread and butter in lane and in teamfights alike — it's where all his uptime comes from.

strengths: Super armor during every skill animation lets him engage straight through enemy CC
Fury stacks make him tankier as fights drag on — brawls are his home turf
Skill 2 refunds Skill 1 when it catches an enemy, fueling relentless in-and-out pressure
Fury converts to HP out of combat, so he re-enters fights faster than expected
weaknesses: With zero Fury right after spawning, he's far squishier than his frame suggests
The Skill 2 blast and the Ultimate's third slam are slow to land and easy for agile enemies to dodge
Poor base movement speed means he's often a step late to the fight

synergy.reason: Pulls enemies together, making it much easier for her to land knockups and her ultimate on multiple targets.
Can lock down powerful enemy assassins, creating a safe backline environment for her to deal damage.

counters.reason: Quickly closes the gap from a distance and bursts her squishy down before she can get her skill combo off.
Can safely interrupt and harass her from afar using long-range stuns.

passive.description: Xiao Qiao gains 25% Movement Speed for 2s on skill hit.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Encouraging Thoughts

skill1.description: Xiao Qiao tosses a spinning fan in the target direction that returns to her after reaching its max range, dealing damage to enemies in its path and again on its way back. The first enemy hit takes 585 (585 + 80% magical attack) magical damage. Damage is reduced by 20% with each subsequent hit, down to 50% of the initial damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Blossoming Fan

skill2.description: Xiao Qiao summons a whirlwind in the target location, dealing 300 (300 +50% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 1.5s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Honeysweet Breeze

skill3.description:
Xiao Qiao calls down meteors for 6s. Meteors randomly target a nearby enemy, dealing 400 (400 + 100% magical attack) magical damage. The meteors prioritize enemy heroes.
Her passive skill effect is activated during the skill's duration. Each enemy can be hit by up to 4 meteors, but subsequent hits deal 50% less damage.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Meteor Storm

strategy.earlyGame: In the mid lane, Xiao Qiao can run her whole laning phase off Skill 1. The fan flies out and boomerangs back, so after the first hit, sidestep so the return path crosses the same target — one cast, two hits, and it clears the wave at the same time. You'll be tempted to use Skill 2 for damage; don't. Before level 4, that 1.5-second knock-up is your only answer to a jungle gank, and Xiao Qiao has no dash to fall back on. Watch your mana, and when the 4:00 Tyrant fight starts, lob fans in from the edge of the river rather than committing to the pit.
strategy.midGame: From level 4 onward, a simple rule keeps you alive: only go all-in when Skill 2 actually lands. During the 1.5-second knock-up, stacking your Ultimate meteors and Skill 1 on top deletes any mage or marksman outright. When Skill 2 is down or missed, go back to fan poke and nothing else. Once your first one or two AP items finish around 7-9 minutes, use the movement speed from your Passive and Ultimate to shove mid and show up in the farm lane — you rotate faster than your lane opponent, and that creates free numbers advantages.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Xiao Qiao does half her job before the fight even starts. Thread fans into the enemy clump during the standoff — a double-hit strips 20-30% off a frontliner, and your team fights noticeably braver with that lead. Whether Skill 2 opens fights or saves your life depends entirely on the enemy comp: if they run a dash-heavy assassin, it stays in your pocket, no debate. Your Ultimate lets you move while it channels, so walk backward toward your team as the meteors fall. That one habit fixes most deaths where you got dropped before your damage finished.
strategy.teamfight: Hold the backline, chip with Skill 1, and the moment someone jumps you, knock them up with Skill 2 — an assassin diving into your Ultimate mid-knock-up has simply traded their life. If you're flipping to offense, the window is when the enemy collides with your frontline and their feet stop: drop Skill 2 into the pile, then Ultimate, then Skill 1, and you're cooking several people at once. Your Passive grants a burst of speed on every skill hit, so keep the rhythm — hit, move, hit. A Xiao Qiao who never stands still is remarkably hard to catch.

combos.title: Knock-Up Full Burst
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (knock-up) → Ultimate (meteors) → Skill 1
combos.description: Stack every source of damage inside the 1.5-second knock-up. Since you only commit after confirming Skill 2 landed, this is maximum damage with near-perfect consistency — her core pattern.

combos.title: Boomerang Double Poke
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (outgoing hit) → sidestep with the Passive speed boost → returning fan hits the same target
combos.description: Land the fan on the way out, use the Passive movement speed to reposition, and catch the same enemy on the return. Lane phase is just this on repeat, and the HP difference adds up fast.

combos.title: Flash Pick
combos.sequence: Flash → Skill 2 → Ultimate → Skill 1
combos.description: The proactive version for breaking stalemates. A point-blank Skill 2 out of Flash is virtually undodgeable, and a fed Xiao Qiao removes the enemy carry before the fight officially begins.

strengths: Skill 1's range and damage let her win the lane poke war one-sidedly
Skill 2's knock-up comes out fast and starts plays on both offense and defense
She accelerates on every skill hit, staying slippery as long as she keeps landing them
Straightforward kit that doubles as an excellent introduction to mage fundamentals
weaknesses: No blink or dash — a targeted stun with no escape tools means death
Skill 1 loses damage each time it passes through a minion, blunting poke through waves
She constantly wrestles with saving Skill 2 for defense versus spending it on offense

107.name: Zilong

synergy.reason: Combines with his ultimate knockup to instantly wipe out enemies with massive magic burst damage.
Significantly boosts his survivability with shields and healing after he dives into the enemy team.

counters.reason: Completely shuts down their mobility with a strong suppression skill, leaving them vulnerable to focus fire.
Stops his engage and prevents his escape using continuous stuns and shields.

passive.description:
Zilong gets stronger the more he fights. As his Health declines, his potential is triggered: he enjoys greater damage reduction, and his basic skills are enhanced.
Hidden Dragon: When his Health is more than 70% and less than or equal to 100%, he gains 5% damage reduction.
Dragon Portent: When his Health is more than 40% and less than or equal to 70%, he gains 10% damage reduction.
Dragon in Flight: When his Health is more than 0% and less than or equal to 40%, he gains 20% damage reduction.
Any Health in excess of the current bracket will be converted into a permanent shield. When a shield Health bracket is full, excess shield value will be converted into Health instead.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Dragon's Roar

skill1.description:
Zilong charges forward with his spear, dealing 350 (350 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage.
The next Basic Attack is enhanced and deals an extra 120 (120 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage and slows the enemy by 25% for 2s.
This skill's cooldown is reset each time his Health enters a new bracket.
Dash distance increases with skill level.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Thunderbreaker

skill2.description: Zilong jabs 5 times, with each jab dealing 200 (200 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies hit and restoring 65 (65 + 2.5% extra Health) Health. The effect of each subsequent jab is reduced by 8%.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Stormpiercer

skill3.description:
Zilong leaps into the air and delivers a lightning strike, dealing 550 (550 +150% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and marking them with an induction effect: skills hitting marked targets within the next 5s deal 30 (30 +10% extra physical attack) magical damage, and launch enemies in the center of the area (for 1s).
Returns 50% cooldown if it misses enemy heroes.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Skysplitter

strategy.earlyGame: Zilong lives in the jungle. Max Skill 2 first — the healing on the five-thrust combo keeps your clear healthy — and grab both buffs on the way to level 4. Keep his Passive in mind while you farm: each time your HP drops past 70% and then 40%, your damage reduction steps up and Skill 1 gets a charge refunded, which means a wounded Zilong is a stronger Zilong. The catch is that none of that protects you at full HP, so don't pick a coin-flip fight during a level-1 invade. Whatever else happens, walk into the 4:00 Tyrant fight with your Ultimate available.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, your Ultimate is the gank button. If it doesn't hit an enemy hero, half the cooldown comes back — so stop treating it as precious and throw it with conviction. Leap in, knock them up, and the shock effect it applies deals bonus magic damage every time another skill connects: collect it with the Skill 2 five-thrust and a Skill 1 follow-up. Around seven minutes, with your first core item done, Zilong is one of the nastiest duelists on the map — he genuinely wins fights that start at half HP. Welcome the scrap; being damaged is your Passive working as intended.
strategy.lateGame: Unless he gets bursted first, late-game Zilong is the last man standing in every teamfight. The 20% damage reduction, Skill 2 healing, and overheal-to-shield conversion all stack up, and every second a brawl drags on tilts it further his way. At Shadow Tyrant and Overlord fights past ten minutes, don't be the first one in — go second, and leap onto the backline with your Ultimate after the enemy has dumped CC on your frontline. From the enemy's perspective, the worst part of fighting Zilong is watching him heal back up mid-fight with Skill 2. The one real counter is anti-heal: respect anyone who built it.
strategy.teamfight: Play the late pick. Let your team take the opening exchange, watch the enemy burn their stuns and knock-ups, then Ultimate onto the softest target you can reach. Once the knock-up and shock effect are applied, run the full string — Basic Attack, Skill 2, Skill 1 — so every hit cashes in the bonus magic damage. If your HP crosses a Passive threshold mid-fight, the refunded Skill 1 charge is your exit ticket or your chase tool, whichever the moment demands. Zilong is at his best in the red — just don't get cocky into a team stacking anti-heal.

combos.title: Leap and Detonate
combos.sequence: Ultimate (knock-up + shock effect) → Basic Attack → Skill 2 (five thrusts) → Skill 1
combos.description: Apply the shock effect first, then every skill that lands adds bonus magic damage on top. With the five-thrust healing running, you win most straight slugfests even when you take damage back.

combos.title: Hit-and-Run Trade
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (dash) → Empowered Basic Attack (slow) → Skill 2 → back off
combos.description: Dash in, slow them so the counterattack limps, then heal back the trade with the five-thrust before leaving. It builds an HP lead while your Ultimate stays in reserve.

strengths: Damage reduction scales up as his HP drops, making him monstrously hard to finish off
The Ultimate refunds half its cooldown on a miss, so ganks can be thrown freely
Skill 2 healing plus overheal-to-shield conversion wins extended trades
The shock effect's bonus magic damage keeps him relevant against armor stackers
weaknesses: Thin defenses at full HP leave him vulnerable to opening burst
As a melee physical fighter, slows and stuns that deny his approach shut him down
Anti-heal items strip away most of what makes him durable

synergy.reason: Groups enemies together, making it much easier to trap multiple targets inside the ultimate's barrier.
Excels at buffing allies and CCing enemies, making it much easier for him to land his long-range stuns.

counters.reason: Can easily interrupt his ultimate channel with wide AoE CC and skill resets.
Dives straight onto the backline, completely shutting down his advantage as a long-range poke hero.

passive.description:
Every 4th Basic Attack is enhanced, dealing 450 (450 + 70% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and knocking them back for 0.75s.
Whenever he uses a skill, he gains 1 stack of shield for 3s, for up to 3 stacks. Each stack negates 300 (300 + 35% magical attack) damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Fight for Peace

skill1.description: Mozi dashes in the target direction, dealing 250 (250 +38% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and enhancing his next Basic Attack.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Peacebringer

skill2.description:
Mozi fires a shell in the target direction. The shell explodes upon hitting an enemy or reaching its max range, leaving behind an electrified crater.
The explosion deals 525 (525 +45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and stuns them for 1s.
The electrified crater lasts for 4s and deals 50 (50 +5% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range every 0.5s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Cannon Blast

skill3.description: Mozi creates an energy barrier around himself that lasts for up to 3.3s. Every 0.5s, it deals 200 (200 +45% magical attack) magical damage and stuns enemies it touches.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Think Inside the Box

strategy.earlyGame: Mozi's lane is entirely about how you aim Skill 2. The shell detonates on the first enemy it touches, so fire it through gaps in the wave — or the moment your opponent steps forward for a last hit. Land the one-second stun and the follow-up is free: Skill 1 dash into the empowered basic attack, guaranteed. Wave clear is no problem — Skill 1 plus the fourth-hit empowered basic from your Passive handles it, and since every skill cast stacks a shield, you can shrug off some return fire. Tag your opponent with one or two stuns before level 4 and they'll flinch every time they step up. That fear is worth more than the damage.
strategy.midGame: This is when Skill 2 turns into gold. A mage who stuns from long range is rare, and the moment your jungler shows up, landing one shell converts directly into a kill. With one AP item and one durability item done around 6-8 minutes, Mozi stops playing like a mage and starts playing like a CC frontliner — stand slightly ahead of your team and let the threat of the stun freeze the enemy's advance. Don't rush your Ultimate barrier out; placed across a narrow corridor or a brush exit, it's far harder to play around.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Mozi is the one who can end a match with a single stun. In the standoffs before Overlord past ten minutes, aim Skill 2 at where the enemy carry will retreat to, not where they stand. One hit and your whole team collapses on the target — that's the objective won on numbers alone. Keep your Passive shield at three stacks and you can eat an assassin's opener, which is exactly why you're allowed to stand a step ahead of any other mage. One warning: your Ultimate roots you while it's deployed, so never lead with it while the enemy still has long-range CC in hand.
strategy.teamfight: Your impact swings heavily on whether the opening Skill 2 catch lands. If it misses, don't panic-force anything — chip the frontline with Skill 1 and empowered basics while the cooldown comes back around. Once the fight turns messy, deploy your Ultimate barrier across the path to your carry: enemies who touch it get stunned repeatedly, and in tight quarters it's a genuine wall. And when everything lines up on one target — stun, dash, empowered basic, barrier — Mozi outputs enough damage to kill anything that isn't a tank.

combos.title: Guaranteed Pick
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (one-second stun) → Skill 1 (dash) → Empowered Basic Attack → Ultimate
combos.description: Land the long-range stun, close the gap with the dash, then seal the escape route with the barrier. The whole combo hinges on covering the distance inside that one second of stun.

combos.title: Push and Shield Cycle
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Basic Attack x3 → Passive Empowered Basic Attack (knockback)
combos.description: Use the fourth-hit empowered basic as an area knockback while shoving waves. The shields stacked from casting skills mean you can afford to clear aggressively even under pressure.

strengths: Every skill carries CC, and the long-range one-second stun creates picks on demand
Passive shields give him frontline staying power no ordinary mage has
The Skill 2 field and Ultimate barrier lock down corridors and choke points
Flexible enough to play both mid and the clash lane
weaknesses: Skill 2 flies in a predictable straight line and gets sidestepped by anyone paying attention
The Ultimate roots him during deployment, inviting ranged punishment
His only mobility is the short Skill 1 dash — his escapes are poor

synergy.reason: Combines Da Ji's reliable point-and-click stun with Sun Wukong's high burst damage for instant kills.
Easily secures chain kills with assassin skill resets after Da Ji bursts down enemy health bars.

counters.reason: Can tank the combo with heavy sword damage reduction and retaliate with devastating burst damage.
Instantly one-shots the squishy Da Ji from stealth before she can even cast a skill.

passive.description: Every time Daji's skills deal damage, she places 1 stack of Captivated on the target, for up to 3 stacks. Each stack reduces the enemy's Magic Defense for 3s by 36-72, depending on her level.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Captivate

skill1.description: Daji unleashes a soul blast in the target direction, dealing 570 (570 +120% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Soul Impact

skill2.description: Daji casts a love spell on an enemy, dealing 285 (285 +66% magical attack) magical damage and stunning them for 1.5s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Strike a Pose

skill3.description:
Daji releases 5 hearts that attack enemies within range at random, each heart dealing 325 (325 +75% magical attack) magical damage.
When multiple hearts hit the same target, subsequent hearts only deal 50% magical damage.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Heartbreaker

strategy.earlyGame: Daji's early game is a patience test: push waves with Skill 1 and wait for level 4. Her fox fires fly at random targets, so her clear is slower than most mages' — don't try to win the shove war, because you won't. What you do have is Skill 2, a targeted stun that cannot miss. The instant your opponent drifts into range, Skill 2 into Skill 1 takes a third of their HP with zero aim required. With no mobility skill, build the habit of stepping back whenever the enemy jungler vanishes from the minimap. Skip forcing the 4:00 Tyrant — holding your mid tower and soaking experience is a perfectly good outcome.
strategy.midGame: From 5-7 minutes, with level 4 and some cooldown reduction online, Daji's best play is roaming for picks. Shove the mid wave, slide into a side brush, and wait. During the 1.5-second guaranteed stun, dumping all five fox fires and Skill 1 — with your Passive shredding their magic defense — erases any mage or marksman on the spot. After a full combo you're staring at long cooldowns, so take the kill and leave immediately; greed is how fed Dajis die. Since landing skills takes no mechanical skill, all your brainpower goes into the real question: when, and on whom.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Daji doesn't win teamfights — she makes them start 4v5. Past ten minutes, lurk in the brushes around Overlord and execute whoever comes to check vision: a support face-checking alone or a carry a step too far forward is a guaranteed kill. With four or more items, her single-target burst is among the best in the game, and anything short of a tank is inside the one-combo threshold. Open 5v5s are a different story — fox fires scatter randomly across multiple targets, so your damage evaporates. Bet everything on the pick before the fight.
strategy.teamfight: If a straight-up teamfight is unavoidable, park Daji in the very back as the counter-assassin. Never fire your Ultimate into a clump — random targeting means it won't find the enemy you actually want dead. What you're waiting for is an isolated target, ideally the assassin who dove your backline: a guaranteed stun into full combo turns their engage into a death sentence. Burn Skill 2 early and you have no self-defense left, so keep asking yourself mid-fight who the stun is being saved for. Positioning alone decides whether Daji ends the game as the MVP or the liability.

combos.title: Guaranteed Stun Execution
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (stun) → Ultimate (five fox fires) → Skill 1
combos.description: Focus all five fox fires into a single target during the 1.5-second stun, then drive Skill 1 through the magic defense your Passive just shredded. The fewer enemies nearby, the harder it hits.

combos.title: Lane Punish
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Skill 1 → back off
combos.description: A two-button trade for the moment your opponent stops to clear minions. The stun can't miss, so there's nothing to whiff — repeat it every cooldown cycle and the HP gap opens on its own.

strengths: Skill 2 is a targeted, unmissable stun — the chosen victim does not get away
Magic defense shred from her Passive synergizes with fox fires for elite single-target burst
The combo is so simple that anyone can reproduce her full damage once items are done
One ambush from a brush can decide a teamfight before it starts
weaknesses: Random fox fire targeting makes multi-enemy fights and wave clear genuinely bad
No mobility skill — outside of Flash, there is no escape plan
After dumping the full combo, long cooldowns leave her nearly helpless

synergy.reason: Acts as a solid frontline to peel enemies, allowing Garuda to safely continuously poke from a distance.
Locks down enemies with wide AoE CC, making it easier to land Garuda's slow-channeling ultimate on multiple targets.

counters.reason: Excels at long-range attacks but is completely defenseless when an enemy uses stealth to get up close.
Uses high mobility to quickly close the gap, completely shutting down their preferred long-range poke.

passive.description: Garuda's Basic Attacks pierce targets and deal 287 (120 + 100% physical attack + 35% magical attack) magical damage. His Basic Attacks deal 50% less damage to structures.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Keen Feathers

skill1.description: Garuda conjures an arrow formation that deals 150 (150 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within it every 0.5s for 2.5s and slows them by 15% for 1s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Arrows of Gold

skill2.description:
Garuda unleashes the power of wishes, gaining 100 Movement Speed that diminishes over 3s, as well as a shield that negates 300 (300 + 55% magical attack) damage. He also deals 200 (200 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
Passive: Gains 15 Movement Speed.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Golden Winged Blessing

skill3.description:
Garuda sends 90 golden arrows of judgment surging forward over 5s, each of which deals 54 (54 + 10% magical attack) magical damage and grants him 20% Movement Speed. He can use other skills at the same time as this skill.
If the skill is used again, Garuda immediately shoots all remaining arrows in every direction, dealing an equal amount of magical damage and inflicting Dread on nearby enemies. He also removes all Physical Attack bonuses granted by their equipment for 2s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Wings of Judgment

strategy.earlyGame: Garuda's lane revolves around basic attacks that pierce and deal magic damage. Angle yourself so the enemy laner stands behind their own minions and your autos farm and poke in the same swing. Lay the Skill 1 feather field on the enemy's escape path rather than under their feet — that's where the slow earns its keep — and treat Skill 2 as insurance for when damage is incoming. Until your Ultimate arrives at level 4, farming and HP discipline beat hero plays. You have speed but no self-peel CC, so once ganks pick up around the four-minute mark, check the minimap more, not less.
strategy.midGame: Mid-game Garuda is about area denial with the Ultimate. Ninety feather arrows over five seconds turns any narrow contest — the Tyrant pit, a mid tower siege — into ground the enemy simply cannot hold. With two AP items around 7-9 minutes, run the mobile-turret loop: feather field down, barrage into the clump, Skill 2 speed to hold your range. One discipline matters above all — don't recast the Ultimate casually. The fear plus physical attack bonus nullification is your trump card against assassins, and while that threat exists, they can't touch you.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Garuda is the worst matchup the enemy's physical carries can face. When an assassin or fighter dives you, the Ultimate recast answers with a two-second fear and nullifies their equipment's physical attack bonus — the assassination just doesn't happen. Past ten minutes, merely holding that button unspent keeps enemies from committing. Set up diagonally behind your frontline, at the angle where piercing basics travel through their tanks into the backline. You have no hard CC to lock down runners, so leave the executions to teammates and do the one thing only you do: keep firing.
strategy.teamfight: Garuda's teamfight is measured in seconds of uninterrupted shooting. On engage, stack the Skill 1 feather field on the frontline and pour the Ultimate's arrows into the thickest part of the enemy team, weaving piercing basics between them. When someone closes the gap, kite out with Skill 2's speed — and if they stick anyway, the Ultimate recast dumps every unfired arrow around you while the fear buys the reset. Self-peel and burst damage on the same button is deeply satisfying, but it's also your whole defense: confirm the threat is real before you press it.

combos.title: Feather Field Barrage
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (place it on the escape path) → Ultimate (barrage) → Skill 2 (speed up to hold range)
combos.description: Pin enemies inside the zone with the slow, then pour ninety arrows and piercing basics into them. Weaving in Skill 2's speed keeps you at a safe distance while the damage keeps flowing.

combos.title: Anti-Dive Reversal
combos.sequence: Ultimate recast mid-channel (two-second fear) → Skill 2 (shield + speed) → Basic Attack
combos.description: The self-defense combo that neutralizes a diving physical assassin with fear and physical attack bonus nullification. For the two seconds their kit does nothing, the fight belongs to you.

strengths: Piercing magic basic attacks deliver relentless damage into clumped enemies
The Ultimate recast's fear and physical attack bonus nullification is elite self-defense
Skill 2's shield and speed let him kite and keep shooting at the same time
Feather fields and the barrage dominate the tight spaces around objectives
weaknesses: No guaranteed hard CC, so he struggles to catch anyone on his own
Using the fear means sacrificing the Ultimate's remaining damage — a genuinely hard call
No blink, so chained hard CC will eventually run him down

synergy.reason: Locks down enemies with strong CC, creating windows for her to safely dish out burst damage.
Forces teamfights with massive AoE knockups, allowing her to move freely and pick off enemies one by one.

counters.reason: Completely shuts down her mobility with guaranteed hard CC, leaving her no chance to escape before being killed.
Stops her in her tracks with long-range stuns, completely denying her hit-and-run playstyle.

passive.description: Lady Sun's Basic Attack reduces Skill 1's cooldown by 0.5s on hit.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Energy Burst

skill1.description:
Lady Sun rolls in the target direction and enhances her next Basic Attack, which will deal 454 (285 + 100% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path. Using the enhanced Basic Attack will reset the following Basic Attack and increase its range.
If there is an enemy hero nearby after she rolls, her Movement Speed will increase by 80%. This effect diminishes over 2s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Rolling Raid

skill2.description:
Lady Sun tosses a grenade at the target location, dealing 380 (380 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and applying extreme slow for 1s. Reduces enemies' physical defense by 10% and marks enemy heroes and minions for 5s.
Her Basic Attacks deal 120 (120 + 36% extra physical attack) extra physical damage to marked enemy heroes, and 240 (240 + 72% extra physical attack) physical damage to marked minions.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Frag Grenade

skill3.description: Lady Sun fires a powerful shot in the target direction, dealing 840 (840 + 250% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy it hits. Upon hitting an enemy or reaching its maximum range, it detonates, dealing 75% damage to enemies in a cone-shaped area beyond the point of explosion.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Ultimate Shell

strategy.earlyGame: Farm-lane Lady Sun is banking for a payoff that arrives after the ten-minute mark. Farm cleanly, and above all, never stop attacking — every basic attack that connects shaves 0.5 seconds off Skill 1's cooldown, so the roll is always coming back as long as you're swinging. The roll into empowered basic into extended-range basic is a real trade pattern, but early on it's better held as insurance for when the enemy jungler goes missing. If your team contests the 4:00 Tyrant, contribute from the back of the river — no heroics required.
strategy.midGame: Once one or two crit items finish around 7-9 minutes, the roll-and-shoot style becomes real damage. Push side waves, and trade with the full package: the Skill 2 bomb shreds 10% of their physical defense and applies a mark, which your empowered basic then cashes in. Rolling near an enemy hero also grants a burst of movement speed, so your hit-and-run game is quicker than it looks. The habit to build now is roll direction: forward only when the kill is certain, sideways or backward everything else, shooting while the cooldown ticks back. That's the whole secret to a long life.
strategy.lateGame: With four or five items, Lady Sun's sustained fire melts frontliners and everything behind them. At Overlord fights past ten minutes, the ideal picture is you at maximum range, cycling empowered basics while your frontline absorbs attention. Choose the Ultimate's job case by case: opening poke before the fight, or a long-range execute on a runner. The ballista travels through walls and brush, and a kill shot arriving from somewhere invisible does real psychological damage. The one iron rule: for a few seconds after you spend the roll aggressively, play one step further back than feels natural.
strategy.teamfight: Lady Sun's greatest teamfight contribution is uninterrupted output from a position nobody can reach. Open by firing the Ultimate past the enemy frontline — the cone explosion carries the damage into their backline. From there, keep basic attacks flowing to recycle Skill 1, and roll laterally to keep breaking the dive angles of enemy assassins. When someone does get close, drop Skill 2 at your feet: the slow plus defense shred makes your counterattack start winning immediately. Think of it as shooting first and rolling as a consequence — that ordering is what lets damage and survival coexist.

combos.title: Roll-and-Shoot Cycle
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (roll) → Empowered Basic Attack → Extended-Range Basic Attack → Basic Attacks to refund the cooldown → Skill 1
combos.description: The Passive's cooldown refunds keep the roll cycling forever — this loop is Lady Sun's lifeline. You've graduated when the roll direction switches naturally between aggression and escape.

combos.title: Marked Target Burst
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (defense shred + mark) → Skill 1 (roll) → Empowered Basic Attack → Ultimate (ballista)
combos.description: Strip their defenses with the bomb, then stack the empowered basic and the ballista's huge hit on top — her maximum single-target damage. Even if they survive, the ballista chases runners from outside their vision.

strengths: Basic attacks refund Skill 1's cooldown, letting her roll and shoot indefinitely
Empowered and extended-range basics give her burst and sustained damage in one kit
Skill 2's defense shred and mark keep her damage honest against tanks
The Ultimate's ballista flies through walls and executes fleeing enemies
weaknesses: Spending the roll aggressively opens a defenseless window with no escape
All her mobility lives in one skill — layered CC leaves her with no answer
Heavily item-dependent, so a rough early game delays her damage badly

synergy.reason: Provides heavy CC to create a safe environment for him to dish out damage.
Provides great frontline sustain, creating the space needed for him to attack freely from the backline.

counters.reason: Ignores the frontline completely to dive and burst them down with high mobility.
Has physical damage immunity, making it extremely hard to win trades against them in the laning phase.

passive.description: After using 4 Basic Attacks or a skill, Luban No.7's next Basic Attack is enhanced to a scattershot that deals damage 3 times in a straight line ahead. Each shot deals physical damage equal to 65 (+4% of the target's max Health, increases by 1% for every 100 extra physical attack), or 207 (120 + 50% physical attack) physical damage to non-hero enemy units.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Suppressive Fire

skill1.description: Luban No.7 hurls a blowfish grenade at the target location, dealing 520 (520 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 2s. He also gains vision of targets hit by the grenade.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Blowfish Grenade

skill2.description: Luban No.7 launches a rocket in the target direction. The rocket knocks back enemies directly in front of him and explodes upon hitting the first enemy hero. The explosion deals 450 (450 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage and magical damage equal to 5% of the target's lost Health to enemies within range.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Shark Cannon

skill3.description:
Luban No.7 summons a blowfish airship in the target direction for 14s, which drops bombs on a random enemy within range. The bombs explode where they landed after a short delay, dealing 520 (520 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1s.
The airship grants him vision of the area it is bombarding.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Air Support

strategy.earlyGame: Let's be honest: Luban No.7's early game is about survival. He has no mobility skill and slow legs, so don't fight for lane priority — hug your tower and collect last hits. The good news is that the Passive strafe and the Skill 1 bomb clear waves quickly, so your farm rarely falls behind even from a defensive posture. Skill 1 also grants vision of anything it hits, which makes it a cheap brush-check when something feels off. The most dangerous moments are when the enemy support disappears from the minimap. Don't chase anything, and leave the 4:00 Tyrant to your teammates.
strategy.midGame: Around eight minutes, with two or three items done, the patience starts paying out. Your strafe deals physical damage scaling with the target's maximum HP, so unlike other marksmen, you only hit harder as their tanks get bigger. In fights, the damage rotation is about strafe frequency: Skill 1, strafe, Skill 2, strafe — every skill cast loads another burst. Your legs haven't gotten any faster, though, so step forward only after your frontline has the enemy's full attention. The Ultimate airship pays for itself even as a pure scouting tool thrown before a fight.
strategy.lateGame: Approaching full build, Luban No.7 is the strongest stationary gun in the game — one strafe visibly moves an enemy HP bar, tanks included. At Shadow Tyrant and Overlord fights past ten minutes, cycling strafes from the absolute backline is your entire job, and the enemy melts front to back. Luban wins by not dying, full stop — always choose the safe position over the kill. Skill 2's knockback is your only self-peel; save it for the assassin, every time. Throw the Ultimate airship at the enemy's staging area before the fight for vision and free pressure.
strategy.teamfight: Everything depends on holding your spot two or three steps behind the frontline. On engage, drop the Skill 1 slow on the clump and run the loop — strafe, skill, strafe — working through whoever stands in front. The strafe fires in a straight line, so when enemies spread out, just aim at the widest target available, usually their tank: the max-HP scaling means that damage is never wasted. The single non-negotiable is the flank. The instant an enemy assassin appears behind you, Skill 2 them away and run toward your team — no hesitation, no exceptions.

combos.title: Double Strafe Cycle
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (slow) → Empowered Basic Attack (strafe) → Skill 2 → Empowered Basic Attack (strafe)
combos.description: Every skill cast empowers your next basic into a strafe — this loop stacks two of them onto a slowed target. Even tanks have to respect that much max-HP damage.

combos.title: Anti-Dive Peel
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (knockback) → Empowered Basic Attack (strafe) → Skill 1 (slow at your feet) → retreat toward your team
combos.description: The survival routine for when someone reaches you: rocket them away, punish with the strafe, and slow the chase with the bomb as you leave. It only works if Skill 2 wasn't already spent on damage.

strengths: Strafe damage scales with the target's maximum HP — even tanks melt late game
Skill 1 and the airship supply their own vision, blunting brush ambushes
Skill 2's knockback is a reliable last line of defense against divers
Rapid wave clear makes him hard to siege out even when pushed in
weaknesses: No mobility skill and slow movement — among the easiest marksmen to catch
Weak early skirmishing forces a patient, defensive start until items arrive
The strafe fires in a straight line, losing value when enemies spread out

113.name: Zhuangzi

synergy.reason: Enables her to maintain her mobility through CC cleanses, allowing her to safely output continuous high damage.
Cleanses enemy CC during his ultimate, ensuring he can channel his deadly AoE damage without interruption.

counters.reason: Relies on overwhelming burst damage rather than CC, completely neutralizing the advantage of CC cleanses.
Uses continuous long-range poke and stuns to kite, forcing them to burn their ultimate.

passive.description:
Enters a Dreamscape every 6s for 2s and recovers 40 (40 + 0.6% extra Health) Health.
Dreamscape: Removes all crowd control effects and grants crowd control immunity, 15% damage reduction, and 15% Movement Speed for 2s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Nature's Will

skill1.description: Zhuangzi sends out dream butterflies in a cone-shaped area, gaining the enhancement from his passive skill for 2s. The butterflies deal 400 (400 +72% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slow them by 30% for 2s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Kaleidoscope

skill2.description:
Zhuangzi deals 250 (250 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and places 1 mark on them for 5s, for up to 5 stacks. Each mark deals 125 (125 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to enemies.
He also places 1 mark on himself and nearby teammates for 5s, for up to 5 stacks. Each mark increases Movement Speed by 3%.
Passive: Zhuangzi uses Skill 2 every 7s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Sleep Starts

skill3.description: Zhuangzi conjures up a dreamscape, removing all crowd control effects from himself and nearby teammates while granting a shield that grants crowd control immunity and negates 600 (600 + 12% extra Health) damage to himself and all teammates for 1.5s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Butterfly Effect

strategy.earlyGame: Zhuangzi's default assignment is glued to his marksman. In lane, your job is landing Skill 1's butterflies on the enemy — the slow scales up to 60%, and every second of it is free damage for your carry. Your Passive cleanses your own CC every six seconds, which is exactly why you can afford to stand one step further forward than most supports and menace the enemy laners. Skill 2 even auto-casts every seven seconds, so simply being near enemies keeps feeding speed stacks to your allies at zero cost. Before the 4:00 Tyrant spawns, face-check the river brush yourself so your jungler starts it safely.
strategy.midGame: Mid-game Zhuangzi is judged on one thing: when, and for whom, the Ultimate comes out. Cleanse plus 1.5 seconds of CC immunity plus a shield can void an entire enemy engage — but cast it early and they'll simply hold their skills and wait it out. The rule is to react: the moment enemy stuns or knock-ups land on your carry, layer it on top. Once your HP items finish around 7-8 minutes, work the frontline of objective standoffs with butterfly slows, and quietly count the enemy's CC. Deciding in advance where your Ultimate goes wins teamfights before they start.
strategy.lateGame: The deeper the game goes, the heavier Zhuangzi's power to undo things becomes. Fights past ten minutes are decided by a single landed CC chain, and the ability to erase one wholesale makes your Ultimate a second life for the entire team. In the standoffs before Overlord, stay welded to your carry at reaction distance from any enemy engage. Skill 1 does double duty — closing the net on runners or buying seconds for a retreating ally. There's no highlight reel here, but the moment the enemy engage hero hesitates because Zhuangzi is standing there, you're already halfway to winning.
strategy.teamfight: Position half a step in front of your carry. When enemy CC comes in, erase it with the Ultimate, then flip the fight with the butterfly slow. On the timing: let it land first. The 1.5 seconds of CC immunity whiffs when cast on prediction, so watching the enemy's key skill actually connect before you answer is the higher-percentage play. Your own Passive cleanse means you can tank a few skills yourself — baiting the enemy into wasting CC on you is legitimate work. And the longer the brawl runs, the more Skill 2's stacking damage and speed support quietly tilts it your way.

combos.title: Counter Cleanse
combos.sequence: Watch the enemy engage land → Ultimate (area cleanse + CC immunity) → Skill 1 (slow to turn the fight)
combos.description: Zhuangzi's signature: see the engage, then delete it wholesale. Layer the butterfly slow onto your freed allies' counterattack and the enemy's own initiation becomes the reason they lose.

combos.title: Carry Escort
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (up to 60% slow) → Passive empowerment (self-cleanse + speed) → retreat with your carry
combos.description: Steal the pursuers' legs with the butterflies and walk out together. Skill 1 also refreshes your Passive on cast, so the same routine doubles as your personal escape when you're the one caught.

strengths: The Ultimate's area cleanse and CC immunity turn enemy engages into whiffs
His Passive periodically cleanses his own CC, hard-countering lockdown comps
Skill 1's up-to-60% slow serves both the chase and the rescue
Periodic healing and damage reduction keep him working the frontline for ages
weaknesses: No hard CC of his own — he almost never creates kills singlehandedly
Only a shield stands between his team and raw burst, so heavy dive can power through
Against low-CC enemy comps, the Ultimate's value drops off a cliff

synergy.reason: Locks down enemies on the frontline, creating a safe environment to unleash massive long-range damage.
Can follow up on his tower dives and CC with continuous attacks to quickly secure kills.

counters.reason: Kites effortlessly with high mobility, whittling them down with true damage from afar before they can even get close.
Provides team-wide movement speed buffs that easily kite his engage, completely neutralizing his strengths.

passive.description: Liu Shan's skills deal equal damage to structures, and his crowd control skills disrupt them for 1.2s. He pillages parts of structures to recover 280 Health when dealing damage to them with his skills.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Magnetic Barrier

skill1.description: Liu Shan activates his shield and initiates an assault, gaining 50% Movement Speed that diminishes over time and a shield that negates 650 (650 + 16% extra Health) damage for 3s. Also enhances Liu Shan's next Basic Attack, in which he leaps up and slams into the ground, dealing 569 (350 + 122% physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 1s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Overcharge!

skill2.description: Liu Shan commands his mechcraft to claw at enemies in a cone-shaped area, dealing 580 (400 + 100% physical attack) physical damage to them and stunning them for 1s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Robo Smash

skill3.skill_name: Skill 3: Take It for a Spin
skill3.description:
Liu Shan commands his mechcraft to spin its arms, dealing 380 (380 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies every 0.5s for 3s and slowing them by 15% for 0.5s every second.
Other skills can be used while spinning.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Take It for a Spin

strategy.earlyGame: Liu Shan roams with his team while constantly shopping for the next structure to touch — a habit no other support needs. His Passive lets skills damage towers, CC skills jam them for 1.2 seconds, and every skill hit on a structure refunds 280 HP. Early on, though, the star is Skill 2: time the tip of the fan-shaped stun with your jungler's gank and the kill is all but booked. His range is short, so always approach behind Skill 1's shield and speed boost. At the 4:00 Tyrant, stand at the front and use the stun to shut down anyone contesting.
strategy.midGame: Liu Shan's mid game peaks in the seconds right after a won fight. The moment the enemy backs off, march to the nearest tower, jam it with Skill 2, and start swinging: the tower's counterattack stops for 1.2 seconds, your skills damage it directly, and the HP refunds let you finish sieges other teams would abandon. With two defensive items around eight minutes, you're also a real engage threat — Skill 1 in, empowered basic knock-up, Skill 2 stun. Take mid's first tower early and your roaming radius explodes.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Liu Shan closes matches with a two-part threat: the CC chain and the siege. In fights, rotating Skill 1's empowered knock-up, Skill 2's stun, and the Ultimate's spinning slow locks enemies down for over two seconds singlehandedly. But what makes him genuinely scary past ten minutes is what happens after the fight. Win at Overlord and he jams towers and the crystal into silence while dismantling them — ending games at the moment other teams would recall to heal. Decide what you're breaking after you win before you ever commit to the engage. That's the Liu Shan way.
strategy.teamfight: Your role is to hold enemies in place where your team's damage can reach them. Enter behind Skill 1's shield and speed, open with the empowered basic knock-up, land the Skill 2 fan stun on the enemy carry, then keep the Ultimate spinning for the area slow. Since other skills stay castable during the spin, the CC never has to stop. The thing to fear is distance: every tool in the kit is point-blank, so chasing deep and dying alone is the classic Liu Shan mistake. Meeting the enemies who dive your backline is the far more reliable version of the same fight.

combos.title: Full CC Chain
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (speed up and close in) → Empowered Basic Attack (knock-up) → Skill 2 (stun) → Ultimate (spinning slow)
combos.description: Shield up, step in, and chain knock-up into stun into slow without a gap. Over two seconds of lockdown is more than enough time for your team's damage to arrive and decide the fight.

combos.title: Tower Demolition Kit
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (jam the tower) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (slam + HP refund) → Ultimate
combos.description: The siege routine only Liu Shan owns, courtesy of his structure-damaging Passive. With the tower's counterattack jammed for 1.2 seconds before you start swinging, a half-HP tower falls with minimal damage taken.

strengths: One-of-a-kind siege power — he jams towers while tearing them down directly
Knock-up and stun in one kit make his CC chain fully self-sufficient
Skill 1's shield and speed make the first step of every engage a safe one
HP refunds on every structure hit keep him healthy through long sieges
weaknesses: Every skill is point-blank — good kiting means he never touches anyone
Skill 1's speed boost is his only gap-closer, so mobile enemies slip away
His personal damage is modest; without allied follow-up, the CC achieves nothing

synergy.reason: Dives into the enemy team and groups them up, making it easy to land their ultimate.
Supports both engages and survivability through movement speed buffs and healing.

counters.reason: Can completely interrupt their ultimate with a powerful suppression skill.
Also possesses a suppression skill, resulting in getting completely locked down upon engaging.

passive.description: After using 3 Basic Attacks or skills, the next Basic Attack is enhanced to an energized chord that deals 290 (290 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Guitar Solo

skill1.description:
Gao plays wild notes, dealing 340 (340 + 47% magical attack) magical damage to up to 2 enemies within range. When these notes hit an enemy, they ricochet into nearby enemies up to 2 times.
When multiple notes hit the same hero, subsequent hits only deal 30% damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Wild Chord

skill2.description:
Gao dashes in the target direction while strumming wildly, dealing 450 (450 + 60% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and slowing them by 15% for 2s. Each hero hit recovers 100 (100 + 15% magical attack) Health, while non-hero units recover half this amount. During the dash, he gains 10% damage reduction and immunity to slow.
Using Wild Chord during the dash allows for another dash.
skill2.name: Skill 2: String Bender

skill3.description: Gao performs passionately, dealing 200 (200 + 20% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s for 5s. While performing, he gains 50% Movement Speed which diminishes over 3s. He also gains 10% damage reduction if there is an enemy hero nearby, plus an extra 5% for every additional enemy hero nearby.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Rock Out!

strategy.earlyGame: Until level 4, Gao's only escape tool is Skill 2, so don't force anything in mid lane. Skill 1's notes ricochet to nearby enemies, so land them on the minion wave and let the bounces chip the enemy laner from safety. Every third performance turns your next basic attack into a piercing energy chord thanks to the Passive, so make a habit of finishing each wave clear with a basic attack to speed up your rotations. Skill 2's heal is cut in half when it hits non-heroes, so unless you're escaping, angle the dash to clip the enemy laner.
strategy.midGame: The moment your Ultimate comes online at level 4, Gao becomes a different hero. At the 4-minute Tyrant, wait behind your frontline, then dash in with Skill 2 the instant the enemy clumps up and start spinning your Ultimate. Its damage reduction stacks an extra 5% for every nearby enemy hero, so counterintuitively, performing in the middle of three enemies keeps you alive longer than half-committing onto one. Casting Skill 1 during Skill 2's dash lets you move again — save it to correct your entry angle.
strategy.lateGame: Once three core items are done around 15 minutes, a single full Ultimate rotation can decide a teamfight. The flip side: while it's on cooldown, Gao is just a squishy mage with a healing dash, so stay off the frontline until it comes back. Before you commit, check which enemy is holding the stun, and only dive after you see it land on your frontline — that's how you finish the channel. The tight corridors around Shadow Tyrant and Overlord suit your bouncing notes, so you contribute plenty with pre-fight poke too.
strategy.teamfight: Open at range with Skill 1 poke — the real play comes when the enemy stacks up. Skill 2 into a Skill 1 recast lands you in the center of their team, and if you survive the Ultimate's full 5 seconds, damage ticks every 0.5 seconds into everyone around you. The 50% move speed on activation decays over 3 seconds, so settle your positioning within the first second or two. If you're about to get dropped mid-performance, don't force the full channel — simply walking back toward your team baits the chase and buys time.

combos.title: Encore Dive
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Skill 1 (recast mid-dash) → Ultimate
combos.description: Using Skill 1 during Skill 2's dash grants a second dash — a two-stage entry into the middle of the enemy team. Start the Ultimate immediately on arrival and the damage reduction that stacks per nearby enemy makes finishing the full performance far more realistic.

combos.title: Three-Beat Pierce
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 → Basic Attack → Basic Attack (energy chord)
combos.description: Skills and basic attacks each count as one performance, and the basic attack right after your third performance becomes an energy chord that pierces everything in its path. It reaches the enemy laner straight through the minion wave, making it excellent safe poke in mid lane.

strengths: Ultimate's damage reduction grows with nearby enemies — the deeper the brawl, the longer he survives
Skill 2's heal and dash recast give rare engage-and-exit mobility for a mage
Passive's piercing basic attack handles wave clear and poke at the same time
weaknesses: With the Ultimate down, both damage and durability are ordinary — he can't start fights
Max damage requires diving the enemy team, and one stun ends the performance
Skill 1's repeat hits on the same hero are heavily reduced, so single-target burst is low

synergy.reason: Provides strong CC to lock down enemies, making it easier to follow up with backline damage.
Groups enemies up and shreds their defense, setting the perfect stage for chain kills and skill resets.

counters.reason: Can tank burst damage and interrupt combos with silence skills and high durability.
Can tank through the damage with high durability and shields, posing a high risk of being killed by the counter-engage.

passive.description: All attacks Arke launches from behind her target are guaranteed to crit, while attacks launched from the front are guaranteed not to crit. Her initial Critical Damage is 125%, and every 1% Critical Rate grants an extra 0.5% Critical Damage. Arke's damage when attacking non-hero units from the front is increased by 20%, and her damage to non-hero units is capped at 2,000.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Kiss of Death

skill1.description: Arke wields her twin blades and attacks 2 times, each dealing 150 (150 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Arclight

skill2.description:
Arke dashes forward quickly and attacks a nearby enemy at her destination, dealing 270 (270 + 85% extra physical attack) physical damage and marking the enemy for 10s. She also gains 40% Attack Speed for 3s.
Her attacks on marked the enemy inflict 25% slow for 1s and reduce Untouchable's cooldown by 1s. She takes 30% less damage from marked enemies.
Only 1 enemy can be marked by her at a time.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Untouchable

skill3.description:
Arke goes into stealth mode after a short delay. While in stealth mode, her Movement Speed increases by 40% and she recovers 150 (150 + 25% extra physical attack + 5% extra Health) Health every 0.5s for 4s.
Attacking an enemy will cancel stealth mode and increase her Physical Attack by 120 for 3s.
When an enemy is hit, her Movement Speed increases by 30% for 1s.
Passive: Defeating a hero or assisting refreshes the cooldown of all skills.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Phantom Dance

strategy.earlyGame: Arke is a below-average assassin until her first kill, so commit to a clean jungle route from the start. Her Passive grants 20% bonus damage when hitting monsters from the front, so there's no need to circle behind camps while farming. The goal is both buffs and level 4 — unlocking your Ultimate — before the 4-minute Tyrant. Until then, ganks lean entirely on Skill 2's blink with no follow-up mobility, and a failed gank sets your whole game behind, so only touch targets you can actually kill.
strategy.midGame: Once the Ultimate is up, stealth approaches out of bushes become your job. The 4-second stealth grants 40% move speed, so path around enemy vision and always open from behind. Arke simply cannot crit from the front, so the extra second spent flanking converts directly into damage. Around 10 minutes, with two crit items done, you can solo the enemy backline, and the kill-resets-all-cooldowns mechanic becomes the engine of your chain kills.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Arke is all about patience before the first kill. At Shadow Tyrant or Overlord, lurk in a bush, confirm the enemy's stuns and locks have been spent on your teammates, then Ultimate behind their carry. Kill one and every cooldown resets — re-stealth with the healing and line up the second. Dive at the opening horn instead and one piece of CC (crowd control) exposes your paper HP bar. Enemies hugging walls deny your backstab, so pick victims standing in the open.
strategy.teamfight: Always enter last. Two to three seconds after the enemy's eyes and skills commit to your frontline is your cue. Stealth around the back with the Ultimate, close from behind with Skill 2 to apply the mark, then unload basic attacks and Skill 1. Every hit on the marked target refunds a second of Skill 2's cooldown and you take 30% less damage from them, so tunneling one target down actually keeps you tougher than switching. Once the kill lands, don't stop moving — take your reset skills to the next backline target.

combos.title: Backstab Blitz
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Skill 2 (blink behind) → Basic Attack → Skill 1
combos.description: Stealth around to the target's back, then blink in from behind with Skill 2 to apply the mark. The Passive makes every attack from behind crit, so cram basic attacks and Skill 1 into the 3-second window of 40% bonus attack speed and delete them.

combos.title: Mark and Chase
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (apply mark) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 → Basic Attack
combos.description: Each hit on the marked enemy refunds a second of Skill 2's cooldown and applies a slow. Skill 2 comes back up before they get away, so the chase never breaks as long as you keep swinging.

strengths: Every attack from behind crits — once ahead, she erases backlines in seconds
Kills and assists reset all cooldowns, giving explosive chain-kill potential
Ultimate's stealth and per-tick healing allow both re-engages and clean exits
30% less damage taken from her marked target makes her surprisingly scrappy in duels
weaknesses: No crits from the front — head-on trades cut her damage in half
No hard CC and paper durability; a single stun usually means death
Weak until the first kill lands, making it hard to create openings from behind

synergy.reason: Can easily follow up on Zhong Wuyan's heavy CC with guaranteed burst damage.
Soaks enemy attacks and provides CC on the frontline, allowing for safe and sustained damage output.

counters.reason: Uses high mobility and long-range poke to kite, making it very difficult for the melee-focused Zhong Wuyan to fight.
Possesses strong long-range poke and CC, chunking them out before they can even close the gap.

passive.description:
Whenever Wuyan deals damage with a Basic Attack or skill, there is a 50% chance to petrify enemies for 0.75s.
The same target can only be petrified once every 8s.
Every 3s, she summons the power of the earth to gain a shield that negates 300 (300 + 8% extra Health) damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Petrifying Strike

skill1.description:
Wuyan dashes in the target direction while enhancing her next Basic Attack for 4s. Her enhanced Basic Attack deals 250 (250 + 50% extra physical attack) extra physical damage to enemies within range and slows them by 25% for 2s.
Using Skill 1 while the Ultimate is active slightly reduces the speed of her dash.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Storm and Stress

skill2.description: Wuyan slams the target area with her hammer, dealing 700 (700 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and an extra 50% damage to enemies in the center.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Shock and Awe

skill3.description:
Wuyan spins her hammer, increasing her Movement Speed by 10% for 3.2s. Every 0.4s, she deals 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and an extra 50% damage to enemies at the edge of her attack range.
While spinning, she gains 5% Movement Speed and a shield that negates 80 (80 + 3% extra Health) damage every 0.4s, for up to 4 stacks.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Hurricane Hammer

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, treat everything up to level 4 as target practice for Skill 2. One cast clears the wave, and center hits deal 50% bonus damage, so aim at the enemy's feet the instant they step up for a last-hit. Open trades with Skill 1's dash and its empowered basic attack; when the 50% petrify chance procs, stack Skill 2 onto the frozen target to win the exchange outright. Your Passive shield refreshes every 3 seconds, so the more short trades you take, the further ahead you get.
strategy.midGame: Once your Ultimate unlocks at level 4, make sure you walk to the 4-minute Tyrant fight in time. During the 3.2-second spin, damage ticks every 0.4 seconds and each tick rolls the petrify check, so simply parking it in a brawl freezes enemies one after another. The spin also ramps your move speed in steps and stacks shields, so you can chase fleeing targets too. One caveat: casting Skill 1 during the Ultimate slows the dash — dash first, then spin, and you'll whiff far less.
strategy.lateGame: With three defensive items done around 15 minutes, your role is holding the front and stopping enemies on repeat. Enter fights with Skill 1 into their clump, then Ultimate immediately. The spin's outer edge deals 50% bonus damage, so a half-step of positioning to keep enemies on the rim turns your damage into something else entirely. Petrify is still a dice roll, though — don't stake everything on it against the one target you absolutely must stop. Keep Skill 2 in reserve for after the spin, and a petrified backliner becomes a free kill to carry home.
strategy.teamfight: Your teamfight job is to spin in the middle of their team and wreck the formation. Skill 1 in, Ultimate out: ticks every 0.4 seconds scatter petrifies across multiple enemies, leaving them unable to fight back or retreat cleanly. Petrify has an 8-second cooldown per target, so rather than chasing someone already frozen, walk your spin onto enemies you haven't stopped yet — total lockdown time goes up. The window right after the spin ends is your biggest opening, and whether Skill 2 goes onto their backline or stays for self-defense there swings the result.

combos.title: Petrify One-Two
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Empowered Basic Attack → Skill 2
combos.description: Dash in, roll the petrify check with the empowered hit, then line Skill 2's center up on the frozen target's feet. The center hit deals 50% bonus damage — a core pattern that works from lane trades all the way to late-game carry deletion.

combos.title: Spin Control
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Ultimate → Skill 2
combos.description: Dash into the brawl and spin for 3.2 seconds, handing out petrifies while walking to keep enemies on the outer edge for bonus damage. When the spin ends, finish survivors with Skill 2 — the full-course teamfight menu.

strengths: Every instance of damage carries a 50% petrify chance — keep hitting and enemies stop moving
Skill 2 center hits deal enough damage to delete backliners even on a tanky build
Passive and Ultimate shields keep cycling, making her tougher than her stats suggest
weaknesses: Petrify is RNG — it can fail at the decisive moment and invite a counterattack
Skill 2's long wind-up makes it hard to land raw on mobile targets
Her only mobility is Skill 1's short dash, so kiting shuts her out completely

synergy.reason: Enables safe positioning and damage output through mobility buffs and silence skills.
Boosts the survivability of low-mobility marksmen through movement speed buffs and healing.

counters.reason: Uses high mobility and burst damage to instantly delete the squishy Sun Bin.
Excels at poke and mobility, constantly applying pressure while easily dodging Sun Bin's skills.

passive.description: Whenever Sun Bin uses a skill, he gains 65-130 Movement Speed for 2s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Hourglass of Time

skill1.description:
Sun Bin throws a bomb in the target direction that deals 200 (200 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to the first enemy it hits and latches onto them.
The bomb explodes 3s later or when the target dies, dealing 575 (575 + 60% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 15% for 2s.
Cleansing the bomb will cause it to detonate immediately.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Time Bomb

skill2.description:
Sun Bin manipulates time, increasing the Movement Speed of himself and nearby teammates by 130 for 2s. After the 2s, he recovers Health equal to 25% of the damage taken during this period.
Passive: He gains 7.5% Cooldown Reduction.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Time Flux

skill3.description:
Sun Bin throws an enhanced bomb in the target direction. Upon hitting an enemy or reaching its max range, the bomb unfurls an energy field, dealing 500 (500 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them immensely for 1s. The field interrupts the enemy's skill and silences them for 1s.
The energy field explodes 5s later, dealing 1,500 (1,500 + 135% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Time Lapse

strategy.earlyGame: Sun Bin is a roaming support built around time manipulation. Start by shadowing your marksman and holding the farm lane bushes; when the enemy commits, Skill 2's team-wide speed boost gets everyone out. The boost heals 25% of damage taken during its duration when it ends, so cast it just before enemy skills connect — not after you've started running — and the HP difference is plain to see. Skill 1's bomb is all about the 3-second detonation, so in skirmishes, sandwich the tagged target with an ally and chase until it pops.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, ganks built around your Ultimate start connecting at a much higher rate. The field applies a heavy 1-second slow on hit and even silences enemies caught mid-cast, making it the answer to targets holding escape skills. At the 4-minute Tyrant and mid-game rotations, ferrying your whole team with Skill 2's +130 move speed is a job only Sun Bin does. Walking speed converts directly into numbers advantages — arrive at objectives five-strong one beat before the enemy, over and over, and the map tilts your way.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, placing your Ultimate is map control in itself. The field detonates 5 seconds after deployment, so drop it in the narrow entrance to Shadow Tyrant or Overlord and the enemy must either fight inside the blast zone or concede the spawn. When fights break out, stick Skill 1 on their key hero and play for the detonation; when your team needs to reset, Skill 2's speed and refund heal rebuild the line. Your personal damage is modest, so operate from behind your team, out of enemy reach, and keep pulling the strings.
strategy.teamfight: Open teamfights by placing your Ultimate on the enemy's escape path, not at their feet. The 1-second slow lets your team's follow-up land, and the 5-second delayed blast catches them on the retreat. Attach Skill 1 to a frontliner and the 3-second fuse plus AoE slow completes the trap. Skill 2 works as an engage tool too, but its best use is covering the exact moment enemy burst lands — with 25% of damage taken coming back a few seconds later, it feels like haggling the enemy mage's full combo down to three-quarters price.

combos.title: Timed Detonation
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 → Basic Attack
combos.description: Attach the bomb, then speed your team alongside the target so they can't shake the 3-second fuse. The blast's AoE damage and slow make your team's follow-up all but guaranteed — the standard gank-support pattern.

combos.title: Cut the Exit
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Skill 1 → Skill 2
combos.description: Catch enemies in the field's heavy slow, stack the bomb on top, then accelerate your whole team to close in. The field's blast 5 seconds later reaches even the enemies who backed off — in tight terrain, this sequence alone can decide the fight.

strengths: Skill 2 speeds up the entire team, winning rotations and chases before they start
25% of damage taken during the boost returns as healing — a strong burst counter
Ultimate silences on interrupt, and its delayed blast dominates whole areas
weaknesses: No stuns or hard CC, so he can't lock down a kill by himself
Both Skill 1 and the Ultimate have delayed payoffs, lacking instant stopping power
Personal damage and durability are below average — a misused speed boost leaves nothing

119.name: Dr Bian

synergy.reason: Uses durable tanks on the frontline to easily stack poison on enemies while keeping allies healed.
Soaks up enemy attacks, creating an ideal environment for dealing sustained damage and healing.

counters.reason: Applies anti-heal and deals burst damage, making it extremely difficult to drag out fights and sustain.
Uses high mobility and burst damage to burst them down before they have a chance to heal.

passive.description:
Dr Bian's Basic Attacks and skills place a poison mark on enemies for 7s (up to 5 stacks), dealing 20 (20 + 5% magical attack) magical damage per second.
Healing skills place a healing mark on teammates and himself for 7s (up to 5 stacks), restoring 3 (3 + 2% magical attack) Health per second to teammates, and 3 (3 + 2% magical attack + 0.15% extra Health) Health per second to himself.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Malicious Practice

skill1.description:
Dr Bian throws a vial of lethal poison that shatters upon impact, releasing a pool of poison for 4s. Every second, it deals 65 (65 + 14% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within the area and slows them by 30% for 2s.
Dr Bian stocks 1 vial every 12.5s. Up to 3 vials can be stocked.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Deadly Panacea

skill2.description: Dr Bian throws a concoction, dealing 130 (130 +30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies hit and restoring 65 (65 +15% magical attack) Health to nearby teammates.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Fatal Diagnosis

skill3.description:
Dr Bian detonates all nearby marks, dealing 150 (150 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to enemies while restoring 70 (70 + 20% magical attack) Health to teammates. Each stack of mark increases damage and healing by 50%.
He also recovers 400 (400 + 30% magical attack + 5% extra Health) extra Health.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Master of Life

strategy.earlyGame: Dr Bian's early game is an exercise in patience. With no burst, mid lane trades are losing propositions until your first core item finishes, so clear waves with Skill 1's poison pools and manage your HP. Vials restock every 12.5 seconds up to a cap of three — always bank one for self-defense. Whenever the enemy jungler is off the map, dropping a pool at your feet before backing off cuts gank success rates dramatically. Basic attacks apply a poison stack through the Passive too, so keep tapping targets from safe range.
strategy.midGame: Around 8 minutes, with one or two items done, you can drag fights into your arena: long skirmishes. In Tyrant standoffs, throw Skill 1 at their feet from behind your frontline, cycle Skill 2 for chip damage and ally healing, and once poison marks build up, detonate them with your Ultimate. Each stack adds 50% to the blast's damage and healing, so holding for 5 stacks instead of panicking at 2 changes what the fight looks like. Past the 10-second mark of any brawl, the poison-versus-healing math starts sinking the enemy team.
strategy.lateGame: The later the game, the more Dr Bian wants to dodge coin-flip bursts and drag everyone into attrition. Line up three poison pools in front of Shadow Tyrant or Overlord and the enemy either fights while melting or gives up the spawn. In teamfights, stand near the center of your team and use the Ultimate's detonation for AoE damage and a team-wide heal in the same instant. Once enemies start buying anti-heal items, your edge shrinks — compensate with timing, detonating earlier, before allies drop below half HP.
strategy.teamfight: Skip the flashy opener — you're the fight's accountant, keeping the books on marks. Open with Skill 1 into their clump, throw Skill 2 at whoever is easiest to hit (usually the frontline) while healing allies around you, and once both teams tangle, detonate everything with the Ultimate. Blowing 5-stack poison across multiple enemies at once is the comeback button: AoE damage and a team recovery in the same moment.
