Skill 2's punch flurry doubles as healing and percent-HP damage, giving you surprising staying power in monster tug-of-wars.
strategy.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, Dharma's grade depends entirely on forcing fights into tight terrain. Start a fight in the corridor outside Overlord or around a jungle corner and you get the dream play — wall-stunning the enemy carry right in front of your team. In the wide-open river center, though, your knockback is just a shove and half your threat disappears. Claiming the strong bush early to control where the fight happens is your hidden late-game job. Keep three Passive stacks rolling and you hold your own in frontline slugfests too.
strategy.teamfight: You have exactly one objective: put an enemy backliner into a wall. Enter with Skill 1's dash, set your angle, then fire the Ultimate — and take the half-second before casting to confirm a wall actually sits behind them, because that pause is the difference between a kill and a whiff. Once the stun lands, finish with the flying kick and Skill 2's punch flurry. Skill 2 lets you steer mid-channel, but your movement is still restricted, so swinging it out in front of an enemy holding burst is asking to die. Canceling early is always on the table — take the kills that are actually there.

combos.title: Wall-Slam Execution
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Ultimate (aimed at a wall) → Skill 1 (flying kick) → Skill 2
combos.description: Dash into range, knock them into the wall for the one-second stun and bonus damage, stack the flying kick's 15% missing-HP hit, and grind out the rest with the punch flurry. Dharma's signature play — just confirm the wall before you commit.

combos.title: Lane Hit-and-Run
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Basic Attack (empowered)
combos.description: Knock-up off the dash, land one slowing empowered basic, and leave. With the Passive's defense buff active during the round trip, you barely take any return damage.

strengths: Huge burst from the wall stun into the flying kick conversion
Strong brawling stats via the Passive's defense buff and Skill 2 healing
Percent-HP damage on Skill 2 chews through high-health targets
Two Skill 1 charges give him flexibility on offense and escape
weaknesses: Loses half his threat in open terrain with no walls
Restricted movement during Skill 2 makes him a target for big skills
A misjudged knockback angle shoves the enemy to safety instead

synergy.reason: Can peel enemies away and maintain distance, safely protecting low-mobility marksmen.
Can engage and lock down enemies, creating openings for high-burst allies to dive safely.

counters.reason: His high mobility and armor-piercing capabilities render tankiness useless.
His armor shred debuff drastically reduces the survivability provided by the passive.

passive.description:
When Xiang Yu's Health drops below 30%, he gains 40% damage reduction for 6s. This effect can only be triggered once every 90s.
After using Righteous Fervor and No Retreat, Xiang Yu gains different enhanced Basic Attacks. Stocks up to 2 charges.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Resolute Will

skill1.description:
Xiang Yu charges in the target direction, knocking back enemies and launching them for 0.75s with a slash. The charge and slash each deal 225 (225 + 5% extra Health) physical damage.
His next Basic Attack is enhanced into a vertical chop that deals 445 (250 + 100% physical attack + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage and is guaranteed to be a critical hit with a base critical damage of 150%.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Righteous Fervor

skill2.description: Xiang Yu roars, slowing nearby enemies by 15% for 2s, dealing 275 (275 + 90% extra physical attack) magical damage, and reducing their damage output by 30% for 3.5s. He then gains an enhanced Basic Attack and a 25% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 2s. The enhanced Basic Attack is a horizontal sweep that restores 350 (350 + 7% extra Health) Health (effect is reduced to 50% against non-hero units; the lower his Health, the higher the recovery, up to a maximum of 50%) and deals 235 (40 + 100% physical attack) physical damage.
skill2.name: Skill 2: No Retreat

skill3.description:
Xiang Yu charges up and unleashes an energy wave with his sword while gaining crowd control immunity and Undying, dealing 900 (900 + 260% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies along the path. Enemies in the inner zone take 50% extra damage and are stunned for 0.75s. The lower Xiang Yu's Health is, the more damage he deals, up to 50% extra damage. 20% of damage dealt is converted into Health.
Undying: Xiang Yu cannot be defeated and his Health will not drop below 1.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Hegemon's Slash

strategy.earlyGame: On the global server, roam is his standard assignment. Attach to your marksman from level 1 and play the bodyguard: in skirmishes, Skill 1's knockback exists to bat divers away from your carry. In trades, Skill 2 is quietly vicious — it cuts the attack damage of every enemy in range by 30% for 3.5 seconds, so slapping it on top of the enemy's engage simply deletes their trade math. Maintain HP with the empowered basic's healing, rush tank items above all else, and be there when your jungler moves for the 4-minute Tyrant.
strategy.midGame: Through the mid game, with one or two defensive items done, Xiang Yu's value is measured in gank follow-ups. Skill 1's dash carries enemies with its knockback, so the trick is angling it to shove a fleeing target back toward your team — connect the knock-up and your side's full damage lands during it. In Tyrant and mid-lane collisions, stand at the very front and stop fearing a shrinking HP bar: drop below 30% and the Passive's 40% damage reduction triggers on its own, wrecking the enemy's damage math. Weaken overchasers with Skill 2 and swallow them whole — that's the mid-game pattern.
strategy.lateGame: The late game belongs to Xiang Yu. Right when enemy damage peaks, his kit peaks harder: 40% damage reduction below 30% HP, and an Ultimate that makes him unkillable — HP cannot drop below 1 — while it's active. The tank who was supposed to die first simply doesn't, and that stolen time becomes your team's counterattack window. The Ultimate also deals more and heals more the lower your HP sits, so a near-death swing hits harder than some fighters' full combos. At Overlord, soak every enemy cooldown at the front, then look for the answering blow.
strategy.teamfight: The job description is short: stand at the front, get hurt, then hit back. Your opening is a choice between shoving their frontline into your team with Skill 1 or batting an assassin off your carry. Fire Skill 2 the instant enemies clump — a 30% attack cut across their whole team visibly shrinks the damage your side takes. The Ultimate is for stepping into the enemy team on low HP: super armor and the unkillable effect mean you cannot die during the charge, and the slash stuns with 50% bonus damage on connect. The moment the Xiang Yu they thought was dead swings back is the moment fights flip.

combos.title: Standard Engage
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Ultimate → Skill 2 → Basic Attack (empowered)
combos.description: Lock them down with the dash's knockback into knock-up, then land the charged slash on a target who can't move. Finish with Skill 2's 30% attack cut and rotate to defense behind the healing empowered basic.

combos.title: Deathbed Reversal
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Ultimate → Skill 1
combos.description: Cut your pursuers' attack damage, then charge the Ultimate at low HP. The unkillable window guarantees the swing comes out, and the slash scales up as your HP drops — the enemy who smelled blood gets carried home instead.

strengths: Gets tougher as he gets lower via the unkillable Ultimate and 40% damage reduction
Skill 2's 30% attack cut suppresses an entire team's damage
Excellent peel with knockback and knock-up to protect his carries
The low-HP Ultimate hits far harder than a tank has any right to
weaknesses: Skill 1 is his only movement and can't cross walls — kiting ruins him
The Ultimate's charge-up is telegraphed and easy to sidestep
Missing the blade's edge means no stun and no bonus damage
Low damage and low pressure while his HP bar is still full

synergy.reason: Their combined high mobility allows them to easily follow up on chunked enemies and snowball with kills.
Groups enemies together, making it much easier to land the ultimate and AoE silence.

counters.reason: Possesses even higher mobility than Sima Yi, allowing him to easily escape or counter-engage.
Can completely peel and protect the target from burst damage with massive shields and CC.

passive.description:
Sima Yi gains vision of enemies casting skills within a range of 2,000 and gains 10 Shadow Force (up to 50).
After using the skill, Sima Yi condenses Shadow Force into a scythe, gaining an enhanced Basic Attack and 20 Movement Speed for 5s. Using the enhanced Basic Attack consumes all Shadow Force.
Each scythe strike deals 230 (230 + 46% magical attack) magical damage and true damage equal to Shadow Force. The first attack allows Sima Yi to dash behind the target and deals 300 (300 + 60% magical attack) magical damage (true damage is doubled).
For every 20 Shadow Force consumed, the enhanced Basic Attack's range increases by 3%.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Quiet Whispers

skill1.description:
Sima Yi gains crowd control immunity and begins controlling a spirit with high Movement Speed that lasts 2.5s.
The spirit deals 115 (115 + 23% magical attack) magical damage to enemies it passes through. When Sima Yi uses a Basic Attack or when the spirit's duration ends, Sima Yi moves to the spirit's location, dealing 115 (115 + 23% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and slowing them by 25% for 1s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Shadow Stings

skill2.description:
Sima Yi releases spiritual energy and suppresses enemies in the surrounding area, dealing 250 (250 + 50% magical attack) magical damage and silencing them for 0.75s. Inside the suppression zone, Sima Yi gains 10% increased recovery.
Passive: When Sima Yi takes magical damage, 25% is converted into Health recovery for 3s (halved for physical damage).
skill2.name: Skill 2: Barren Lands

skill3.description:
Sima Yi steps back and charges up briefly, then dashes to the target location, where he deals 500 (500 + 100% magical attack) magical damage (damage halved to enemies along his path).
If this skill is interrupted, 90% cooldown is returned.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Death Descends

strategy.earlyGame: Sima Yi lives in the mid lane. Before level 4, keep an eye on your Passive: every skill an enemy hero casts nearby feeds you 10 energy, up to 50. When you are near the cap, harass with the empowered basic attack — its first hit teleports you behind the target, so even enemies hugging their minion wave can't hide from it. Into a mage matchup, Skill 2's passive heals you for 25% of magic damage taken, which means you can accept extended trades. One hard rule: never step forward while both your mana and your energy are empty.
strategy.midGame: Once the 4-minute Tyrant contest starts, shove mid and rotate for ambushes on the side lanes and jungle. The spirit from Skill 1 is immune to crowd control and moves fast, so your body stays safe while you set up the approach — coming in sideways through brush is ideal. Chip with the behind-the-back empowered basic, then land Skill 2's 0.75-second silence to lock out their blink or CC before finishing the job. Your Passive also grants vision of enemy heroes who cast skills, so anyone charging a skill in brush gives away their position and hands you the ambush.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, with Savant's Wrath and Void Staff complete, your one-shot threat is real — but you're as fragile as ever. Let teammates take the first hit in teamfights, and move only after the enemy has dumped skills, feeding you both energy and vision. Your Ultimate is a backstep into a long charged dash that works for offense or escape, and since an interrupted charge refunds 90% of the cooldown, deliberately showing the wind-up to bait enemy CC becomes more and more valuable as the game goes on.
strategy.teamfight: Your spot in a brawl is second wave. Because enemy skill casts charge your energy, entering from the flank right after their engage beats opening with a full combo — better damage, better safety. Hunt the isolated mage or marksman: the instant the empowered basic teleports you behind them, layer Skill 2's silence so they physically can't press their escape while you shred them. Skill 1 is effectively a blink since you can relocate to the spirit's position, so keep one charge in reserve as an exit — it changes your survival rate completely.

combos.title: Backstab Ambush
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (spirit approach) → Empowered Basic Attack → Skill 2 → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Close the gap with the spirit, teleport behind the target with the empowered basic, then silence them before they can answer. Build your energy to around 50 before committing — the true damage payoff grows dramatically.

combos.title: Long-Range Engage
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Skill 2 → Empowered Basic Attack → Skill 1 (exit)
combos.description: Charge in from distance, lock the target with the silence, get your hits in, then leave through the spirit. The dash deals half damage to enemies along its path, so always angle it to strike your real target directly.

combos.title: Charge Bluff
combos.sequence: Ultimate (charge only) → Cancel → Recharge
combos.description: Abuse the 90% cooldown refund on an interrupted charge: show the wind-up, force the enemy to burn their dodge skills, then reset. Especially effective in late-game standoffs.

strengths: Energy charged by enemy skill casts plus a behind-the-target teleport gives elite ambush power
Skill 2's silence and 25% magic-damage healing make him a nightmare for mages
The CC-immune spirit doubles as a gap-closer and an escape route
Interrupted Ultimate refunds 90% of its cooldown, so he can always re-engage
weaknesses: Healing is halved against physical damage, so marksmen grind him down
Damage depends on passive energy — enemies who hold their skills starve him
A clear damage trough opens right after his empowered basics are spent
Low base durability; a failed kill attempt invites an instant counter

synergy.reason: Can constantly out-rotate and confuse the enemy using a combination of split-pushing and recalls.
Can lock down enemies for a long duration with his ultimate, creating a safe window to unleash maximum DPS.

counters.reason: Can easily win auto-attack trades thanks to superior mobility and damage reduction.
Constantly gets knocked back and kited, making it extremely difficult to close the gap and stack auto-attacks.

passive.description: Whenever Fuzi lands a Basic Attack, he gains 1 stack of Admonition for 5s, up to 5 stacks. At full stacks, he becomes enhanced for 5s. While enhanced, he gains 60 Movement Speed and 30% Attack Speed, while each Basic Attack deals an extra 80 (80 + 28% extra physical attack) true damage and reduces his Skill 1 and Skill 2's Cooldown by 1s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Ancient Wisdom

skill1.description: Fuzi swings his ferule in the target direction, pulling enemies within range toward him and dealing 320 (320 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage while slowing them by 25% for 1.5−2.5s (duration scales with skill level).
skill1.name: Skill 1: Corporal Punishment

skill2.description:
Fuzi enhances himself for 2s, during which he gains 25% Movement Speed and 45% damage reduction.
While enhanced, he reflects 50% of the damage taken after being hit by the first Basic Attack and slows his attackers by 15% for 2s. This reflected damage carries his Basic Attack's on-hit effects.
Passive: His Basic Attack has a 25% chance of being followed up with another Basic Attack that inflicts 50% damage and on-hit effects.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Intuition

skill3.description: Fuzi charges in the target direction, dealing 600 (600 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy hero hit and binding them to his lamppost. While bound, the enemy hero will be confined for 5s within the area where his Ultimate hit, and deal 20% less damage.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Sage's Might

strategy.earlyGame: Take Skill 2 first in the clash lane — the damage reduction and bonus-attack procs let you clear the opening wave and trade at the same time. Fuzi's lifeline is his Passive: whether you have five stacks banked from hitting minions before you commit changes the fight entirely. The empowered state adds true damage and shaves the cooldowns of Skills 1 and 2, so at even HP you win most slugfests on math alone. Don't chase before level 4, and any time the enemy jungler disappears from the map, assume the river brush and back off.
strategy.midGame: At the 4-minute Tyrant fight, your job is to open by binding the enemy fighter or jungler with your Ultimate. Five seconds of restricted movement plus 20% reduced damage output means they fight the whole skirmish at a disadvantage. In lane, lean on your 1v1 strength to push the side, and drag anyone who collapses on you into melee with Skill 1. Skill 2 reflects 50% of the first basic attack you take while it's active — read the tell on an enemy's empowered attack and pop it in response, and you win the trade on that alone.
strategy.lateGame: True to his late-game label, Fuzi peaks once Doomsday and Blood Rage come online after 15 minutes. Five-stack true damage all but ignores armor, so almost nobody wins a straight brawl against you. But games are decided at Shadow Tyrant and Overlord, not in a side lane. Leave the 1v1 thirty seconds before the objective spawns, regroup with your team, and claim the position that lets you land your Ultimate as the fight's opening move.
strategy.teamfight: The dream scenario: bind the enemy carry right before the brawl starts and turn it into a 5v4. The dash latches onto the first hero it touches, so when their frontline is walling you out, look for a flank angle. Once the bind lands, activate Skill 2's 45% damage reduction and never stop swinging — as long as your basics connect, the stacks and cooldown refunds keep cycling, and Fuzi only gets stronger the longer the fight runs. Standing around without a target is the one thing that kills you.

combos.title: Opening Bind
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Skill 2 → Basic Attacks → Skill 1 (pull back)
combos.description: Dash in, tie their ace to the lantern, then keep swinging under the damage reduction. Anyone drifting to the edge of the restricted zone gets yanked back with Skill 1. Since the bound target deals 20% less damage, you can afford to eat the counterplay.

combos.title: Full-Stack Trade
combos.sequence: Basic Attack ×5 (max Passive stacks) → Skill 2 → Skill 1 → Basic Attacks
combos.description: The standard lane pattern: stack your Passive on minions, then commit in the empowered state. With true damage and cooldown refunds rolling, you can swallow opponents who started the fight with an HP lead.

combos.title: Counter Reflect
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (on reaction) → Skill 1 → Basic Attack
combos.description: See the enemy's dive or empowered attack coming, activate Skill 2 to bounce 50% of that first basic attack back, then pull them in and punish. It flips the entire damage exchange on its head.

strengths: Five-stack true damage makes him one of the game's best 1v1 brawlers
Skill 2's 45% damage reduction and reflect turn enemy aggression against them
The Ultimate's 5-second bind and 20% damage cut shuts down the enemy ace
A late-game power curve that keeps climbing as items complete
weaknesses: Needs uninterrupted basic attacks to function — kiting shuts him down hard
His only real gap-closer is the Ultimate; missing it leaves a long window
Skill 1's pull radius is small and whiffs against high-mobility targets
Without stacks, both his damage and durability are merely average

synergy.reason: The movement speed buff makes it easy to maintain his empowered charge state.
Provides shields and CC peel, allowing for safe dives into the enemy backline and clean disengages.

counters.reason: His ultimate restricts movement, completely shutting down the ability to maintain the charge state.
Her point-and-click stun easily stops the engage, leaving him vulnerable to heavy burst damage.

passive.description:
Normal Stance: Guan Yu gains 2% Movement Speed for every 200 units of distance he moves, entering Charge Stance upon moving 2,000 units. When Movement Speed drops below 375, exits Charge Stance, and the accumulated distance is reset after 0.7s.
When standing stationary near brush, recovers 30 Health and Energy every 0.5s.
Charge Stance: Enhances next Basic Attack, charging forward to deal an extra 500 (500 + 125% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and knocking them back. Gains 20% Movement Speed when moving toward enemy heroes.
When in Normal Stance, he can use Basic Attacks while moving.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Rider of Triumph

skill1.description:
Normal Stance: Guan Yu swings his blade, dealing 500 (500 + 140% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies.
Charge Stance: He charges forward, dealing 360 (360 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and knocking them back. He then attacks again, dealing 500 (500 + 160% extra physical attack) physical damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Heroic Charge

skill2.description:
Normal Stance: Guan Yu removes all crowd control effects from himself and gains 30% Movement Speed for 2s.
Charge Stance: He removes all crowd control effects from himself and leaps forward, dealing 650 (650 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies near his landing point and knocking them back. He also gains 30% Movement Speed for 2s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Soaring Green Dragon

skill3.description:
Normal Stance: Guan Yu enhances himself for 10s. While enhanced, the distance required to enter Charge Stance is reduced by 75%.
Charge Stance: Guan Yu summons heavy cavalry on either side of himself that charge forward with him, dealing 620 (620 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in their path and knocking them back. He then enhances himself for 10s. While enhanced, the distance required to enter Charge Stance is reduced by 75%.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Razor Cavalry

strategy.earlyGame: Guan Yu starts in the clash lane, but after the first two waves your top priority is simple: never stop moving. His Passive enters the charge state after 2000 units of travel, so every second spent standing in a lane staring at your opponent is a second spent being weak. Loop through the river and your own jungle to build a runway, then knock enemies flying with the charged basic attack, disengage, and repeat. Until level 4, resist every urge to chase — hit, knock them back, and leave. That alone wins you lane priority.
strategy.midGame: The game becomes Guan Yu's around the 4-minute Tyrant. Objective standoffs hand you runways for free, and a single blindside knockback into their backline can decide the fight before it starts. Using your Ultimate first halves the travel distance needed to enter the charge state, so you can re-engage faster. When ganking, angle your approach so enemies get knocked toward your tower or your teammates — punting them to safety in their own territory is the classic first mistake every new Guan Yu makes.
strategy.lateGame: With two or three defense items like Overlord's Platemail and Blazing Cape done by 15 minutes, the 10% max HP damage on your charged basics starts hurting even tanks. At Shadow Tyrant and Overlord, your job is to crash sideways into the brush they're holding, wedge yourself between the boss pit and their team, and split their formation. You lack solo kill power, so leave knocked-back targets to your teammates and immediately start building the next runway. While an enemy with strong slows is alive, take the long way around and come from behind — never the front.
strategy.teamfight: Your teamfight prep starts 30 seconds early: run the perimeter and keep the charge state alive. The ideal entry clips their marksman and mage in a single line, and once you've run someone over, do not stop — Skill 2 cleanses crowd control and re-accelerates you for a second and third pass. Planting your feet in the middle of the scrum is the worst thing you can do. Keep making passes back and forth through their team, and the enemy never reforms their line while your own backline shoots for free.

combos.title: Cavalry Charge
combos.sequence: Build momentum (charge state) → Ultimate → Skill 1 → Basic Attack
combos.description: Summon the troop charge from the charge state to knock the enemy team flying, then follow with Skill 1's dash and sweep. The stacked max-HP percentage damage lets you blast through frontliners, not just around them.

combos.title: Cleanse and Rerun
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (cleanse CC) → Move to rebuild momentum → Charged Basic Attack
combos.description: The moment you're caught, break the crowd control with Skill 2, accelerate away, rebuild your runway, and charge again. For Guan Yu, the courage to leave a fight is literally your next source of damage.

combos.title: Lane Trade
combos.sequence: Build momentum (charge state) → Basic Attack (knockback) → Skill 1 (sweep) → Disengage
combos.description: The bread-and-butter early trade: knock them away with the charged hit, add the sweep, and be gone before their answer arrives. The knockback opens the distance for you, making the trade almost entirely one-sided.

strengths: Charged basics deal 10% max HP damage with knockback — painful for everyone
Skill 2 self-cleanses CC, making him extremely hard to pin down
Elite formation-breaking; he creates teamfight openings single-handedly
Gets stronger just by running, so his farm dependency is low
weaknesses: Standing still drops the charge state, leaving him weak in tight scrums
Stacked slows or chained CC stop his feet and get him focused down
Demands runway knowledge and heavy mechanics — a genuinely hard hero
Lacks solo kill power; his knockbacks need teammates to convert

synergy.reason: The AoE CC cleanse allows her to continuously dance inside her ultimate without being locked down.
Can group enemies with his powerful AoE taunt, maximizing the AoE damage of her ultimate.

counters.reason: His suppress ultimate cannot be cleansed by Purify, completely shutting down her mobility.
High burst damage and silence create a huge risk of getting one-shot before being able to cycle skills.

passive.description: Every time one of Diaochan's skills deals damage, it places a floral mark on the target for 8s. At the maximum of 4 stacks, the marks will be activated, restoring 140 (140 + 1.5% extra Health) Health to her while dealing 140 (140 + 40% magical attack) true damage to nearby enemies and slowing them by 25%-50% for 1s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Explosion of Fragrance

skill1.description: Diaochan sends out a lotus in the target direction, dealing 260 (260 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and again on its way back.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Returning Lotus

skill2.description: Diaochan blinks to the target location and launches 3 lotus petals at nearby enemies. Each petal deals 140 (140 + 28% magical attack) magical damage and reduces Skill 2's Cooldown for up to 3s based on the locations of her and the target hit.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Petals in the Wind

skill3.description:
Diaochan conjures a lotus circle that deals 210 (210 + 50% magical attack) magical damage upon its appearance and disappearance. When she is in the circle, the cooldowns of her Skill 1 and 2 are further reduced.
Tapping the skill again will close the lotus circle.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Flowery Potential

strategy.earlyGame: Mid lane, and until level 4 it's a patience game. Skill 1's lotus travels out and back, so catching an enemy with both halves stacks two marks in one cast — that alone covers your waveclear and poke. Skill 2 is Diaochan's only escape, so don't throw it away on offense while gank threat exists. Since four marks detonate for damage and healing, you can actually take extended HP trades more confidently than your frame suggests. Your first item goal is an early Holy Grail to erase your mana problems.
strategy.midGame: From around 7-8 minutes, with Holy Grail and cooldown items online, Diaochan becomes a true close-range mage. On roams, close instantly with Skill 2 — landing all three orbs point-blank refunds 12 seconds of its cooldown and lets you move again immediately. In skirmishes before Tyrant, lay down your Ultimate's field first, then cycle Skills 1 and 2; the true damage and healing from mark detonations can push back even a numbers disadvantage. But diving while enemy stuns or silences are still up is suicide — count who has spent their CC before you go in.
strategy.lateGame: In the late game, Diaochan's detonation true damage hits tanks and squishies alike, no matter how much armor they've stacked, so her relative damage actually rises. After 15 minutes, never take a teamfight without your Ultimate field down — inside it, your Skill 1 and 2 rotation speeds up, and with the healing included you become a different hero entirely. The one matchup to respect is burst: if an enemy assassin has the damage to delete you before your healing catches up, hold Purify or Flash and let a teammate take the first engage.
strategy.teamfight: Teamfighting Diaochan comes down to one sentence: enter the middle the instant enemy CC is gone. With your field down, the enemy clump is your fuel — hitting multiple enemies chains mark detonations until your healing outpaces the damage coming in. The ideal is catching two or three enemies in the field and confusing their aim with Skill 2's teleports while you dance. The flip side: a single stun collapses everything, so before the fight starts, know exactly who on their team holds CC and what they haven't used yet.

combos.title: Field Dance
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Skill 2 → Skill 1 → Skill 2
combos.description: Drop the field, get point-blank, and cycle Skill 2 as your engine with the cooldown acceleration running. Every orb that lands refunds 4 seconds, so inside an enemy clump you almost never stop moving.

combos.title: Four-Mark Detonation
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (two hits out and back) → Skill 2 (three orbs) → Detonation
combos.description: Stack two marks with the lotus round trip, then teleport in and run the count to four with the orbs. The detonation's true damage and slow leave the choice of chasing or leaving entirely up to you.

combos.title: Emergency Exit
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (teleport backward) → Skill 1 (cover the retreat)
combos.description: The moment a gank lands, teleport toward a wall or your teammates and throw the lotus back to punish pursuit. Remember: the window right after you've spent Skill 2 on offense is exactly when you're most hunted.

strengths: The detonation loop of true damage and healing gives elite staying power in brawls
Skill 2's teleport refunds cooldown on every orb hit, so she never stops moving
Inside her Ultimate's field, faster skill cycling shreds multiple enemies at once
True damage core means her output never falls off against late-game tanks
weaknesses: A silence or stun that stops the combo gets her deleted instantly
Low base durability — burst damage before marks detonate is lethal
A melee-range mage at heart; long-range poke comps never let her touch them
Very Hard difficulty — below full mastery she's just a squishy melee

synergy.reason: Cleanses CC, allowing them to safely channel their vulnerable ultimate.
Acts as a durable frontline with shields, locking down enemies so skillshots can land easily.

counters.reason: Uses high mobility to quickly close the gap and easily kill her while she's rooted during her ultimate.
Can lock her down with point-and-click hard CC and instantly burst her squishy down.

passive.description:
Every time Angela deals damage with one of her active skills, she places 1 stack of Burning on the target while gaining 1 stack of increased Movement Speed herself. Both max out at 10 stacks and last for 3s.
Stacks on enemies cause the target to take an extra 10 (10 + 2% magical attack) magical damage from her active skills, while stacks on Angela increase her Movement Speed by 2%.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Flame Incantation

skill1.description:
Angela unleashes 5 fireballs in the target direction. When a fireball hits an enemy hero, it disappears and deals 280 (280 + 30% magical attack) magical damage. Fireballs deal an equal amount of damage to non-hero units in their path.
When multiple fireballs hit the same target, subsequent fireballs only deal 30% damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Scorching Barrage

skill2.description:
Angela unleashes a fireball in the target direction, which forms a flame vortex upon hitting an enemy or reaching its max range, stunning the first enemy hit for 1s.
The vortex deals 125 (125 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies every 0.5s and slows them by 30% for 1.5s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Chaos Cinder

skill3.description:
Angela channels a blazing beam in the target direction, dealing up to 12 strikes of 150 (150 + 21% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its way. Angela can adjust the direction of the beam while channeling.
While channeling the beam, Angela gains a shield that grants crowd control immunity and negates 850 (850 + 88% magical attack) damage.
Use the skill again after 0.5s to cancel the channeling.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Blazing Brilliance

strategy.earlyGame: Start Skill 1 in the mid lane. All five fireballs deal full damage to non-heroes, giving Angela some of the fastest waveclear in the game — prioritize the clear until level 4 and spend leftover fireballs poking your opponent. Skill 2's 1-second stun is your lifeline, but the projectile is straightforward and easy to read; throwing it early and missing turns you into a free target, so only aim it when the enemy stops to last-hit. Your Passive stacks burn and movement speed as skills land, so keep the output flowing.
strategy.midGame: From around 7 minutes with Savant's Wrath complete, almost anyone hit by Skill 2 is coming home with you. Shove mid, show yourself along the river, and time Skill 2 with your jungler's ganks. At Tyrant fights, the fire vortex's damage-over-time and slow let you seal off chokepoints, so you have a job even when you'd rather not take a straight shootout. Your Ultimate is your damage centerpiece, but you can only steer it while firing — while enemy blinks are unaccounted for, choose your starting position carefully.
strategy.lateGame: Once Void Staff joins the build after 15 minutes, a full combo off Skill 2 evaporates everything short of a tank. But enemy assassins are also complete, so stand diagonally behind your frontline at all times. Getting dove is actually your moment: the Ultimate grants an 850 shield with super armor, and dumping all twelve beam ticks point-blank means the assassin who came for a kill melts instead — the signature Angela experience. In the tight paths near Shadow Tyrant, pre-place Skill 2 to watch the entrance.
strategy.teamfight: The single biggest teamfight rule: don't spend Skill 2 at the start. Hitting a frontliner wastes the stun into shields and armor. Wait until the enemy divers jump onto your allies, then land it on their stalled backline or the assassin coming for you. From the stun, chain a burn-stacked Skill 1 and the Ultimate — nothing non-durable survives the sequence. The beam can be cancelled 0.5 seconds after it starts, so build the habit of cutting it the moment your target drops and saving the rest for the next exchange.

combos.title: Stun Full Burst
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (stun) → Ultimate (point-blank beam) → Skill 1 (finisher)
combos.description: Pin the target with the 1-second stun, pour the beam in at point-blank range, and mop up whatever escapes with fireballs. The more burn stacks accumulate, the harder the back end hits — backliners simply don't survive it.

combos.title: Counter Beam
combos.sequence: Enemy dives → Ultimate (shield + super armor) → Skill 2 → Skill 1
combos.description: Catch a diving assassin on the shield and feed them all twelve beam ticks while super armor ignores their CC. The vortex and fireballs then close their escape route — self-defense that turns into a kill.

combos.title: Choke Lockdown
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (pre-placed in a choke) → Skill 1 (follow-up)
combos.description: Use the vortex's damage-over-time and slow to close a narrow path for several seconds. Even without a direct hit it reliably delays the enemy advance, which is worth gold in objective standoffs.

strengths: One landed Skill 2 stun lets her solo-delete an enemy backliner
Ultimate's shield and super armor let her ignore CC and finish the beam
Passive burn stacks make consecutive skill hits snowball her damage
Five-projectile Skill 1 gives extremely fast waveclear
weaknesses: Every skill is a skillshot — strafing enemies are hard to hit
No blink, so self-defense is paper-thin right after Skill 2 misses
The Ultimate only steers while firing; a bad starting position is fatal
Skill 1 fireballs decay after the first hit on a hero, so single-target damage is inconsistent

synergy.reason: Groups enemies together, making it easier for Luna to land skills on multiple targets and consistently reset her ultimate.
Provides CC cleanse and immunity, supporting the squishy Luna to safely dive into the enemy backline.

counters.reason: Can completely lock down Luna with strong targeted hard CC, neutralizing her ultimate's mobility.
Possesses reliable CC and burst damage, able to interrupt Luna's combo and burst her down.

passive.description:
Luna's Basic Attack has two forms. When the target is out of melee range, it automatically switches to the ranged form.
While in melee form, the 1st of every 3 of her Basic Attacks causes her to charge toward the enemy.
Every 3rd Basic Attack deals an extra 150 (150 + 35% magical attack) magical damage and marks the enemy for 5s. Structures cannot be marked.
For every 1 Magical Attack, she gains 0.03% Attack Speed.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Moonlight Dance

skill1.description: Luna unleashes a moon wave, dealing 400 (400 +65% magical attack) magical damage to enemies and marking them.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Crescent Slice

skill2.description:
Luna pulls in nearby enemies, dealing 120 (120 + 31% magical attack) magical damage. The attack stuns them for 0.5s and slows them by 25% for 2s. Luna also gains a shield that negates 450 (450 + 80% magical attack) damage for 2s.
Pulled enemies will also be marked.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Searing Stab

skill3.description:
Luna dashes to the target location, dealing 420 (420 + 65% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in her path.
If she hits a marked enemy, this skill's cooldown is reset and the mark is consumed.
skill3.name: Skill 3: New Moon

strategy.earlyGame: Luna is a jungler first. Open on both buffs and the camps between them and race to level 4, drilling the Skill 1 → Ultimate → third basic attack order into muscle memory as you clear. Everything Luna does rests on one rule: hitting a marked enemy with the Ultimate resets its cooldown. On your first ganks after level 4, resist the urge to show off a long chain — landing Skill 2's pull and stun to hold the target for your laner succeeds far more often than a greedy solo play.
strategy.midGame: From around 8 minutes, with one or two magic attack items done, Luna headlines every skirmish. The base pattern at Tyrant and mid: tag from range with Skill 1, enter with the Ultimate, refresh the mark with your third basic and Skill 2, and keep weaving in and out. Marks stick to minions too, so learn to chain Ultimates through waves and camps as transportation — it puts your chases and escapes in a different dimension. As long as you don't die, nobody out-farms you.
strategy.lateGame: Teamfights after 15 minutes are won before you enter. A Luna walking in the front door is just a squishy melee, so always start from a flank or the rear with a mark already on a perimeter enemy. Touch once and leave before their stuns and silences turn your way, then start the real dance once their CC is down. Skill 2's shield and 0.5-second stun erase hundreds of damage in a scrum — when you feel surrounded, restart from the pull rather than the attack and your survival rate climbs.
strategy.teamfight: A dropped chain is death, full stop. Throughout the fight, keep the next marked Ultimate target decided two steps ahead, and the instant one dies, switch to another enemy or a minion. While a mark lives, you enter and exit the fight at will — from the enemy's seat, an uncatchable nightmare. But one missed reset deletes your escape plan, so build the habit of confirming your exit mark one step before every overextension. Luna returns exactly what you put into her, and she demands commitment.

combos.title: Core Reset Loop
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (mark) → Ultimate → Third Basic Attack (refresh mark) → Ultimate
combos.description: Mark from range, dash in, refresh with the third basic, and dash again. This four-step loop is Luna's foundation — repeat it in training mode until it happens without conscious thought.

combos.title: Pull Reset
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (pull + stun + mark) → Ultimate → Third Basic Attack → Ultimate
combos.description: When enemies stick to you, buy a beat with the stun and shield, then re-enter the loop off the mark Skill 2 just applied. The moments you're being attacked are exactly when the pull turns defense into offense.

combos.title: Wave Hopping
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (mark a minion) → Ultimate → Ultimate to another marked target
combos.description: Use minions and jungle camps as stepping stones, chaining Ultimates for long-distance chases or escapes. Even outside of fights, marks are public transportation.

strengths: Endless Ultimate resets grant mobility no one else in the game matches
Skill 2's pull, stun, and shield keep her alive in the center of brawls
Free entry and exit lets her bait enemy CC before the real engage
At full mastery, she can win a teamfight single-handedly
weaknesses: The instant the reset chain breaks, her escape disappears with it
A stun or silence mid-loop reduces her to a squishy melee
One of the hardest heroes in the game — low mastery means zero output
Tunnel vision mid-combo makes her slow to react to counter-ganks

148.name: Jiang Ziya

synergy.reason: Provides a solid frontline and CC, creating an environment where Jiang Ziya can safely focus on poking from the backline.
As a carry, she heavily benefits from Jiang Ziya's passive level cap increase, drastically boosting her late-game DPS.

counters.reason: Can instantly close the gap with high mobility and stealth, easily one-shotting the immobile Jiang Ziya.
Can safely deal poke and burst damage from an even further range than Jiang Ziya.

passive.description:
When Ziya deals damage to a target and they are defeated within 3s, he gains 1-3 EXP orbs.
When he reaches level 15, Sanctification Power is restored, granting the one-time skill Sanctify and increasing his level cap to level 25. Each level gained grants 20 Magical Attack.
Sanctify grants 1,200 EXP to a teammate, allowing them to break through their level cap, and potentially gain EXP orbs.
If Ziya acts as a support in the match, he grants additional Sanctification effects based on the teammate's class.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Sanctification

skill1.description: Ziya places a divine seal on enemies in the target area, dealing 70 (70 + 14% magical attack) magical damage, followed by 60 (60 + 12% magical attack) magical damage every 0.4s for a total of 7 hits. Sealed enemies will gradually lose up to 30% of their Movement Speed and 10% of their [icon] and 10% of their [icon]. If the skill hits any enemy, he gains a 30% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 1s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Divine Seal

skill2.description: Ziya unleashes divine retribution on wrongdoers, conjuring a magic circle that deals 3 strikes of damage to enemies in the target area. Each strike deals 60 (60 + 12% magical attack) magical damage. After a short delay, the magic circle explodes, dealing 300 (300 + 70% magical attack) magical damage to enemies and launching them for 0.75s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Divine Punishment

skill3.description:
Ziya channels divine energy in the target direction, unleashing 3 shockwaves. The first 2 shockwaves each deal 120 (120 + 20% magical attack) magical damage, while the last deals 560 (560 + 80% magical attack) magical damage.
Upon reaching level 15, Ziya's Sanctification Power is restored, and there is a 20% chance of entering the Sanctifier state, allowing him to launch a shockwave while moving. Each subsequent level gained increases the chance of entering the Sanctifier state by 20%.
The charging lasts up to 2s, and moving or using the Ultimate again will immediately unleash the shockwaves. Charge time affects the attack range of the shockwaves, up to a distance of 1,800. Shockwaves deal 10% damage to structures in their path.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Universal Law

strategy.earlyGame: Ziya holds the mid lane, and until level 15 the job description reads: survive and soak experience. Place Skill 1 where the wave and the enemy overlap and it handles clearing, harass, and defense shred in one cast. Your Passive drops EXP balls from kills you've damaged, so pick them up religiously to build a level lead. With no blink, never leave tower range while the enemy jungler is dark. Skill 2's knock-up is your self-defense — waste it on offense and the bill arrives with the next gank.
strategy.midGame: At level 15 — roughly the 10-minute mark — comes your once-per-game Sanctification decision. Used on yourself, the level cap rises to 25 with magic attack growth every level, completing you as an artillery piece. Used on an ally, 1200 EXP pushes your ace a full tier higher. The rule of thumb is simple: a fed carry on your team gets it, an even game means keep it. From then on, your charged Ultimate reaches a maximum of 1800 range, letting you apply one-sided pressure in Shadow Tyrant standoffs and tower sieges.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Ziya stands behind the backline — the deepest position on the map. Past level 20, your magic attack ranks among the game's highest, and two charged Ultimates connecting is enough to halve an enemy formation. Before Overlord, start seeding the chokepoints with Skill 1 thirty seconds ahead of the spawn to strip defense and speed until the fight favors you. Track the enemy assassin at all times, and when they're missing, hold the charge. If you get touched mid-channel, the lost fight is mostly on you.
strategy.teamfight: Seventy percent of Ziya's teamfight happens before the fight. Skill 1 walls off approach paths, and Skill 2 goes down early on the spot where their diver will land — press it before they jump, because pressing it after never connects. That's the field lesson worth remembering. Once the brawl starts, thread charged Ultimates in from maximum range and drive the lowest-HP enemies out of the fight one by one. While your blessed teammate rampages up front, you conduct the battle from beyond anyone's reach.

combos.title: Seal Zoning
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (seal slow) → Skill 2 (knock-up) → Ultimate (charged)
combos.description: The slow and defense shred hold enemies inside the zone, making the delayed Skill 2 dramatically easier to land, and the charged shockwave finishes the stack. Sealed enemies simply can't walk out of it in time.

combos.title: Max-Range Siege
combos.sequence: Ultimate (2-second charge) → Skill 1 (follow-up)
combos.description: Extend the shockwave to its 1800 range and fire it at enemies under their tower — or the tower itself, which takes 10% damage. Shelling from beyond retaliation range is Ziya's exclusive privilege.

combos.title: Counter Knock-Up
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (pre-placed on the landing spot) → Skill 1 → Retreat
combos.description: Read where the diving enemy will land, place Skill 2 there in advance, and layer the seal on them while they're airborne as you fall back to your team. The correct timing to place it is before they jump — always.

strengths: Sanctification is a one-of-a-kind buff that raises an ally's level cap
1800-range charged Ultimate enables safe poke and siege from another zip code
Skill 1's slow and defense shred dominates pre-objective standoffs
Passive EXP balls make building a level lead easy
weaknesses: No blink — self-defense rests entirely on predicting with Skill 2
Charging the Ultimate leaves him wide open, a gift for assassins
Power spikes at level 15, so falling behind early is hard to repair
Misusing the Sanctification target or timing halves his late game

synergy.reason: A powerful marksman who can maximize the benefits of Liu Bang's global ultimate protection.
Creates a powerful combo by syncing his ultimate with an assassin diving deep into the enemy backline, following up instantly with CC.

counters.reason: Has true damage and %HP damage, allowing him to easily shred through Liu Bang's shields and high durability.
His high-burst true damage ignores shields and armor, easily overwhelming Liu Bang in the laning phase.

passive.description: Liu Bang gains 1 mark every second, for up to 4 marks. Basic Attacks expend all marks, dealing an additional 80 (80 + 10% magical attack) magical damage per mark. At maximum marks, the next Basic Attack is enhanced into a ranged attack that deals 474 (294 + 100% physical attack + 42% magical attack) magical damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Royal Ambition

skill1.description:
Liu Bang gains a shield that negates 650 (650 + 20% extra Health) damage for 5s. Upon expiry, the shield detonates and deals 650 (650 + 90% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
After 1.5s, using the skill again will detonate the shield immediately. If the shield is broken, it will only deal 50% damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Dominator's Shield

skill2.description:
Liu Bang dashes a distance of 275−550 in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 40% magical attack)−600 (600 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and stunning them for 0.75s.
This skill can be charged for up to 1s, and its effects depend on charging time. If the charge is interrupted or canceled, the cooldown will be reduced by 40%.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Staggering Charge

skill3.description:
Liu Bang selects a teammate and starts channeling in place, granting the teammate a shield that negates (480 + 12% target's extra Health)−(960 + 24% target's extra Health) damage. After 2.2s, he teleports to the teammate.
Upon arriving, Liu Bang gains 30% Movement Speed and restores 300 (300 + 8% extra Health) Health to himself and nearby teammates. He also fully charges Staggering Charge, keeping it charged for 10s.
After channeling for 0.4s, this skill can be used again to immediately teleport to the teammate, remove their shield, and deal 200 (200 + 40% magical attack)−400 (400 + 80% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies. However, he will not gain the recovery effect.
The longer he channels, the stronger the shield becomes and the more damage he deals upon ending the channeling early.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Battlefield Command

strategy.earlyGame: Liu Bang's default home is the clash lane. Until level 4, Skill 1's shield and delayed blast handle the waves, while the Passive's four-stack ranged empowered basic lets you chip melee opponents without ever being touched. Skill 2's charged dash is your only stun and it's precious — through the early game, hold it as the counter-punch for enemy jungler ganks. Liu Bang's real value unlocks with his Ultimate and its map-wide reach, so through this window, simply banking experience without dying earns a passing grade.
strategy.midGame: After the 4-minute Tyrant, your two-front war begins. Shove side waves, and the moment a teammate gets touched anywhere on the map, channel your Ultimate and warp to them. You arrive delivering shields, and for 10 seconds after warping, Skill 2 sits at max charge — meaning an immediate full-range stun dash the second you land. The 2.2-second channel is a complete opening, so always cast from brush or behind a tower. Your goal is planting one thought in every enemy's head: if Liu Bang is off the map, this could be a 5v6.
strategy.lateGame: With three or more defense items after 15 minutes, split push and make two defenders deal with you. A detail worth banking: your Ultimate's shield scales with the target's bonus HP, so it lands biggest on your beefiest tank or fighter. The gold-standard pattern is pushing a side lane until seconds before Overlord, then warping in as it spawns. And if five enemies start collapsing on you, the warp to a distant ally is itself your escape hatch.
strategy.teamfight: Fighting with your team from the start, the job is catching the enemy carry with Skill 2's stun and layering Skill 1's blast on top. The shield can be manually detonated 1.5 seconds after casting, so when enemies glue themselves to you, pop it yourself and waste nothing. Arriving from a side lane instead, drop onto their backline mid-fight and let the max-charge Skill 2 flip the board. Engage together or arrive late — read the enemy comp and pick your policy in the first half, and the hesitation disappears.

combos.title: Warp Counter
combos.sequence: Ultimate (warp) → Skill 2 (max-charge stun dash) → Skill 1 → Basic Attack
combos.description: Immediately after warping to an ally, spend the guaranteed max-charge Skill 2 to stop the enemy cold. With the shield delivery and heal landing at the same time, you can turn a losing skirmish around on arrival.

combos.title: Point-Blank Detonation
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (shield) → Skill 2 (stun) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 re-tap (detonate)
combos.description: Shield up, step in, pin them with the stun, and slam the 1.5-second manual detonation at point-blank range. Popping the shield yourself before the enemy breaks it is the trick to maximizing the damage.

combos.title: Charge-Cancel Feint
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (charge) → Cancel → Recharge
combos.description: Cancelling the charge refunds 40% of the cooldown, so you can show the dash wind-up repeatedly just to back enemies off. Quietly effective when you need space to shove a wave.

strengths: The Ultimate projects pressure onto any fight from anywhere on the map
One warp delivers shields, healing, and his own escape in a single skill
A guaranteed max-charge Skill 2 stun for 10 seconds after every warp
Passive ranged empowered basics let him poke melee laners for free
weaknesses: The 2.2-second channel is a total opening and struggles when watched
Low personal burst — he rarely closes out a kill alone
Built around split play, so one bad Ultimate creates instant man-down fights
No CC beyond the single stun, so mobile enemies slip away repeatedly

synergy.reason: Provides reliable lockdown on enemies, creating openings for Han Xin to safely close the gap and unleash his burst damage.
Stops enemy movement with long-range stuns, heavily supporting Han Xin's engages and disengages.

counters.reason: If his escape routes are completely blocked by the ultimate, he cannot utilize his high mobility and will easily be killed.
Can dodge Han Xin's attacks with high mobility and i-frames, turning the fight around with sustained counter-damage.

passive.description: Han Xin's every 4th Basic Attack launches the enemy for 0.5s and deals an extra 90 (90 + 35% extra physical attack) physical damage with 20% Physical Lifesteal. He gains 25-50% Attack Speed after landing a hit with a skill or an enhanced Basic Attack.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Killing Spear

skill1.description:
Han Xin leaps to the target location, dealing 250 (250 +85% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 0.5s.
He can leap again within 5s, dealing an equal amount of physical damage to enemies within range.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Ruthless Assault

skill2.description:
Han Xin dashes backward and enhances his next Basic Attack into a sweep for 3s, which deals 120 (120 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range.
If the Fight or Die! sweep is his 4th Basic Attack, it carries the 4th Basic Attack's extra effects.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Fight or Die!

skill3.description:
Han Xin executes a 4-strike flurry with his spear in a cone-shaped area in the target direction, each strike dealing 250 (250 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range, with the final strike launching enemies within range for 0.5s.
While using his Ultimate, he gains crowd control immunity and 30% damage reduction.
skill3.name: Skill 3: The Unrivaled Spear

strategy.earlyGame: Han Xin junglers almost always open from the blue buff side. The Passive's fourth-hit knock-up and 20% lifesteal mean that simply spacing out clean four-hit sequences keeps your HP topped while you clear at speed. Once your Ultimate unlocks at level 4, start ganking the lane being shoved in or any enemy slow to back off. Skill 1's double jump crosses walls, so appear from the wall behind your target rather than the river — suddenly there is no correct direction for them to run.
strategy.midGame: From around 7 minutes with your first core item done, Han Xin's hunting ground moves to the enemy jungle. Bounce through unwarded territory on double jumps, catch farmers alone, and vanish — that loop alone visibly stunts the whole enemy team's growth. Skip the opening exchanges at Tyrant and mid; your role is entering from the side once both teams are worn down and collecting what's left. And before every invade, decide your exit route first. Skip that step, and all the mobility in the game won't carry you home.
strategy.lateGame: After 15 minutes, Han Xin loses half his value the moment he stands in a front-on 5v5. Instead, push a side lane deep: two enemies come, hop a wall and vanish; one comes, kill him. That single repeated decision keeps the map in your team's hands. At Overlord, lurk in a flanking position and dive their backline after the fight starts. Your Ultimate carries super armor and 30% damage reduction while spinning, so committing under a tower or through a wall of enemy CC is a play you're allowed to make with confidence.
strategy.teamfight: Wait on the perimeter until the enemy's CC and attention are committed to your frontline, then take Skill 1 into their isolated backline. Land three basics, then time Skill 2's sweep as the fourth hit for a guaranteed knock-up, and spin your Ultimate through them to finish — that's the ideal script. When the target drops, don't chase; leave on Skill 1's remaining jump. A Han Xin who spent every movement skill on the way in is just a fragile spearman, so always keep one in the tank for the road home.

combos.title: Standard Assassination
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Skill 1 → Basic Attack → Ultimate → Skill 1 (second jump)
combos.description: Stick to the target with the sweep and jump, spin through their CC with the super-armored Ultimate, then leave on the remaining jump. For Han Xin, the entry and the exit are one package deal.

combos.title: Fourth-Hit Knock-Up
combos.sequence: Basic Attack ×3 → Skill 2 (sweep counts as the fourth hit) → Ultimate
combos.description: Bank three hits, then let Skill 2's sweep inherit the fourth-hit bonus: the knock-up guarantees your Ultimate connects. With the lifesteal rolling at the same time, this is the winning line in any 1v1.

combos.title: Triple-Jump Escape
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (first jump) → Skill 1 (second jump) → Skill 2 (reverse dash)
combos.description: Two jumps plus the reverse dash cross multiple walls in seconds. Remember Skill 2 dashes opposite to the direction you aim — the more panicked the moment, the more that input deserves your attention.

strengths: Double jumps and the reverse dash give mobility few heroes can match
Passive knock-up and 20% lifesteal keep his HP healthy through repeated fights
Ultimate's super armor and 30% reduction let him finish combos through CC
Elite wall-hopping makes enemy jungle invades and escapes routine
weaknesses: Fragile base stats — one CC chain after his jumps are spent is lethal
Skill 2's reverse input is unique, and precision directly equals survival
Damage is built around reaching the fourth hit, so split-second trades underwhelm
Long stretches of solo play mean vision-starved games blunt his edge

synergy.reason: Draws enemy attention and provides lockdown on the frontline, making it much easier for Wang Zhaojun to land her Skill 2 freeze.
Overlapping their massive AoE magic damage can absolutely decimate the enemy team in teamfights.

counters.reason: Her high mobility makes it easy to dodge the freeze skill, allowing her to quickly close the gap and burst Wang Zhaojun down.
His strong CC cleanse and immunity skills can completely neutralize Wang Zhaojun's biggest strength, her freeze, for the entire enemy team.

passive.description:
Upon leaving combat, Wang Zhaojun gains a shield that negates 450 (450 + 58% magical attack) damage. Enemies that deal physical damage to the shield will be chilled. When the shield disappears, it deals 400 (400 + 75% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and chills them.
Her every third Basic Attack will be enhanced, firing 3 icicles that deal a total of 180 (180 + 36% magical attack) magical damage. Each icicle applies 100% of the Basic Attack's on-hit effects.
Hits from her active skills and enhanced Basic Attacks will chill enemies, reducing their Movement Speed by 25-50% and Attack Speed by 25-50% for 2s. These effects diminish over time.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Frozen Heart

skill1.description: Wang Zhaojun conjures a burst of exploding ice in the target location, dealing 350 (350 + 50% magical attack) magical damage and inflicting chill to enemies within range. She also gains vision of the area and any enemies hit for 2s.

skill2.description:
Wang Zhaojun summons a freezing circle in the target location. After a short delay, she deals 250 (250 +50% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and freezes them for 2.5s.
She deals an extra 150 (150 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to frozen enemies.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Frigid Prison

skill3.description:
Wang Zhaojun summons a snowstorm in the target location for 5s. The snowstorm deals 200 (200 + 35% magical attack) magical damage and inflicts chill to enemies within range every 0.5s.
Summoning a snowstorm grants her the shield from her passive.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Winter Is Here

strategy.earlyGame: In the mid lane, Skill 1 is your everything until level 4. It clears waves, and since it grants 2 seconds of vision at the impact point, firing scout shots into the river brush warns you of ganks before they happen. Your Passive shield regenerates out of combat and chills any physical attacker who breaks it, so trade confidently whenever the shield is up. Skill 2 has a long delay before it triggers, so at this stage only aim it at enemies rooted in place clearing the wave — anything else is a coin flip.
strategy.midGame: Wang Zhaojun's setup game begins with the 4-minute Tyrant. Drop your Ultimate's blizzard on the river entrance and that path is closed for 5 seconds — anyone forcing through eats chill that strips both movement and attack speed. When a gank arrives, pre-place Skill 2 on the enemy's escape route — more precisely, on the spot where they'll stand after using their blink. Land the 2.5-second freeze with your jungler present and the kill is all but booked. The Ultimate also refreshes your Passive shield, which is exactly the license you need to play forward.
strategy.lateGame: With Savant's Wrath and Void Staff done after 15 minutes, the blizzard's ticks turn genuinely heavy. Before Shadow Tyrant and Overlord fights, seed the chokepoint with your Ultimate early, warp their formation, and give your team the signal to commit. If the freeze → Skill 1 → empowered third basic sequence reaches their backline, the numbers advantage ends the game on the spot. You have zero mobility, so live in the deepest position — and when the enemy assassin vanishes from the map, your first thought should be about your own feet.
strategy.teamfight: Your contribution is decided by who you chill. Cooling down their frontline tank moves nothing. The target is their marksman: chill strips up to 50% of both movement and attack speed, which functionally disarms a carry — damage and kiting gone in one status effect. The ideal opening: blizzard on their backline's heads, Skill 2 on the retreat path, then Skill 1 and empowered basics to follow. Frozen enemies also take bonus damage, so tell your team before the fight to focus whoever's frozen first — it visibly changes the results.

combos.title: Frozen Execution
combos.sequence: Ultimate (pre-placed) → Skill 2 (freeze) → Skill 1 → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Let the blizzard slow their feet first and the delayed freeze becomes dramatically easier to land. Pour everything into the 2.5-second lockdown — this is Wang Zhaojun's ideal sequence.

combos.title: Gank Freeze
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (pre-placed on the retreat path) → Skill 1 → Basic Attack (empowered third hit)
combos.description: Time it with your jungler's approach and read where the enemy will fall back to. Aiming for the moment right after their blink is spent sends the success rate through the roof.

combos.title: Scout and Poke
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (into brush) → Check vision → Keep clearing if safe
combos.description: A small habit with big returns: use Skill 1's 2-second vision as reconnaissance. From the 4-minute mark when ganks pick up, routine shots into the river brush cut your death count sharply.

strengths: Skill 2's 2.5-second freeze converts into a near-guaranteed kill with follow-up
Chill strips movement and attack speed at once — brutal against marksmen
The Ultimate refreshes her Passive shield, making her tougher than she looks
Skill 1's vision grant makes her excellent at scouting and dodging ganks
weaknesses: Skill 2's trigger delay makes it nearly impossible to land unassisted
No movement skill — once an enemy reaches her, she rarely gets away
Damage lives in placed zones, so constantly moving enemies out-trade her
Enemies who step out of the blizzard halve her teamfight output

Draws enemy attention during teamfights, making it much easier for a stealthed Prince of Lanling to flank and assassinate the enemy marksman.

counters.reason: Can secure vision with his skills, allowing his team to anticipate and counter Prince of Lanling's stealth engages.
Possesses extremely high durability and CC, able to tank Prince of Lanling's burst damage and counter-engage with lockdown.

When marks disappear, the enemy takes physical damage equal to 152 (140 + 12% lost Health) (plus an extra 1% for every 50 extra physical attack). The dagger is destroyed upon hitting an enemy hero.

skill4.name: Skill 4: Secret Skill - Shadow

strategy.earlyGame: Start on your own buffs and rush level 4. The reason is simple: Gao Changgong's assassination kit only comes online once the Ultimate's dash links into Skill 2's follow-up stun. His Passive grants 20% bonus move speed only while moving toward enemy heroes, so approach ganks through bushes rather than down the lane. Touch the bottom side of the map at least once before the Tyrant spawns at 4:00 — showing up with a numbers advantage decides that first objective more often than the smite does.
strategy.midGame: Your assassination power peaks around 8-10 minutes, when two core physical and penetration items are done. Skill 2's mark detonates for 24% of the target's max HP three seconds after it lands, so instead of forcing an extended brawl, you can tag a target, back off, and let the mark do the work. Re-attacking a marked enemy stuns for 1 second and heals you, which makes even greedy dives surprisingly survivable. Before the Shadow Tyrant arrives at 10:00, walk the enemy jungle bushes once to map out your ambush routes.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, tanks get too beefy and your value in front-to-front fights drops. Hunt the enemies who leave the group instead: the side laner pushing alone, the support walking out for vision. If Skill 2 connects, the stun plus percent damage almost always converts into a kill. Deleting one enemy right before the Overlord contest is your real win condition — treat full 5v5s as a last resort and only fight with a numbers edge.
strategy.teamfight: Never be the first one in. You are paper-thin, and a single crowd-control effect will end you, so wait until the enemy dumps their lockdown on your frontline before circling to the backline. Always open with Skill 2 — the 90% slow means nobody escapes — then close with the Ultimate and convert the re-attack stun. Skill 1's clone automatically hunts the lowest-HP enemy hero, so in a scrum it cleans up chunked targets you can't physically reach.

combos.title: Mark Detonation Assassination
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (mark + slow) → Ultimate (dash) → Basic Attack (stun on the marked target) → Skill 1 (clone)
combos.description: Cut off the escape route with the slow, dash in, and re-attack the mark for a 1-second stun. Counting the 24% max HP detonation that lands three seconds later, this kills targets who started the fight at 70% health.

combos.title: Hit-and-Run Deposit
combos.sequence: Ultimate (dash) → Skill 1 (clone) → Skill 2 (mark while backing off)
combos.description: For fights you can't commit to. Deposit damage with the dash and clone, then leave a parting Skill 2 — the slow and mark keep chewing on the target after you're gone, and the heal on the mark gets you back into action faster.

strengths: Elite single-target burst built on Skill 2's 1s stun and 24% max HP detonation
Passive move speed makes chases and bush ganks reliably stick
Healing off marked targets lets him survive aggressive dives and chain fights
The clone auto-targets the lowest-HP enemy hero and cleans up scraps
weaknesses: Paper-thin defenses — a single CC chain usually kills him
Missing Skill 2 deletes the stun and percent damage, half his kit
No frontal fighting tools, so his impact fades in late 5v5s
The Ultimate is his only mobility, making exits after deep dives rough

strategy.earlyGame: Mulan starts in the clash lane, and the early game belongs to her dual blades. That stance grants bonus move speed and stacks marks with basic attacks and skills, so build your laning around short trades that push toward the 5-stack silence burst. Because picking up your thrown sword refunds Skill 1's cooldown, throw it toward your own escape route rather than behind the enemy — retrieval stays safe. Until level 4 unlocks the greatsword, don't force kills; spend the time drilling mark management and sword pickups into muscle memory.
strategy.midGame: Level 4 is when Mulan actually starts playing. The core loop: stack five marks in dual-blade stance to land the silence, swap to the greatsword with your Ultimate, and drive the charged slash home. A silenced enemy can neither fight back nor run, which is exactly what lets the charge finish. Greatsword skills grant unstoppable (CC immunity) and damage reduction while they're active, so swing through the retaliation. Any laner below half HP dies to the full string.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, split your time between pushing side lanes and playing silence-bot in teamfights. Mulan's silence is a hard answer to mages and channeled skills — muting one key enemy for a few seconds reshapes an entire fight. At Overlord contests, use dual-blade mobility to flank, then time the greatsword swap onto a marked target the instant fighting starts. Walk in through the front and you'll get surrounded and accomplish nothing; the entry angle is everything.
strategy.teamfight: Your job in a teamfight is to silence the one action the enemy most wants to take. Orbit the edge in dual-blade stance spreading marks, and save the fifth stack for the target you need muted. Watching an enemy mage start their cast animation and slamming the silence on top of it feels fantastic — their entire damage output just evaporates. Then swap to the greatsword and lean on the unstoppable frames to land a charged slash in the scrum. Even when you don't kill, the damage reduction gets you out alive more often than it should.

combos.title: Silence Lock (Dual Blades)
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (double dash to close) → Skill 1 (sword throw) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (sword pickup)
combos.description: The dual-blade bread and butter: stack marks with dashes and attacks until the 5-stack burst lands silence plus slow. Retrieving the sword refunds Skill 1's cooldown, so the next trade starts almost immediately.

combos.title: Silence into Full Burst
combos.sequence: 5-Stack Detonation (silence) → Ultimate (greatsword swap) → Skill 1 (charged slash) → Skill 2 (follow-up slash)
combos.description: The silence guarantees no retaliation, letting the greatsword charge complete safely. Greatsword skills carry unstoppable, so even if reinforcements arrive mid-swing you can finish the string and still walk out.

strengths: The 5-stack silence plus slow creates windows where enemies simply can't answer
Unstoppable and damage reduction on greatsword skills shrug off CC-heavy comps
No mana — she trades on cooldowns alone, forever
Swaps between dual-blade mobility and greatsword burst to fit the moment
weaknesses: Charged greatsword swings whiff entirely if the enemy makes distance
Gap-closing leans on dual-blade Skill 2, so she gets kited hard
Picking the wrong stance leaves her with neither damage nor speed
No built-in sustain — holding lane after getting chunked is miserable

155.name: Erin

synergy.reason: Builds a stable frontline with strong CC and durability, creating an environment where Erin can safely dish out sustained DPS from a distance.
Physically peels enemies away, greatly increasing the survivability of the mobile kiting Erin.

counters.reason: A powerful assassin who can instantly close the gap with overwhelming mobility and one-shot the squishy Erin.
Combines long-range poke with rapid dashes to instantly close the gap, bursting Erin down before she can react.

passive.description:
Erin's Basic Attacks deal 166 (100% physical attack + 20% magical attack) physical damage and grant Energy. When Energy is at max, Erin speeds up, gains 1 stack of Laurel, and enhances her next Basic Attack.
Speed Up: Erin spends Energy to fly, increasing 30 Movement Speed per 100 magical attack, up to a maximum increase of 450 Movement Speed.
Enhanced Basic Attack: Erin's enhanced Basic Attack deals 269 (70 + 120% physical attack + 30% magical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path.
Her Pierce and Lifesteal stats are linked. Physical Pierce/Lifesteal and Magical Pierce/Lifesteal each use the higher of the two stats.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Elf Dance

skill1.description:
Erin shoots a laurel leaf, dealing 525 (525 + 120% extra physical attack + 110% magical attack) magical damage to enemies hit and gaining a stack of Laurel. Upon hitting an enemy hero or flying to its maximum range, the leaf starts flying in a circle, and enemies that come into contact with the circle take 175 (175 + 40% extra physical attack + 37% magical attack) magical damage and are slowed by 15% for 1s.
The skill's cooldown is reduced by 0.1s for every 100 Magical Attack, for a reduction of up to 1.5s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Dance - Leaf Greeting

skill2.description:
Blessed by the Luminescent Forest, Erin immediately recovers full Energy, gains her Passive effect (including Speed Up, 1 Laurel stack, and an enhanced Basic Attack) and obtains another stack of Laurel.
Erin also becomes immune to slow and gains 20% Attack Speed for 3s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Twirl - Forest Whisper

skill3.description:
At max Energy, Erin gains a stack of Laurel. When the skill is activated, she gains 10% Movement Speed and continuously consumes Laurel stacks to shoot leaves. Each leaf shot deals 130 (72 + 35% physical attack + 30% magical attack) magical damage to the enemy within range with the lowest Health. Each shot also reduces the cooldown of Twirl - Forest Whisper by 0.2s.
Waltz - Laurel Bloom is only unlocked at 6 Laurels. Laurel can be stacked up to 12 times.
Every 3 leaves counts as 1 Basic Attack.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Waltz - Laurel Bloom

strategy.earlyGame: Spend the first four minutes in the farm lane doing nothing but securing last hits. Erin is built around an unusual scaling scheme — magic attack raises both her move speed and her skill rotation — so finishing that first magic item is her real first power spike. Skill 1 is your harass tool: it stacks laurel marks on hit and deploys a slowing ring. Manage energy on a rhythm of one glide per three basic attacks and you'll stay half a step faster than the opposing marksman at all times.
strategy.midGame: Around the 10-minute mark, two completed magic items plus the Ultimate unlocking at 6 marks send her sustained damage through the roof. In Tyrant fights and skirmishes, gliding half a step off an enemy skill's flight path cuts your damage taken dramatically. When you get ganked, Skill 2 is the lifeline: it refills energy, grants slow immunity, and boosts attack speed all at once, which is enough to outrun one full rotation of chase. You're fragile while it's on cooldown, so pick the moment carefully.
strategy.lateGame: Erin approaching full build is the whole point of picking her. Her penetration and lifesteal apply whichever of physical or magic is higher, so her damage goes through any defensive itemization and she rarely loses an extended DPS race. Always fight from behind your frontline. Don't overthink targeting either — hit the nearest safe enemy, and the Ultimate's leaves will chase down the lowest-HP target on their own. Her win condition is uptime, not burst: staying alive and firing is the play.
strategy.teamfight: Hold the perimeter and settle into the rhythm of basic attack, glide, basic attack. When an assassin dives you, hit Skill 2 to speed up, ignore their slows, and slide behind your frontline. The Ultimate's leaves keep flying while you retreat, so your damage never actually stops. One habit worth building: don't glide just because you're pressured. Wait until you've seen one enemy dash skill before spending energy on movement, and you'll still have some banked when it really matters.

Glides plus slow immunity give her some of the best escapes of any marksman
The Ultimate's leaves hunt the lowest-HP enemy and secure cleanup on their own
No mana — she camps lane indefinitely and out-farms her opposite number
weaknesses: Low burst, so out-damaging heals and shields takes real time
Loses all mobility the instant her energy runs dry
No answer to point-and-click CC — getting caught means dying
Heavily item-dependent, with little teamfight presence before 10 minutes

skill2.name: Skill 2: Power Word - Fate
