If he finishes using this skill without being interrupted, a magic field is summoned at the target hero's location for 0.5s. Enemies that step into the field take 240 (240 +30% magical attack) magical damage and are stunned for 0.75s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Power Word - Control

strategy.earlyGame: Skill 2 runs Liang's early mid lane. The circle deals 50% bonus damage to non-heroes for fast waveclear, and since two can be maintained at once, parking one in a river bush doubles as vision. Once the wave is shoved, use that vision to move with your jungler, and hit level 4 as fast as possible — the 2.2-second suppression is one of the longest lockdowns in the game, and from the moment it unlocks, your mid lane carries constant kill threat.
strategy.midGame: Mid game, your biggest job is picks with your jungler — catching an isolated enemy before objectives. Suppress whoever walks up for vision before the Tyrant or Shadow Tyrant and the objective is yours without a fight. One caution: Liang is rooted for the entire suppression. Only cast it within reach of your team's damage, or you'll land a perfect lockdown and then get left behind alone. Also, walk through your own Skill 2 circles when rotating — the move speed boost is a small habit with real mileage.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, who you suppress IS the match. The default target is the enemy's main carry, but the Ultimate is also a first-class counter to assassins diving your backline: read the landing spot of their dash, wait, and suppress on contact — they melt without taking a single action. Use Skill 1's four barriers to zone retreat paths and chokepoints, and let the Passive's true damage grind down even the frontline tanks.
strategy.teamfight: Stay behind your frontline at the very edge of Ultimate range. Open by dropping Skill 1 across the enemy's approach to stagger their entry with the multi-stuns, and lay Skill 2 at your feet to claim ground for your team. Don't rush the Ultimate — hold it for the most dangerous enemy, like the assassin the instant he commits. A stun zone lingers at the target's feet when suppression ends, so tell your team in advance to burst during that 0.75-second window; the kill rate difference is night and day.

combos.title: Guaranteed Pick Lockdown
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (place for vision) → Ultimate (2.2s suppression) → Skill 1 (barriers at the target's feet) → Basic Attack (start Passive ticks)
combos.description: Laying barriers under the target mid-suppression extends the lockdown even further — the end-of-suppression stun zone chains into the barrier stun. Non-negotiable condition: cast it within reach of allied damage.

combos.title: Anti-Dive Counter

combos.description: The self-defense sequence for when someone jumps you. Barrier stuns interrupt the chase and the circle's move speed reopens the gap. This survives more often than panic-casting the Ultimate.

Passive true damage keeps hurting even fully stacked tanks

strategy.earlyGame: Early mid lane is not the time to force anything. Mai's energy only refunds meaningfully on skill hits, so whiffing repeatedly leaves you unable to act at all. Clear waves with Skill 2's fan — it pierces to the unit behind the first target it hits, so lining it through a minion onto the enemy laner clears and harasses in one throw. Level 4 unlocks the Ultimate, and with rolls woven in, she finally becomes the ambush hero she's meant to be.
strategy.midGame: From level 4 on, shove mid quickly and roam the side lanes. Every engage starts with Skill 2 — the 50-point magic defense shred lasts 3 seconds, and the same combo does visibly different damage depending on whether it led. Sliding the stick during an empowered basic or skill triggers a roll, and the small habits pay huge dividends: roll to the wall side to cut off the escape, or roll out of the flight path of their answer skill. One extra input, dramatically better survival.
strategy.lateGame: Late game is entirely about timing your entry, not the size of the hit. One CC kills you, so hover the perimeter of frontal fights flashing roll threats, and commit Skill 2 into Skill 1 the instant the enemy's point-and-click CC or lockdown gets spent elsewhere. The Ultimate's knockback and 20% physical attack shred double as insurance — landing it on the enemy marksman buys defense and cuts their damage at once. Having the discipline to leave based on your energy bar is what actually decides your win rate.
strategy.teamfight: The ideal teamfight entry is three seconds late, after the scrum has started. Shred a target's magic defense with Skill 2, stack Skill 1's knock-up on top, push with the empowered basic, and finish with the Ultimate. When the full string lands, squishy targets simply disappear — but decide your roll-out path BEFORE you dive. The same input handles both aggressive and escaping rolls on this hero, so the escape route you hold in your head is your actual lifeline.

combos.title: Shred-First Full Combo
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (magic defense -50) → Skill 1 (dash knock-up) → Basic Attack (empowered, knockback) → Ultimate
combos.description: Landing the shred first amplifies every magic hit that follows, which is why Skill 2 must lead. If the empowered basic connects during the knock-up, the Ultimate is free to secure the kill or cover the exit.

combos.title: Double-Hit Fan Poke
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (pierce through a minion) → Roll (adjust the angle) → Basic Attack (empowered)
combos.description: The fan also damages the unit behind its first target, so enemies hiding behind minions get punished hardest. It refunds energy too, making this the pattern that wins lane priority.

strengths: Skill 2's 50-point magic defense shred multiplies her entire combo
Two dashes plus rolls deliver elite in-and-out mobility
Knock-up, knockback, and an attack shred give her real self-defense
Energy loops indefinitely as long as skills keep connecting
weaknesses: Whiffed skills drain energy and create dead time where she can't act
Zero defensive tools — a single CC ends her
Misrolled inputs send her the wrong way, straight into danger
High skill floor: her damage tracks directly with practice

synergy.reason: Dolia can reset his powerful AoE ultimate, allowing them to completely dominate teamfights.
Resetting her ultimate allows for extremely powerful chain-kill potential.

counters.reason: His strong lockdown abilities can disrupt her positioning, bursting her down before she has a chance to reset an ally's ultimate.
Can disrupt Dolia's supportive actions with continuous CC, severely reducing her impact in teamfights.

passive.description:
Dolia takes the form of a mermaid while in water, reducing slow effects by 50% and recovering 60 (60 + 1% extra Health) Health and 5 Mana every second. Her Basic Attacks become splashes of water that deal area damage.
Her Recovery skill becomes Mermaid's Gift, which can be used to form a covenant with a selected teammate. This teammate becomes the priority target for Celestial Melody.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Mermaid's Gift

skill1.description:
Dolia sings, unleashing 4 soundwaves that spread out around her. The first 3 deal 130 (130 + 20% magical attack) magical damage and inflict a 7.5% slow.
The 4th soundwave deals 250 (250 + 40% magical attack) magical damage and inflicts a 30% slow for 1s. This soundwave triggers echoes when hitting enemies, dealing 150 (150 + 24% magical attack) magical damage. While in water, it stirs up a wave that knocks back nearby enemies and stuns enemies next to her.
Echoes triggered by non-hero units have a shorter range and only deal 50% damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Ode

skill2.description:
Dolia leaps forward and transforms into a mermaid. If she lands on solid ground, she creates a pool of water and restores 320 (320 + 40% magical attack) Health to her and her nearby teammates. While in the pool, teammates recover Health and Mana at the same rate as Dolia's.
Cooldown is reduced by 25% if used while in water.
The pool disappears if she leaves it for 4s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Wavemaker

skill3.description:
Dolia channels for a short time, resetting the cooldown of a skill for a teammate within range. The skill that gets reset is the one with the longest remaining cooldown. In return, Dolia takes on a Cooldown of 10 (+120% of the current skill Cooldown) seconds herself.
If the teammate does not use the reset skill, the cooldown of Celestial Melody is reduced by 20%. If the teammate uses the reset skill within 5s, it does not consume Energy, and any earnings from defeating enemies with that skill are shared evenly with Dolia.
This skill prioritizes the teammate with whom she has formed a covenant. If no teammates are nearby, she resets one of her own skills. If the reset fails, the cooldown of Celestial Melody is significantly reduced.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Celestial Melody

strategy.earlyGame: Pick your contract partner at spawn — usually the marksman or jungler who'll be your late-game gun. Shadow that partner early and actively force skirmishes around the river, because Dolia in water is a different hero: Mermaid mode passively regenerates her HP and MP, and Skill 1 upgrades into an AoE knockback plus stun. The 4-minute Tyrant fight happens in the river, and it's her first showcase — simply standing in the water before the enemy arrives is already an advantage.
strategy.midGame: Mid game is for drilling the Ultimate's timing into muscle memory. It resets the skill with the longest remaining cooldown in range, so casting it right after an ally fires their ultimate returns that ultimate almost every time. Shadow Tyrant and Overlord contests are her home turf — river terrain stacked with Skill 2's water field generation. Even on dry land, Skill 2's landing zone hands sustained healing to every ally standing in it.
strategy.lateGame: Her late-game value collapses into one sentence: your ace's ultimate fires twice. Partner's ultimate lands, Ultimate immediately after — whether that single input happens determines the entire teamfight's math. From the enemy's perspective, the big skill they just played around is coming again, and there's essentially no answer. If you die, the reset supply stops, so position behind even your contract partner. Not dying is itself your biggest contribution — accept that fully.
strategy.teamfight: Step one of fight prep: lay a water field at your feet with Skill 2 before it starts. On the water, you sustain while fighting, and diving assassins get bounced by Skill 1's knockback and stun. From there, just sync the Ultimate with your team's big cooldowns. It isn't flashy, but when your allies out-sustain everything on the field and every enemy engage gets bounced back, the fight turns more one-sided than any scoreboard suggests. Even retreats favor you — moving through water halves slows on her.

combos.title: Water Field Counter-Peel
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (create water field + landing heal) → Skill 1 (cast in water for knockback + stun) → Basic Attack (splash AoE)
combos.description: Even on land, making your own water turns Skill 1 into hard CC. This is textbook peel — bounce the diver off your carry, stun them, and let the splash attacks chip them out.

combos.title: Double Ultimate Supply
combos.sequence: Ally Ultimate lands → Ultimate (cooldown reset) → Skill 2 (water field sustain)
combos.description: The reset targets the longest remaining cooldown, so the moment right after a big cast is the sure window. Contract priority means the partner you chose at spawn is exactly who benefits here.

strengths: The Ultimate's instant reset of allied ultimates is unique support power
In water she gains healing, hard CC, and AoE attacks all at once
Skill 2 carries a water field anywhere, so she works far beyond the river
The contract system stacks resources on your ace and sharpens the win condition
weaknesses: The Ultimate's cooldown depends on ally skills, so it rotates poorly alone
Out of water, Skill 1 loses its CC and her self-defense collapses
Almost no personal damage — she creates nothing by herself
Her value craters when teammates don't understand the reset mechanic

synergy.reason: Provides massive AoE CC, creating a safe environment for Nakoruru to unleash her burst damage.
Can group enemies while providing stealth and armor shred, perfectly setting up Nakoruru's engages.

counters.reason: Can neutralize Nakoruru's dive and burst damage with massive shields and knockbacks.
Can easily burst Nakoruru down in close quarters using his i-frames and overwhelming damage.

passive.description: When Nakoruru hits an enemy with a skill, her next Basic Attack is enhanced, for up to 3 stacks. Her next Basic Attack summons Mamahaha, who deals damage to nearby enemies based on the number of stacks, with each stack dealing 120 (120 + 37% extra physical attack) physical damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: DANCING SWORD ARTS

skill1.description:
Nakoruru summons Mamahaha to attack the enemy, dealing 380 (380 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage and marking them with an Eagle Eye Mark.
Further damage dealt by her will activate the marks, dealing physical damage equal to 6% of the target's Health (max damage to monsters from the mark capped at 300).
Every 40 additional Physical Attack increases max Health by 1%. Activating the mark will reduce the cooldown of AMUBE YATORO by 2.5s and recover 35 Mana.
skill1.name: Skill 1: AMUBE YATORO

skill2.description:
Nakoruru dashes forward, dealing 400 (400 + 130% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. For every enemy hero hit, she recovers 400 (400 + 5% extra Health) Health.
When this skill hits a monster, it deals 50% more damage. Hitting non-hero units restores 50% of the Health restored when hitting heroes.
skill2.name: Skill 2: RERA MUTSUBE

skill3.description:
Nakoruru summons Mamahaha, gaining 50% Movement Speed for 6s which diminishes over time. She can ignore terrain once while flying.
Using this skill again causes her to charge toward the target area, dealing 600 (600 + 190% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. Enemies hit by her are slowed by 25% and deal 30% less damage for 3s.
Passive: Nakoruru summons Mamahaha to fly with her after staying out of combat for 4s, increasing her Movement Speed by 10%. She loses the Movement Speed increase upon re-entering combat.
skill3.name: Skill 3: KAMUI MUTSUBE

strategy.earlyGame: Nakoruru lives in the jungle. Skill 2 deals 50% bonus damage to monsters and heals on hit, giving her both clear speed and sustain through camps. Take both buffs and head straight to level 4 — the moment the Ultimate's 50% speed boost and terrain hop unlock, the quality of her ganks changes completely. The early trap is mana: detonating Skill 1's mark with any other damage refunds 35 MP, so build the habit of always following up a mark instead of leaving it to expire.
strategy.midGame: Mid game, wall-hop ganks from outside vision are your main weapon. Fly in through an unwarded route, mark with Skill 1, and detonate with the charge — with the max HP percent damage included, that string takes most targets to half or lower. At Tyrant and Shadow Tyrant contests, the standard play is landing the Ultimate's charge on the enemy jungler: their damage output drops 30% for 3 seconds, which tilts the entire objective burn in your favor on paper.
strategy.lateGame: The mark's max HP percent damage keeps her honest against tanks even late. But she has no exit tool after committing, so opening a fight from the front is off the table. Wait in side bushes and hunt chunked or isolated enemies instead. Her Ultimate's flight passive — activating after 4 seconds out of combat — quietly wins the late game's map movement: reset in a bush after each fight and you'll reach the next one before anybody else.
strategy.teamfight: Enter from the flank or the back. Your first job isn't damage — it's landing the Ultimate's charge on the enemy's main damage dealer to shred their output by 30%. Put that debuff on their marksman and your frontline's lifespan visibly stretches. From there, loop Skill 1 marks into detonations while weaving empowered basics onto chunked targets. Each detonation refunds 2.5 seconds of Skill 1's cooldown, so as long as you keep connecting, the pressure never stops.

combos.title: Wall-Hop Ambush Gank
combos.sequence: Ultimate (speed boost + terrain hop) → Skill 1 (mark) → Ultimate recast (charge, detonates the mark) → Skill 2 (follow-up dash) → Basic Attack (empowered)
combos.description: The standard fog entry with an instant detonation. The percent damage and the 30% output-shred debuff land together, so even a target who slips away is left easy for teammates to clean up.

combos.title: Clear Sustain Cycle
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (monster bonus + heal) → Skill 1 (mark) → Basic Attack (detonate, empowered)
combos.description: The jungle route pattern. Detonations refund cooldown and MP, so following this exact order heals you through camps at maximum speed. Time yourself — the difference versus mindless hitting is measurable.

strengths: Out-of-vision ganks powered by the 50% speed boost and terrain hopping
The mark's max HP percent damage stays relevant against tanks
The charge debuff cuts an enemy ace's damage output by 30%
Skill 2's healing and monster bonus keep clears fast and healthy
weaknesses: An all-in kit with no escape when the dive goes wrong
MP-hungry — missing mark detonations leads to fast burnout
No answer to hard CC; getting caught means dying on the spot
The speed boost decays over time, so prepared enemies blunt the ambush

synergy.reason: Absorbs enemy CC on the frontline, creating a safe environment for Ukyo to channel his ultimate.
Can peel for Ukyo with shields and heavy CC, creating openings for him to secure kills.

counters.reason: His high durability and CC like silences can completely shut down Ukyo's skill combos.
Can dodge Ukyo's attacks with overwhelming mobility while consistently dealing damage.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: CONCEALED SABRE HAZY BLADE
passive.description:
Ukyo Tachibana's next Basic Attack is enhanced to a quick-draw slash that has longer range, dealing 40 (40 + 35% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 15−30% (scales with hero level) for 2s. Enemies on the edge of the attack take 80 (80 + 70% extra physical attack) extra physical damage. Damage is halved against non-hero units. He recovers 125 (125 + 2% extra Health) Health.
The quick-draw slash has a cooldown of 4−5s (scales with hero level). Cooldown is shortened by 0.5s upon dealing skill damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: CONCEALED SABRE HAZY BLADE

skill1.description:
Ukyo Tachibana leaps backward and slashes enemies in his path, dealing 330 (330 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage and activating the skill's second phase. If no enemy units are hit, the second phase will be activated after 2s.
If he returns near the start point of phase 1 after using phase 2, he enhances the second phase to slash enemies in a larger range, and his Ultimate's Cooldown is reduced by 1s for every enemy hero hit (halved for non-hero units). For every 2% Health lost by the target, this skill's damage is increased by 1%.
skill1.name: Skill 1: CONCEALED SABRE SWALLOW SWIPE

skill2.description:
Ukyo Tachibana slashes in the target direction, dealing 580 (580 + 190% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range.
Enemies at the far end of the area are stunned for 0.75s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: CONCEALED SABRE HEAVENLY HACK

skill3.description:
Ukyo Tachibana quickly slashes 4 times in the target direction, with each slash dealing 210 (210 + 65% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. If an enemy hero is hit, each slash restores 300 (300 + 4.5% extra Health) Health to him.
The healing is halved if only non-hero units are hit.
skill3.name: Skill 3: CONCEALED SABRE SNOWFALL SLASH

strategy.earlyGame: Ukyo is primarily a jungler, though his dueling power makes clash lane workable. Clear camps around the Ultimate's four slashes and Skill 1, weaving the Passive's iai slash into every camp — skill damage refunds 0.5 seconds of its cooldown per hit, so clean rotations alone speed up your route. What matters before level 4 is internalizing tip range: both the iai slash and Skill 2 only pay their bonuses when they land at the very edge of their reach.
strategy.midGame: Around 10 minutes, with two physical items done, Ukyo wins almost any small-scale fight he takes. The ideal engage starts with Skill 2's tip stun — pour the Ultimate's four slashes into the 0.75-second lock, and the healing per enemy hero hit lets you out-sustain the brawl. He has genuine 1v2 potential, but he also folds instantly to CC, so while enemy lockdown is still up, measure the fight from one step back.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, his bait game on side lanes shines. Shove the wave; if one enemy comes, cook them at tip range — if two come, double-jump out with Skill 1. Repeat, and you're feeding your team a permanent numbers advantage. Never enter teamfights through the front: the CC-saturated middle is a death zone for Ukyo. Flank, wait for the formation to crack, and enter on a chunked target with the tip stun.
strategy.teamfight: Ukyo's teamfight is a continuous act of measuring tip distance inside the chaos. Too close and the bonus vanishes; too far and nothing lands. Watch for the enemy's dash, jump backward with Skill 1, and land the iai slash at the tip as they arrive — when that counter connects, the aggressor is the one who gets shredded. Angle the Ultimate through as many enemy heroes as possible: the healing stacks per hit, so slashing through two or three from the side actually keeps you healthier than dueling one target point-blank.

combos.title: Tip-Stun Execution
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (tip hit stuns 0.75s) → Ultimate (four slashes) → Basic Attack (iai slash) → Skill 1 (exit)
combos.description: Land all four slashes inside the stun. The per-hit healing against heroes lets you shrug off some return fire and still push through. Once it's done, don't chase — the Skill 1 exit is the safe close.

combos.title: Double-Jump Poke Trade
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (backward jump slash) → Basic Attack (iai slash at tip range) → Skill 1 (second jump near the first cast point for the empowered slash)
combos.description: Landing the second stage near where the first was cast upgrades it to the empowered version. With the tip bonus and its healing riding along, this trade is close to free — and it repeats.

strengths: Tip hits pay out damage, healing, and a stun all at once
The Ultimate's multi-hit healing wins extended small-scale brawls
Skill 1's double jump covers both aggression and clean exits
Skill hits refund the Passive's cooldown, keeping his output constant
weaknesses: Everything depends on spacing — wrong range means no damage and no healing
Fragile at baseline; getting CC'd is his number one cause of death
Skill 1's unusual movement takes real practice to stop misplaying
Struggles to show his strengths in CC-heavy frontal teamfights

synergy.reason: Can safely unleash high DPS from a distance by following up on Arthur's silences and knock-ups.
Can easily secure assassinations from behind while Arthur keeps the enemies silenced.

counters.reason: His true damage ignores Arthur's armor, allowing him to easily shred through him, shields and all.
Her high self-sustain and mobility completely neutralize Arthur's close-quarters brawling, allowing her to easily win trades.

passive.description: Arthur invokes the Holy Vanguard to recover 100 (100 + 2.5% extra Health) Health every 2s. If his Movement Speed is impaired, he recovers an extra 100 (100 + 2.5% extra Health) Health every 2s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Holy Vanguard

skill1.description:
Arthur gains 30% Movement Speed for 3s and enhances his next Basic Attack, where he dashes forward to deal 325 (325 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage and silence the target for 1.25s.
The enhanced Basic Attack also marks the target enemy hero for 5s. His Basic Attacks and skills deal extra magical damage to marked enemies equal to 1% of their Health.
Allies near marked enemies gain 10% Movement Speed.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Valiant Charge

skill2.description: Arthur summons holy shields that orbit him for 5s, dealing 285 (145 +80% physical attack) physical damage every second to nearby enemies.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Whirling Strike

skill3.description:
Arthur raises Excalibur and leaps at the target enemy hero, dealing magical damage equal to 16% of their max Health and leaving behind a holy seal. Enemies within range of the seal are launched for 0.5s.
The seal lasts 5s and deals 85 magical damage to enemies within range every second.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Might of Excalibur

strategy.earlyGame: Arthur takes any clash lane matchup. He has no mana, and his Passive restores 1% of max HP every 2 seconds, so getting chunked never forces him out — that regen is his early lifeline. From level 1, trade with Skill 1's dash plus 1-second silence and follow up with the Skill 2 spin. Against melee fighters, let Skill 2 handle the wave and hit level 4 first. At the 4-minute Tyrant, rotate to the river as the designated silence-bot for enemy interrupt skills.
strategy.midGame: Once the Ultimate unlocks, his gank follow-up becomes elite. It's a point-and-click leap with a knock-up that cannot miss — when your jungler shows up, stacking Ultimate into Skill 1 chains nearly 2 seconds of lockdown, and kills usually just happen. Make roaming mid a habit after every shove. A failed Arthur roam costs almost nothing thanks to the Passive's regen and move speed, and a successful one hands you mid priority outright. It's simply good investment.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, you're the frontline trigger for engages. The Ultimate deals 16% of the target's max HP as magic damage, so HP-stacked enemies actually take more — the jump works whether you point it at a carry or a frontliner. The prime target is the enemy mage: slam Skill 1's silence onto their cast animation and their big spell fizzles entirely, which is miserable to play against. Just confirm your team is actually following before you go in, or you're volunteering as the death vanguard.
strategy.teamfight: The teamfight plan is refreshingly simple: Ultimate the priority target, Skill 1 to silence the retaliation, keep Skill 2 spinning, keep swinging. Because the mechanics are easy, target selection is your entire contribution — default to the enemy backline, but if your side is collapsing, switch to bouncing the assassin who dove your own carries. Skill 2 keeps dealing damage while you move, so spin it on the chase and the retreat alike; it's never wasted.

combos.title: Point-and-Click Full Engage
combos.sequence: Ultimate (leap + knock-up) → Skill 1 (dash + silence) → Basic Attack → Skill 2 (spin for sustained damage)
combos.description: An engage that cannot whiff, locking one target out of the fight for roughly 2 seconds. This is the fight-starter and the gank follow-up — no reads required, just the right target.

combos.title: Spin-First Lane Trade
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (start the spin) → Skill 1 (dash + silence to stick) → Basic Attack → Passive (regen resets the trade)
combos.description: The lane bread and butter. Spinning before you dash means Skill 2 ticks the entire time you're attached, and the Passive's regen afterward banks the trade's profit for you.

strengths: No mana plus constant regen makes him impossible to shove out of lane
The point-and-click Ultimate and silence make every catch stick
16% max HP damage on the Ultimate hurts even stacked frontliners
A simple kit that doubles as the best classroom for fighter macro
weaknesses: Ranged kiting can whittle him down before he ever closes the gap
No shields or immunity — his only answer to focus fire is regen
Flat damage scaling; he can't become the late-game carry
Spending Skill 1 to engage leaves him no tool to disengage

synergy.reason: Can quickly follow up on Wukong's burst damage to secure the kill.
Can draw aggro and chunk enemies, making it much easier for Wukong to safely dive in and clean up.

counters.reason: Has high armor and CC, allowing him to tank Wukong's burst damage and counter-engage.
Can counter Wukong's engage with AoE damage and damage reduction, easily bursting him down in return.

passive.description:
After using a skill, Wukong enhances his next Basic Attack, where he charges at the target to deal 648 (475 + 100% physical attack) physical damage. This skill fully benefits from critical hit bonuses.
He has a base Crit Rate of 20%, but his base Crit Damage is only 150%.
passive.name: Passive Skill: The Great Sage

skill1.description:
Wukong chants a protective spell that lets him resist the next enemy skill used on him. The spell lasts up to 1.5s. If a skill is successfully resisted, he becomes invincible for 0.2s and gains a shield that negates 859 (600 + 150% physical attack + 15% extra Health) damage for 4s.
He gains 40% Movement Speed for 1s when using this skill.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Protective Shroud

skill2.description:
Wukong dashes in the target direction. If he dashes into an enemy, he leaps into the air and gains 90% Movement Speed that diminishes over 1s. Using a Basic Attack or skill will interrupt this leap.
Monster Slayer: Dashing into monsters will deal 274 (240 + 20% physical attack) true damage to them. If the monster has less than 15% Health, it will take grievous damage. This does not affect Overlords or Tyrants.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Furious Advance

skill3.description:
Wukong rams his staff into the earth, dealing 250 (250 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and launching them for 1s.
He also places 3 marks on enemies within range. When his Basic Attacks hit a marked enemy, the target loses a mark and takes an extra 270 physical damage.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Golden Cudgel

strategy.earlyGame: Wukong owns one of the fastest jungle clears in the game. Skill 2 deals true damage to monsters and outright executes any monster below 15% HP (Tyrant and Overlord excluded), so his full clear beats most junglers by a camp. The catch: his crit damage starts capped at 150%, so his early dueling is weaker than the highlight reels suggest. Farm to level 4 without greed, and keep one eye out for the enemy jungler's invade — that's the only real threat.
strategy.midGame: Everything changes around 8-10 minutes with one or two attack speed and crit items done. His post-skill empowered basics always crit, which means every point of crit damage on your items is pure scaling. Gank by entering with Skill 2's dash, then empowered basic into the Ultimate's knock-up into detonating brands with basics. Hold Skill 1 in reserve as insurance against their answer skill instead of burning it for movement — your success rate climbs immediately.
strategy.lateGame: At full build, a single empowered basic deletes backliners. His body stays soft, though, so never walk in through the front. Wait in side bushes or behind walls and strike from behind the moment enemy eyes face forward. One trick: pre-channel Skill 1 right before you dive. Catching their reaction skill is far easier that way than pressing it reactively, and a successful block's shield plus 0.2 seconds of immunity transforms your odds of walking out alive.
strategy.teamfight: Opening the teamfight is a mistake. Wukong's job is spotting the handful of seconds when the enemy backline's peel thins out. Enter with Skill 2's speed, empowered basic, Ultimate knock-up, then detonate the brands with basics while another guaranteed crit lands. Everything crits, so squishy targets die before the knock-up ends. Finish, then take Skill 2's second dash to complete the exit. Whether you chase a second kill comes down to one question: is Skill 1 still up?

combos.title: Standard Backline Burst
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (dash + speed) → Basic Attack (guaranteed crit) → Ultimate (knock-up + brands) → Basic Attack (detonates a brand) → Skill 1 → Basic Attack (guaranteed crit)
combos.description: Every skill press recharges the empowered basic, so this string weaves in the maximum number of guaranteed crits. Land the second one during the knock-up and squishy targets simply don't survive.

combos.title: Skill-Block Counter
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (channel, block an enemy skill) → Shield gained → Skill 2 (dash) → Basic Attack (guaranteed crit) → Ultimate
combos.description: Deliberately stand in their counter-CC with the block up, then turn on them with the shield and immunity in hand. Their key skill is gone from the duel, which creates upset potential even against stronger opponents.

strengths: Post-skill empowered basics always crit, giving elite late-game burst
Skill 1 can nullify one key enemy skill and flip entire duels
The monster execute makes his jungle clear among the fastest anywhere
Speed boosts on every skill give him fast engages and faster exits
weaknesses: His damage stays modest until crit items actually come online
Whiffing the Skill 1 block exposes just how soft his defenses are
Reliant on empowered basics — attack-dodging enemies blank him
The knock-up is his only CC, so fleeing targets are hard to pin

synergy.reason: Lian Po provides strong AoE CC and armor buffs, creating a safe environment for Huang Zhong to siege.
Lian Po's massive AoE knock-up allows Diaochan to safely set up her ultimate and dominate the teamfight.

counters.reason: His high mobility makes it easy to dodge Lian Po's skills, and his true damage effortlessly shreds through tanks.
His true damage ignores armor and shields, rendering Lian Po's tankiness completely useless.

passive.description: Lapulapu gains 100 Physical and Magical Defense. When there are teammates within a range of 800, the teammate with the lowest Health also gains this bonus. When there are no teammates within range, Lapulapu gains an extra 50% Physical and Magical Defense.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Sea Beast's Favor

skill1.description:
Tap: Lapulapu slashes with his blade, dealing 498 (320 + 110% physical attack) physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 30% for 1s. This skill's cooldown is then reduced by 50%. He recovers 100 (100 + 2% extra Health) Health for each enemy hit by the slash. Effect is halved against non-hero units.
Tap and hold: Lapulapu throws his weapon in the target direction, dealing 498 (320 + 110% physical attack) physical damage to enemies hit and slowing them by 15% for 1s. After his weapon drops to the ground, it continuously deals 99 (75 + 15% physical attack) physical damage. When Lapulapu retrieves his weapon, he slashes nearby enemies and knocks them back.
When this skill hits an enemy, it reduces their [icon] by 50 for 2s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Torrential Blade

skill2.description: Lapulapu charges in the target direction, dealing 529 (400 + 80% physical attack) physical damage to enemies along the path and launching them for 0.75s. After they land, enemies are slowed immensely for 1s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Island's Blessing

skill3.description:
Lapulapu briefly charges up, then cleaves the ground, dealing 650 (650 + 180% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range, launching them for 1s, and interrupting their skill use.
The ground remains fractured for 5s, and enemies caught in the fissures take 80 (80 + 25% extra physical attack) physical damage per 0.5s, and are slowed by 30%.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Raging Sea

strategy.earlyGame: Start the game glued to your marksman in the farm lane. Lapulapu's Passive, Sea Beast's Favor, raises defenses for both himself and the lowest-HP ally nearby, so simply standing next to your carry does work — camping a bush alone wastes the buff. Once you have Skill 2, punish any enemy who steps up by dashing in for a short trade with the knock-up. Skill 1's tap slash comes back fast and heals you on every hit, so spam it freely whenever a brawl breaks out. And don't forget to rotate toward mid before the Tyrant spawns at four minutes.
strategy.midGame: From level 4 onward, Lapulapu's hidden strength is that his Ultimate interrupts enemy skill casts. One charged strike can cancel a channeled ultimate or a Recall mid-cast, so at Tyrant fights, time it on top of the enemy jungler's Punish attempt. Between roams, you can also pre-throw your weapon with Skill 1 (hold) to tag enemies with the 50 physical defense shred before your team commits. You're the one eating hits at the front of every fight, so start playing forward in earnest around the six-minute mark, once your first core defensive item is finished.
strategy.lateGame: The Shadow Tyrant fights after ten minutes are where you earn your keep. Skill 2 into Ultimate chains two knock-ups for roughly 1.75 seconds of total airtime — whether your team's damage lands inside that window decides the fight, so only engage within range of your allies. The rift lingers for five seconds, and dropping it across a narrow chokepoint in front of the Overlord pit dramatically slows any enemy approach. The Passive does boost your defenses by another 50% when you're alone, but you have no kill threat, so never chase deep. In retreats, cover the back line with the weapon throw's slow.
strategy.teamfight: Skill 2 is your signal to start the fight. Drag the knocked-up target into your Ultimate's charge and force the brawl on top of the rift — that's the ideal shape. Once the scrap starts, keep landing Skill 1's tap slash; the healing and cooldown refunds make you far harder to kill than you look. Be picky about who you launch: aim for an overextended mage or marksman, never the enemy tank. And the instant you see a healing or recall channel start, cancel it with your Ultimate's interrupt. It's unglamorous work, but it wins games.

combos.title: Double Knock-Up Engage
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Ultimate → Skill 1 (Tap)
combos.description: Pin the target with the dash's knock-up, finish charging your Ultimate during the 0.75 seconds they're airborne, and chain straight into the second knock-up. Roughly 1.75 seconds of lockdown is plenty for your team to follow up. Land, then hold your ground with the healing slashes.

combos.title: Weapon Throw Zoning
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Hold) → Retrieve Weapon → Skill 2
combos.description: Toss your weapon at the enemy's feet to apply the physical defense shred and slow, then let the grounded weapon's damage-over-time seal off the path. Picking the weapon back up triggers a knockback slash, so the retrieval itself doubles as a tool for shoving attackers off you.

strengths: Passive raises defenses for himself and the lowest-HP nearby ally at once
Ultimate interrupts enemy skill casts, shutting down channeled abilities
Skill 1's healing and cooldown refunds make him excel in extended brawls
Skill 2 into Ultimate chains a punishing double knock-up
weaknesses: Low personal damage — his lockdown is wasted without allied follow-up
Ultimate needs a charge-up and often misses high-mobility targets
Skill 2 is his only dash, leaving no escape after he commits
No answer to long-range poke and gets chipped down for free

synergy.reason: Provides sustained healing, allowing them to survive longer in teamfights and dish out continuous auto-attack damage.
Provides massive shields and excellent peel to protect the low-mobility Hou Yi from diving assassins.

counters.reason: Ignores terrain to directly dive the backline and easily burst down the defenseless Hou Yi.
Uses high mobility to close the gap, chaining attacks and silences to burst them down before they can react.

passive.description:
Hou Yi gains 1 stack of Chastising Shot every time he hits an enemy with his Basic Attack, for up to 3 stacks. Each stack increases his Attack Speed by 2–4% for 3s.
At max stacks, he becomes enhanced for 3s. While enhanced, his Basic Attacks shoot 3 arrows (counts as 1 Basic Attack), dealing a total of 120% of a normal Basic Attack's physical damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Chastising Shot

skill1.description: Hou Yi enhances his Basic Attacks to deal 214 (90 + 75% physical attack) physical damage. While the Passive's enhancement is in effect, using Skill 1 will cause the 3 arrows to deal a total of 120% of a normal Basic Attack's physical damage plus 50% damage to 2 more enemies or structures in front of him within range (without on-hit effects). This effect lasts 5s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Arrow Volley

skill2.description:
Hou Yi orders the Sun Tower to attack the target area, gaining vision of the area.
After a short delay, he deals 480 (480 + 110% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and reduces their Movement Speed by 25–50% for 2s. Damage and slow effects are halved against enemies on the edge of the skill's range.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Afterglow

skill3.description:
Hou Yi shoots a flaming arrow in the target direction, which explodes upon hitting an enemy hero. The explosion deals 800 (800 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range.
The arrow stuns the first enemy hero hit for 0.75–3.5s (depending on how far it has flown), while slowing enemies in the explosion's range by 30% for 1s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Burning Sun Arrow

strategy.earlyGame: Your first job in the farm lane is building those three Passive stacks cleanly. Chastising Shot empowers Hou Yi after three basic attacks, turning each shot into a spread of three arrows, so the laning rhythm is simple: step up and trade only while empowered, back off when it drops. With zero mobility skills, stay away from the river bushes around the four-minute Tyrant whenever you've lost track of the enemy jungler. Skill 2 grants vision at range, so fire it into bushes ahead of time — it's your cheapest insurance against ganks while you farm.
strategy.midGame: Once you hit level 4, Hou Yi joins fights he isn't even standing in. The Ultimate's stun scales up to 3.5 seconds with flight distance, and a cross-map arrow flipping a skirmish is a regular occurrence — when your teammates start posturing at mid, line one up from an off-angle. From around seven minutes, with one or two attack speed items finished, you become the primary teamfight damage source: lay Skill 2 across the enemy's escape path for the slow, and learn to hold ground behind your front line pumping triple arrows.
strategy.lateGame: At Shadow Tyrant and Overlord standoffs, the single most important question is whether your Ultimate is still in your pocket. Land it on the enemy carry from long range and the extended stun hands you a free numbers advantage; miss it, and Skill 2's slow is your only anti-dive tool left. So the iron rule: only fire once the enemy formation has settled. Empowered Skill 1 also sends 50% damage into two enemies in front of you and towers, so keep three stacks rolling and melt turrets with it during sieges. Hold your position one step behind the front line, no exceptions.
strategy.teamfight: Hou Yi's spot is the very back row, yet his damage reaches the whole battlefield. Opening the fight with your own Ultimate is perfectly fine — if it tags the mage lurking behind the enemy tank, your win condition is all but locked in. Once the brawl starts, lean on the triple arrows' natural spread and shred the front line together with everyone stacked behind it. When an assassin dives you, drop Skill 2 at your own feet, let them walk into the slow, then re-space. Save Flash as your final trump card instead of burning it at the first sign of danger.

combos.title: Cross-Map Pick
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Skill 2 → Basic Attack (repeat)
combos.description: A Burning Sun Arrow landed near max range stuns for up to 3.5 seconds. Layer Afterglow under the immobilized target to queue up the follow-up slow, then hammer in basic attacks — by the time your teammates arrive, the duel is already decided.

combos.title: Triple-Arrow Max DPS
combos.sequence: Basic Attack ×3 → Skill 1 → Basic Attack
combos.description: Casting Skill 1 while empowered at three Passive stacks fires the triple volley on activation, then layers bonus damage for five seconds. Since 50% of the damage spills onto two enemies in front and onto towers, this is your highest-efficiency pattern for sieges and messy brawls alike.

strengths: Empowered triple arrows shred multiple enemies and towers at once
Ultimate's cross-map stun picks off targets from outside the screen
Skill 2 scouts bushes safely with long-range vision
Simple mechanics make him an ideal first rapid-fire marksman
weaknesses: No mobility skills whatsoever — once caught, he can't escape alone
Damage lives in basic attacks, so attack speed debuffs cripple him
Skill 2's delayed impact makes it hard to land on its own
Missing the Ultimate leaves almost nothing to stop divers

synergy.reason: Pulls enemies in, making it easier for Liu Bei to land his close-range shotgun burst.
Can lock enemies down with strong CC, creating openings for Liu Bei to unleash his burst damage.

counters.reason: Can completely shut down Liu Bei's engage with her heavy arsenal of CC.
Can easily dodge Liu Bei's attacks while consistently poking him down with her high mobility and range.

passive.description:
Liu Bei's shotgun holds 4 shells. The two middle shells deal 87 (50% physical attack) physical damage to the enemy, while the other two shells on either side deal 52 (30% physical attack) physical damage. Every hit on an enemy hero grants him 1 stack of Combat Instinct, giving 5–10 Physical Pierce for 6s. Combat Instinct stacks up to 12 times.
Only the 2 middle shells from each shot can crit and trigger equipment effects. Structures are not affected by extra shells.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Reinforced Shells

skill1.description: Liu Bei increases his Movement Speed by 40% for 1.5s. The next Basic Attack is a double shot, with each shell dealing 148 (110 + 22% physical attack) physical damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Dual Shot

skill2.description:
Liu Bei smashes into the enemy, knocking them back and dealing 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage before stopping.
Hitting an enemy hero reduces this skill's cooldown by 2s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Leading the Charge

skill3.description:
Liu Bei cleanses himself of all crowd control effects and gains crowd control immunity for 3s.
He also gains 100 physical attack and a shield that negates 1,000 (1,000 + 15% extra Health) damage for 6s.
While the shield is active, 60% of the damage he deals to enemy heroes and 20% of the damage he deals to minions and monsters is added to the shield.
Shield points are capped at 150% of the initial value.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Hearts and Minds

strategy.earlyGame: Liu Bei is played jungle first. His Passive shotgun fires four pellets and all four only connect at point-blank range, so hug every buff monster while you clear — your camp speed improves visibly. Level 4 and the Ultimate unlock is your first real decision point; until then, don't force anything and just bank your second buff rotation. When you do gank, enter with Skill 2 from the enemy's escape side so the knockback shoves them toward your teammates. Every pellet that lands stacks physical defense shred, so make it a rule: fight inside their face and empty everything.
strategy.midGame: Six to eight minutes, when your core damage item finishes, is when Liu Bei runs wild. The Ultimate cleanses CC, grants three seconds of CC immunity, and converts 60% of the damage you deal to heroes into shield — press it the moment enemy CC turns toward you and the brawl becomes one-sided. Before Tyrant and Overlord Punish wars, pre-stack pellet shred on the objective to win the burn-down. When you spot an isolated target, walk them down while saving Skill 2 for the chase — holding the dash in reserve is what separates good Liu Bei players from impatient ones.
strategy.lateGame: Past ten minutes, switch to entering fights second. The moment enemy CC and attention lock onto your front line, flank with Skill 2 onto their back line and delete a squishy with point-blank pellets — that's Liu Bei's signature win condition. The Ultimate's shield rebuilds as long as you keep shooting, so answer panicked CC chains with your immunity window and simply out-damage them. Once it expires, though, you're just a melee hero; don't get greedy after a kill. Secure the Shadow Tyrant buff, then close out with the numbers advantage.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, Liu Bei becomes the star a few seconds after the opening, not at it. Wait until the enemy dumps skills and CC on your front line, then Skill 2 onto something soft and unload — pellets, Skill 1's double shot, more pellets. If they try to stop you, cleanse instantly with your Ultimate and keep firing. The outer two pellets whiff at range, so your teamfight position is permanently inside the enemy's pocket. From their perspective, the fight is basically lost the moment lockdown stops working on you. Cycling shields in the middle of the scrum, he plays like a fighter wearing a marksman's tag.

combos.title: Point-Blank Shotgun Burst
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Basic Attack → Skill 1 → Basic Attack
combos.description: Dash into melee range and land all four pellets while weaving in the double shot. Each pellet hit stacks physical defense shred up to 12 times, so the longer you stay on the same target, the harder every blast lands.

combos.title: CC-Reversal All-In
combos.sequence: (Enemy CC lands) → Ultimate → Skill 2 → Basic Attack
combos.description: The instant a stun or pull connects, cleanse it with your Ultimate, then dash in and unload during the three seconds of CC immunity. With 60% of hero damage converting into shield, you can absorb their counterattack while walking straight through it.

strengths: Devastating point-blank burst when all four pellets connect
Ultimate's cleanse and 3-second immunity walk through enemy CC
Damage dealt converts into shield, so he gets tankier as he swings
Pellet hits stack armor shred, keeping damage high even into tanks
weaknesses: Damage falls off sharply at range as the outer pellets stop connecting
Skill 2 is his only dash; miss it and he can neither chase nor leave
Extremely vulnerable to CC the moment his Ultimate wears off
Only the two center pellets crit, making item efficiency awkward

synergy.reason: Thanks to Zhang Fei's shields and CC, she can safely dish out massive DPS from the backline.
Zhang Fei locking down the frontline creates a safe environment for her to hunt for burst damage opportunities.

counters.reason: Her high mobility and true damage render Zhang Fei's shields and durability completely useless.
His true damage ignores Zhang Fei's massive shields, allowing him to deal devastating damage.

Zhang Fei smashes the ground, dealing 741 (600 + 150% extra physical attack + 4% Health) physical damage to enemies within range. Enemies in the center are launched for 0.5s.

skill1.description:
Zhang Fei swings his snake spear, dealing 600 (600 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range and knocking back enemy heroes.
Hitting an enemy unit increases Madness by 3.

skill2.name: Skill 2: Leaping Savior / Stampede

forms.description:
Zhang Fei leaps to the target location and activates a mark, granting a shield that negates 650 (650 + 13% extra Health) damage to teammates within range.
He gains 3 Madness from using the skill and 1 extra Madness for each shield granted to teammates.
Zhang Fei leaps to the target location, trampling enemies within range and dealing 621 (480 + 120% extra physical attack + 4% Health) physical damage. Enemies in the center are launched for 0.5s.

skill2.description:
Zhang Fei leaps to the target location and activates a mark, granting a shield that negates 650 (650 + 13% extra Health) damage to teammates within range.
He gains 3 Madness from using the skill and 1 extra Madness for each shield granted to teammates.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Unbridled Outburst
skill3.description:
Zhang Fei roars in the target direction for 1.25s, generating a powerful gust of wind and gaining a shield that negates damage equal to 40% of his Health for 15s. While roaring, he gains crowd control immunity and invincibility. The wind knocks enemies back and deals 600 (600 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage, and enemies at the end of its path are stunned for 1.5s. His Movement Speed increases by 50% while he is in the wind.
Ferali Form: While he is in Ferali Form, his Basic Attacks deal an extra 220 (220 + 100% extra physical attack) damage. When Ferali Form ends, Forbidden Domain is automatically triggered.

strategy.earlyGame: The lane opens with you swinging basic attacks next to your marksman. It looks menial, but Zhang Fei gains 3 Fury per swing, and how fast you reach transformation is quite literally how strong you are. Skill 2's landing shield covers multiple allies at once and grants extra Fury for each ally shielded, so stack it the instant a teammate is about to eat damage — that's maximum value. In trades, cut off enemy chases with Skill 1's knockback. Bank a full Fury bar before the Tyrant spawns at four minutes and you'll have the transformation ready for the first skirmish.
strategy.midGame: Whether your Ultimate is available defines mid game Zhang Fei — with it up, he's a different hero. The roar carries 1.25 seconds of invincibility and CC immunity, so its strongest use is a head-on counter to enemy engages. Enemies caught at the far edge of the storm are stunned for 1.5 seconds, which means the clean blast comes from half a step back rather than point-blank. Around Tyrant and Overlord, sit on the transformation and answer whoever moves first. While transformed, your basic attacks carry bonus damage, so you can moonlight as a damage threat too.
strategy.lateGame: In teamfights after ten minutes, Zhang Fei's reason to exist is entering the fight holding a shield worth 40% of his max HP. During Shadow Tyrant standoffs, stand one step forward so the enemy initiation lands on you, absorb it, then answer with the roar. Just manage the knock-away direction carefully — launching the enemy carry toward your team is game-winning, while launching them to safety makes you the villain instantly. Remember that Skill 1 auto-casts when the transformation ends, so you can factor that final knockback into your closing sequence.
strategy.teamfight: Zhang Fei's teamfight is a checklist. Pre-shield your team with Skill 2, answer the enemy's dive with the roar, split their formation with the storm — and only then start swinging. The 1.25 seconds of invincibility exists to make enemy ultimates whiff, so firing it early with nothing to counter is a waste. Watch for the enemy ult animation, then blow them away, and the battlefield goes quiet in an instant. While transformed, every skill you cast also slows nearby enemies, so you can even run down the stragglers yourself.

combos.title: Counter Roar
combos.sequence: (On enemy engage) Ultimate → Skill 1 → Basic Attack
combos.description: The 1.25 seconds of the roar are CC-immune and invincible. Absorb the enemy's dive skill, blast them away, then follow the sweep onto anyone stunned at the storm's edge. Take the hit first, answer second — that's Zhang Fei's core philosophy.

combos.title: Shield Interpose
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Skill 1 → Basic Attack
combos.description: Leap onto a focus-fired teammate, catch the damage with the landing shield, then peel the attackers off with the knockback. Every ally you shield also feeds you Fury, so protecting your carry actively speeds up your next transformation — defense and progress in one motion.

strengths: A 40% max HP shield and an invincible roar create massive comeback power
Skill 2 shields multiple allies with a single leap
The storm's knock-away and edge stun wreck enemy formations
Bonus damage and constant slows while transformed make him a real threat
weaknesses: Low damage and only a knockback for CC until Fury is charged
A misdirected blast saves enemies and betrays your team's follow-up
Mobility depends entirely on Skill 2's leap, limiting self-defense
No ranged tools — he spectates during poke wars

synergy.reason: Absorbs damage on the frontline, allowing the squishy Qisha to safely switch weapons and position.
Groups enemies up, allowing you to burst them down instantly with AoE skills.

counters.reason: High sustain and CC make it easy to lose damage trades against him.
High mobility allows him to engage quickly, bursting you down before you can react.

passive.name: Passive Skill: Forge Inheritor
passive.description:
Chicha cycles through her five ancestral weapons (polearm, spear, dagger-axe, halberd, and bow). Each Basic Attack restores 20 (20 + 0.3% extra Health) Health and switches to the next weapon with increased range. Each Basic Attack or skill hit grants 1 stack of Fighting Spirit (lasts 4s, up to 8 stacks), with each stack granting 4% Attack Speed (can exceed the Attack Speed cap).
Holding a polearm or spear puts her in Defense Form, dagger-axe or halberd puts her in Offense Form, and bow puts her in Overkill Form.
Each form grants different Skill 1 and Skill 2 effects. Entering Overkill Form instantly reduces Skill 1 and Skill 2 [icon] by 50%.

skill1.name: Skill 1: Peak-Crushing Polearm / Hell-Binding Dagger-Axe / Sky-Shattering Bow

forms.description: Defense Form: Chicha swings her weapon and leaps forward in the target direction, dealing 225 (225 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in the path and carrying them to the landing point. After landing, thrusts forward, dealing 225 (225 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage and launching enemies for 0.75s.

Offense Form: Chicha hurls her weapon toward the target direction and propels forward, dealing 250 (250 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path and pushing them to the skill's endpoint. After landing, she smashes the ground, dealing 250 (250 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage and launching enemies for 0.75s.

Overkill Form: Chicha launches a flying kick in the target direction, firing a piercing arrow that deals 275 (275 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking back enemies for 0.75s. If enemies hit a wall, they are restricted to a fixed area for 2s and take 275 (275 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage.

skill1.skill_name: Skill 1: Peak-Crushing Polearm / Hell-Binding Dagger-Axe / Sky-Shattering Bow
skill1.description: Defense Form: Chicha swings her weapon and leaps forward in the target direction, dealing 225 (225 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in the path and carrying them to the landing point. After landing, thrusts forward, dealing 225 (225 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage and launching enemies for 0.75s.

skill2.name: Skill 2: World-Splitting Spear / Realm-Sweeping Halberd / Star-Felling Arrow

forms.description: Defense Form: Chicha thrusts forward in the target direction, dealing 450 (450 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking back enemies (without applying crowd control). For each target hit, she recovers 180 (180 + 3% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).

Offense Form: Chicha sweeps in the target direction, dealing 475 (475 + 160% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking back enemies (without applying crowd control). For each target hit, she recovers 180 (180 + 3% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).

Overkill Form: Chicha aims in the target direction, locking onto all enemies in range (up to five, prioritizing heroes). After aiming, she shoots arrows at all locked-on targets, dealing 500 (500 + 170% extra physical attack) physical damage, plus true damage equal to 10% of the Health the target has lost, and knocking back enemies (without crowd control). For each target hit, she recovers 180 (180 + 3% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).
While using this skill, Chicha gains crowd control immunity and 15% damage reduction.

skill2.skill_name: Skill 2: World-Splitting Spear / Realm-Sweeping Halberd / Star-Felling Arrow
skill2.description: Defense Form: Chicha thrusts forward in the target direction, dealing 450 (450 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking back enemies (without applying crowd control). For each target hit, she recovers 180 (180 + 3% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).

skill3.name: Skill 3: Return of the Armsmaster
skill3.description:
Chicha unleashes all five weapons, gaining a Movement Speed boost for 2s and 35% Attack Speed, and breaking the Fighting Spirit stack limit for 6s.
During this time, she commands all five weapons to attack, with each Basic Attack dealing an extra 40 (40 + 13% extra physical attack) physical damage.
While using this skill, she can use her Basic Attack while moving. Overkill Form will remain active once entered.

strategy.earlyGame: Chicha is a rare marksman whose brawling literally heals her. Every basic attack restores HP and cycles her to the next, longer-ranged weapon, so in the farm lane your first rule is to never stop swinging. Fervor stacks vanish after four seconds — keep the gaps between attacks short. Overextending while holding the defense-form polearm or spear is how you die, so only step to enemy heroes when the bow's Extreme Form comes around. Learning this rhythm of pressure and patience is your lifeline until level 4.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, one question drives everything: can you cast your Ultimate while in Extreme Form? Using it while holding the bow locks the form in, and with Skill 1 and Skill 2 cooldowns cut in half, you attack on the move and simply out-trade whoever stands in front of you. Once your first attack speed item finishes around six minutes, start showing up to Tyrant fights — with healing on every basic attack, you don't lose extended damage races. One quiet trick that wins real games: pre-cycle your weapon on minions until you're two or three swings from the bow before the fight starts.
strategy.lateGame: With three or four items done past the ten-minute mark, Chicha's Fervor — which pushes attack speed beyond the normal cap — makes her about the scariest sustained duelist on the map. She's also the priority target, so open teamfights behind your front line and use the Ultimate as your counterpunch once the divers commit. At Shadow Tyrant standoffs, prioritize positions where you can keep swinging over hiding and waiting. The moment your attacks stop, Fervor drops, the healing stops, and everything Chicha is falls apart. Never stopping is your best defense.
strategy.teamfight: Half of Chicha's teamfight is decided by which weapon she's holding when it starts. The ideal is the bow's Extreme Form: halved Skill 1 and Skill 2 cooldowns layered under the Ultimate's move-and-shoot, kiting backward while shredding their whole front line. Every basic attack heals you mid-brawl, so a chunk of the damage you take can simply be punched back. When an assassin jumps you, fighting back — and cycling your weapon forward — often keeps you alive longer than running would. The six seconds of her Ultimate, all five weapons unleashed, contains her entire teamfight in miniature.

combos.title: Extreme Form Lock-In
combos.sequence: Basic Attack (cycle to the Bow) → Ultimate → Skill 1 → Skill 2
combos.description: Entering the bow's Extreme Form cuts Skill 1 and Skill 2 cooldowns by 50%, and casting your Ultimate in that state locks the form in place. Spend the six seconds of move-and-shoot with bonus damage dumping the shortened cooldowns as fast as they return — this is her maximum damage pattern.

combos.title: Fervor Uptime Kiting
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Basic Attack (attack on the move)
combos.description: Fervor stacks with every hit and pushes attack speed past the normal cap, but it disappears after four seconds. Kiting backward with the Ultimate's move-and-shoot so your attacks never stop is the simplest way to protect your damage and your healing at the same time.

strengths: Healing on every basic attack wins brawls and sustains her lane
Fervor stacks push attack speed past the normal cap
Ultimate's move-and-shoot keeps damage flowing while kiting
Five cycling weapons adapt her range to any situation
weaknesses: Weapons cycle in fixed order, making a specific form hard to hold
Four seconds without attacking drops Fervor and craters her damage
Hit-count design makes attack speed debuffs and hard CC brutal
Form management takes real practice before she comes online

173.name: Fang

Provides peel and CC, creating a safe window to stack explosive marks.

counters.reason: Strong chain CC shuts down Fang's mobility and stops him before he can output full damage.
Skill 2 cleanses Fang's explosive marks, nullifying his lethal burst damage.

passive.description:
Fang's big ears allow him to sense nearby movement and pick up the trail of enemy heroes, gaining their vision for 1s. This skill works on the same hero once every 6s.
He can also identify monster weak spots, letting him deal 7.5-15% extra physical damage to monsters.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Going Undercover
