Fang marks an enemy with a Dark Mark that explodes after 4s, dealing 230 (230 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. His Basic Attacks place 1 stack of Dark Mark, for up to 4 stacks, with each stack dealing an extra 230 (230 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage. The Dark Marks detonate immediately upon reaching 4 stacks.
He also gains 35% Attack Speed and 75 Attack Range for 4s when using this skill.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Target Sighted

skill2.description: Fang launches his blade in the target direction and catches it on the other end with uncanny speed. He is untargetable while using this skill. The blade deals 260 (260 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path and slows them by 15% for 2s. He also leaves a burning trail behind him for 2.9s, which deals 110 (110 + 30% extra physical attack) physical damage every 0.25s to enemies treading on it and slows them by 15%.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Wheel Away

skill3.description:
Fang throws his blade to the target location, dealing 320 (320 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range. After reaching its destination, it spins for 5.4s, dealing 140 (140 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies within range every 0.5s while slowing them by 50%.
The blade deals double damage to enemies at the center and places Dark Marks on them.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Bladestorm

strategy.earlyGame: Fang works in the farm lane or the jungle, and either way the game plan is the same: four mark stacks, instant detonation. In lane, hit Skill 1 for the attack speed and range boost, land four basic attacks on your opponent, and watch the trade swing hard your way. His Passive adds bonus damage against monsters, so as a jungler he burns down the four-minute Tyrant about as fast as anyone in the game. That same Passive reveals enemy heroes lurking nearby, which makes bush ambushes far easier to smell out. Whatever you do, keep Skill 2 in reserve as your escape.
strategy.midGame: From around seven minutes, with one or two damage items finished, you become an objective monster — the monster bonus and mark detonations stack up, and Tyrant and Overlord visibly melt a size faster under your shots. When a teammate catches someone, the standard play is dropping your Ultimate's tornado on their escape route to box them in. Damage inside the tornado is doubled and tornado ticks also stack marks, so layered with Skill 1, squishy targets rarely make it out. Just remember Skill 2 is your only self-defense tool; spend it with care.
strategy.lateGame: Late game Fang designs teamfights around tornado placement. Pre-place it on the tight terrain in front of Shadow Tyrant and the enemy must either eat the doubled-damage core or break formation walking around it. Past ten minutes, cut back on solo play: Skill 2's untargetable dash is excellent, but the seconds after it's spent leave you genuinely defenseless, and getting caught there kills you through any item lead. In sieges, mark detonations splash onto enemies packed under the tower, so lean on your front line and grind forward together.
strategy.teamfight: Open every teamfight with the tornado. Place it where the enemy back line will retreat — or where your front line will shove them — and let the five-plus seconds of doubled damage shrink the battlefield. From there, boost your attack speed with Skill 1 and stack marks off everything the tornado touches; a brawl with chained four-stack detonations is Fang's private playground. When assassins dive, slip through them with Skill 2, leave the burning trail's slow behind, and re-position behind your front line. The detonations are area damage — the tighter the enemy clumps, the harder you hit.

combos.title: Instant Four-Stack Detonation
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Basic Attack ×4 (marks detonate instantly)
combos.description: Boost your attack speed and range with Skill 1, then land four basic attacks and the Dark Marks explode with no waiting. The blast is area damage, so even when trading across a minion wave, the explosion swallows the enemy marksman standing behind it.

combos.title: Tornado Closeout
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Skill 1 → Basic Attack (repeat)
combos.description: Place the tornado on the escape route, catch them in the 50% slow and doubled inner damage, then finish the four mark stacks with basic attacks — tornado hits count toward them too. This is Fang's kill pattern for anyone your team catches out.

combos.title: Untargetable Bait
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Skill 1 → Basic Attack
combos.description: While traveling with the chakram, you're untargetable. Let the assassin's dive whiff clean through you, pin them with the burning trail's slow, then boost your attack speed and swing back. It's your one trump card, so where you spend it matters more than anything.

strengths: Mark detonations plus a monster bonus give elite objective speed
Skill 2's untargetable dash dodges burst skills outright
Doubled damage inside the tornado dominates tight-quarters fights
Passive reveals lurking enemies, defusing bush ambushes
weaknesses: Damage depends on stacking marks; single-hit burst is modest
Badly exposed after Skill 2 is spent and melts to focus fire
Late-game sustained damage trails pure basic-attack marksmen
If enemies sidestep the tornado, his teamfight control halves

synergy.reason: Strong CC locks enemies in place, creating openings to land Consort Yu's long-range poke and ultimate.
Provides guaranteed peel against assassin dives, buying time for safe damage output.

counters.reason: As an ADC with magic damage basic attacks, Erin renders Consort Yu's physical immunity completely useless.
High mobility and continuous true/magic damage completely bypass Consort Yu's physical immunity for an easy kill.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: Blessing of the Dryads
passive.description: Basic Attacks have a 25% chance of shooting an extra bolt, which deals 110 (90 + 12% physical attack) physical damage and places 1 stack of slow on the enemy, for up to 2 stacks. Each stack slows enemies by 10−20% for 2s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Blessing of the Dryads

skill1.description:
After charging up, Consort Yu shoots a powerful bolt in the target direction, dealing damage to enemies in its path. The bolt deals 740 (740 + 230% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy it hits. Damage is reduced by 15% for every subsequent enemy hit, down to 40% of the initial damage.
When her Attack Speed is increased by 0%/40%/80%/120%/160%/200%, her charging is accelerated by 0%/20%/40%/60%/80%/100%.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Oak Bolt

skill2.description:
Consort Yu enhances herself for 2s. While enhanced, her Movement Speed is increased by 20%, Attack Speed is increased by 12.5%, and she becomes immune to physical attacks.
When using Skill 2, she briefly gains crowd control immunity, removing all slow effects from herself and enhancing her next Basic Attack within 5s to trigger the Blessing of the Dryads.
Passive: She increases her Attack Speed by 12.5%.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Protecting Winds

skill3.description:
Consort Yu gains crowd control immunity and jumps on the target enemy, stunning them for 0.5s and slowing them immensely for 2s.
She then flips backward to her original location while shooting 1 bolt at the same enemy. The bolt deals 340 (340 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage. Upon landing, she gains 20% Attack Speed for 4s.
When her Attack Speed is increased by 0%/40%/80%/120%/160%/200%, she shoots 1/2/3/4/5/6 bolt(s). The second bolt that hits the same target deals 60% damage, while subsequent bolts deal 20% damage.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Vaulting Shot

strategy.earlyGame: Treat Consort Yu's early game as a waiting room until attack speed items come online. Her charged shots fire faster the more attack speed she has, so with a bare inventory the wind-up is clumsy and forced poke just bleeds HP and mana. Focus on clean last-hits, and only fight back with Skill 2 when the enemy physical marksman starts a trade — for a short window she takes no physical damage at all, turning their confident all-in into a total whiff. At the four-minute Tyrant, simply follow your team's call; you have nothing to force there yet.
strategy.midGame: From six or seven minutes, one finished attack speed item turns her into a different hero. The charge visibly speeds up, and the Ultimate's volley count grows with attack speed too, so every item purchase translates directly into damage you can feel. Against a physical lane opponent, fight face-to-face around Skill 2 and shove them off the tower. When the enemy mage shows up instead, the immunity means nothing — take your positioning a full step deeper. At objective fights, the iron rule is to hold Skill 2 until the actual engage.
strategy.lateGame: After ten minutes, decide in advance whose skill your Skill 2 is answering — plan it before the fight, not during. If the enemy carry is physical, canceling their main burst with one well-timed immunity breaks the entire teamfight math. During Shadow Tyrant standoffs, charge your shot from the very back row and commit to punishing anyone who backs off too slowly. The Ultimate returns you to your starting position after the pounce, so even a deep catch has a guaranteed ride home. Magic burst is the one thing you can't answer, though — never give the enemy mage a clean angle on you.
strategy.teamfight: Consort Yu stands in teamfights holding a few seconds that erase physical damage entirely. The highlight play is timing Skill 2 the instant the enemy's physical assassin or marksman commits, then beating them down with the empowered basic attack while their damage does nothing. With the Passive's follow-up shots and slow layered on, you can kite them to death from there. Hold the Ultimate until the enemy's plan shows itself, then use the stun to set up your team's focus fire. Charged shots root you briefly, so pick windows when enemy CC is pointed somewhere else.

combos.title: Physical Immunity Counter
combos.sequence: (On enemy physical attack) Skill 2 → Empowered Basic Attack → Basic Attack
combos.description: Trigger it against the enemy marksman's confident trade or a physical assassin's dive, and their biggest hit simply doesn't happen — then swing back. Absorb first, win second: that's Consort Yu's entire plan against physical damage.

combos.title: Pounce Catch
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Skill 1 → Basic Attack
combos.description: Pounce in for the slow and stun, then pour the volley on as you return to your starting position. A stunned target eats the full charged shot guaranteed, letting you run the whole sequence from lockdown to execution by yourself.

strengths: Skill 2's physical immunity dominates physical-heavy lineups
Attack speed uniquely converts into faster charges and bigger volleys
Passive follow-up shots and layered slows make her a natural kiter
Ultimate returns her to her starting spot, keeping catches safe
weaknesses: Immunity blocks physical only — helpless against magic damage
Mistiming Skill 2 leaves her with no self-defense at all
Charged shots are hard to land on mobile targets without practice
Underwhelming damage and skill uptime until attack speed items finish

synergy.reason: Follows up on Zhong Kui's hooks with overwhelming artillery burst to instantly delete enemies.
Can easily follow up on hooked targets with massive burst damage for quick kills.

counters.reason: High sustain and CC resilience allow him to escape Zhong Kui's control and turn the fight around.
Extremely tanky during his ultimate; hooking him can result in your team taking massive damage instead.

passive.description:
Kui detonates an explosion when taking damage that exceeds 10% of his current Health in a single hit, dealing 166 (60 +60% magical attack +3% Health) magical damage to nearby enemies. This effect has a 2s Cooldown.
3s after he's defeated, he explodes, dealing 664 (240 +240% magical attack +12% Health) magical damage to nearby enemies.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Ethereal Outburst

skill1.description: Kui hammers the ground, dealing 320 (320 + 32% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 15% for 1.5s. Enemies next to him take 250% magical damage, are slowed by 15% for 1.5s, and are marked with Into the Void.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Mortals!

skill2.description:
Kui throws his chain hook in the target direction, marking the first enemy hit with Into the Void and pulling them to him, dealing 550 (550 + 60% magical attack) magical damage.
Passive: Defeats and assists grant 1 stack of Void Devour, increasing his Health by 180, for up to 20 stacks.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Join Me

skill3.description:
Kui opens up the portal to the void and devours enemies up to 16 times, dealing a total of 1,920 (1,920 + 288% magical attack) magical damage and continuously stunning targets marked by Into the Void.
He also gains a shield that negates 46 (46 + 1% extra Health) damage with each devour.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Into the Void

strategy.earlyGame: Kui roams as an aggressive support, but the early job isn't landing hooks — it's standing where a hook is possible. Fade into the mid bushes or along the river, and the moment an enemy steps forward, drag them in with Skill 2. One connected hook becomes a first-blood setup for your team, and every kill or assist permanently grows Kui's HP. The punishment for whiffing is severe, so until level 4, only pull targets who aren't hiding behind their minion wave. The four-minute Tyrant spawn is also prime time for an ambush hook on anyone rotating in.
strategy.midGame: Level 4 completes the kill script. Hooked enemies are marked, and against marked targets your Ultimate's multi-hit slow upgrades into a stun — one caught enemy is simply not getting away. Before Tyrant or Overlord, a single hook from outside vision forces the enemy to start the fight a player down. Choose your target well: the enemy marksman or mid laner. Nobody on your team celebrates a hooked tank. Keep stacking kill participation and your HP quietly climbs until you're as durable as a front-liner.
strategy.lateGame: Late game Kui bets entire matches on one hook. During Shadow Tyrant standoffs, lurk in a bush half a step behind your front line and wait for the enemy carry's positioning mistake — patiently, for as long as it takes. When the pull lands, chain your Ultimate and Skill 1 for lockdown and damage while your team collapses on the target. The reverse is just as true: with no mobility skill, getting caught means dying on the spot. The Passive does splash damage around you when you take a massive hit or die, so even your worst moments carry a threat — but play careful, and make the one hook count.
strategy.teamfight: The ideal teamfight starts before the teamfight: one clean pull. Yank a back-liner out of formation with Skill 2 and you begin the fight five against four. Once the brawl starts, stack your Ultimate onto marked enemies for the upgraded stun and grind them down with Skill 1's area damage. Because Kui's effects cluster around his own body, you'll inevitably wade into the enemy's side of the fight — whether you survive that depends on all the HP you've banked. When the hook whiffs, don't linger trying to salvage it; fall back into your lines immediately.

combos.title: Hook Into Guaranteed Lockdown
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Ultimate → Skill 1 → Basic Attack
combos.description: The hook marks its victim, upgrading your Ultimate's slow into a stun. Layer Skill 1's area damage while the lockdown runs, add your team's focus fire, and the one you pulled in almost never walks home.

combos.title: Bush Ambush Hook
combos.sequence: (Wait in a bush) → Skill 2 → Basic Attack → Ultimate
combos.description: A hook thrown from an unseen bush is nearly impossible to react to. During objective standoffs, wait for the enemy carry to drift half a step too far forward. Choosing who to hook is the entire skill ceiling of this hero.

strengths: One hook creates a numbers advantage before the fight even starts
The mark upgrades his Ultimate's slow into a reliable stun
Kills and assists permanently stack HP toward front-liner bulk
Deals damage around him even in death, so he's never a free kill
weaknesses: No mobility skill — once caught, he usually just dies
Whiffing the hook leaves him nearly useless for several seconds
His effects center on his own body, forcing risky positioning
A pull without allied follow-up is just a one-way ticket

synergy.reason: A frontline tank with great sustain, maximizing the value of Yang Yuhuan's continuous healing and damage support.
Mutual heals and movement speed buffs boost the team's overall sustain and mobility, making them highly resilient in extended fights.

counters.reason: Overwhelming mobility allows him to close the gap instantly, bursting Yang Yuhuan down before she can heal her team.
Safely pokes with ultra-long-range snipes from well outside Yang Yuhuan's damage and healing radius.

After using the skill, the next Basic Attack will deal 150 (150 + 20% magical attack) extra magical damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Tragic Beauty

skill2.description: Yuhuan plucks the strings, gaining 50% Movement Speed that diminishes over time. After 1.5s, she deals 275 (275 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to all enemies within a range of 600−800 and stuns them for 0.75s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Mournful Tempo

skill3.description: Yuhuan rises into the air and plays a melody, becoming untargetable while airborne and removing all crowd control effects. When finished playing, she recovers 960 (800 + 120% magical attack + 5% extra Health) Health, restores 50% of this amount to allies within a range of 500, and deals 500 (500 + 75% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Unending Sorrow

skill4.description:
Yuhuan changes the melody to Melody of Peace, in which skills provide area healing.
War: Skills deal 90 (90 + 15% magical attack) extra magical damage to enemy units within a range of 800.
Peace: Skills restore 35 (35 + 6% magical attack) Health to allies, while also restoring (+ 6% extra Health) Health to herself.
skill4.name: Skill 4: Melody of Peace

strategy.earlyGame: Mid lane Yuhuan starts with learning the Passive toggle. Clear waves in the damage stance for the bonus minion damage, and flip to the healing stance the moment you take poke — that one habit alone transforms her lane sustain. Skill 1's notes home in on enemies, and following through with the empowered basic attack refunds a second off all your cooldowns, so the pre-level-4 gameplan is simply notes, empowered hit, repeat. Even when the enemy jungler collapses on you, Skill 2's speed boost and delayed stun turn the gank around — she can push the lane far more confidently than she looks.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, everything hinges on one decision: is the Ultimate for healing, or for dodging? While performing, Yuhuan is untargetable and cleansed of CC, so timing it against enemy burst makes their biggest cooldowns hit air. Wait until you see the enemy assassin's ult animation before you rise — wasting their entire combo never stops feeling great. At Tyrant and Overlord fights, your job is holding the line: patch up chipped teammates with the healing stance and the post-performance area heal. From around eight minutes, your second magic item brings real poke damage online too.
strategy.lateGame: After ten minutes, Yuhuan plays the unkillable back-liner. You don't have the burst to delete anyone, so during Shadow Tyrant standoffs, chip away with the homing notes and answer dives with Skill 2 first, Ultimate second. Simply having the Ultimate available is deterrence — enemy assassins hesitate to jump a target who can vanish mid-combo. When your front line runs low, stabilize them with the healing stance and the area heal, and drag the fight into the long, grinding version that favors you. The only way Yuhuan loses is panicking and stepping forward at the wrong moment.
strategy.teamfight: Your teamfight spot is half a step behind the front line. Once it starts, flip to the damage stance for the bonus area damage and keep cycling Skill 1's notes into empowered basic attacks. When a diver turns onto you, drop Skill 2's soundwave, speed away, and let the stun land 1.5 seconds later as they chase — lockdown over your shoulder. If burst stacks onto you, rise with the Ultimate: the enemy wastes their damage, then eats your area heal on the way down. Leave the kills to your teammates; your job is making the enemy's math stop working, over and over.

combos.title: Note Poke Rotation
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Empowered Basic Attack → (after CD refund) Skill 1
combos.description: After landing the homing notes, always follow through with the empowered basic attack — it shaves a full second off every cooldown and brings the next notes back sooner. This small loop, repeated all lane phase, is where the HP difference comes from.

combos.title: Delayed Stun Reversal
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Skill 1 → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Cast the soundwave the moment someone closes in, open distance with the speed boost, and wait out the stun that triggers 1.5 seconds later. Once it lands, turn and punish with notes and the empowered hit. The stun is delayed, so think of it less as something you aim and more as something you make them chase into.

combos.title: Burst Denial
combos.sequence: (On enemy burst) Ultimate → Skill 2 → Skill 1
combos.description: While performing, you're untargetable and cleansed of CC. Rise into it against the enemy's ult animation and their damage vanishes into nothing while you heal yourself and your team. Just check your landing spot before you come down — that's the one moment they can punish.

strengths: Passive toggle covers damage and healing in a single kit
Ultimate's untargetability and cleanse make enemy burst whiff
Empowered basic attacks refund cooldowns for relentless uptime
Area healing sustains her team through long teamfights
weaknesses: Low burst damage — she rarely finishes kills alone
Skill 2's stun lags 1.5 seconds behind and isn't guaranteed
Thin self-defense against dives while the Ultimate is down
Can't carry alone; her impact depends on allied damage

synergy.reason: Thick shields and strong peel create a safe environment for the squishy Cang to set up traps and output damage.
Abundant CC locks enemies down, helping Cang land her long-range attacks and skills accurately.

counters.reason: Stealth engages and high burst damage will instantly delete her before she can use her mobility to escape.
Strong targeted dive and CC completely shut down Cang's hit-and-run playstyle.

passive.description:
While in the brush, Chano gains 10-20% increased Movement Speed and accumulates Concealment, which reaches its maximum after 1s. When leaving the brush, he consumes Concealment to perform a leap, with the distance increasing based on the amount accumulated.
Entering the brush also enhances his next Basic Attack into a double shot (counts as 1 Basic Attack), with each arrow dealing 175 (70 + 60% physical attack) physical damage. The double shot has a 4s cooldown.
He deals 25% more damage to monsters while in the brush.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Hunting

skill1.description:
Chano leaps into the air, gaining a Movement Speed boost and the ability to traverse terrain. While airborne, his Basic Attack becomes a powerful long-range arrow, dealing 475 (230 + 140% physical attack) physical damage and knocking back enemies (without applying crowd control), while also extending his air time.
Each 1% Attack Speed increases the arrow's damage by 2.
If he doesn't use the enhanced Basic Attack while airborne, he stores one with normal Attack Range for 3s upon landing.
If he uses the enhanced Basic Attack while moving the movement wheel away from the target, he dashes for a short distance in that direction.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Soaring Signal

skill2.description:
Chano throws a wolf spirit trap at the target location, exposing the enemy that triggers it and dealing 380 (380 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage. A wolf spirit is also summoned at the trap's location to attack the enemy that triggered it.
Traps become invisible 2s after deploying. Up to 4 traps can be deployed simultaneously.
The wolf spirits inherit 25% of Chano's base stats and half of his Critical Damage, and each attack slows the target by 5-10% for 1s, for up to 5 stacks.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Lupine Trap

skill3.description:
Chano activates his Leader Stance, summoning (2 + Skill 2 charges) wolf spirits to charge in a designated direction, consuming stored charges of Skill 2 and activating all nearby traps.
He gains the Mounted Archery ability, allowing him to move while attacking and increasing his Movement Speed by 10%, Physical Attack by 50, and Attack Speed by 20% for 8s.
Each Basic Attack activates nearby targetless wolf spirits to join the attack.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Leader Stance

strategy.earlyGame: Chano defaults to the farm lane, but his Passive's 25% bonus monster damage inside bushes makes jungle a well-established alternative. Either way, one rule governs everything: touch a bush before you swing. Entering one empowers your next basic attack into a double shot, and leaving one converts stored stealth value into a jump whose distance scales with how long you lurked. In lane, weave between the river and your own bushes — land the double shot, jump away, repeat — and you'll hold an HP lead through nothing but hit-and-run. Also get in the habit of placing Skill 2 traps at the river entrances before level 4.
strategy.midGame: From six or seven minutes, with your first attack speed item done, trap management becomes the center of your job. Skill 2 holds up to four charges, and each trap is vision, damage, and a wolf-spirit attacker in one package. Seed them around Tyrant, Overlord, and the enemy jungle entrances, and gank detection and gank punishment become the same action. When someone closes in, escape skyward with Skill 1 and shove pursuers back with the powerful arrow's knockback. The recoil trick — inputting away from your target as the arrow fires to slide backward — is worth drilling in the practice room until it's muscle memory.
strategy.lateGame: Late teamfights are decided by the setup, not the fight. Lay two to four traps around the Shadow Tyrant pit, then wait in a bush with full stealth value — that's the ideal opening stance. On engage, detonate everything at once with your Ultimate, send the wolf-spirit pack charging in, and kite backward through the eight seconds of mounted archery. That rolling barrage while sliding away from their front line is Chano's whole kit in one motion. Whatever you do, avoid flat open ground: without bushes, he loses most of his mobility and turns into an ordinary marksman.
strategy.teamfight: Chano's teamfight starts from the side bushes, not the front line. Chip from the outside with stealth jumps and double shots, and when heads turn toward you, take to the air with Skill 1. Slide your landing spot with the recoil movement so nobody can pre-aim your touchdown. Save the Ultimate as a counter to the enemy's dive — the wolf pack plus its stacking slows flips the momentum in one cast. Keep steering enemies toward wherever your traps still sit. Chano's teamfight is half over the moment the battlefield has become his backyard.

combos.title: Bush Hit-and-Run
combos.sequence: (Stealth in a bush) → Empowered Basic Attack (double shot) → Passive Jump
combos.description: Entering a bush empowers your next basic attack into a double shot, and leaving converts stealth value into jump distance. Hit, jump, next bush. This loop is Chano's entire lane phase — from the opponent's seat, it feels like being bled dry by someone they can never touch.

combos.title: Full Trap Detonation
combos.sequence: Skill 2 ×2-4 (pre-placed) → Ultimate → Basic Attack (mounted archery)
combos.description: Detonate your planted traps with the Ultimate, sending a wolf spirit charging in for every stack spent, while you kite backward firing on the move. Enemies buried under the stacked wolf slows can neither catch you nor get away.

combos.title: Aerial Snipe Escape
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Aerial Basic Attack → Recoil Movement (input away)
combos.description: When cornered, leap skyward, knock pursuers back with the powerful arrow, and slide toward your input direction to displace your landing spot. The leap clears terrain too, so combined with a wall hop it shakes off nearly any chase.

strengths: Ultimate's mounted archery keeps damage flowing on the move
Bush stealth jumps and double shots enable pure hit-and-run
Four traps handle vision, zoning, and ambush punishment at once
Bonus monster damage in bushes makes jungle a genuine option
weaknesses: Lacks burst, so low targets often escape before they die
Loses most of his mobility on open ground without bushes
Damage leans on basic attacks and wolves, weak to attack speed debuffs
High mechanical demands — stealth and recoil tricks take practice

synergy.reason: Easy to follow up on burst damage, ensuring targets are pushed past the kill threshold.
Pokes and wears down enemies in teamfights, setting up perfect kill opportunities for dives.

counters.reason: High mobility and CC allow her to kite effectively, making it extremely difficult to land skills on her.
Overwhelming mobility allows her to dominate close-quarters combat and completely outplay you.

Heaven-Earth Form: Yang Jian gains Resistance (up to 60-90%, scaling with Ultimate level) when his Basic Attacks and skills deal damage. Upon reaching max Resistance, he enters Heaven-Earth Form, gaining crowd control immunity. Attacking a hero in this state knocks back nearby enemies, enhances his skills and Attack Range, and grants 600 Max Health.
Heavenly Eye: Hits with his skills grant 1 stack of Energy (up to 3 stacks). When enemies move away from Yang Jian, the Heavenly Eye fires light beams, dealing 80 (+25% extra physical attack) physical damage and recovering 60 (+1% extra Health) (halved against non-hero units).
Outside Heaven-Earth Form, Yang Jian's Resistance is capped at 25%.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Mind Games

While the mark is active, he can use the skill again to dash to the enemy, dealing 300 (300 + 90% extra physical attack) physical damage, as well as additional physical damage equal to 15% of the target's lost Health.
If the skill misses, Heaven Hound will remain at the endpoint, searching for targets. When Yang Jian approaches, Heaven Hound returns to its master, reducing this skill's remaining cooldown by 25%-50%.
If an enemy dies while marked, this skill's cooldown is reset.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Unleash the Hound

skill2.description:
Yang Jian sweeps with his spear, dealing 350 (350 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in range, slowing them by 15% for (2s) and stunning them for (1/2s, doubled if the target's remaining Health percentage is higher than Yang Jian's).
After hitting an enemy with this skill, Yang Jian's Basic Attacks deal an additional 125 (125 + 36% extra physical attack) true damage (lasts 5s).
skill2.name: Skill 2: Vain Disillusionment

skill3.description:
Yang Jian uses Heavenly Eye to fire 3 light beams, dealing 340 (340 + 110% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in their path, while recovering 300 (300 + 4.5% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).
If multiple light beams hit the same target, subsequent light beams deal only 30% damage and recover 50% Health.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Sight of Origin

strategy.earlyGame: Yang Jian wants to fight in the Clash Lane before level 4, not after. Skill 2's stun doubles in length when the target's HP percentage is higher than yours, so trading back after eating some damage is where he shines — never fear an even exchange. If a bush looks suspicious, send in Skill 1's War Hound first; five seconds of vision on whatever it touches exposes any ambush before it springs. Once the Ultimate arrives at level 4, its built-in healing transforms your staying power, so start forcing 1v1s and take the lane by the throat.
strategy.midGame: When the Tyrant spawns at 4:00, shove your wave before rotating. Landing Skill 1 pre-fight applies the mark and vision, and the recast dash adds missing-HP damage that finishes chases. Against enemy heroes, the Passive shifts into its empowered mode with bonus HP and resistances, which makes small skirmishes Yang Jian's home turf. Around 7-8 minutes, with one core item done, run a loop: pick a 1v1 on the side, and when two enemies collapse, use the hound's vision to back off clean. That XP gap compounds fast.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, baiting enemies out in a side lane beats standing in the middle of every 5v5. Your 1v1 stays strong even at even items, and when you cannot secure the kill, the Ultimate's healing still lets you hold ground. Always shove a wave before Shadow Tyrant or Overlord starts — every defender the enemy sends is a body missing from the objective fight. Since your resistances stack into super armor, entering brawls two or three seconds late means less CC (stuns and other lockdown) aimed your way and a much longer rampage.
strategy.teamfight: Yang Jian's teamfight is a flank job: circle the edge and delete enemies who are already chipped. The five-second true-damage window after Skill 2 connects is the core of your output, so squeeze in every basic attack you can while the stun holds. The Ultimate's lasers heal more when they strike multiple enemies — the moment you get surrounded is exactly when to fire. One habit worth stealing: hold the Skill 1 recast until the enemy burns their blink, and the dash almost never whiffs. As long as the mark is up, you can always re-chase.

combos.title: War Hound Run-Down
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 1 Recast → Skill 2 → Basic Attack
combos.description: Mark the target and grab vision with the hound, dash in with the recast, then stack true-damage basic attacks during the Skill 2 stun. This is Yang Jian's bread-and-butter line of attack.

combos.title: Underdog Reversal
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Basic Attack → Ultimate
combos.description: The stun lasts twice as long against enemies healthier than you, so punch back while the lasers heal you up. Yang Jian's fight truly starts after he takes damage.

combos.title: Kite-Back Turnaround
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Skill 1 → Skill 1 Recast
combos.description: Heal up with the lasers while creating space, then punish overextended chasers with a hound-into-dash re-engage for the reverse kill.

strengths: Skill 2's stun doubles when he is lower on HP, making counter-trades brutal
Passive resistances stack into super armor, winning long brawls
Ultimate and Passive healing let him hold ground through item deficits
War Hound's vision exposes bush ambushes while he engages
weaknesses: Missing Skill 1 removes his only gap closer until the cooldown returns
Anti-heal items gut the sustain his whole game plan leans on
Fishing for the doubled stun by staying low on HP is a risky gamble
Long-range poke that never lets him close distance leaves him without a play

synergy.reason: Maintains a solid frontline, creating a safe environment to poke from a distance.
Strong CC locks enemies down, making it much easier to land long-range skill combos.

counters.reason: High mobility allows him to bypass walls and frontlines to dive the backline instantly.
Stealth engages make it easy to assassinate Nuwa due to her lack of escape options.

passive.description: Nuwa gains 10-20% vision, Basic Attack range, and skill range (increases with hero level).
passive.name: Passive Skill: Divine Consciousness

skill1.description:
Nuwa unleashes energy in the target direction, dealing 225 (225 + 42% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and knocking them back. After hitting an enemy, the energy gradually stops and expands in a cross shape, forming a matrix. This deals 225 (225 + 42% magical attack) magical damage to enemies hit.
The cross deals an extra 50% damage to enemies at its center, and sets off explosions if it touches matrices.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Divine Glow - Creation

skill2.description:
Nuwa creates a matrix that only she can traverse and enemy heroes cannot pass through. Each matrix lasts 3.5s.
Whenever a matrix is hit by one of Nuwa's other skills, it sets off an explosion that deals 210 (210 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
When matrices fuse, they deal 180 (180 + 35% magical attack) magical damage (+50% extra damage in the center) on collision and knock back enemies for 0.5s. Collisions gain up to 30% extra range based on the initial distance between matrices. Up to 3 matrices can be stocked. When multiple matrices explode simultaneously, they only deal damage to the same target once.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Divine Glow - Coalescence

skill3.description: Nuwa teleports to the target location while gaining 30% Movement Speed and a shield that negates 600 (600 + 9% extra Health) damage for 2s. She also deals 300 (300 + 57% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within the target area and slows them by 25-50% for 0.5s. Enemies take less damage the farther away they are from her, down to 50% of the initial damage.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Divine Glow - Emergence

skill4.description: Nuwa releases pure energy, dealing 600 (600 + 115% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path. The pure energy will set off an explosion if it touches a matrix.
skill4.name: Skill 4: Divine Glow - Annihilation

strategy.earlyGame: Nuwa's Passive extends her basic attack and skill cast range, so from level 1 she farms mid from a step farther out than her opponent can reach. There is no reason to push up — thread Skill 1 through the spot where the enemy overlaps their minions and let the chip damage add up. Skill 2's walls are insurance before they are offense: block the gank path your jungler is not watching and any dive loses a full beat. Sit on your Ultimate. A Nuwa without it is a free kill, so keep it pocketed until the gank threat is genuinely gone.
strategy.midGame: The Tyrant spawn at 4:00 begins Nuwa's setup game. Lay two Skill 2 walls in the narrow paths leading to the pit, then thread Skill 1 into anyone touching them — the chain explosions plus the cross's bonus damage carve chunks out of enemies before the fight even starts. Since the matrix blocks only enemy heroes, smart placement seals both their retreat and their reinforcement route. After your first core item, her damage takes a real jump, so cycle between shoving mid and spending time on wall placement until the objective area belongs to you.
strategy.lateGame: Once Shadow Tyrant and Overlord are on the line after 10 minutes, a single wall rewrites the geometry of a fight. Seal the pit entrance and the enemy eats a detour while your team pokes them apart. Ideally you bank all three Skill 2 charges before anything starts. Stay at the absolute back, and treat your Ultimate as an anti-assassin escape button, never an engage tool — warp out, drop one more wall behind you, and the chase simply dies. A prepared Nuwa is oppressive; an unprepared one is a minion with a health bar.
strategy.teamfight: Nuwa's job starts ten seconds before the fight does. Read the enemy's approach path, pre-lay walls, and thread Skill 1 into the densest clump for chain explosions. Once the brawl is live, wall placement is the judgment call that defines her: cut off a fleeing enemy at the nose, or drop one between their assassin and your carry as a screen. The most painful mistake in practice is walling off your own team's retreat — when in doubt, bias the placement toward the enemy side. Keep the Ultimate's warp and shield in reserve as your final card.

combos.title: Matrix Chain Detonation

combos.sequence: Ultimate → Skill 2 → Skill 1
combos.description: Warp out with the shield and slow, seal the chase route with a wall, then turn Skill 1 back onto the stalled diver. Nuwa's full self-defense package in one motion.

Provides strong shields and CC to hold the frontline during messy post-dive teamfights.

Continuous damage and sustain allow her to completely neutralize close-range dive attempts.

strategy.earlyGame: Nezha's first four levels are about patience. Do not force wins in the Clash Lane — tag enemies with Skill 1, let the five-second true-damage burn and its healing reduction do the grinding, and settle for short trades. Every skill hit on an enemy hero banks a true-damage shield, so lots of brief touches beat one long slugfest. Skill 2 rolls you behind a target for free hits, but remember it locks out on that same target for three seconds and burns your escape route. Priority number one is simple: reach level 4 without dying.
strategy.midGame: The moment you learn the Ultimate, Nezha's game begins. Spot a low-HP or isolated backliner on the minimap and fly — the landing knockback plus an ally collapsing from the other side is the standard execution. For four seconds after landing you take 10% less damage and gain 20% resistances, so you can commit harder than it looks. During the 4:00 Tyrant standoff, pressuring the opposite side of the map without showing yourself forces the enemy to split bodies. Build the habit of glancing at the minimap for follow-up before every flight; it erases most of this hero's deaths.
strategy.lateGame: After 15 minutes Nezha is the teamfight start button — but the Ultimate is a one-way ticket, so only fly onto targets your team can reach within five seconds. The dream window is the enemy marksman stepping forward: dive, knock them back, then slap Skill 1's healing reduction on so their support cannot patch them up in time. During Shadow Tyrant or Overlord standoffs, simply hovering with the Ultimate available warps the enemy backline's positioning. The difference between good and great Nezhas is saving it for the two or three moments per game that actually decide something.
strategy.teamfight: Nezha flies first or flies last — nothing in between. If your team has another initiator, the late dive is safer: wait for the enemy CC (stuns and other lockdown) to be spent, then drop on whoever is left carrying. After landing, stack Skill 1's burn to three, keep rolling behind fleeing targets with Skill 2, and let the true damage cook. Your shield rebuilds as long as skills keep connecting, which makes the center of the brawl the safest place you can stand. What you cannot beat is a spread formation kiting you in the open, so push for fights in tight terrain.

strategy.earlyGame: Gan & Mo outrange the entire mid lane from level 1. Everything about the duo's damage flows from crossing Skill 2's short-range blades with the Ultimate's long-range blades at a single point, detonating the sword qi bonus on impact — so spend the first waves calibrating that intersection distance on stationary minions. Blade casts run on shared charges that only refill every five to six seconds, which means never stepping forward right after emptying them. If someone jumps you, Skill 1's knockback-and-hop-back buys exactly one reset. That is the only insurance policy you own; price it accordingly.
strategy.midGame: From about 7-8 minutes, with your first core item finished, one clean intersection removes close to half of an enemy mage's HP. Before the 4:00 Tyrant or the 10:00 Shadow Tyrant, simply raining blades from maximum range onto anyone entering the pit forces the enemy to open the fight pre-chipped — that is Gan & Mo's brand of pressure. Skill 1 banks bonus magic attack on every kill and assist, so involvement snowballs the damage curve on its own. Skip the roams. Push mid, step back, carve sword qi into whoever contests, repeat.
strategy.lateGame: With Skill 1 grown to 15-20 stacks, a single intersection deletes a marksman outright — which is precisely why the enemy will spend everything to reach you. Two non-negotiables: stand behind every teammate, and never fight with a wall at your back. Do not hunt with Skill 1 either; hold it as the reaction card you play the instant someone commits to the jump. During Overlord fights, dropping blades from outside the pit's perimeter slowly bends the enemy formation out of shape until someone makes the mistake you have been waiting for.
strategy.teamfight: Gan & Mo never need to walk forward in a teamfight. From the deepest backline, punish any enemy frontliner who stops moving by crossing the short and long blades on their feet — that alone is a full shift's work. Priority targets: pre-fight clumps and anyone locked down by your team's CC. Chasing sprinting targets with blades is wasted ammunition. Skill 1's 150 magic defense shred also boosts your allied mage, so land it on the focus target first. Empty the charges, take one step back, wait for the refill. Guard that rhythm and you survive.

strategy.earlyGame: Athena's laning is a level-2 trade loop: jump in with Skill 2, land the empowered basic attack, dash out with Skill 1 — and because a connected Skill 1 refunds Skill 2's cooldown, you immediately get another round trip. Run that cycle and only your opponent's health bar moves. The empowered hit adds 6% of the target's missing HP, so the more chipped they are, the harder it lands. Level 4 unlocks the full all-in: two shields with CC immunity layered on top. The only real way to throw it is whiffing, so pick your jump target with care.
strategy.midGame: Around 7-8 minutes, one core item in, Athena's mobility starts cashing checks. Shove your side wave, then use Skill 2's leap to cut through the river and hit the 4:00 Tyrant or any skirmish from the flank. Before diving, count the enemy's key lockdown skills — if one is still up, time Skill 1's one second of CC immunity to slide through it and reach the backline safely. Do not rush the Ultimate out either. Its retaliation grows every time enemies strike the braced shield, so the moment they focus you is the moment it starts printing damage.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Athena is a time bomb strapped to the enemy backline. As long as Skill 1 and the Ultimate keep connecting, Skill 2 keeps refreshing, and no amount of running rescues a marksman you have decided to keep. Do not overlook the Passive: on death she respawns at the nearest allied tower with a knock-up burst, so in defensive scenarios even a death converts into a play. That insurance barely functions when you are the one diving deep, so measure your entry. At Shadow Tyrant, slide in from behind after both sides have traded skills — that is where she cuts deepest.
strategy.teamfight: Decide one thing before every teamfight: whose face are you living in. Athena's damage is stacked empowered basics, so swapping targets mid-fight means killing no one. The ideal is single-minded pursuit of the enemy marksman. Slip the first lockdown with Skill 1's CC immunity, raise the Ultimate against their counterattack so every hit feeds the retaliation, then dump it back on them. One detail everyone forgets in practice: you can walk while the shield is braced. Drifting toward your escape route during those seconds is often the difference between a reset and a respawn.

combos.title: Reset Round Trip

combos.description: Eat the enemy's counterattack on the braced shield to fatten the retaliation, then keep leaping through resets until the target is gone. Sync the CC-immunity windows to their lockdown and the combo never stalls.

strengths: Skill 1 and Ultimate hits refund Skill 2, so her mobility never runs dry

weaknesses: A whiffed Skill 1 or Ultimate stalls the reset engine mid-combo
No burst, so disciplined enemies can recover before she finishes them
Respawn is fixed to the nearest allied tower — weak while sieging
Reset bookkeeping is expert-level; sloppy play accomplishes nothing
