strategy.earlyGame: Cai Yan's assigned seat is directly beside her marksman from minute zero. The early job is not damage — it is making sure your partner cannot die. When the enemy commits, answer with Skill 2's ricochet stun; if they are tangled up with their minion wave, the bounces chain-stun and the trade collapses in your favor. After every exchange, walk alongside with Skill 1 running and the chip damage simply refunds itself, letting your partner keep farming instead of recalling. Until the Ultimate arrives at level 4, check bushes, hold position, and refuse to be the one caught forward.
strategy.midGame: Cai Yan's presence grows from the 4:00 Tyrant onward. While your team burns the boss, the flank is the most dangerous moment on the map — meet whoever walks in with Skill 2, and the ricochet stuns stall the contest cold. Her Ultimate spends five seconds auto-targeting the lowest-HP ally in range with healing and a defense buff, so rather than panic-casting mid-brawl, open it just before the enemy's burst lands. Between the Passive's speed surge on taking damage and her self-heal, she is far harder to catch than the health bar suggests.
strategy.lateGame: Late fights become a staring contest over Cai Yan's Ultimate — the enemy wants it forced early, you want it perfectly timed. Absent anti-heal, its five seconds of rolling heals and defense buffs absorb an entire round of enemy focus. Stand diagonally behind your carry, and cast it where only the ally you intend to save sits inside the ring; that placement is the entire skill expression of this hero, because a frontliner soaking the heal is a wasted Ultimate. Fill your slots with team utility items and forget your own scoreline entirely.
strategy.teamfight: Cai Yan's teamfight reduces to two real decisions: spend Skill 2 on the enemy's entrance or on their retreat, and choose whose feet the Ultimate covers. The ricochet multiplies against clustered enemies, so its highest value is meeting the opening dive; if it misses, drop back and wait out the cooldown. A teamfight where the healer dies first is close to an automatic loss — never surrender the backmost position, no matter how won the fight looks. And triage coldly: the ally who can still fight outranks the ally who is already doomed.

combos.title: Anti-Dive Answer
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Ultimate → Skill 1
combos.description: Catch the dive with ricochet stuns, stand the focused ally back up with the Ultimate's heavy healing and defense buff, then pull everyone out together under Skill 1's speed and rolling heals.

combos.title: Retreat Escort
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2
combos.description: Use the 40% movement speed to catch up to retreating allies while spreading heals, and leave a ricochet stun as a parting gift. Overeager chasers regularly end up frozen in a clump.

strengths: Ultimate auto-locks the lowest-HP ally with heavy healing and defenses
Ricochet stuns multiply against clumped divers
Passive speed burst and self-heal make her deceptively hard to catch
A simple kit that delivers steady value in every single game
weaknesses: Near-zero damage of her own; she cannot create a win condition alone
Anti-heal items cut her entire reason for existing in half
Ricochet targets are uncontrollable; pinning one specific enemy is hard
Caught by CC first, she dies before a single heal goes out

synergy.reason: Can perfectly chain massive burst damage while enemies are locked down by your ultimate.
Creates engage opportunities for your ultimate by grouping enemies and providing movement speed.

counters.reason: Pokes safely from outside your ultimate's range, whittling down your health before you can close the gap.
High-damage artillery skills from long range will completely prevent you from engaging.

passive.description:
Whenever a dark orb of Donghuang's hits an enemy, it deals 100 (100 + 50% magical attack) magical damage, plus extra magical damage equal to 3% of the target's Health. At the same time, he recovers 162 (96 + 40% magical attack + 2% Health) Health.
When a dark orb hits a non-hero unit, he recovers 1% Health.
He can have up to 3 dark orbs orbiting him simultaneously.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Soul Sacrifice

skill1.description:
Releases a burst of power, dealing 300 (300 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and creating a dark orb that orbits around him. Can have up to 3 dark orbs orbiting simultaneously.
When this skill hits an enemy, its Cooldown and Mana cost are reduced by 50%. If there are already 3 dark orbs present, restores 150 (150 + 60% magical attack) Health instead.
The number of dark orbs will influence the strength of Dark Impact.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Eclipse

skill2.description:
Donghuang consumes all of his dark orbs (there must be at least one) to barrage the target location, with each orb targeting a further area than the last. Orbs deal 500 (500 + 60% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range. When he uses this skill, he gains 30% Movement Speed for 1s. He gains 10% Movement Speed for every extra dark orb consumed.
The first orb slows enemies within range by 30% for 1s, the second slows enemies within range immensely for 1s, and the third will stun enemies within range for 1s.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Dark Impact

skill3.description:
Donghuang suppresses an enemy hero for 2s. While the enemy is suppressed by him, both share all damage taken.
He instantly gains 3 dark orbs when his Ultimate is used. During suppression, the orbs orbit 25% faster. Every 50 Magical Attack makes them orbit 5% faster, to a max of 100%.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Forsaken Contract

strategy.earlyGame: Play Donghuang's roam aggressively from the opening seconds. Spin up three dark orbs with Skill 1 and walk into the enemy jungle alongside your own jungler — every orb touch deals percent max-HP magic damage and heals you, so even-numbers shoving matches in tight bushes are fights you simply do not lose. Contest every river crab to stunt the enemy jungler's curve. Your first real kill window opens the moment the Ultimate arrives at level 4, and here is the quiet truth: enemies still holding Flash are usually the careless ones.
strategy.midGame: The midgame runs through the 4:00 Tyrant and Overlord control afterward. Camp the bushes around the pit early, flush corridors with Skill 2 for damage and slows, and fish for the third orb's stun. The headline play is Flash into the Ultimate: two seconds of suppression that nothing interrupts, with the damage share letting your team pour burst into their star while they carry part of the bill. Track your own Flash cooldown obsessively — whether that card exists changes how far the enemy backline dares to walk.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Donghuang is a walking arrest warrant with the enemy carry's name on it. Just pacing the frontline with the Ultimate available forces their marksman to hang at maximum range, halving their output before anything happens. Spend the suppression exclusively on marksmen and assassins — never tanks, because the damage-share math simply does not produce a trade against beefy targets. The counter-suppress is just as strong: when an assassin lands on your backline, clamp them, press your orbs into their face, and grind them down.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights Donghuang either authors the opening or erases the enemy's. Attacking, Flash plus the Ultimate binds their centerpiece for two seconds while your team's burst flows in. Defending, catch divers with orbs and Skill 2's stun. The critical caveat: you are rooted during your own suppression, so casting it in the middle of their team is a signed confession — the beating starts the instant the lock ends. Suppress inside your team's range, no exceptions. And since activating the Ultimate instantly refunds three orbs, your grind damage never stops ticking while you hold them.

combos.title: Flash Suppression
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Flash → Ultimate → Skill 1
combos.description: Stitch their feet with the third orb's stun, Flash the gap, and lock in two seconds of suppression. The three refunded orbs keep grinding through the hold while your team finishes the job.

combos.title: Point-Blank Grind
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Stay in Contact → Skill 2 at Point-Blank Range
combos.description: Hug the target with three orbs spinning, letting percent damage and self-healing win the slugfest. At point-blank range all three orbs of Skill 2 connect easily, flowing naturally into the closing stun.

strengths: Suppression shares damage, trading his life for their fed carry
Orb percent damage and self-healing dominate close-range brawls
Flash plus the Ultimate is a simple, nearly unmissable pick tool
A tank who moonlights as an early-game invade threat
weaknesses: Long-range poke comps never let his orbs touch anyone
He is rooted during suppression; casting beyond ally range is fatal
Skill 2's trajectory is honest and demands predictive casting
No mobility skill, so his Flash timer quietly decides fights

synergy.reason: Perfectly follows up your group pull with devastating AoE burst damage.
Massive AoE burst damage perfectly synergizes with your pull and lockdown combo.

counters.reason: Uses i-frames to dodge your pull and counters with heavy burst damage.
Strong long-range CC stops your engage attempts dead in their tracks before you can get close.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: The Laws of Nature
passive.description:
After Guiguzi leaves the enemy's field of vision for 3s, his next Basic Attack will be enhanced, dealing 300 (300 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 25%−50% (increases with level) for 1.5s.
If he is not in the enemy's field of vision when using the enhanced Basic Attack, this skill's cooldown will be increased to 10s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: The Laws of Nature

skill1.description:
Guiguzi covers himself in spriteflies that camouflage him from enemy sight for 4s. While camouflaged, he gains 40% Movement Speed and deals 450 (450 + 60% magical attack) magical damage to each enemy he touches, while reducing their [icon] and [icon] by 25% for 4s. This effect can only be triggered once on each enemy.
The camouflage disappears when he deals damage to enemies in any other way.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Prophecy - Hidden Hand

skill2.description: Guiguzi summons a large number of spriteflies that surround him, dealing 100 (100 + 15% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s for 2s to enemies within range, after which he pulls them in and stuns them for 1s, dealing 400 (400 + 60% magical attack) magical damage. If an enemy hero is hit, Guiguzi and teammates within range gain a shield that negates 600 (600 + 120% magical attack) damage.
skill2.name: Skill 2: The Animist

skill3.description:
Guiguzi orders spriteflies to cover himself and teammates within a range of 1,500, camouflaging everyone after 1s. The camouflage lasts for 4s, during which he and his teammates gain 30% Movement Speed and vision of the nearest enemy hero.
While camouflaged, using Basic Attacks, skills, or inflicting debuffs on enemies will immediately remove it.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Prophecy - Out of Sight

strategy.earlyGame: Guiguzi should have walked half the map before his first recall — that is the correct pace. Touch the mid wave for a moment, then slide toward a side lane under Skill 1's camouflage and 40% movement speed. Ghost through the enemy laner's back, and merely brushing them carves 25% off both defenses; your laner collapsing onto that debuff turns into a kill from thin air. One rule above all: attacking anything breaks the camouflage. The touch already did the work, so keep your hands to yourself.
strategy.midGame: Guiguzi's busiest window is the thirty seconds before each Tyrant spawn. Tuck into the pit-side bush with your jungler, and anyone who wanders up eats Skill 2's pull-and-stun — objective and numbers advantage in one motion. The Ultimate's team-wide camouflage can hand your side the opening of an entire teamfight, but spending it casually on travel leaves nothing for the moment that matters; commit it to engages, full stop. The free vision of the nearest enemy hero it grants sharpens every ambush you set.
strategy.lateGame: In the late game a single engage decides everything, which makes Guiguzi's stealth the trump card of trump cards. The script: cloak all five with the Ultimate, spread across the objective approach, and land Skill 2's pull on the enemy's structural piece — usually the carry. But understand that your durability is paper against late-game damage, and the two-second channel can be burned through, shield and all. Always start the play from inside your team's effective range. Solo hero-ball adventures are this hero's number one loss condition.
strategy.teamfight: The ideal sequence never changes: vanish the team with the Ultimate, thread Skill 1 through the enemy line to stamp the 25% defense shred on priority targets, then channel Skill 2 in the thick of their formation. Two seconds later the pull and stun compress them into one tidy package for your team's AoE. The shield on hero contact absorbs some of the opening fire, but the channel is your single point of failure — start it while their attention is fixed on your frontline, in that stolen instant when nobody is looking at you.

combos.title: Cloaked Team Strike
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Skill 1 → Skill 2
combos.description: Close the distance with the whole team invisible, stamp the defense shred on the way through, and channel in the clump. Two seconds later the pull-stun lines up your team's full burst — the standard winning opener.

combos.title: Bush Pick
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Creep in quietly from an ambush and vacuum the target in. The empowered basic's slow, charged by three seconds unseen, holds them in place until your team arrives.

strengths: Team-wide camouflage lets him dictate exactly when fights begin
Pull-stun engage plus ally shields makes his openings devastating
Skill 1's 25% dual-defense shred raises the whole team's damage
Stealth and speed give him unmatched roaming range for ambushes
weaknesses: Paper durability — a failed engage usually costs him his life
Skill 2's two-second channel whiffs badly against anyone who reads it
His openings evaporate if teammates do not follow up instantly
Close to zero solo damage or kill threat

synergy.reason: Hard CC guarantees lockdown on enemies, allowing Kongming to safely land his combo and ultimate.

counters.reason: Can invade early when mobility is low to apply pressure and disrupt Kongming's farm.
Can survive the burst damage and stick tightly to shut down Kongming's mobility.

passive.description:
Kongming gains 1 mark for 10s every time his active skills hit an enemy, for up to 5 stacks. Upon reaching max stacks, he summons 5 prisms, which circle around him for 10s and attack the nearest enemy unit, dealing 135 (135 +25% magical attack) magical damage.
Prisms prioritize enemy heroes. They deal 40% less damage to monsters and 40% extra damage to minions.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Time for Tactics

skill1.description:
Kongming fires 3 prisms in the target direction, each dealing 450 (450 + 70% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path. When multiple prisms hit the same enemy, subsequent hits only deal 20% damage.
Each prism triggers 1 Strategic Mark. He stocks Arcane Assault every 7.5s, for up to 2 charges.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Arcane Assault

skill2.description:
Kongming blinks in the target direction, creating magic fields at the start and the end of the dash that each deal 350 (350 + 52% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies. When an enemy takes damage twice from this skill within 5s, they are inflicted with extreme slow. This effect diminishes over 3s.
When an enemy takes damage from multiple fields at the same time, the second magic field only deals 50% damage.
He stocks 1 charge of this skill every 7.5s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), for up to 2 charges.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Time Shift

skill3.description:
Kongming targets an enemy and starts channeling a Spirit Bomb, which deals 450 (450 + 55% magical attack) magical damage. Non-hero enemy units that are targeted or in the Spirit Bomb's path will take extra damage and be launched for 0.5s. Enemies take 2% extra damage from Spirit Bombs for every 1% Health lost.
When a Spirit Bomb hits and defeats an enemy hero, Kongming gains a full stack of marks, and this skill's Cooldown is reduced by 80%.
If the targeted enemy hero is defeated while the Spirit Bomb is being channeled, the Cooldown of this skill will still be reduced by 80%.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Winning Strategy

strategy.earlyGame: How the midgame treats Kongming is decided by how cleanly he plays before level 4. Fan Skill 1 through waves to farm seal stacks, keep the five-stack orbs orbiting, and take short trades while they hover — the orbs fly at the nearest enemy automatically, so your opponent stepping up for a last hit is your cue to chip them. Skill 2 carries two charges, but the arithmetic is fixed: spend one aggressively, and the other is your ticket home, always. Finish this phase without dying once and you have already passed.
strategy.midGame: Kongming's show starts when the Ultimate comes online. Hunt anything below half HP — the missile scales with missing health, so a chipped target eats far more than the tooltip suggests. Land the kill and 80% of the cooldown refunds with seals instantly maxed, and the hunt loops straight into the next victim. Shove mid, show up to the 4:00 Tyrant, and fan Skill 1 from the perimeter to pre-chip the fight. One discipline: while the enemy still holds two or more lockdown skills, forcing entries with Skill 2 stays in the pocket.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Kongming demands almost unreasonable patience. Enemies walk in tight packs with magic defense stacked, and a casual entry is nothing but food for their lockdown. So orbit the fight, cycle Skill 1 to keep the seals alive, and watch the blinks and CC leave their hands. The instant someone's HP crosses the execute line, cut an angle with Skill 2 and let the Ultimate fly. After the first kill, resets start flowing with a full orbit of orbs — flip from statue to storm and keep pressing. That toggle between stillness and violence is the entire hero.
strategy.teamfight: Kongming starts every teamfight outside its walls. Sprinkle Skill 1 to hold the seals, let the orbs freelance in the frontline scrum, and study which target is bleeding. The Ultimate gets blocked by whoever stands in between, so create diagonal firing lines with Skill 2 or Flash before releasing. A detail most players miss: even if an ally finishes the target during your charge-up, the 80% refund still triggers — never hesitate over kill-secure anxiety. The moment after firing is your most defenseless; confirm the exit before you ever commit.

combos.title: Execute Reset
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 to Engage → Skill 1 → Ultimate
combos.description: Farm seals with the first fan, blink for range and angle, land the second fan, then execute the chipped target. The kill refunds the cooldown and the seals, and the next victim is already in the crosshairs.

combos.title: Kiting Poke
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 to Retreat → Passive Orb Follow-Up
combos.description: Land all three orbs point-blank, hop to safety, and let the passive orbs punish anyone who chases. The harder they run at you, the more it hurts — classic Kongming spite.

strengths: Kills refund 80% of the Ultimate's cooldown and instantly max his seals
Two blink charges create angles and escapes on demand
Auto-attacking orbs apply constant pressure while he stays out of reach
Missing-HP scaling on the Ultimate erases anything left low
weaknesses: The Ultimate is body-blocked by enemies standing in the way
Paper-thin the moment both blink charges are spent
Ordinary damage whenever his seal stacks lapse
Misjudge the execute line and he becomes a decoration

synergy.reason: Combines strong basic attacks and CC to fully capitalize on Da Qiao's rapid engages and disengages.
Teleporting allies in to follow up on Mulan's ambushes gives a huge advantage in teamfights.

counters.reason: Exceptional mobility allows him to dive the backline and burst Da Qiao down before she can support her team.
High disengage capabilities make it easy to negate Da Qiao's ultimate summons.

passive.description:
Da Qiao boosts her own Movement Speed by 30.
When the koi in Leaping Koi Tide and Severing Surge leaps past another skill's tide, it triggers a tide explosion, dealing 140 (140 + 25% magical attack) magical damage and slowing enemies by 30% for 1s.
For every 250 Magical Attack, the skill range of Leaping Koi Tide and Severing Surge increases by 50, with a maximum increase of 200.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Law of Infinity

skill1.description: Da Qiao summons a koi that leaps in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and launching them for 0.5s. The koi creates a tide that deals 75 (75 + 12% magical attack) magical damage to enemies every 0.5s for 2.5s. Using skills increases Da Qiao's Movement Speed by 30% for 2.5s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Leaping Koi Tide

skill2.description:
Da Qiao conjures a magic circle for 4s that grants vision. When it closes, she teleports a teammate to the spawn point, removing all debuffs. They can return via the portal at the Crystal.
If no hero teleports, the magic circle leaves behind a mark a teammate can touch to recall.
Using the skill again clears the mark. If no hero has teleported, 50% [icon] is returned. Da Qiao teleports first. No channeling is required to touch the recall mark.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Sea of Fate

skill3.description: Da Qiao summons a koi that leaps from left to right, dealing 300 (300 + 55% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and launching them for 0.5s. The koi creates a tide that deals 75 (75 + 12% magical attack) magical damage to enemies every 0.5s for 2.5s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Severing Surge

skill4.description: Da Qiao summons a whirlpool at the target location, dealing 500 (500 + 90% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range. The whirlpool lasts for 8s, during which teammates can teleport to it by tapping the Eye of the Whirlpool button. Da Qiao and teammates gain a shield that negates 350 (350 + 50% magical attack) damage while in the whirlpool. Da Qiao gains an extra shield that negates damage equal to 7% of her extra Health.
skill4.name: Skill 4: Eye of the Whirlpool

strategy.earlyGame: Early Da Qiao rides shotgun in the farm lane, using koi knock-ups to widen her marksman's safe farming pocket. The real product is Skill 2: an elevator that ships a wounded ally to base, refills them completely, and warps them straight back to the line. With that running, your partner can spend HP in trades like it grows back — because it does — and no war of attrition is losable. If nobody takes the ride, the cooldown refunds by half, so placing it on spec costs nothing. One genuinely critical prep step: explain the circle to your duo in the first minute, or the first accidental trip home will be theirs.
strategy.midGame: Midgame Da Qiao turns both edges of the map into simultaneous fronts. Hand Skill 2 to whoever is pushing a side lane, and the push, full-heal, and warp-back cycle forces the enemy to over-commit defenders every single time. That distortion converts directly into a numbers advantage at the 4:00 Tyrant and the 10:00 Shadow Tyrant. In skirmishes, cross Skill 1's koi through the Ultimate's current so the Passive's explosion and slow tangle enemy feet. Since her skill radius grows with magic attack, sneak some AP into the build alongside the usual support items.
strategy.lateGame: The late-game siege is Da Qiao's private stage. Lay Skill 2 behind the siege line before committing, and a rotation forms on its own: chipped allies cycle home, refill, and warp back, while the defenders burn damage into a five-stack that never stays hurt. The circle takes four seconds to fire, so the entire skill is deciding early — it will never save someone already inside a burst window. See an ally dip below half, and place it even if they look fine to keep fighting. That one habit quietly drags your late-game win rate upward.
strategy.teamfight: Da Qiao manages the entrance to the fight from the very back row. The instant an assassin leaps at your carry, flip them with Skill 1's knock-up, then sweep the Ultimate's koi across for a second launch plus the current explosion's slow — most dives simply end there, unfinished. She has no engage of her own, so walking forward to farm damage numbers is banned. Keep Skill 2 away from healthy allies' feet while winning; that is exactly when accidental trips home happen. Once both koi are spent, fall back on the Passive's movement speed and kite the gap out politely.

combos.title: Double Knock-Up Peel
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Ultimate
combos.description: Launch the diver with the vertical koi, then sweep the horizontal koi through for a second launch. When one koi crosses the other's current, the explosion and slow all but cancel the dive outright.

combos.title: Elevator Play
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Full Heal at Base → Warp Back to the Fight
combos.description: Ship a battered ally home, wash the debuffs off with the trip, and return them to the line at full strength. Placing it behind the siege line ahead of time is the accident-free version — and her signature move.

strengths: Skill 2 sends allies home for a full refill and warps them right back
Two knock-ups plus current explosions shut down backline dives
Skill radius scales with magic attack, stretching her control zone
An untaken Skill 2 refunds half its cooldown — a free safety net
weaknesses: Minimal personal damage; her impact never shows on the scoreboard
Skill 2's four-second delay cannot answer sudden burst
Uninformed teammates trigger accidental trips home mid-fight
Self-peel is knock-ups only; two divers at once will run her down

synergy.reason: Strong shields and peel can fully protect a stationary Huang Zhong from enemy dives during his ultimate.
Holds the frontline and provides chain CC, creating a safe zone for Huang Zhong to fire his artillery.

counters.reason: High mobility allows him to poke from outside Huang Zhong's range and then dive in for burst damage.
Can deal massive damage with high-powered snipes from outside Huang Zhong's ultimate range, winning trades completely.

passive.description: Huang Zhong's Basic Attacks increase his physical attack by 6-12 and Critical Rate by 0.75%-1.5% (increases with hero level) for 1.5s, for up to 5 stacks. These buffs are doubled when he is in Turret Mode. When he enters or exits Turret Mode, the buffs' durations are refreshed, and the buff multiplier is replaced with the multiplier of the current mode.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Gunner's Spirit

skill1.description:
Huang Zhong unleashes his potential, gaining 70% Movement Speed that diminishes over 2s. If he is in Turret Mode, he can leave it immediately.
Passive: He gains 20 physical attack (doubled while the skill is active).
skill1.name: Skill 1: Unleash Your Potential

skill2.description:
Huang Zhong places a landmine at the target location that grants him vision around it. The landmine deals 360 (360 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies that come into contact with it, while also granting him vision of them for 3s. The landmine slows heroes by 25% and inflicts 10%-20% Sunder for 2s (value scales with skill level). At the same time, he gains a shield that negates 360 (360 + 5.5% extra Health) damage for 3s. While not in Turret Mode, he gains increased skill use speed if there are enemies within range.
Up to 2 landmines can exist at the same time.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Lay the Mines

skill3.description:
Huang Zhong dashes for a certain distance and deploys a turret. For the next 15s, he is immobile and gains 200 [icon] and 200 [icon]. Each of his Basic Attacks deals 350 physical damage to enemies at the center (40% less to enemies on the edge). He returns to his normal mode after 5-9 Basic Attacks (number scales with skill level). Damage to towers is reduced by 50%.
Passive: When he enters Turret Mode, the [icon] of Unleash Your Potential will be refreshed.
Using the skill again allows him to exit Turret Mode.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Bring out the Artillery

strategy.earlyGame: Huang Zhong is a hyper-late-game marksman who farms up in the farm lane. Until level 4, don't force trades — just collect last hits, because his turret only hits like a truck once crit items come online. Gank protection is entirely Skill 2's job: drop a mine in the river bush and you get 3 seconds of vision, a slow, and a shield all in one cast. Whenever the enemy jungler is missing from the map, hold your mines for defense instead of poke.
strategy.midGame: Start rotating to your team around the 10-minute mark, once two crit cores are finished. The turret deals 50% less damage to towers, so during sieges the right call is shooting the heroes defending it, not the building. Shove the wave in, set up behind your teammates, and the enemy simply can't step forward while the tower chips away. Always place a Skill 2 mine on your escape route before you sit down — deploying while three or more enemies are missing from the map is suicide.
strategy.lateGame: The clumped-up fights around Shadow Tyrant and Overlord in the final minutes are where Huang Zhong takes over. In turret mode his Passive buff doubles and he gains 200 physical and magic defense, so just parking one step behind your frontline and firing melts the enemy line. The catch: you cannot move at all. If an assassin flanks you, don't get greedy — hit Skill 1 to instantly exit turret mode and retreat with the 70% speed boost. Also remember that re-entering turret mode resets Skill 1's cooldown; that detail alone changes your survival rate.
strategy.teamfight: The single most important rule: never set up where you'll be hit first. Wait until the enemy's dive skills have been burned, then deploy behind your frontline. The bombardment deals full damage at the center of its area and 40% less on the edges, so aim at the middle of the enemy clump and your damage jumps dramatically. Put mines at your own feet or in a side bush — enemies who touch them get slowed and armor-shredded while you get a shield, so one mine doubles as assassin insurance and damage support.

combos.title: Mine First, Then Sit
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (mine on your escape path) → Ultimate (deploy the turret) → Spam Basic Attacks
combos.description: Locking down your escape route and flank with a mine before sitting down is the foundation of turret play. The mine's slow and armor shred boost your defensive firepower while the shield covers accidents — the same bombardment lasts far longer this way.

combos.title: Skill 1 Emergency Exit
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (instantly exit turret mode + 70% speed) → Skill 2 (mine at your pursuer's feet) → Basic Attacks while kiting
combos.description: Your lifeline when an assassin collapses on you. Skill 1 cancels turret mode and speeds you up in one press, so drill the exit-speed-mine sequence until your fingers do it without thinking.

strengths: Turret mode adds 200 to both defenses and doubles his Passive, turning him into a fortress
A single Skill 2 mine covers vision, a shield, armor shred, and a slow
Skill 1's 70% speed boost makes disengaging from turret mode fast
Best-in-class AoE damage among marksmen once crit items are complete
weaknesses: Completely immobile while the turret is deployed, helpless against hard CC and dives
No mobility skill; mines are his only answer to ganks
The turret deals 50% less to towers, so his solo siege power is poor
Mediocre fighting power until two core items are finished forces a patient early game

synergy.reason: Provides attack and movement speed buffs that greatly enhance Kaizer's single-target burst and chase potential.
Provides shields and CC to boost Kaizer's survivability and mobility, enabling him to run rampant in teamfights.

counters.reason: Denies Kaizer's engage while dealing continuous damage, allowing her to easily kite him in a 1v1.
Hard suppression ultimate completely locks Kaizer down before he can wreak havoc with his ultimate.

passive.description: Kaizer's Basic Attacks and Skill 2 deal 50% more physical damage when hitting only a single enemy.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Demon Soul

skill1.description:
Kaizer throws a blade in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 85% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy hit and slowing them immensely for 1s.
The blade then ricochets between nearby enemies (hitting each enemy only once), with each hit dealing an equal amount of damage and slowing the target by 15% for 2s.
If the blade hits at least one enemy or finishes ricocheting, it returns to him, and he recovers 350 (350 + 5% extra Health) Health. This skill's Cooldown is also reduced by 30%, and he gains 15% Attack Speed and 15% Movement Speed for 3s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Vortex Brand

skill2.description:
Kaizer slashes twice in the target direction, with each slash dealing 160 (160 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage. The second slash launches enemies for 1s. His next Basic Attack is enhanced, causing him to dash toward the target and deal 130 (130 + 35% extra physical attack) extra physical damage.
Passive: After leaving combat, he gains 10 Movement Speed and recovers 1% Health and max Mana every second.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Blade Tempest

skill3.description: Kaizer summons his demonic suit of armor. After a 1s delay, he deals 250 (250 + 25% extra physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and enhances himself for 8s. While enhanced, he gains 500 Health, 100 physical attack, 50 Movement Speed, and 60 Block, while also dealing 50 (50 + 16% extra physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies every 0.5s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Invincible Warrior

strategy.earlyGame: The clash lane 1v1 is where Kaizer shines brightest. Start trading with Skill 1's thrown blade from level 1 — when the blade returns to you it heals and refunds 30% of its cooldown, so you consistently come out of trades with the HP lead. Keep his Passive in mind: basic attacks and Skill 2 deal 50% more damage when they hit only a single target. Don't chase enemies hiding inside their minion wave; manage the push to drag your opponent into an isolated spot, then start swinging.
strategy.midGame: Once you learn your Ultimate, those 8 seconds of +500 max HP, +100 physical attack, and +60 damage block are pure stat-check violence — almost nobody beats you 1v1. At the 4-minute Tyrant fight, don't walk in through the front. Catch isolated enemies from the river bushes instead: knock them up with Skill 2's second slash and chase with the empowered basic attack's dash and they're not getting away. But once the buff expires you're a different, far weaker hero — if you can't finish the kill within 8 seconds, don't commit at all.
strategy.lateGame: You're still a duelist late, not the guy who runs face-first into five enemies. Enter teamfights late from the flank, transform, and beeline straight for their marksman or mage — a fed Kaizer deletes squishy backliners in two or three hits with the empowered basic attack. Before Overlord, deliberately showing yourself so the threat of your Ultimate forces their formation backward is part of the job. When your transformation has under 2 seconds left, stop chasing and disengage while picking up Skill 1's heal.
strategy.teamfight: Rotate to a side bush before the fight starts, and go in the instant your team draws the enemy's attention. Skill 1 slows the target while speeding you up, then transform with your Ultimate and close the gap with Skill 2's knockup. Commit to exactly one target. Even in a scrap, pick the moment your victim is standing alone — the Passive's 50% bonus kicks in and they drop noticeably faster than they expect. While the enemy is still clumped, sometimes the right call is chipping them with the transformation's aura damage and waiting.

combos.title: Transform Execution
combos.sequence: Ultimate (transform) → Skill 1 (slow + self speed) → Skill 2 (second hit knocks up) → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: The core combo: dump everything into one target during your 8-second stat surge. If the victim is away from minions and other enemies, the Passive's 50% bonus applies and any backliner dies to the full sequence.

combos.title: Flash Knockup Ambush
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (start the slash) → Flash → second-hit knockup → Empowered Basic Attack → Skill 1
combos.description: An advanced trick: Flash mid-animation on Skill 2 to erase the gap and land an unreactable knockup. Whiffing it wastes everything, so save it for moments where the kill is guaranteed.

strengths: Passive adds 50% damage to basics and Skill 2 against isolated targets
Ultimate's 8-second stat surge makes him one of the best 1v1 heroes in the game
Skill 1's heal and cooldown refund win extended trades and sustain the lane
Skill 2's knockup plus dash lets him complete picks entirely on his own
weaknesses: Drops back to base stats when the Ultimate ends and folds to counterattacks
Single-target damage profile struggles against clumped frontline fights
Skill 2 is his only gap-closer, so ranged kiting shuts him down
Every engage depends heavily on whether his Ultimate is off cooldown

synergy.reason: Guaranteed hard CC locks targets down, ensuring Xuance's hook combos land perfectly.
Provides CC cleanse and damage reduction to prevent Xuance from being locked down and bursted when diving.

counters.reason: Instantly provides shields and damage reduction to targeted backliners with his ultimate, completely denying Xuance's kill.
Strong silence and instant burst damage can delete Xuance before he can even chain his skill combo.

passive.description: Xuance's chained sickles deal an extra 56 (33% physical attack) physical damage to enemies at long range, reducing their Movement Speed by 15% while increasing his own Movement Speed by 15% for 0.75-1.5s.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Crazed Prelude

skill1.description:
Xuance dashes in the target direction, enhancing his next Basic Attack to deal an extra 4% Health physical damage (increases by 0.05% for every 10 extra physical attack). If he has marked an enemy with his sickle, they are pulled a certain distance toward him when the dash ends.
The Movement Speed increase and slow effects of Crazed Prelude are enhanced as Flailing Sickles levels up.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Flailing Sickles

skill2.description:
Xuance wields his sickle, charging up to gain 30% Movement Speed and gradually increasing its range. He then throws it in the target direction, dealing 320 (320 + 140% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path and immobilizing them briefly. The sickle will mark the first target hit as Hunted, and will return upon reaching its max range. Xuance deals an extra 10% damage to Hunted targets and takes 15% less damage from them.
For the duration of the mark, he can use the skill again to consume the mark and pull the target behind him, dealing 320 (320 + 140% extra physical attack) physical damage (deals 50% extra damage to monsters).
Canceling the charge-up reduces the cooldown of Nightmare Hooks by 50%. If the Hunted target dies or is marked by Crimson Blur, 40% of the cooldown will be returned immediately.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Nightmare Hooks

skill3.description:
Xuance dashes behind a target marked by Nightmare Hooks, dealing 420 (420 + 200% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path. Beyond a certain distance, he'll dash toward them instead.
If he has not marked an enemy, he will instead dash to the target's location and mark them, dealing 200 (200 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage.
He takes 50% less damage during the dash.
Passive: He gains 30% Movement Speed (diminishes over time) and 25% Attack Speed for 5s for each kill or assist, for up to 3 stacks.
He can stock 1 use of Crimson Blur every 6s, for up to 3 uses in total.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Crimson Blur

strategy.earlyGame: You're the jungler. The moment you hit level 2 off your first buff, start planning the opening gank — Xuance's game is decided by whether he moves one beat faster than the enemy and steals first blood. Everything revolves around Skill 2's hook, and its 50% bonus damage to monsters keeps your clear speed respectable too. One detail worth memorizing: canceling the charge partway refunds 50% of the cooldown. If the angle feels wrong, don't throw it — cancel and rotate to the next bush. The discipline to hold the hook is often worth more than a kill.
strategy.midGame: The mid game is about erasing isolated enemies one at a time. Charge Skill 2 from outside their vision (you gain 30% move speed while charging) and release the instant a sightline opens. On hit, reactivate to hurl the target behind you — deliver them straight to your team. While your Ultimate carries you through an enemy you take 50% reduced damage, so diving under towers is safer than it looks. Every kill or assist triggers the Ultimate's passive attack speed and move speed surge, which even speeds up your travel to the next victim.
strategy.lateGame: A head-on 5v5 is your worst-case scenario — even full-build Xuance is made of paper. During the standoff before Shadow Tyrant, keep orbiting the perimeter. Your cue is seeing the enemy's stuns get burned on your teammates. Then hook a chipped backliner out of their formation, throw them, and finish with the Ultimate. Xuance's real terror is the chain reaction: one kill stacks the Ultimate's passive and the snowball starts rolling. Focus entirely on taking the first pick safely and the rest falls into place on its own.
strategy.teamfight: Never, ever take the job of engaging first. Sit on the edge of the fight with Skill 2 charged, waiting for a lane to open toward their marksman or mage. When the hook lands, pull yourself in with Skill 1 and the empowered basic attack, then reactivate Skill 2 to throw them into your team's kill zone. If you miss, back off immediately and wait out the cooldown. Playing hit and miss as two completely separate game plans — that discipline is what decides Xuance's winrate.

combos.title: Hook and Toss
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (charged hook lands) → Skill 1 (pull in + Empowered Basic Attack) → Skill 2 (reactivate to throw them behind you) → Ultimate
combos.description: Xuance's signature play: hook an enemy, throw them into your team, and finish with the pass-through strike. Always think of the throw direction as toward your own side — it prevents the classic overextension death.

combos.title: Assault Without the Hook
combos.sequence: Ultimate (dash to the target and latch the scythe) → Skill 1 (pull in + Empowered Basic Attack) → Skill 2 (charge)
combos.description: Your workaround for enemies who are hard to hook directly. Even without a hooked target, the Ultimate dashes near the victim and latches the scythe onto them, letting you close the gap with Skill 1 and force a brawl.

strengths: A self-sufficient pick machine: hook, throw, and follow-up all live in one kit
Kill-and-assist stacking passive makes his snowball terrifyingly fast
50% damage reduction while the Ultimate is in motion keeps dives safe
The charge-cancel cooldown refund lets him attempt hooks again and again
weaknesses: Missing Skill 2 silences both his damage and his mobility at once
Paper-thin base durability; a single stun or hard CC deletes him
Cannot play the frontline role in a head-on teamfight
Hook accuracy takes practice, so results swing wildly before mastery

synergy.reason: Long-range stuns lock enemies down, making it extremely easy for Shouyue to land his snipes.
Holds the frontline with heavy CC, buying plenty of time for Shouyue to safely snipe.

counters.reason: Her physical immunity skill allows her to completely negate Shouyue's snipe damage.
Provides shields and damage reduction to snipe targets via his ultimate, blocking potential kills.

passive.description:
Shouyue gains 1 stack of Ambush for every 1.5s he is out of combat, for up to 5 stacks. When he has Ambush stacks, he gains 20% Physical Pierce and 70-140 (+ 15% extra physical attack) physical damage. Every Basic Attack hit on enemy heroes consumes 1 stack of Ambush, while every skill hit consumes 5 stacks.
Accuracy: For every 1% Critical Rate, he deals 4 extra damage with Wild Wind and 2 extra damage with Getaway.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Accuracy

skill1.description:
Places a scouting device that provides vision within a range of 600-1,000 for 300s. He stocks 1 device every 35s, for up to 3 devices. Devices become ineffective when occupied by enemy heroes, and they become ineffective more quickly when occupied by multiple enemy heroes.
Passive: When out of combat and near natural terrain or a scouting device, he disguises himself, gaining 15% Movement Speed and 15% Attack Speed. After losing his disguise, the Attack Speed boost will remain in effect for 3s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: The Tranquil Eye

skill2.description:
Takes aim and snipes in the target direction, dealing 750 (750 + 250% extra physical attack) physical damage to targets hit, plus extra physical damage equal to 8% of the target's Health while slowing them immensely for 0.5s.
Aiming takes 2s, and bullets fired before the full duration have reduced accuracy. Up to 3 bullets can be stocked at a time. Landing a Basic Attack hit reduces the time taken to aim by 4%.
Wild Wind: When his Attack Speed is increased by 40%/80%/120%/160%, his aim time is reduced by 0.25/0.5/0.75/1s. The time taken for him to exit the aiming state is also reduced.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Wild Wind

skill3.description:
Leaps backward and fires in the target direction, dealing 750 (750 + 180% extra physical attack) physical damage and slowing enemies in the path by 15% for 2s. Upon landing, gains 15% Movement Speed for 2s. Bullets stocked are shared with Wild Wind, and 1 bullet is used with each skill use.
Using Basic Attacks or skills removes the Movement Speed boost instantly.
Passive: Increases Basic Attack range by 15 with every skill level upgrade.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Getaway

strategy.earlyGame: Play the farm lane or mid lane, and train yourself to hug walls first. Skill 1's passive turns you camouflaged while out of combat near terrain, adding 15% move and attack speed. The lane phase revolves around Skill 2's snipe — a frankly unfair 750 base plus 8% max HP per shot from level 1, so landing two or three forces your opponent to recall. Practice the flick shot early: keep the laser aimed somewhere else and snap it onto the target at the last instant. Your hit rate becomes a different animal.
strategy.midGame: Before the 4-minute Tyrant fight starts, place Skill 1's vision devices at the river junctions and enemy jungle entrances. You can stock up to three and each lasts 300 seconds, so never skimp on replacing them — that vision alone visibly cuts your whole team's gank deaths. On offense, keep sniping tower defenders with Skill 2 until they're at half HP and forced back, then siege with your team. Rounds stack up to three; never fire your last one for poke — always keep a bullet for self-defense.
strategy.lateGame: Chipping the enemy carry to half HP before the fight even starts — that's Shouyue's late-game job. The Passive's Focus buff builds after 1.5 seconds out of combat, granting 20% physical defense pierce and bonus damage, so take one breath between shots and each one hits noticeably harder. Because crit rate converts into Skill 2 and Ultimate damage, past 25 minutes a full-crit snipe erases a mage-sized HP bar in one shot. You never need to step forward. The very back, with walls and bushes behind you, is your permanent address.
strategy.teamfight: One step further back than your own backline — that's your spot. Once the fight starts, snipe whoever's in your sightline with Skill 2, but prioritize wounded targets. When an assassin dives you, leap backward with your Ultimate while firing (it slows on hit), then follow up with a stocked Skill 2 round. Aiming a snipe leaves you defenseless for about 2 seconds, so fight with basic attacks while the enemy's dash skills are still up, and only settle in to snipe after they've been spent. That patience is what keeps you alive.

combos.title: Flick Shot
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (aim the laser away from the target) → snap onto the target just before firing → Basic Attack follow-up
combos.description: A snipe is nearly undodgeable if the enemy never sees the laser line. Aim at a wall or behind you, then flick onto the target the moment they relax. Shouyue's winrate lives and dies on the precision of this one move.

combos.title: Anti-Assassin Jump Shot
combos.sequence: Basic Attack → Ultimate (backward leap + slow) → Skill 2 (fire the stocked round)
combos.description: Your self-defense package for when someone dives you. The leap's slow opens the gap, letting you land the follow-up Skill 2 calmly after touching down. Keeping one bullet in reserve at all times exists for exactly this moment.

strengths: Skill 2's extreme-range snipe adds 8% max HP damage, so every shot hits like a truck
Three Skill 1 vision devices let him build his own safe zones on the map
Terrain camouflage hides his position while he lines up sightlines
Crit converts into snipe damage, so his one-shot power never stops scaling
weaknesses: Aiming a snipe takes about 2 seconds, leaving a huge opening up close
The Ultimate's backward leap is his only escape; chained dives kill him
A run of missed snipes craters his damage contribution
Sustained DPS lags behind rapid-fire marksmen in messy extended brawls

synergy.reason: Strong CC locks enemies down, helping to keep them trapped inside Yixing's ultimate.
Can easily dive in and clean up kills on enemies trapped by Yixing's massive ultimate.

counters.reason: Extreme mobility allows him to dodge Yixing's skills and dive the backline for an instant kill.
Uses i-frames and high mobility to easily navigate Yixing's zone, avoiding CC while dealing damage.

passive.description:
Yixing's Basic Attacks deal magical damage, and skill hits apply 1 stack of Anti-Qi. At 4 stacks, a Weiqi stone is summoned below the enemy, dealing 100 (100 + 10% magical attack) magical damage. This Weiqi stone is then pulled to the center of Skill 2's Weiqi formation, dealing 170 (170 + 11% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path. He gains 1 permanent Weiqi stone every time Anti-Qi marks are triggered, as well as 5 Weiqi stones every 60s and whenever he scores a kill or assist. Each permanent Weiqi stone grants 1 magical attack.
When taking fatal damage, he enters the void, summoning a Weiqi stone below his feet while gaining immunity to all damage and 30% Movement Speed for 1s. This effect has a cooldown of 150s.
When Weiqi stones summoned by Anti-Qi marks hit an enemy multiple times within a short duration, subsequent hits deal only 50% damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Maintaining Initiative

skill1.description:
Places a Weiqi stone at the target location, gaining vision around it for 3s, dealing 100 (100 + 18% magical attack) magical damage, and reducing Taking Liberties' cooldown by 0.5s. The Weiqi stone lasts for 12s, and if a Weiqi formation is created, it will be pulled toward its center, dealing 180 (180 + 36% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path while slowing them by 25% for 1s. Hitting an enemy in this way will enhance his Basic Attack to deal 223 (120 + 60% physical attack + 18% magical attack) magical damage.
At 50/110/181 permanent Weiqi Stones, he gains an extra one-off skill that further improves his enhanced Basic Attack and grants a burst of Movement Speed for 5s. The enhanced Basic Attack improvements are a scattershot effect/17% damage boost/34% damage boost.
He stocks 1 Weiqi stone every 6s, for up to 2 stones. If an enemy is hit by multiple Weiqi stones being pulled to the Weiqi formation within 0.5s, subsequent hits only deal 50% of the initial damage. On-hit effects of enhanced Basic Attacks are reduced to 30%.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Sliding Stones

skill2.description:
Yixing deals 160 (160 + 25% magical attack) magical damage in the target area, which expands into a Weiqi formation. Enemies within the central area take 160 (160 + 25% magical attack) extra magical damage and are pulled toward the center of the formation.
The Weiqi formation lasts 10s. If Yixing passes through the formation's edge, he gains a 50% Movement Speed increase that diminishes over 1s, while enemy heroes that do so gain a stack of Anti-Qi. Each effect can only be triggered once. If Yixing moves too far away from the formation, it disappears.
This skill deals 180% more damage to non-hero units.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Taking Liberties

skill3.skill_name: Skill 3: The World is My Board
skill3.description:
Yixing's position becomes the corner of a void Weiqi board. After 1.5s, the board takes shape and launches enemies within it for 0.5s. The Weiqi board lasts for 4s, during which enemy heroes cannot leave it. The board adds 3 Anti-Qi marks to enemy heroes over time and exposes their location. If he successfully traps an enemy hero, he gains 1 charge of Sliding Stones.
The smaller the Weiqi board, the shorter the cooldown, for a maximum reduction of 25%.
When the Weiqi board is fully formed, Yixing gains 30-70% Movement Speed that diminishes over time.
skill3.name: Skill 3: The World is My Board

strategy.earlyGame: Yixing is a mid-lane setup mage who builds a board across the battlefield. Take Skill 2 at level 1 — it deals 180% bonus damage to non-heroes, so dropping the formation on a wave finishes your minion clear by itself. That clear speed is your early edge: it frees you to show at the river, and spare Skill 1 stones tossed into enemy jungle bushes buy 3 seconds of vision. Your durability is paper, but the Passive negates fatal damage for 1 second as a once-per-150-seconds insurance policy — if you get ganked, don't panic; use its speed boost and walk out.
strategy.midGame: This is where formation play separates good Yixing players from great ones. Skill 2 drags enemies near its center and slides any Skill 1 stones inside the area toward the middle for multi-hits, so burn the order into your hands: stones first, formation on top. Marks from skill hits and accumulated stones grow your magic attack for the entire game, which means from 6 to 10 minutes, every skill you land is literally banking late-game damage. The narrow river paths before Tyrant are the formation's best terrain — whoever lays their board first owns the fight.
strategy.lateGame: Past 10 minutes, the clumped fights over Shadow Tyrant and Overlord are your Ultimate's showcase. It has a 1.5-second formation delay, so overlap it on moments the enemy cannot back away — mid-attack on an objective, or right after allied CC lands. Trapped enemies can't leave the board for 4 seconds while marks stack on them automatically. The smaller you draw the board, the shorter its cooldown (up to 25% off), so cycling quick, small boards that lock down just two enemies is a genuinely strong late-game pattern.
strategy.teamfight: Anchor yourself in the backline and start laying Skill 1 stones along the enemy's approach path. The instant they push in, drop the Skill 2 formation on top — the pull plus stone multi-hits shreds their shape. If you smell a dive coming, drawing a small Ultimate around your own feet is a defensive play you'll use constantly in real matches. Blink users tend to escape during the 1.5-second windup, so don't burn the Ultimate on a single target — hold it until the enemy is clumped with nowhere to retreat. That's the win condition.

combos.title: Board Prison
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (formation) → Ultimate (trap them on the board) → Skill 1 (slide stones into the center) → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: The classic sequence: stop their feet with the pull, then seal the lid with the board. Pour Skill 1 stones in during the 4-second lockdown and you've built an inescapable multi-hit blender.

combos.title: Fast Wave Clear
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (place a stone) → Skill 2 (formation on the wave) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Skill 2's 180% bonus against non-heroes means dropping it straight onto a minion wave nearly finishes the clear alone. Spend the time you save on river vision — that's Yixing's standard early rhythm.

strengths: The Ultimate's inescapable board is a lockdown no other hero can replicate
Stone accumulation grows his magic attack automatically across the whole game
Skill 2's 180% bonus damage to non-heroes makes wave clear effortless
The Passive's 1-second fatal-damage negation insures against burst deaths
weaknesses: Low instant burst; his damage needs setup time before it comes online
The Ultimate's 1.5-second formation delay lets blink users walk out
No regular mobility skill, making him a favorite assassin target
The stones-then-formation sequencing takes real practice to master

synergy.reason: Provides movement speed buffs to compensate for Mengqi's lack of mobility, allowing quick backline dives.
Provides shields and massive CC, creating a space for Mengqi to run wild on the frontline in teamfights.

counters.reason: Silence and heavy burst damage can quickly melt Mengqi before he even has a chance to cast skills.
Team-wide CC cleanse completely nullifies Mengqi's engage and disruption potential.

passive.description:
Menki gains Mass when he uses skills. For every 10 Mass, he gains 6 physical attack, 8 Physical Defense and 8 Magic Defense.
He loses 5 Mass per second while in combat, and 15 Mass per second when out of combat.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Dream-eating

skill1.description:
Menki uses Dream Power to gain a shield that negates 431 (175 + 150% physical attack) damage for 4s, while also dealing 371 (260 + 65% physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and increasing his Mass by 30.
This skill's Cooldown is reduced by 0.5s every time he hits an enemy with his Basic Attack.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Lingering Dream

skill2.description:
Menki throws a Dream Bubble in the target direction and gains 30% Movement Speed for 2s.
After reaching its max range, the Dream Bubble returns to him.
Upon catching the Dream Bubble, he throws it again at a nearby enemy, and it returns to him after it reaches its max range.
The Dream Bubble deals 130 (130 + 25% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and places 1 stacks of slow on them for 2s, for up to 4 stacks. The slow effect is dependent on Menki's physical attack.
After retrieving the Dream Bubble a second time, he gains 30 Mass and the bubble turns into a Dream Bomb. He can throw the Dream Bomb in a target direction to deal 100 (100 + 24% magical attack)-550 (550 + 132% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range of its explosion.
The longer the Dream Bubble flies, the higher the damage of the Dream Bomb, with maximum damage dealt at 5.5s of flight time.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Dream Bubble

skill3.description: Menki performs a dream roam, dealing 201 (150 + 30% physical attack + 30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path while continuously gaining Mass. He briefly gains crowd control immunity at the start of the dream roam. Using the skill again stops the roam immediately, dealing 201 (150 + 30% physical attack + 30% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and launching them for 0.75s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Dream Roam

strategy.earlyGame: Menki is a clash lane fighter who brawls while banking Mass. Every skill cast adds Mass, and each 10 points grants +6 physical attack and +8 to both defenses, so the golden rule is cycling skills to charge up before you commit. It drains 5 per second while in combat, so the longer a brawl drags, the more you fizzle — keep that in mind. Open trades behind Skill 1's shield: every basic attack shaves 0.5 seconds off its cooldown, so as long as you keep swinging, you can keep re-shielding. Lane opponents hate it.
strategy.midGame: Skill 2 carries your mid-game damage. The bubble flies out and returns, then launches at a nearby enemy and returns again — after two retrievals it becomes the Dream Bomb, which at 5.5 seconds of flight time detonates for up to 550 plus 132% magic attack. In a 1v1, stack the bubble's slows while punching, then slam the grown bomb onto their escape path. Push the side lane, and when a river fight breaks out, join with your Ultimate's roam. The super armor at activation lets you start the rotation straight through enemy CC — quietly one of his best tools.
strategy.lateGame: Your late game changes faces with your build: physical items make you a backline diver, defensive items make you a frontline wrecking ball. Either way, cycle skills on jungle camps and minions to top off your Mass before joining any fight. Entering at zero Mass versus full Mass is a difference of dozens of points of attack and both defenses — literally a different hero. At Overlord standoffs, your job is arriving from an unexpected angle with the Ultimate and splitting their formation with its ending knockup.
strategy.teamfight: Enter deliberately. First, send Skill 2 bubbles through their line to spread slows while the bomb grows. Once your team commits, roam to their backline with the Ultimate and time the reactivation knockup right under their marksman's feet. The instant you land, press Skill 1 — shield plus 30 Mass in one cast — then cycle basic attacks to reset it and squat in their backline through a second and third shield. Overstaying until your Mass runs dry makes you crumble fast, so the moment it starts dropping, back out and recharge.

combos.title: Grow the Bomb, Then Pop It
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (retrieve the bubble twice) → throw the Dream Bomb → Skill 1 (shield) → Basic Attack
combos.description: Two retrievals convert the bubble into the bomb, and its damage scales with flight time. Throw it to land where a fleeing enemy is headed, not where they are, and you'll connect in the maximum-damage window far more often.

combos.title: Roam into the Backline
combos.sequence: Ultimate (roam → reactivate for the ending knockup) → Skill 1 (shield + 30 Mass) → Basic Attack → Skill 2 (slow)
combos.description: The dive pattern: time the ending knockup under the enemy marksman's feet. Whether you immediately press Skill 1 on landing to armor up decides whether you walk out of that dive alive.

strengths: His stats at full Mass rank among the best of any fighter in the game
A fully grown Dream Bomb detonates for up to 550 plus 132% magic attack
Skill 1's shield recycles constantly thanks to basic-attack cooldown reduction
Super armor on the Ultimate makes rotations and backline dives reliable
weaknesses: Fighting at zero Mass leaves both his damage and durability below average
Mass drains every second in combat, so long fights taper off badly
The bomb needs travel time to grow, so he has no instant burst on demand
The Ultimate's super armor only covers the start; CC catches him mid-roam

synergy.reason: Da Qiao's recall and teleport skills drastically improve Gongsun Li's survivability and map presence.
Movement speed buffs and heals further enhance Gongsun Li's hit-and-run playstyle.

counters.reason: Targeted hard CC will completely shut down her mobility.
Guaranteed stuns and massive burst damage can instantly one-shot the squishy Gongsun Li.

passive.description:
Arli's Basic Attacks place 1 stack of Maple on enemies for 5s, for up to 4 stacks. At max stacks, she detonates the Maples, dealing 220 (220 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage to the target and enemies near them, and placing 1 stack of Maple on them.
If she uses an active skill, she can use it again within 4s to teleport to the parasol's location and retrieve it. Otherwise, she will automatically retrieve the parasol after 4s. When she isn't holding her parasol, she gains 30-60 Movement Speed and 10-20% Attack Speed (increases with level).
Every time she uses a skill or retrieves her parasol, her next Basic Attack will be enhanced, launching an extra Basic Attack that deals 53 (20 + 20% physical attack) physical damage. She can stock up to 2 enhanced Basic Attacks.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Falling Leaves

skill1.description:
Arli blinks in the target direction.
If she is carrying her parasol, she will leave it behind at the location she blinked from.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Lithe Step

skill2.description:
Arli attacks nearby enemies twice, each attack dealing 300 (300 + 72% extra physical attack) magical damage. Using the skill also knocks down nearby enemy projectiles.
If she is holding her parasol, it will fly in a circle around the location where she used the skill.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Maple Dance

skill3.description:
Arli deals 400 (400 + 90% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies in the target direction and knocks them back.
If she is holding her parasol, she will throw it in the same direction. Upon reaching a certain distance, the parasol will continue to fly at a slower pace.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Autumn Storm

strategy.earlyGame: Arli is a farm lane marksman who dances with her umbrella. From minute one, internalize the rhythm: skills leave the umbrella behind, and recasting within 4 seconds blinks you back to it. Dash in with Skill 1, tag the enemy with an empowered basic attack for maple marks, then recast home before the counterattack arrives. Repeat this harass and your opponent can forget about last-hitting. That said, she lacks damage until her first attack item is done, so never overstay. Marks detonate at 4 stacks for AoE physical damage — two round trips for 4 stacks is the right level of greed.
strategy.midGame: Once two attack items are finished, she becomes unreasonable in river skirmishes. The trump card is Skill 2's projectile destruction: casting it erases enemy projectiles in range, letting you brawl straight through a marksman's shots or a mage's barrage. The catch is that the destruction only happens on the instant of the cast, so the expert habit is saving it for their biggest skill. In Tyrant fights, always leave the umbrella on the safe side, weave in and out, and stack mark detonations to grind down their frontline.
strategy.lateGame: Full-build Arli's razor's-edge dance decides matches. Her base durability is rock bottom — a single targeted stun and she evaporates — so fight exclusively on the fight's outer edge. Against diving assassins, the two-layer defense is your lifeline: knock them back with the Ultimate, then change angles with Skill 1 and slip away. As long as you're breathing, your mark detonations keep splashing AoE physical damage every 4 hits and will chew through even tanks. Picking the angle where you don't die, over and over, IS how you maximize her damage.
strategy.teamfight: Never stand in the same spot for a full second — that's the iron rule. Blink around with Skill 1 while spreading marks, keeping your next position unreadable from the enemy's screen. When you spot a lethal projectile skill coming, shoot it down with Skill 2. If a frontliner dives you, shove them off with the Ultimate and recast to the umbrella to resume kiting. The most dangerous moment in her kit is losing track of the umbrella, so while you're learning her, simply commit to one rule — the umbrella always stays on your team's side — and your accidental deaths will plummet.

combos.title: Two-Beat Harass
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (dash in) → Empowered Basic Attack → Skill 1 (recast to return to the umbrella)
combos.description: Arli's fundamental motion: step in, apply marks, and blink home before retaliation lands. Building this rhythm into your hands during the lane phase pays off directly as teamfight survival later.

combos.title: Three-Step Anti-Dive
combos.sequence: Ultimate (knockback) → Skill 1 (blink sideways to escape) → Skill 2 (destroy the follow-up projectiles)
combos.description: The full self-defense package against a diving assassin: shove them away, change your angle, then erase the projectiles chasing you. Execute the three steps calmly in order and you survive almost anything.

strengths: Every skill doubles as an umbrella blink, giving her the game's best evasion
Skill 2 erases enemy projectiles outright at the moment of cast
Mark detonations plus empowered basics deliver heavy AoE burst
The Ultimate's knockback peels assassins off her without any help
weaknesses: Rock-bottom durability; targeted CC deletes her before she can react
Misplacing the umbrella can blink her straight into the enemy team
Rated Very Hard for a reason — mastery takes serious time
Damage stays underwhelming until her attack items come online

synergy.reason: The link boosts her basic attack range and damage, allowing her to melt enemies from a safe distance.
Buffing a highly mobile ADC makes it incredibly easy to snowball the early game.

counters.reason: High mobility and burst damage pose a huge threat, as he can instantly wipe out both Ming and his linked ally.
Insane burst damage can delete allies before Ming even has a chance to heal them.

passive.description:
Every 5s, the next Basic Attack deals 238 (70 + 100% physical attack + 20% magical attack) magical damage and steals Health from the hit enemy, restoring 225 (225 + 40% magical attack) Health to the linked teammate and to Ming. Ming additionally recovers 4% extra Health.
Hitting a non-hero enemy unit only restores 50% Health.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Good Omens

skill1.description:
Ming throws his instrument. If it hits a teammate, it links to them. If it misses, it automatically links to a teammate within range. The instrument increases the linked teammate's main attack stat by 20 (20 + 10% magical attack) (1 main attack stat = 1 physical attack or 2 magical attack) and their Attack Speed by 10%. If the instrument hits a teammate, increases the main attack stat boost by an extra 25% (rapidly diminishes over 4s).
Enemies who touch the link take 30 (30 + 25% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s.
Passive: Increases his physical attack by 30, magical attack by 65, and Movement Speed by 7.5%.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Time - Carefree

skill2.description:
Ming throws his instrument. If it hits an enemy hero, it links to them. If it misses, it automatically links to an enemy hero within range. The instrument reduces the linked enemy's physical defense and magical defense by 10%. If the instrument hits an enemy hero, it reduces their physical defense and magical defense by an extra 25% (rapidly diminishes over 4s).
Enemies who touch the link take 30 (30 + 25% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s.
Gains vision of the linked enemy.
Passive: Increases his physical defense and magical defense by 15%.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Mastery - Glide

skill3.description:
After channeling for 0.75s, Ming deals true damage to an enemy linked to his instrument and restores Health to a linked teammate.
If the instrument is linked to 1 target, Ming spends 600 (600 + 125% magical attack) of his own Health to deal an equal amount of true damage to the target if it's an enemy, or to restore an equal amount of Health if it's a teammate.
If the instrument is linked to 2 targets, Ming steals 600 (600 + 125% magical attack) Health from the enemy and gives it to the teammate.
If the targets die before Ming finishes channeling, 70% of the cooldown is returned. The Health spent is slowly restored over 5s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Peace - Longevity

strategy.earlyGame: Open the game by linking Skill 1 to your jungler at their first buff — the attack and attack speed boost speeds up the clear — then follow your marksman to lane. Ming's link directly pumps an ally's main attack stat, so any 2v2 next to your linked partner is numerically in your favor. Play forward and push that edge. Skill 2 links to an enemy and cuts both their defenses by 10%, or an extra 25% on a direct hit. Stick it on the lane opponent right before a trade and the exact same combo from your carry chunks visibly harder.
strategy.midGame: From here on, the default is gluing yourself to your most fed teammate. Keep the link alive and weave in the Passive's empowered basic attack every 5 seconds — on hit it drains HP and heals both you and your linked ally, and that quiet little hit decides wars of attrition. Skill 2 doubles as a vision tool: if the link is still attached when an enemy ducks into a bush, their position stays lit up. Tag the enemy jungler with it before a Tyrant fight and you're moonlighting as the team's gank alarm.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, become the carry's shadow. Your Ultimate, after a 0.75-second cast, changes with your links: linked to one ally, you burn 600 plus 125% magic attack of your own HP to instantly heal them the same amount; linked to both an enemy and an ally, it drains the enemy to heal your ally with zero self-damage. Time it against the enemy's burst on your carry and it's effectively a second life. The consumed HP does trickle back over 5 seconds, but be very careful about self-damage casts while you're near death yourself.
strategy.teamfight: Lock your position half a step behind your linked ally and never open enough distance to break the link. On engage, throw Skill 2 at their ace or the assassin diving in — up to 35% defense shred means your team's focus fire suddenly goes through. The soul chain also damages enemies it touches, so deliberately placing your body so the chain drags across enemies is a real micro-play worth practicing. Hold your Ultimate through the opening exchange and heal reactively after their burst lands. Casting it early is only justified when you're certain you've read the play.

combos.title: Double-Link Free Heal
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (link an ally) → Skill 2 (link an enemy) → Ultimate (drain the enemy to heal your ally)
combos.description: With both an ally and an enemy linked, the Ultimate steals HP from the enemy to heal your ally at zero cost to you. Keeping both links alive going into a teamfight is the ideal preparation.

combos.title: Shred into True Damage
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (direct hit for 35% defense shred) → Passive Empowered Basic Attack → Ultimate (true damage)
combos.description: The finishing sequence for a wounded target: strip their defenses with a direct-hit Skill 2, then stack your own true damage on top of your team's focus fire. Just watch your remaining HP for the self-damage cost.

strengths: Skill 1's link permanently boosts one ally's offensive output
Skill 2's defense shred and vision tagging set up focus-fire kills
The Ultimate's instant burst heal acts as a second life for the carry
The Passive's drain attack heals both Ming and his linked partner at once
weaknesses: Nearly zero solo combat power or self-peel; dies instantly when isolated
Link range is limited, so highly mobile allies can leave him behind
No hard CC of his own to stop an enemy engage
The Ultimate can self-damage; a mistimed cast gets both of you killed

synergy.reason: Provides strong CC and defensive buffs from the early game, perfectly supporting Pei's aggressive jungle invades.
Long-range poke whittles down enemies, making it easy for Pei to clean up kills in Tiger form.

counters.reason: High mobility and i-frames allow her to dodge Pei's burst and easily counterattack.
Team-wide health rewinds and movement buffs in teamfights severely reduce Pei's kill potential.

passive.name: Passive Skill: Blast / Beastly Instincts
passive.description: While in human form, Pei's Basic Attack range is increased and each Basic Attack restores 5 Energy to him. His Basic Attack also deals an extra 20 magical damage. This extra damage can stack up to 3 times when attacking the same target within 3s.

forms.description: While in human form, Pei's Basic Attack range is increased and each Basic Attack restores 5 Energy to him. His Basic Attack also deals an extra 20 magical damage. This extra damage can stack up to 3 times when attacking the same target within 3s.
While in tiger form, Pei gains 25 physical attack, 60 physical defense, 60 magical defense, and 25 Movement Speed.

Pei fires Inner Energy in the target direction, dealing 275 (275 + 130% extra physical attack) (+ 8% of target's current Health) magical damage to enemies in its path, and slowing them by 25% for 1.5s.

skill2.name: Skill 2: Guarding Stance / Leaping Tiger Stance

forms.description:
Pei envelops himself in Beastly Instincts, dealing 100 (100 + 70% extra physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies while creating a shield that negates 450 (450 + 170% extra physical attack) damage and increasing his Attack Speed by 30% for 5s.
While the shield is active, he deals 20 (20 + 14% extra physical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies every 0.5s.

Pei pounces in the target direction, dealing 160 (160 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path.
