skill3.description:
Pei switches to tiger form, gaining 15% Movement Speed for 1s and enhancing his next 2 Basic Attacks for 5s.
First Enhanced Basic Attack: He dashes at the target, dealing 185 (20 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage and inflicting them with extreme slow. After using the first enhanced Basic Attack, the duration of the second will change to 5s.
Second Enhanced Basic Attack: He deals 185 (20 + 100% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range in front of him.

forms.description:
Pei switches to tiger form, gaining 15% Movement Speed for 1s and enhancing his next 2 Basic Attacks for 5s.
First Enhanced Basic Attack: He dashes at the target, dealing 185 (20 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage and inflicting them with extreme slow. After using the first enhanced Basic Attack, the duration of the second will change to 5s.
Second Enhanced Basic Attack: He deals 185 (20 + 100% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies within range in front of him.

Pei switches to Human Form, gaining 15% Movement Speed for 1s and enhancing his next Basic Attack for 5s.
The enhanced Basic Attack allows him to fire a stronger Inner Energy at the target, dealing 265 (100 + 100% extra physical attack) magical damage to the target and enemies in a cone-shaped area behind them.

strategy.earlyGame: Pei toggles between human and tiger with an Ultimate available from level 1, giving him one of the fastest jungle starts in the game. Shred your first buff with tiger-form empowered basics, and once the second buff is down, start eyeing an invade — almost no jungler beats Pei in a straight early-game scrap. Human form has longer basic attack range, and hitting the same target within 3 seconds scales the damage up to triple the base, so finish camps in human form: the kill is faster and the energy refunds come quicker.
strategy.midGame: The gank template is a two-act play: chip in human, execute in tiger. Human form's Skill 1 deals 8% of current HP plus a slow, so even tanks feel the poke, and adding Skill 2's shield plus 30% attack speed makes you genuinely scary at range. Once the target drops below half HP, swap to tiger and pounce with the wall-crossing double dash into empowered basics. Constantly weigh the 4-minute Tyrant against the enemy's buffs — the instant you spot their jungler, steal the resources on the opposite side. Half-map control is the mid-game ideal.
strategy.lateGame: Late teamfights are an exercise in patience. Both forms stay fragile, so open every fight in human form from the very back: throw Skill 1, maintain Skill 2's shield, and kite. The only time you swap to tiger is when the enemy's CC is spent and a target below 40% HP is clearly in view. Dive, finish them with empowered basics, and even after the kill, immediately return to human form and re-establish distance. Repeating 'tiger is for executions only' like a mantra puts you at exactly the right level of caution.
strategy.teamfight: Your default is playing human form like a marksman: chip the frontline with Skill 1's percent damage, cycle your shield, and kite backward. The reason you never tiger-dive the clump is simple — the instant you transform, multiple CCs come flying. Your go signals are the enemy's stuns being spent and the backline's HP bars. When both line up, swap to Tiger Form, use a side wall for the double dash to erase their reaction time, and get into their carry's face. Secure the kill, skip the chase, and return to human-form range to rejoin the line. That whole loop is one set.

combos.title: Human-Tiger Execution
combos.sequence: Human Form Skill 1 (percent damage + slow) → Ultimate (swap to Tiger Form) → Tiger Form Skill 2 (double dash off a wall) → Empowered Basic Attack → Tiger Form Skill 1 (bite)
combos.description: Pei's signature: soften from range, then erase the gap as the tiger. Set up your dash angle across a wall and you'll appear in their face from outside their field of view.

combos.title: Human Form Kite
combos.sequence: Ultimate (return to human form) → Human Form Skill 2 (shield + 30% attack speed) → Basic Attacks while kiting → Human Form Skill 1 (slow)
combos.description: The defensive pattern for when you're being chased or the tiger dive isn't there. Fall back behind your range and attack speed, and keep hitting the same target so the damage scales toward its triple-base maximum.

strengths: Form swapping covers both ranged poke and melee burst in one kit
The Ultimate is available from level 1, giving elite early fighting power
Human Form Skill 1's percent damage cuts through even tanks
Tiger Form's wall dashes open up a rich menu of ambush angles
weaknesses: Both forms are fragile; teamfight focus fire melts him quickly
No hard CC of his own, so picks depend on allied lockdown
Fighting at the wrong range for his current form halves his damage
Without an early snowball, his late-game presence thins out fast

synergy.reason: Stealth and a strong group pull make it incredibly easy for Kuang Tie to land his AoE skills on multiple targets.
Ultimate shields and teleportation safely back up Kuang Tie's aggressive dives.

counters.reason: Strong shields negate Kuang Tie's damage, leading to losing trades in the laning phase.
True damage completely bypasses Kuang Tie's reliable shields to deal massive damage.

passive.description:
Biron's mace accumulates charge when he lands hits with Basic Attacks or unenhanced skills.
At 30 charge or more, his mace becomes Electrified. Basic Attacks deal 40 (40 + 14% extra physical attack) physical damage and restore 70 (70 + 1.5% extra Health) Health to him. Skills also receive different enhancement effects, but hits from enhanced skills do not build up charge.
Basic Attack hits accumulate 5−10 charge, and skill hits accumulate 8−16 charge. He can stock up to 90 charge.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Fearless Chariot

skill1.description:
Swings his weapon twice, dealing 265 (265 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage each time and restoring 100 (100 + 1.5% extra Health) Health, plus an extra 2% of lost Health.
Electrified Enhancement: Damage is increased to 400 (400 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage, and restoration is increased to 200 (200 + 2.3% extra Health) Health, plus 4% of lost Health.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Electrifying Charge

Dashes forward, dealing 281 (150 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path. The next Basic Attack after the dash is enhanced, dealing 375 (200 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage and slowing enemies by 25% for 2s.
Electrified Enhancement: If he has accumulated 30 charge or more, the enhanced Basic Attack deals 562 (300 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage. It also launches and stuns targets for 1s, then slows them by 25% for 1s.
The first enhanced Basic Attack costs 30 Energy.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Storm Strike

skill3.description:
Biron slams his mace into the ground, dealing 450 (450 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage and slowing enemies by 30% for 1.5s. He also generates a shield that negates 900 (900 + 18% extra Health) damage for 6s.
Electrified Enhancement: Increases damage to 580 (580 + 195% extra physical attack) physical damage and boosts the shield to negate 1,450 (1,450 + 21% extra Health). Also generates an electric wave that deals 200 (200 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and steals 25 Movement Speed from each hero, granting it to Biron.
The range of the electric wave increases with the Ultimate's level.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Force Field Suppression

strategy.earlyGame: Biron is one of the strongest early brawlers in the clash lane — but only while he has Energy. Basic attacks generate 7, skill hits generate 10, and at 30 or more all his skills become empowered, so always punch minions to build the gauge before starting anything with your opponent. Empowered Skill 1's healing grows by 1% for every 1% HP you're missing, which means low-HP slugfests actually swing back in your favor. The moment your opponent thinks they've chunked you down and steps in for the kill is, quite often, exactly where you win.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, once empowered Skill 2's knockup and stun come online, Biron transforms into a premier gank-followup hero. Clear waves while banking Energy, and the second your jungler arrives, dash in with Skill 2 and lock the target down for a full second with the empowered basic attack — that's essentially a guaranteed kill. The iron rule before the 4-minute Tyrant: fill your gauge before walking down to the river, because empty-gauge Biron is just a target. After shoving your lane, hit the enemy's jungle camps to keep the gauge topped up while you raid.
strategy.lateGame: Late game you're the frontline diver and disruptor. Empowered Ultimate delivers AoE damage plus a 1500-point shield, so absorb the enemy's opening burst with it and buy your team the window to counterattack. It also heals per enemy hero hit, which makes the dead center of the brawl exactly where Biron belongs. The only thing to fear is being kept at range: against comps that stack slows from distance, save Flash as your instant gap-closer until the very end. Managing Energy and Flash — that's the entire late game.
strategy.teamfight: The fight starts 30 seconds before the fight. Hit nearby minions or jungle camps to bank Energy, then walk in loaded. Engage with Skill 2's dash, stop their momentum with the empowered basic attack's knockup, and immediately follow with the Ultimate's shield and AoE slow. Close with empowered Skill 1 in the middle of their clump — the more enemies it hits, the more you heal. And once you're below half HP, empowered Skill 1's healing spikes hard, so the longer you persist in the scrum, the harder you become to kill.

combos.title: Full-Gauge Engage
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (dash) → Empowered Basic Attack (knockup + stun) → Ultimate (shield + slow) → Empowered Skill 1 (AoE damage + heal)
combos.description: Biron's finished form: charge the gauge fully, then go. Lockdown flows into shield flows into healing with no gaps, letting you absorb the counterattack while you grind them down.

combos.title: Deathbed Reversal
combos.sequence: Confirm 30+ Energy → Empowered Skill 1 (healing scales with missing HP) → Skill 2 (dash out to disengage)
combos.description: The comeback pattern built on Skill 1's missing-HP healing scaling. Heal to full in your chaser's face, then dash away — and suddenly the only one who lost anything is the enemy who overextended.

strengths: With all three empowered skills up, few clash laners match his overall kit
Empowered Skill 1's healing scales with missing HP for dramatic comebacks
Empowered Skill 2 chains a dash into a reliable stun to start plays
Empowered Ultimate's 1500 shield lets him live in the middle of the brawl
weaknesses: At zero Energy his damage, healing, and CC all turn mediocre at once
Short skill range leaves him helpless against long-range kiting
Needs pre-fight gauge charging, so he reacts poorly on short notice
Skill 2's dash is his only mobility, leaving few retreat options

synergy.reason: Compensates for the lack of mobility with speed buffs, facilitating smooth tower sieges with summoned bots.
Peels enemies away, creating a safe environment for Milady to summon bots and land her ultimate.

counters.reason: Ignores the bots and uses high mobility to quickly close the gap and instantly burst them down.
Can easily wipe out entire armies of painstakingly summoned bots with wide AoE skills.

passive.description:
When Milady defeats an enemy, a mechanical minion is summoned to automatically attack other enemies for 6s. At the end of their duration, minions merge with another nearby minion of the same level and upgrade themselves (up to a max of Lvl 3). If there are no suitable minions to merge with, they self-destruct, dealing 200 (200 + 30% magical attack) magical damage (explosion radius increases with minion level).
Minion Basic Attack: 120 (120 + 25% magical attack) magical damage. Health: 500 (500 + 110% magical attack).
Movement Speed: 450 (450 + 10% magical attack).
Minions deal 75% damage to structures. Merging increases Basic Attack and self-destruction damage by 30%, and max Health by 20%.
Up to 4/2/1 minion(s) can exist at the same time. Once exceeding the limit, older minions will attempt to merge or self-destruct.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Mechanical Minions

skill1.description:
Milady commands an aircraft to fly in the target direction, attacking the enemy nearest to it multiple times along its path. Each attack deals 65 (65 + 10% magical attack) magical damage. After every two attacks, the aircraft attacks the nearest target an extra time, dealing 140 (140 + 20% magical attack) magical damage.
Using this skill again during flight splits the aircraft into two smaller aircraft. Each attacks the enemy nearest to it multiple times, dealing 65 (65 + 10% magical attack) magical damage. Enemies attacked by both aircraft have their Movement Speed reduced by 25% for 1.5s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Air Superiority

skill2.description:
Milady airdrops 2 mechanical minions in the target location, dealing 100 (100 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies upon landing. The mechanical minions activate after a 1s delay to search for the nearest enemy to attack.
She stocks 1 charge of this skill every 12−15s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), up to 3 charges.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Forced Invasion

skill3.description:
Milady fires a signal device at a target enemy or structure, marking it for 3s. Non-structure units are stunned for 0.75s. While marked, the target takes 80 (80 + 4% magical attack) magical damage every 0.5s and is slowed by 15%. When the mark expires, it explodes, dealing magical damage to the target and nearby enemies, equal to 25% of the total damage taken during the mark's duration.
If the target dies while marked, immediately summons 3 mechanical minions. While the Ultimate is active, allied mechanical minions in range gain 100% Attack Speed and Movement Speed, and will rush to attack the marked target.
Can be used on structures, but does not stun them.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Chaos Field

strategy.earlyGame: Milady's job from the first wave is simple: drop robots with Skill 2 and shove everything into the enemy tower. Skill 2 banks a charge roughly every 15 seconds up to three stocks, so resist the urge to dump all of them — with no mobility skill in her kit, a robot dropped at your own feet is the only gank insurance you have. When the enemy jungler vanishes from the minimap, hug your tower. Skip the 4-minute Tyrant fight entirely and keep shoving mid instead; the pressure you generate is what lets your teammates rotate freely.
strategy.midGame: Around the 10-minute mark, the moment the enemy mid laner drifts to a side lane is your cue to take the tower. Your Ultimate fires directly at towers and crystals, ticking damage while the mark lasts and detonating for an extra 25% of the damage dealt when it expires — stack that with your robots and towers evaporate. Never cross an unwarded river alone; a caught Milady is a dead Milady. After the tower falls, don't chase. Wait for the next wave and your Skill 2 stocks to recover before stepping up again, and the throws stop happening.
strategy.lateGame: You lose the burst race against traditional mages late, so win with siege instead. Nobody else can chip high-ground towers while robots soak the tower shots — you don't even need a minion wave to start the job. If the enemy turtles, don't force a dive; grind them down with Skill 1 fighter jets and endless robot waves and win the patience war. Before Overlord or Shadow Tyrant spawns, bank all three Skill 2 stocks about 30 seconds early and the standoff practically plays itself.
strategy.teamfight: Your spot in teamfights is the very back. Keep Skill 2 rolling to feed robots forward, and recast Skill 1 to split the fighter jet in two — enemies clipped by both take a 25% slow that lets your team close the gap. When an assassin jumps you, land your Ultimate on them for the 0.75-second stun, sic your frenzied robots on the target, and walk away. Milady doesn't win face-to-face damage races, so hold your position until you've seen at least one enemy dash hit the ground.

This effect has a 60−48s cooldown (depending on skill level).

Yaria directs a soul with her staff, dealing 250 (250 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path and knocking them back. The soul will track the nearest enemy hero after reaching its max range, dealing 250 (250 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to them, launching them for 0.5s, and exposing them for 5s.
Deer Spirit Form: Deer spirit form ends instantly.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Wandering Beam

Yaria deals 200 (200 + 30% magical attack) magical damage to the 3 closest random enemies within 5s, prioritizing heroes. She cannot use Basic Attacks for the duration of the skill.
Deer Spirit Form: Leaps forward.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Accelerating Blitz

skill3.description:
Attaches to a teammate, granting them a shield that negates 1,000 (1,000 + 60% magical attack + 8% of target's extra Health) true damage. Attachment ends when the shield is exhausted or when leaping in the target direction to detach. She becomes untargetable and unable to use Basic Attacks while attached.
Attaching to a hero immediately reduces her active skills' cooldown by 30% and grants them these extra effects:
Skill 1: Soul tracking range increased by 20%.
Skill 2: Attack range increased by 20%.
Ultimate: Manually detaching reduces Ultimate's cooldown by 50%.
Deer Spirit Form: Slow aura's area of effect widened.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Verdant Protector

strategy.earlyGame: Start the game standing behind your mid laner or marksman, letting Skill 2's auto-targeting bolts help with the chip damage while you fire Skill 1 into bushes for safety checks. The energy orb homes in and knocks up any hero it detects, so one cast tells you whether an ambush is waiting. Until Yaria learns her Ultimate attach at level 4, she is honestly just a soft target — take river vision only inside your allies' range, because nothing in her kit justifies walking ahead alone.
strategy.midGame: From level 4 on, the default play is attaching to your best-fed carry — usually the jungler or the marksman. You hand them a shield that absorbs all damage types, and while attached your own cooldowns drop by 30%, so Skill 1 and Skill 2 cycle faster too. The key habit: detach yourself before the shield breaks. A manual detach refunds 50% of the cooldown, which beats eating the full downtime every single time. Hold the attach in reserve right before the 4-minute Tyrant or any Shadow Tyrant fight after 10 minutes.
strategy.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, your one shield decides whether the carry lives. Assassin burst is instant — reacting after the dive starts is usually too late, so climb on as soon as a fight looks likely. Watch the shield's remaining health, hop off just before it shatters to collect the cooldown refund, then climb right back on. The window immediately after you detach is your most dangerous moment; hard CC triggers your Deer form (once per 60 seconds), but it will not save you from the second stun.
strategy.teamfight: Stay mounted on your carry, spread Skill 2's sustained damage, and knock up divers with Skill 1 to blunt their momentum. Your Passive Deer form only triggers on hard CC like knock-ups and knock-backs, making you untargetable while slowing everyone nearby — trading it for one wasted enemy engage tool is a clean win. Picking the right host is part of the job, too. Sitting on an ally nobody is attacking wastes the shield, so identify the one player actually being focused and move.

combos.title: Shield Cycling Loop

combos.description: Abuses the 50% cooldown refund on manual detach to maximize shield uptime. Waiting until the shield breaks is already too late — hop off at around 20 to 30% shield health remaining.

combos.title: Bush Check Into Push

combos.description: If the orb reacts, the ambush is confirmed; if it sails through, the path is clear. Scouting and the go signal packed into a single cast is Yaria's quietest strength.

passive.description:
Once Cirrus reaches level 4, he takes flight and can permanently ignore terrain. Using Basic Attacks grants Breath, which increases Movement Speed by 0-60 but drains quickly. When hitting enemies with Basic Attacks or skills, he places stacks of Lacerate on them for 2s, for up to 5 stacks. Lacerated enemies take physical damage equal to 0.24% Health when they move (increases by 0.02% for every 50 extra Physical Attack). Damage increases with stack count, for up to 10 times the initial value.
Lacerated enemies take 4.6 (2.7% physical attack) physical damage every 0.2s. Lacerated heroes only take 50% of this damage when not moving, while minions and monsters take full damage regardless of whether they are moving.

skill1.description:
Cirrus charges up, gaining 60% Movement Speed, then dashes forward, gaining a shield that negates 300 (300 + 100% extra physical attack) damage. He deals 200 (200 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage and stuns enemies hit for 0.5s. If he hits a hero, he can also jump back a certain distance in any direction.
Dashing will knock back non-hero units. Canceling the charge-up will return 20% [icon].
skill1.name: Skill 1: Cloud Descending

skill2.description: Cirrus throws wind blades, dealing 150 (150 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies twice and slowing them by 12.5% for 1s. For the next 4s, he gains 20% Attack Speed, and his Basic Attack gains increased range and unleashes 3 razor-sharp feathers. The feathers deal 34 (20% physical attack), 51 (30% physical attack), and 85 (50% physical attack) physical damage respectively, each one traveling farther than the last.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Razor Wind

skill3.description:
Cirrus gains 30% damage reduction for a short time and sweeps the target hero into the air, removing any crowd control effects he is under. During this time, he is untargetable and can move. Upon landing, he deals 360 (360 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage, and launches the target for 0.5s.
He deals 10% more damage on landing for every stack of lacerate. The target sent flying will only take damage from Cirrus while in the air. Cirrus's Movement Speed in the air scales with his level. If there's no enemy within range as he takes flight, he'll still deal the same amount of damage upon landing.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Soaring Whirlwind

strategy.earlyGame: Keeping flight active is Cirrus's lifeline. Flight persists as long as you keep crossing terrain, so plan jungle routes that hop walls between camps and shave travel time. Airborne basic attacks deal 4% of the target's max HP, so camps die fast and level 4 comes early. Until then, keep deep invades to a minimum — getting ambushed with no wall nearby means no way out. Only touch the 4-minute Tyrant when your team can collapse on it from both sides.
strategy.midGame: Level 4 is where Cirrus comes online. Gank from over-the-wall angles that wards rarely cover: hold Skill 1 to build speed, then release for a dash that stuns for 0.5 seconds and drops you behind the target. Since you land on their escape path, anyone without Flash rarely gets away. Every hit while airborne stacks move speed and armor penetration up to three times, so the longer you swing, the better the fight gets. Finish a core item by 10 minutes and farm isolated side laners to snowball your lead.
strategy.lateGame: A frontal late-game collision is a death sentence for Cirrus. Wait at a flank or behind a wall, and only commit once one or two enemy CC skills have been burned. Skill 1 stun into basic attacks, Skill 2's 30% damage reduction when the return fire arrives, then the Ultimate's 0.5-second untargetable window when everyone turns on you — keep that order intact. Thanks to the percent-HP damage, you still have a shredding job against tanky frontlines even when diving isn't on the table.
strategy.teamfight: Never call the engage yourself. After your tank soaks the opening, fly in from fog straight onto the enemy marksman or mage. Stun with Skill 1, carve percent-HP damage with basic attacks, and slip back over a wall using Skill 2's slow and damage reduction if you're chased. The Ultimate works as a finisher or as insurance, but the feather rain after the dive adds real damage, so my preference is saving it as the kill confirm. One target at a time — greeding for a second kill is how you never make it home.

combos.title: Backline Backstab
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (hold, then release for the stun) → Basic Attack → Skill 2 → Basic Attack → Ultimate
combos.description: The staple combo on the global server. Stun onto the target's back, weave percent-HP basic attacks, ride out the counterattack with Skill 2's 30% reduction, then close it out with the dive.

combos.title: Focus Dodge

combos.description: The exit plan for when you dove too deep. Blank the enemy burst with the 0.5-second untargetable window, then charge Skill 1's speed boost and vault a wall to safety.

weaknesses: Paper-thin defenses; eating CC first usually means dying first

Open ground with no walls strips away his mobility edge

strategy.earlyGame: Until level 4, Li Xin is one of the last heroes in the clash lane you want brawling with. His base mode hits soft, so stick to flicking Skill 2's sword qi from range for last hits and harass, and dash out with Skill 1 the moment someone commits onto you. The Passive's base mode grants bonus EXP whenever a basic attack or Skill 2 tags a hero, so even safe poke pays out experience. Against a lane bully, conceding waves under tower is exactly the right amount of cowardice.
strategy.midGame: At level 4 you pick a path: Light (Dominance) or Dark (Berserk), locked in for the rest of the match. If your team lacks a frontline and plans to group, take Dominance — bonus attack speed converts into physical damage reduction, making you far sturdier in straight brawls. If you want side-lane 1v1s and split pushing, take Berserk — bonus physical attack converts into attack speed and you drown people in swings. Energy drains 10 per second, so flip the mode on right before contact; burning it while walking around is the most expensive mistake you can make.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, Dominance Li Xin holds the front during tower defenses and Overlord standoffs, using the damage reduction to eat the enemy's opening swing. Berserk Li Xin skips the main fight entirely, split pushing and deleting whoever peels off to stop him in a 1v1. Either way, activating the Ultimate refills your energy to full, so re-trigger it on the engage call. Just remember: an energy-dry Li Xin plays uncomfortably close to his base-mode self.
strategy.teamfight: In Dominance, fight half a step behind your tank, sliding Skill 2's sword qi into the crowd and deciding on every cooldown whether to chase with Skill 1 or hold it. The damage reduction is real, but you are not an actual tank — stay out of stacked CC zones. In Berserk, enter from the fight's outer edge and use your attack speed to delete an isolated backliner first. Your best window is the first fight, before the enemy has read your mode — show them steel or show them speed, and warp how they play the rest of the game.

Upon destroying the magic circle, she gains 20% Movement Speed and 20% Critical Rate if she is inside it, or half of these bonuses if she is outside it. Creating or destroying the magic circle will deal 380 (380 + 85% extra magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range.
Passive: Critical hits from her Basic Attacks reduce the target's Movement Speed by 30% for 0.5s. If her Basic Attack lands a critical hit on the same target again within 1s, the Movement Speed reduction is increased to 50%.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Sphere of Purity

strategy.earlyGame: Garo's early game in the farm lane is an exercise in restraint. Skill 1's longbow adds 150 range but drains 50 MP per arrow that lands, so leaving it on permanently runs you dry. Use the longbow for wave clear and a few pokes, then stow it — basic attacks with the bow stowed restore MP, at triple value against heroes, and learning that toggle rhythm is the fastest way to improve on her. She has no mobility skill, so stay off the river bushes whenever the enemy jungler is unaccounted for. Until your first crit item finishes, farm beats fighting every time.
strategy.midGame: Garo's game starts around 10 minutes, once one or two crit items are done. The Ultimate's passive slows targets on every critical hit, so as long as you keep landing arrows, nobody closes the distance. When sieging, abuse the longbow's range to chip towers from beyond any retaliation. The moment an enemy initiator shows their face, stop them cold with Skill 2's 0.5-second silence. Walking anywhere alone, however fed you are, remains a death sentence.
strategy.lateGame: A full-build Garo is a stationary artillery platform that deletes everything in reach. Deploy the Ultimate for 20% bonus crit rate for you and nearby allies, then fire from maximum longbow range — the chained slows mean enemies simply cannot walk to you. If someone does get close, manually collapse the circle for a 3-second, 20% move speed burst and reset the fight. Before Overlord fights, glance at your MP bar first. A Garo who can't afford her longbow is just a slow marksman.
strategy.teamfight: Open teamfights by dropping your Ultimate underfoot and shooting the nearest frontliner from inside the circle. Don't force shots at their backline; hitting whatever is in range is how the crit slows stay unbroken. When an assassin dives, answer with Skill 2's silence and 50% slow, collapse the circle for the speed burst, and kite behind your tank. Her Passive repeats every instance of damage against shields, so shielded carries — normally the hardest targets on the map — melt fastest of all against Garo.

He can disembark while moving by using the skill again. When the ship collides with a wall, structure, ancient monster, or enemy hero, or when the time is up, it will explode. skill3.name: Skill 3: Set Sail!

strategy.earlyGame: Sun Ce hunts for lane control with level 2 trades in the clash lane. The core pattern is Skill 1 in, Skill 2, weave a basic attack, then Skill 2 again — each Skill 2 cast hits 25% harder and resets your basic attack cooldown, so punctuating casts with swings hurts far more than mashing. His Passive stacks physical defense every time he takes physical damage, so against AD matchups, brawl freely; the empowered basic attack every 6 seconds heals enough to win the war of attrition.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, the boat is Sun Ce's calling card. While sailing you have super armor — immune to knock-ups and the like — and can carry one teammate, so scooping up your mid laner for a gank is a devastating play. The ideal rhythm: sail to a side lane before the 4-minute Tyrant, create a numbers advantage, then arrive at the pit on spawn. The boat detonates on contact with walls and enemies, knocking targets up, so watch your spacing against terrain, not just your target. Winding routes are where boats go to die.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, Sun Ce is the team's designated engage. The longer the boat sails, the longer the knock-up — up to 1.5 seconds — but steering gets harder too, so pre-plan the shortest hidden approach before you commit. Aim for their backline. If the hit misses, swallow your pride, hop off mid-route, and join the frontline fight with Skill 1 and Skill 2. A boat that connects cleanly on the right target ends the teamfight before it begins; a solo boat launched beyond your team's reach is Sun Ce's single most common way to lose.
strategy.teamfight: Launch from bushes or from behind walls. Hop off just before impact so only the boat connects — you stay free to act during the knock-up, letting you layer a max-range Skill 1 for the second knock-up in the chain. With the target locked down, unload all three Skill 2 casts with basic attacks in between. While enemy Flashes are still up, holding the boat and firing it as the follow-up to an ally's CC is the disciplined play. With his defense stacks rolling, Sun Ce is far harder to kill than he looks.

strengths: The boat crosses the map and ferries an ally straight into ganks
Boat explosion plus Skill 1 chains two knock-ups back to back
Stacks physical defense when hit, winning drawn-out AD brawls
Empowered-attack healing outlasts lane wars of attrition
weaknesses: The boat detonates on walls, so one steering error wastes the engage
Missing both the boat and Skill 1 leaves no CC and easy kiting
Solo engages without follow-up lock enemies down but kill nothing
Noticeably soft at fight start before his defense stacks build

synergy.reason: Pulling enemies together makes it much easier for Wan'er to land the AoE burst from her intersecting brush strokes.

counters.reason: His point-and-click suppression CC interrupts her dash, stopping her from taking flight.

passive.description:
Enhances every 3rd Basic Attack, dealing an extra 255 (255 + 50% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in a line. When brush strokes intersect, nearby enemies take 255 (255 + 50% magical attack) magical damage (damage is reduced by 50% for successive hits within 1s).
Recovers 100 (100 + 22% magical attack) Health and gains an enhanced Basic Attack when near intersecting brush strokes.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Piercing Brush

skill1.description: Flings a powerful drop of ink in the target direction, dealing 200 (200 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to enemies hit. Upon reaching the end of its range, the ink explodes, dealing 200 (200 + 40% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Ink Burst

skill2.description:
With her current location as the finishing point, Shangguan starts writing from a target location, dealing 150 (150 + 20% magical attack) magical damage where her brush lands. Enemies touched by her brush strokes take 300 (300 + 40% magical attack) magical damage and are slowed by 25% for 2s.
This skill can be stocked every 10s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), for up to 2 uses.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Seething Script

skill3.description:
Dashes wildly with her brush, dealing 250 (250 + 32% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in her path. If she hits an enemy or ink left behind by another active skill, she can dash again in the target direction within 3s. If she dashes 3-5 times, she will jump into the air, becoming untargetable and cleansed of all crowd control effects, and perform continuous attacks on nearby enemies, dealing 460 (460 + 70% magical attack) magical damage. The number of attacks is decided by the number of dashes, with 3/4/5 dashes yielding 4/7/10 attacks. When hitting the same unit multiple times, subsequent hits deal only 25% damage.
She can dash up to 5 times, and she can attack and use skills between dashes. If interrupted, the skill's [icon] is reduced by 20%-80%, depending on the number of dashes performed.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Finishing Stroke

strategy.earlyGame: Before level 4, Shangguan is a paper mage who can't take off yet. Use Skill 2's brush and Skill 1's ink for wave clear, and fish for the Passive detonation that triggers where the two trails cross — it chips enemies and heals you at the same time. Simply playing around that intersection roughly doubles your harass output on the exact same casts. Her gank resistance is poor, so sit toward your tower whenever river vision is down, and don't bother showing up for the 4-minute Tyrant before level 4.
strategy.midGame: The moment you learn your Ultimate, Shangguan becomes an assassin. Dash three to five times through ink or enemies and you ascend — untargetable, cleansed of all CC, raining ink on everything below, with five dashes granting the maximum number of strikes. You can do this under an enemy tower with total impunity, so the mid-game job is roaming to the farm lane and solo-diving the enemy marksman. With a core item done by around 10 minutes, anyone caught under a clean take-off simply melts.
strategy.lateGame: Late game, one failed take-off can be the losing moment of the match. If your dashes get interrupted you are stranded in the middle of five enemies, so before committing, confirm the enemy's lethal lockdown — any suppression-style ultimate — has already been spent. Always enter from a flank. Poke with the Skill 2 into Skill 1 crossing detonation until your target drops below roughly 70% HP and their escape is burned, and your take-off success rate climbs dramatically. The landing recovery is long, so have the discipline to skip take-offs you can't confirm.
strategy.teamfight: Spend the fight's opening at the back, scattering crossing detonations and collecting the heals while you read the fight. Two or more enemy CCs down is the take-off signal. You can dash along your own ink trails without touching a single enemy, so pre-draw your approach route in ink. Once airborne, keep the reticle glued above their carry — the barrage steers, so even a Flash gets chased from the sky. Land toward your own team, always. Taking off through the enemy frontline is a mistake everyone in the lobby can identify.

combos.title: Standard Take-Off
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Skill 1 → Ultimate (5 dashes along the ink)
combos.description: Lay the brush and ink along the same line, then shuttle along the trail for all five dashes before ascending. Maximum strike count, maximum damage from the air.

combos.title: Staggered Take-Off
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Step back → Ultimate (2 dashes) → Skill 1 → Ultimate (remaining 3 dashes)
combos.description: Use the returning brush to bank early dashes, then bend the route with a fresh ink line. Against opponents who react to your first move, this is the take-off they can't read.

strengths: Untargetable and CC-immune while airborne, dealing unanswerable damage
Crossing brush and ink detonations poke and heal simultaneously
Solo tower dives delete enemy backliners from level 4 onward
Flexible dash routes make her entry angle nearly unreadable
weaknesses: Among the hardest heroes in the game; one missed dash means death
Hard CC before take-off shuts down her entire game plan
Long landing recovery invites the counter-kill if the target survives
Minimal self-defense before level 4 and extremely gankable

synergy.reason: He can dive in alongside Allain's ultimate to instantly burst down the enemy core.
Her shields and true damage strongly support Allain's survivability and damage output.

counters.reason: His point-and-click suppression completely shuts down Allain's combos and prevents him from becoming untargetable.

passive.description:
Allain's Basic Attack speed is very high. For each attack, he strikes once with each of his dual swords Crimson Shadow and Spirit Guardian, dealing 75 (22 + 30% physical attack) magical damage and 75 (22 + 30% physical attack) physical damage. Every first Basic Attack lets him dash to the target. Every third Basic Attack, he swings both swords at the same time, dealing 115 (36 + 45% physical attack) true damage and then entering a longer Basic Attack cooldown. When his Basic Attacks and skills hit enemy heroes, he gains Fury, increasing his Physical and Magical Pierce by up to 40% and damage reduction by up to 20%. Upon reaching max Fury, he recovers 168 (80 + 50% physical attack) Health, with a cooldown of 8s.
The lower his current Health, the more Health he recovers, for up to 3 times the base recovery.
His Physical Lifesteal takes 75% effect and applies to magical and true damage. His Basic Attacks only carry 60% of on-hit effects.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Howling Blade

skill1.description:
Allain swipes upward, dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) magical damage, 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) physical damage twice, and launching targets directly in front of him for 0.75s. After the initial strikes of this skill, he performs different follow-up strikes depending on how many marks he has stacked.
1 Mark: Strikes twice more, the first strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) magical damage and the second strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) physical damage.
2 Marks: Increases the launch range and strikes another 2 times, the first strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) magical damage and the second strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) physical damage. He can move slowly while performing the strikes.
3 Marks: Increases the launch range and strikes another 2 times, the first strike dealing 177 (110 + 38% physical attack) true damage and the second strike dealing 312 (180 + 75% physical attack) true damage. He can move slowly and gains crowd control immunity while performing the strikes.
He gains stacks when his Ultimate and Basic Attacks hit enemies. Skill 1 can trigger 50% of the Basic Attack's on-hit effects, and can grant lifesteal and deal critical damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Meteor Kill

skill2.description:
Allain dashes in the target direction, dealing 144 (100 + 25% physical attack) physical damage and 144 (100 + 25% physical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and reducing their Movement Speed by 15% for 1.5s. He also gains 10% Movement Speed for 3s, and his next 3 Basic Attacks gain 40% extra Attack Speed.
He stocks 1 charge of this skill every 10s (affected by Cooldown Reduction), for up to 2 charges.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Moonlight Flash

skill3.description:
Allain selects a target hero and leaps into the air for 1.5s, during which he can move and is untargetable. He then smashes into the ground, dealing 254 (175 + 45% physical attack) physical damage and 254 (175 + 45% physical attack) magical damage to enemy heroes. The closer the heroes are to him, the more damage they take, for up to 100% extra damage. He gains marks and Fury for every enemy hero hit.
This skill produces different effects depending on whether the targeted hero is an enemy or a teammate. When he lands, he grants himself or the targeted teammate a shield that negates 627 (450 + 100% physical attack) damage. For every extra enemy hero hit, the shield's strength is increased by 1/3.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Death at Sunset

strategy.earlyGame: Allain's first rule in the clash lane: never commit before your marks are stacked. Marks build from basic attacks and Ultimate hits, and at three stacks Skill 1 becomes a different move entirely — true damage, super armor, and a wide knock-up. Until level 4, build marks through short basic-attack exchanges, fire Skill 1, and step back without chasing. His Passive heal at full rage scales with missing HP — up to triple — so a slightly bruised Allain wins brawls that look even on paper.
strategy.midGame: From about 10 minutes, once a lifesteal item finishes, Allain stops losing side-lane 1v1s. That 75% lifesteal applies to his magic and true damage too, so the longer a brawl runs, the more HP flows back. The base pattern is split pushing to bait defenders, then running them down with Skill 2 dashes. Join teamfights late from a flank bush, and time the Ultimate's 1.5-second untargetable window against the enemy's biggest skill to make it hit nothing but air.
strategy.lateGame: Your late-game job is diving the enemy carry — but always on the counterpunch. Wait for enemy CC to land on your teammates, then close with Skill 2 and deliver basic attacks into a three-stack Skill 1. The Ultimate can finish a chase, but the play that wins late games is casting it on an ally the instant you're focused: you vanish for 1.5 seconds, share the landing shield, and reset the exchange. The one thing to never forget — the moment marks and rage lapse, Allain turns abruptly soft.
strategy.teamfight: Pick the single most dangerous enemy and refuse to leave them alone. Skill 2 holds two charges, so spend the first to close and the second to cut off the escape route. Three basic attacks into Skill 1 pushes through most interrupts thanks to super armor, lifting everyone around the target. Because rage grants penetration and damage reduction as it builds, Allain is at his strongest in a fight's second half — surviving the opening volley is the entire job description.

combos.title: Three-Mark Trade
combos.sequence: Basic Attack ×3 (build marks) → Skill 1 (empowered)
combos.description: The three-stack Skill 1 is the maximum version: true damage, super armor, and a wide knock-up. An unstacked Skill 1 is a different, far worse move — don't fire it early.

combos.title: All-In Chase
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (dash) → Basic Attack → Skill 1 → Ultimate
combos.description: The dash speeds up your next three basic attacks, feeding marks as you go. The closing Ultimate flexes between finisher and a 1.5-second disappearing act if the fight turns.

combos.title: Emergency Shield Share
combos.sequence: Ultimate (on an ally) → Skill 2 (exit)
combos.description: When the focus fire arrives, leap to a teammate and split the landing shield between you. The shield grows for every enemy hero the landing damages, so dropping into the thick of the brawl makes it bigger.

strengths: Physical, magic, and true damage; no defensive build blanks him
75% lifesteal swings every extended brawl in his favor
Three-stack Skill 1 is a super-armored, wide-area knock-up
One Ultimate covers chasing, dodging, and shielding an ally
weaknesses: His real damage only arrives once marks and rage are stacked
Chained slows and kiting starve his stacks and his healing
Basic attacks apply item effects at only 60%, demanding build knowledge
Mobility lives on Skill 2; with charges spent he can't chase or run

synergy.reason: His movement speed boost and healing heavily support the kiting needed to maintain the soul chain.

counters.reason: Her excessive mobility makes it easy to break the soul chain and kite away.

passive.description:
Augran's Basic Attacks vibrate his dagger-axe to resonate with an enemy's soul for 3s. The soul resonance deals 88 (50% physical attack) physical damage upon connection and will continue to deal damage with increasing frequency unless it is broken. When it ends, it deals a further 211 (70 + 80% physical attack) magical damage.
The soul resonance's initial and final damage carry 100% of the on-hit effect, while the rest carries 50%.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Soul Resonance

skill1.description:
Augran carves a path to the afterlife, dealing 280 (280 + 95% extra physical attack) magical damage to targets it hits.
The path accelerates after hitting walls or the Life-Death Border, then deals an additional 150 (150 + 60% extra physical attack) magical damage to enemies hit. While on the path, Augran ignores terrain and gains 50% Movement Speed. The first time the path hits a wall, it creates an afterlife bridge. When Augran traverses the bridge, he gains a burst of Movement Speed, while nearby enemies are slowed by 15%.
Augran can use this skill again to recall his dagger-axe, entering the Seer State for 4s. If his Basic Attacks target an enemy with less than 10% Health (750-1,500 for monsters depending on hero level), Augran will instantly execute them.
This skill deals full contact damage to non-hero units. The dagger-axe will automatically be summoned back when the skill's cooldown ends.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Path of Passing

skill2.description:
Augran swings his dagger-axe, dealing 200 (200 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in front and slowing them by 25% for 1s. He then leaves behind a Life-Death Border, marking enemies who touch it. Enemies who touch the dead branches on the border also take 140 (140 + 45% extra physical attack) magical damage and are slowed by 25% for 1s.
Augran enhances his next Basic Attack, dealing 50% extra damage to the target and recovering 80 (80 + 1.5% extra Health) Health for himself. If there are marked enemies within range, the resonance applies the same extra damage and recovery effect for each marked target.
This skill also knocks back non-hero units. The resonance can link to up to 3 targets. When resonating with non-hero units, the recovery effect is only 50% effective.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Death's Precipice

skill3.description:
Augran channels his divine power and descends from the sky, dealing 380 (380 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and knocking them back for 0.5s. If he hits an enemy hero, he recovers 750 (750 + 12% extra Health) Health and conjures their spirit counterparts to assist him for 8s.
After descending, he enters the Seer State for 8s. If his Basic Attacks hit a target with less than 10% Health (750-1,500 for monsters depending on hero level), they will deal a fatal blow instantly.
Every enemy hero hit increases recovery by 50%, up to a max increase of 100%. The conjured spirits inherit 30% of Augran's physical attack. They can only use Basic Attacks, but have higher Movement Speed and Attack Speed.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Conductor of Souls

strategy.earlyGame: Augran's jungle clear runs on never letting the Passive's soul link drop. Basic attacks tether souls, and weaving in Skill 2's empowered attack pushes damage and healing into several targets at once — double camps barely scratch your HP bar. Full clear to a fast level 4, then lay down Skill 1's path and gank from an angle the terrain was supposed to forbid. Pick the lane where the enemy is overextended rather than the one being shoved in; the success rates aren't close. Take the 4-minute Tyrant off the momentum of a converted gank.
strategy.midGame: From level 4, Skill 1's path becomes the axis of your game. On the path you ignore terrain and move 50% faster, and touching a wall builds a bridge that accelerates you further — arriving behind someone from a route that never appears on their screen is a feeling no other jungler offers. In fights, Skill 2's wall marks multiple enemies so your empowered attacks drain all of them at once; that healing is your lifeline. When a target runs low, recast Skill 1 for the execute stance and finish anyone under 10% HP with a basic attack. Learn to harvest that final sliver and your kill count doubles.
strategy.lateGame: In late teamfights, the correct Augran timing is right after the opening burst exchange ends. Your burst is modest, but as long as links and walls keep touching multiple enemies, the healing never stops — the longer the brawl runs, the harder you are to remove. Once low-HP enemies start piling up, drop the Ultimate into their midst. Its healing scales with every enemy hero struck, up to double, and the landing grants 8 seconds of execute stance to cull dying targets in sequence. The phantom that mirrors an enemy even papers over a numbers disadvantage now and then.
strategy.teamfight: Position where the soul link can reach at least two enemies at all times. Place Skill 2's wall across predicted paths so every marked enemy eats the empowered attack's echo and feeds you healing. The Ultimate also doubles as an emergency heal button — cast even after the focus fire lands, it often stands you back up. The only real fear is chained CC. Both the links and the executes require standing next to enemies, so against multiple stunners, wait until your teammates have baited the CC out before stepping forward.

combos.title: Path Ambush Package
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (approach on the path) → Skill 2 (wall and marks) → Basic Attack (hold the link) → Skill 1 (recast for the execute stance)
combos.description: Enter from a terrain-ignoring angle and win the exchange through link healing. The recast comes when the target is about to cross below 10% HP — that's the execute signal.

combos.title: Descent Full Combo
combos.sequence: Ultimate (descend) → Skill 2 → Basic Attack → Skill 1 (execute stance)
combos.description: Drop into the crowd on the Ultimate's massive heal, mark several enemies with the wall to drain them all at once, then spend the 8-second execute window finishing the dying in order.

strengths: Soul links and empowered attacks heal off several enemies at once
Execute stance culls anyone who drops below 10% HP
The terrain-ignoring path hides his gank angles completely
Ultimate's huge heal and phantom flip losing brawls
weaknesses: Low burst; enemies who disengage early escape his damage
Healing and executes demand melee range, so chained CC ruins him
Link damage needs time to ramp and loses short exchanges
Managing the path and recasts is busy work that takes practice

synergy.reason: His massive shields and proactive engage CC create a safe environment for him to output damage.

counters.reason: Her projectile negation and high mobility make it easy to avoid his burst damage.
Her physical damage immunity completely shuts down his damage output.

passive.description:
The elemental Dragon Souls from Ao'yin's last 2 skill attacks will be attached to his primary and secondary swords. He deals 165 (100% physical attack) physical damage with his primary sword, and if there are other enemies nearby he will also attack them with his secondary sword to deal 57 (35% physical attack -70% physical attack) physical damage.
When using skills, he gains 1 Dragon Soul mark (up to 3 marks) and 1 enhanced Basic Attack. Using the enhanced Basic Attack expends all marks, unleashing Dragon Souls that attack the target (Each mark grants 1 extra attack, with subsequent hits dealing half damage). Effects vary depending on the type of Dragon Soul attached to his primary sword.
When switching between elements, Dragon Souls of the same element is prioritized.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Hidden Dragon

skill1.description:
Ao'yin unleashes a wave of sword energy, gaining 1 extra Dragon Soul mark and dealing 270 (270 + 70% extra physical attack) physical damage and 70 (70 + 16% extra physical attack) true damage (and 50% splash damage behind the target) to up to 3 targets within range.
Use of Flaming Palm attaches 1 Fire Dragon Soul to his sword, allowing him to deal an extra 15 physical damage during Basic Attacks. If a Fire Dragon Soul is attached to both swords, he deals 50% more damage. If a Fire Dragon Soul is attached to his primary sword, the first strike of his enhanced Basic Attack will deal 97 (48 + 30% physical attack) true damage while the subsequent two strikes will deal an equal amount of physical damage.
Skill use speed scales with Attack Speed.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Flaming Palm

skill2.description:
Ao'yin unleashes sword energy, dealing 180 (180 + 45% extra physical attack) physical damage to up to 3 targets within range (dealing 50% splash damage behind the targets), and recovering 150 (150 + 2.5% extra Health) Health upon hit.
Use of Downpour attaches 1 Water Dragon Soul to his sword, allowing him to recover 18 Health and 0.5% Mana from Basic Attacks. If a Water Dragon Soul is attached to both swords, he recovers 50% more. If a Water Dragon Soul is attached to his primary sword, his enhanced Basic Attacks will deal 97 (48 + 30% physical attack) physical damage each strike, for a total of 3 strikes. Landing a hit on the enemy recovers 150 (150 + 2.5% extra Health) Health.
Recovery effects are halved against non-hero units. Skill use speed scales with Attack Speed.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Downpour

skill3.description:
Ao'yin unleashes a wave of sword energy, gaining 30% Movement Speed (diminishes over time). He also deals 180 (180 + 45% extra physical attack) physical damage (with 50% splash damage) to up to 3 targets within range and knocks them back.
Use of Riding the Wind attaches 1 Wind Dragon Soul to his sword, granting him 16 Movement Speed. If a Wind Dragon Soul is attached to both swords, he gains an extra 50% Movement Speed. If a Wind Dragon Soul is attached to his primary sword, he will deal 97 (48 + 30% physical attack) physical damage and knock back the enemy with every strike of his enhanced Basic Attack, for a total of 3 strikes.
Skill use speed scales with Attack Speed.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Riding the Wind

skill4.description:
Ao'yin reveals his true white dragon form and soars into the sky for up to 4.5s, then dives forward. During this time, he is untargetable and ignores terrain, but cannot attack. He deals 400 (400 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and slows them by 15%.
Upon landing, he deals the same amount of physical damage and applies Dread to nearby enemies for 1s. Targets afflicted with Dread will involuntarily move away from Ao'yin.
Ao'yin then unsheathes his True Dragon Sword, gaining 20% [icon] and 25 Attack Range, and the ability to attack up to two additional targets for 10s.
Ao'yin can switch his swords' elemental Dragon Souls while in flight.
Flight speed increases with his Ultimate's level.
skill4.name: Skill 4: Infinite Vastness

strategy.earlyGame: Ao'yin spends the early farm lane playing around Skill 2. The backward hop feeds into an empowered basic attack that heals, letting him refund enemy poke on his own — a luxury most marksmen never get. Every skill cast banks a mark (up to three), and a basic attack spends them all on a flurry, so waves die faster if you stack marks before swinging. Until your first attack-speed core item is done, your job is collecting CS from behind your support's shoulder, nothing more.
strategy.midGame: Around 10 minutes with two core items, Ao'yin's engine revs up fast. His Passive grants attack speed every time a skill connects, and all of his skills cast faster as attack speed rises — so the more you build, the quicker the whole loop spins. In trades, enter with Skill 1's dash and lock targets down with the fourth basic attack's knock-up. The Ultimate's airborne dive is your control window, boosting attack speed and range for a few seconds — hold it as the trump card for taking or defending towers.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Ao'yin wins through flexibility: chased, hop out with Skill 2 and heal; chasing, dash with Skill 1; need a group lift, spend Skill 3. The order you cast in changes what your next basic attack does, so taking one beat to ask which empowerment you actually want is what separates good Ao'yin players from great ones. At Overlord standoffs, hold a spacing where enemy CC can't reach you — stopping a frontline dive with the fourth-hit knock-up single-handedly relaxes your whole team.
strategy.teamfight: In teamfights, Ao'yin sits behind the frontline and keeps the damage flowing. Never start the fight yourself — wait out one or two enemy dash skills first. If someone sticks to you, hop back with Skill 2, heal through the empowered attack, and peel them off with Skill 3's knock-up if they keep coming. The moment the enemy's momentum fully dies is the Ultimate dive's cue: for those few seconds of extended attack speed and range, shred everything in reach. Simply walking around holding two or three marks changes your instant burst when a pick appears.

combos.title: Three-Mark Flurry Burst
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (hop to set up) → Skill 1 (dash) → Skill 3 (knock-up) → Basic Attack (flurry spending all marks)
combos.description: Bank the maximum three marks across your skills, then dump them in one flurry. The combo isn't finished until the closing flurry lands — that's where the damage lives.

combos.title: Anti-Dive Turnaround
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (hop back) → Basic Attack (heal) → Skill 3 (flurry toward your exit)
combos.description: The hop dodges the opening hit, the empowered attack heals the damage back, and the knock-up kills the diver's momentum so you can transition into kiting.

combos.title: Fourth-Hit Lockdown
combos.sequence: Basic Attack ×3 → Basic Attack (fourth-hit knock-up) → Skill 1 (chase)
combos.description: Count your swings and stack the dash on top of the lifted target. The more attack speed you build, the more often this little lockdown comes back around.

strengths: Skill hits stack attack speed, so the longer he swings, the faster he loops
Skill 2's hop and healing give him rare marksman self-peel
The fourth basic attack's knock-up stops enemy dives cold
Mark flurries and the Ultimate dive cover both burst and area control
weaknesses: Skill order changes his buffs, and a misplay directly cuts his damage
The loop is slow before attack-speed items, muting his early pressure
His defense hinges on one hop; layered CC runs him down
Busy piloting; sloppy mark management leaves him a jack of no trades

synergy.reason: His strong CC reliably locks down the target, ensuring the ultimate's tether doesn't break.
Her high burst damage guarantees a kill on enemies the moment they exit the illusion.

counters.reason: Her multiple blinks allow her to instantly create distance and easily break the ultimate's tether.
His point-and-click suppression can interrupt his skill while he is channeling the ultimate.

passive.description: Haya carries up to 3 moon crystals. Using Crescent Wave or Wayward Rays consumes 1 moon crystal. Once all are used, the skills enter full cooldown, and she gains an enhanced Basic Attack that fires 3 extra orbs, each dealing 50 (50 + 10% magical attack) magical damage. Targets hit by Crescent Wave or Wayward Rays will be marked, and hitting them again will trigger different effects.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Moon's Farewell

skill1.description:
Haya unleashes a beam of moonlight forward, dealing 350 (350 + 75% magical attack) magical damage.
If the beam triggers a mark, the target also takes 100 (100 + 22% magical attack) true damage.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Crescent Wave

skill2.description: Haya unleashes 3 glazed orbs, the first dealing 120 (120 + 22% magical attack) magical damage, and the next 2 dealing 60 (60 + 11% magical attack) magical damage. She also gains a shield that negates 250 (250 + 40% magical attack) damage for 3s and gradually gains Movement Speed over the next 2s, maxing out at a 30% increase. If she hits marked enemies, they will be stunned for 0.5s. Subsequent hits will only inflict 50% of the stun effect.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Wayward Rays

skill3.description:
Haya links to a hero for 1.5s, gaining 50% damage reduction. The link breaks if they move too far apart, refunding 75% of Moonscape Mirage's cooldown. If the link remains unbroken after 1.5s, both enter the mirage, granting her a shield that negates 300 (300 + 70% magical attack) damage.
While inside the mirage, her skill cooldowns are reduced by 50%. If she uses Moonscape Mirage again while inside the mirage, she moves 700 units away from the target.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Moonscape Mirage

strategy.earlyGame: In the mid lane, Haya's bread and butter is landing Skill 1 at max range, then hitting the imprinted target again to stack true damage on top. While you still hold moon rings, Skill 1 and Skill 2 cycle on very short cooldowns, but spending all three drops you onto normal cooldowns—so keep one cast of Skill 2 in your pocket for escapes whenever the enemy jungler's shadow appears. Skill 2 also grants a shield and a speed boost, so until you unlock the Ultimate at level 4, avoid overextending and fight around the imprint stun as a counter tool.
strategy.midGame: Around the 4-minute Tyrant spawn, the Ultimate starts paying off. Group with your jungler and link onto an enemy support warding the river or an isolated mid laner. Hold the link for 1.5 seconds and you drag them into the mirage, where the 50% cooldown reduction lets you dump Skill 2's stun and Skill 1's true damage on them one-sidedly. A practical tip worth remembering: cast the link right after the enemy burns their blink, and it's far harder to break. Once your first magic core item is done, the imprint combo alone puts enemy mages at death's door.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Haya is all about choosing who disappears into the mirage. Isolate the enemy marksman or mage with the Ultimate before a teamfight starts and you've effectively created a 4v5. Link a tank by mistake, though, and you can lose the brawl inside the mirage—pick your target carefully. After spending all three moon rings, your empowered basic attack fires three orbs' worth of damage, so always tack it onto the end of a combo. The vision fights before Shadow Tyrant after 10 minutes are exactly where a single-target catch hits hardest.
strategy.teamfight: Don't join the opening scrum head-on. Sit behind your frontline, spread imprints, and keep Skill 2's shield in reserve. If an enemy assassin dives your backline, link them with the Ultimate and recast inside the mirage to forcibly shove them 700 units away—that's real peel. When attacking, punish whoever steps up out of position with the Skill 1 into Skill 2 imprint stun and focus them down with your team. You have no area damage, so committing everything to deleting one target beats spraying into a clumped enemy team.

combos.title: Imprint Stun Fundamentals
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Crescent Wave) → Skill 2 (Wayward Rays) → Skill 1 → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Imprint with Skill 1, then land Skill 2 on the marked target for the 0.5-second stun plus a shield. Stack Skill 1's true damage on the stunned enemy and finish with the empowered basic attack unlocked by spending all three moon rings.

combos.title: Mirage Isolation
combos.sequence: Ultimate (Moonscape Mirage) → Skill 2 → Skill 1 → Skill 2
combos.description: Hold the link for 1.5 seconds to pull one enemy into the mirage with you. The 50% cooldown reduction inside lets you open with Skill 2's stun and cycle the imprint combo twice to burn them down.

combos.title: Displacement Peel
combos.sequence: Ultimate (link) → Recast inside the mirage
combos.description: Link the enemy fighter or assassin glued to your carry, then recast inside the mirage to shove them 700 units away. The link also grants 50% damage reduction, so you can afford to be the one soaking hits.

strengths: Repeated single-target burst through imprint true damage and stuns
The Ultimate isolates one enemy in the mirage, forcing a pseudo-1v1
Moon rings enable low-cooldown spam plus a shield and speed for self-defense
The link's displacement doubles as peel to protect your carries
weaknesses: Everything flows through imprints, so whiffing the first hit stalls the kit
The link breaks at range, making high-mobility heroes miserable matchups
Thin area damage means weak waveclear and zone control
Juggling rings, imprints, and links earns the Very Hard difficulty tag

synergy.reason: Clumping enemies up allows Yao to unleash all of his strong AoE damage at once.
His movement speed boost and healing further amplify Yao's core strengths of high mobility and sustain.

counters.reason: His point-and-click suppression locks down his mobility and bypasses his damage mitigation.
Likewise, his strong suppression entirely nullifies Yao's combos and evasiveness, resulting in a quick death.
