strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Yao lives on repeated short trades powered by the Passive, which heals you every time a skill connects. Touch with Skill 2's arcing dash, land Skill 1's full-circle slash, and back off immediately—repeat this loop and your HP bar drains slower than your opponent's. Star Power management is the key detail: your skills are only empowered for 3 seconds at max stacks, so never commit while the buff is down. Unlocking the Ultimate at level 4 lets you delay 40% of incoming damage and snap back to where you stood 2 seconds ago, erasing it—which is when shallow tower dives start to work.
strategy.midGame: The mid game is about shoving side waves and winning skirmishes with your in-and-out mobility. From around 6 to 8 minutes, once your first physical core item is finished, combos built around the empowered Skill 2 knock-up start killing squishy targets outright. The single biggest habit on this hero: always track where you stood 2 seconds ago, and step through a safe spot before you commit. As long as your return point is secured, even getting collapsed on by the enemy jungler and support isn't fatal—the Ultimate wipes the delayed damage and carries you out.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Yao is a second-wave diver whose job is touching the enemy backline. Don't burn skills at the start of a teamfight; watch the enemy's targeted crowd control get used on someone else, then enter with Skill 2. Going in at max Star Power lets you pile on pressure with empowered skills and the charging empowered basic attack. Even when you soak heavy damage, returning 2 seconds back with the Ultimate cancels it—but returning into the middle of the enemy team is worthless, so design your entry path as your route home from the start.
strategy.teamfight: The ideal teamfight is a cycle: dart in, heal off skill hits, dart out, and do it again. Leave the first engage to your tank, sweep in from a flank with Skill 2 into Skill 1, layer empowered skills, and disengage. One piece of hard crowd control is your death sentence—the delayed Star Split damage collapses on you all at once—so never stop respecting the enemy support's stun. And if you spend the Ultimate aggressively, you lose the safety net for the next burst you eat, so take a breath before every cast.

combos.title: Star Power Trade
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Star Rush) → Skill 1 (Starlight Slice) → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Close the gap with Skill 2's slow, then land Skill 1's full-circle slash to heal. At max Star Power, the basic attack after an empowered skill becomes a charging empowered strike, widening your trade margin considerably.

combos.title: Return to Dust Write-Off
combos.sequence: Step through a safe spot → Skill 2 → Skill 1 → Ultimate (Return to Dust)
combos.description: Walk over safe ground 2 seconds before you commit, then dive in and finish the combo while your incoming damage sits delayed. The Ultimate returns you to that spot and wipes the accumulated Star Split damage on the way out.

strengths: Healing on every skill hit wins the war of repeated short trades
Max Star Power spikes hard with empowered skills and the charging basic attack
The Ultimate delays 40% of damage taken and can erase it entirely
Skill 2's mobility gives you the initiative on both chase and escape
weaknesses: Individual skills hit softly, so full combo execution is the price of damage
The Ultimate returns you to a fixed spot from 2 seconds ago—unplanned casts get you killed
Hard crowd control stops the loop and stacked Star Split damage deletes you

synergy.reason: Gathering enemies allows Xi Shi to effectively chain her pull CC and AoE damage.
Xi Shi's pull can forcefully drag enemies right into Huang Zhong's massive attack range.

counters.reason: His AoE cleanse and CC immunity completely neutralize Xi Shi's pull CC.
His strong dive potential and silence allow him to close the gap and burst Xi Shi before she can pull him.

passive.description: Shi's skills deal more damage as the distance between herself and the enemy increases. For every 100 distance, the damage is increased by 5%, for up to 40%.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Maiden's Trick

skill1.description:
Shi throws an artifact to the target location, dealing 120 (120 + 24% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in the area. Enemies are pulled toward the artifact, and 1 enemy is wrapped in Silk Imprint. The skill can be used again within 5s to pull that enemy a short distance while interrupting the enemy's skill use.
If the enemy is too far from Shi, they will not be affected. Silk Imprint deals double damage to non-hero units.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Silk Imprint

skill2.description:
Shi releases an energy orb that stops if it hits a monster. The energy orb attacks nearby enemies every 0.5s, dealing 160 (160 + 50% magical attack) magical damage. The first hit slows enemies by 15% for 1.5s. Subsequent hits on the same target only deal 25% damage.
The orb explodes after 2s, dealing 160 (160 + 33% magical attack) magical damage, and double damage to enemies at the center of the blast. The orb will move toward the target wrapped in Silk Imprint.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Silky Beauty

skill3.description: Shi enhances herself for 8s, gaining a greater field of vision and resetting Skill 2's cooldown. While enhanced, hitting an enemy with Skill 1 lets her manipulate their movements twice, and Skill 2's cooldown is reduced by 50%. She gains 50% Movement Speed for 0.5s when using this skill.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Sole Focus

strategy.earlyGame: In mid, Shi clears waves quickly before level 4 thanks to Skill 1 dealing double damage to non-heroes, then spends the spare time poking from maximum range. The Passive adds 5% damage per 100 units of distance, capping at 40%, so firing from the very edge of your range is always the better trade. Skill 2's energy orb drifts toward enemies wrapped by Skill 1's silk, so never throw it on its own—always pair the two. Land even one pull-into-kill early and the enemy mid laner will stop standing inside Skill 1 range for the rest of the lane.
strategy.midGame: Once you learn the Ultimate, Shi becomes the best gank launchpad your jungler could ask for. Before the 4-minute Tyrant fight, hook an enemy from a river bush with Skill 1 and drag them into your side of the map—that alone locks in a numbers advantage. During the Ultimate you can pull twice per Skill 1 hit and Skill 2's cooldown is halved, so you handle everything from the catch to the sustained damage by yourself. Pull diagonally back toward your team's damage, not straight toward yourself; drag them in a straight line and you're the first one getting hit.
strategy.lateGame: In the late game, half the fight is decided the instant Skill 1 connects. Past 15 minutes with three magic core items, simply dropping a hooked enemy onto the center of Skill 2's explosion—which deals double damage there—vaporizes marksmen. But the downtime after a miss is heavier than ever, and the pull fizzles if the target gets far enough away, so resist the urge to chase deep. Don't forget the defensive job either: from behind your frontline, interrupt enemies winding up long channels by tagging them with the bind's crowd control.
strategy.teamfight: Shi's teamfight contribution is the pick before the fight ever starts. In the standoffs before Overlord or Shadow Tyrant, catch whoever's positioning is sloppy with Skill 1, drag them into your team, and start the fight 5v4. Once it turns into a brawl, pull diving frontliners away from your carry and roll Skill 2 at their feet to stack sustained damage. Your distance Passive rewards you for orbiting the outer edge of the fight, far from the enemy clump, so hold that perimeter the whole way through.

combos.title: Standard Catch
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Silky Beauty) → Skill 1 (Silk Imprint) → Skill 1 recast (pull)
combos.description: Roll the energy orb out first, then bind with Skill 1. The orb automatically drifts toward the silk-wrapped enemy, so recasting to pull them into the blast center stacks the double damage on top.

combos.title: Ultimate Double Pull
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Ultimate (Sole Focus) → Skill 1 recast x2 → Skill 2
combos.description: Empowering after the bind lets you pull twice, moving the enemy a huge distance. With Skill 2's cooldown halved, the follow-up damage arrives in time and you can convert the catch into a solo kill.

strengths: Skill 1's forced displacement rips enemies straight out of their formation
The distance Passive makes max-range poke from total safety genuinely painful
The bind's crowd control interrupts enemy channeled skills
Double damage to non-heroes from Skill 1 keeps waveclear fast
weaknesses: Missing Skill 1 leaves her close to useless for several seconds
Almost no self-peel, and the distance Passive dies once enemies close in
The pull fizzles at long range, demanding precise spacing at all times

synergy.reason: With him peeling on the frontline, it's easy to safely output sustained DPS from long range.
Her strong utility and healing create the perfect environment to continuously deal damage in teamfights.

counters.reason: She can close the gap with high mobility and use her high burst damage to delete immobile targets.
His high early-game pressure and mobility allow him to easily engage and deal heavy damage.

passive.description:
For every 5% increase in Attack Speed, gains 1% Cooldown Reduction. Gains 5 Anger upon Basic Attack and skill hits (10 upon critical hits). At max Anger, enters the Excited state.
Excited: Enhances all skills and reduces the cooldowns of Awesome Barrage and Heavy Shot by 25%−50% while recovering (0−3 + 1% physical attack) Health for every 1 surplus Anger.
When not gaining any Anger for 3s, Anger will begin to diminish over time.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Fiery Temper

skill1.description:
Uses the Apocalyptor to strafe continuously for 5s. Each bullet deals 96 (40 + 34% physical attack) physical damage. While strafing, he is slowed by 50. Enters cooldown after use.
Excited: Bullets have a piercing effect, dealing 50% damage to subsequent enemies. Firing speed is increased by 1% for every 2% Attack Speed, up to 100%.
Tap and hold to use. Damage can deal critical hits. Strafing can be paused temporarily to use other skills. Hits grant 5 Anger, while critical hits grant 10 Anger.
Every 2% Attack Speed increases skill casting speed by 1%.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Awesome Barrage

skill2.description:
Shoots a heavy round in the target direction, dealing 200 (200 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage to all enemies hit and slowing them by 25% for 2s. When the round hits an enemy or wall, or reaches its maximum range, it explodes and splits into 5 splinters that can ricochet off walls and deal 410 (410 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy they hit.
Excited: The number of splinters increases from 5 to 9.
Gains 5 Anger every time rounds or splinters hit an enemy. If multiple splinters hit the same target within 1s, subsequent hits only deal 25% damage.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Heavy Shot

skill3.description:
Meng Ya scans the vicinity and marks the locations of enemies within range when they take damage from his teammates (up to 5 locations can be marked). When the scan is complete, he fires missiles that deal 450 (450 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage. Subsequent hits on the same target deal 75% less damage and grant 10 Anger. He continues to fire up to 1 missile every second for 8s after the scan. 50% of the skill's cooldown is refunded if the skill is canceled or interrupted.
Excited: The minimum interval between subsequent missiles is reduced from 1s to 0.5s.
The skill button can be held down for up to 3s to expand the scan range. He gains 50% Movement Speed while scanning.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Missile Mayhem

strategy.earlyGame: In the farm lane, Meng Ya's job starts with grinding Fury off every basic attack and skill from minute zero. Bounce Skill 2 off a wall and let the shrapnel chip your lane opponent—that's your safe poke, and each pellet packs 100% of your bonus physical attack, with several landing in tight spaces. You have zero mobility skills, so stay away from the riverside bushes whenever the enemy jungler is missing from the minimap. His whole design revolves around skills only being empowered at full Fury, so never wander into a fight with an empty gauge—always start the fight topped up.
strategy.midGame: From around 7 minutes, once your first attack speed item is finished, Meng Ya's barrage becomes the real thing—his Passive converts every 5% attack speed into 1% cooldown reduction, so his skills cycle faster with every item. For Tyrant fights and mid-game skirmishes, layering the Ultimate from the backline is ideal: allies' attacks mark enemies and missiles rain down for up to 8 seconds, letting you join fights without stepping forward. Hold the back row, sweep Skill 1 across the fight, and let the full-Fury overflow healing keep you on the front.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, plant Meng Ya two steps behind your frontline as a walking artillery piece. At full Fury, Skill 1's bullets pierce, shredding enemies stacked in a line—defending narrow corridors is his personal kingdom. But you slow yourself while spraying and have no dash, so never be caught alone while the enemy assassin's position is unknown. One trick that will save your life in late-game close quarters: stand with a wall at your back and Skill 2's shrapnel ricochets straight back into whoever is in your face.
strategy.teamfight: Open every teamfight by firing the Ultimate. Hold the button to widen the search area, mark everyone your teammates touch, and let the missile rain begin. From there, spray Skill 1 from the very back and tag divers with Skill 2's slow to keep them off you. At full Fury, overflow keeps converting into healing, so you win plenty of extended shootouts even while taking damage. Your positioning rule of thumb: stand where no enemy can reach you with a single skill. Keep that true and Meng Ya is still standing when the teamfight ends.

combos.title: Wall-Bounce Burst

combos.title: Opening Salvo

strengths: Full Fury empowers every skill and overflow converts into constant healing
Attack speed feeds cooldown reduction and fire rate, so no stat goes to waste
The Ultimate supports fights from far outside enemy reach
Wall-bounced Skill 2 spikes to absurd damage in tight corridors
weaknesses: No mobility skill whatsoever—once reached, he cannot escape on his own
Skills underperform on an empty Fury gauge, so pre-fight ramp-up is mandatory
Spraying Skill 1 slows him, making enemy skillshots hard to dodge
The Ultimate depends on allies attacking and does little in a solo fight

528.name: Lam

synergy.reason: His strong CC locks down enemies, creating the perfect opening to guarantee the high-burst combo hits.
By disrupting the enemy formation and drawing aggro on the frontline, he creates a safe opportunity to dive the backline.

counters.reason: His silence prevents the spamming of mobility skills, completely locking them down.
Frequent long-range stuns prevent any engages, making it hard to utilize high mobility.

passive.description: When the enemy's Health drops below 30%, Lam will mark them as Prey. Lam's skills and Basic Attacks deal an extra 7.5-15% true damage to Prey.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Hunter

skill1.description:
Lam submerges himself for 3s and gains 40 Movement Speed for 3s. After the duration expires, he returns to normal and 50% of the [icon] is returned.
If he uses this skill again while submerged, he will burst out of the water and dash in the target direction, dealing 300 (300 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in his path and slowing them by 25% for 1.5s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Wavebreaker

skill2.description:
Lam attacks nearby enemies and slices open their wounds, dealing 2 strikes of 235 (235 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage and recovering 100 (100 + 1.5% extra Health) Health for every enemy hero hit (recovery is halved for non-hero units). He gains 1 mark when using the skill, and gains 1 additional mark every time a different enemy is hit, for up to 3 stacks.
While he has a mark, his Basic Attack is enhanced, consuming 1 mark to dash and deal 197 (70 + 75% physical attack) physical damage while recovering 100 (100 + 1.5% extra Health) Health. Each follow-up attack reduces the cooldown of this skill by 10%-20%.
When using this skill while submerged, he will dash in the target direction and reduce Skill 1's [icon] by 25%.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Space Split

skill3.description:
Lam throws his dagger in the target direction, slowing enemies in its path immensely for 0.5s. After a short delay Lam dashes toward the dagger, dealing 520 (520 + 180% extra physical attack) physical damage and dragging enemies in his path along with him.
When using this skill while submerged, he will drag enemies to the dash destination, and Skill 1's [icon] will be reduced by 50%.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Death From Below

strategy.earlyGame: As a jungler, Lam's first goal is using Skill 1's dive mode (+40 movement speed) to cut travel time between camps and secure level 4 plus the Ultimate before the 4-minute Tyrant spawns. The on-hit healing from Skill 2 keeps your HP topped up mid-clear, so you can often full-clear without recalling. Pick gank targets around the Passive: enemies below 30% HP take bonus true damage, so hit lanes where the enemy is already chipped. Train your eyes on that 30% line on every health bar—the number of kills you convert changes visibly.
strategy.midGame: Mid-game Lam owns the river. Use dive mode's speed to slip into the enemy jungle and drag isolated targets to the dash endpoint with the Ultimate, delivering them into your team's arms. Cast during dive mode, the Ultimate hauls every enemy along its path, so the dream opening at objectives is abducting the enemy jungler before the fight starts. Around 10 minutes, with two physical core items done, the mark-chase combo alone chips squishy enemies to 30% HP—then the Passive's true damage zone finishes the job.
strategy.lateGame: The late game is an exercise in patience. Lam is not a first-engage piece; he's a finisher who slips into the backline seconds after enemy targeted crowd control and attention lock onto your frontline. Stack marks with Skill 2, weave the empowered basic attack's dash and healing, and execute enemies in order as they cross below 30% HP. Resetting after each kill matters too—whether you can ride out cooldowns in dive mode is the difference between life and death. In Overlord standoffs, keep showing the enemy marksman the threat of a dive-mode Ultimate abduction.
strategy.teamfight: Lam's teamfight motto: enter second, outlast everyone. Circle the perimeter in dive mode at the start, and the moment enemy crowd control is spent, drag out their squishiest member with the Ultimate. From there, cycle Skill 2 into empowered basic attack dashes, healing through the on-hit sustain while you execute targets one at a time. The Passive works harder as health bars drop across the fight, so simply surviving the early chaos is itself a damage steroid. If chasing deep means ending up 1v3, dive out and wait for the next victim instead—that composure defines good Lam play.

combos.title: Dive-Mode Abduction
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Wavebreaker, dive) → Ultimate (Death From Below) → Skill 2 (Space Split) → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: The Ultimate cast from dive mode drags everyone it hits to the dash endpoint. Mark the delivered target with Skill 2, then stack the empowered basic attack's dash and healing to finish—the fundamental catch combo.

combos.title: Mark Cycling
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Space Split) → Empowered Basic Attack x2 → Skill 2
combos.description: Bank marks with Skill 2 and spend them on basic attacks for dashing follow-ups. Every chase shortens Skill 2's cooldown, so the loop barely stops in a brawl—and the built-in healing makes it his sustain engine.

combos.title: Dive Escape
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (dive) → Skill 2 (dive-mode dash)
combos.description: Speed up in dive mode and use the dive-mode Skill 2 directional dash to slip past walls. It also refunds part of Skill 1's cooldown, so keep this pattern in your back pocket for when you're being run down.

strengths: True damage below 30% HP means chipped targets never escape
Chained dashes from dive mode and mark chases make him hard to pin down
Skill 2's on-hit healing keeps him brawling on the frontline
The dive-mode Ultimate hauls enemies to the dash endpoint—a premier catch
weaknesses: Missing the Ultimate strands him alone in the middle of the enemy team
Hard crowd control breaks the dash chain and his thin frame melts fast
Managing dive mode, marks, and empowered attacks at once demands high APM

synergy.reason: Her massive AoE CC stops enemies in their tracks, setting up a perfect engage to unleash skill combos.
They both share high mobility and burst damage, easily wiping out the enemy backline together.

passive.description:
Jing and her mirror image apply 2 different types of marks on enemies when they deal damage. If an enemy has both types of mark at the same time, the marks shatter, dealing physical damage equal to 4% of their lost Health and refreshing the Cooldown of Reflective Assault and Shattered Illusions. This effect has a cooldown of 5s (2s during the Ultimate).
The damage dealt and recovery provided by the mirror image is only 30% of her real body. The farther the image is from her real body, the greater the damage and recovery, up to 80% of the real body. The image only deals 10% of the real body's damage to towers.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Lethal Reflections

skill1.description:
Jing dashes in the target direction, dealing 200 (200 + 100% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path and slowing them by 15% for 1.5s.
Her next Basic Attack is enhanced to deal an extra strike of 50 (50 + 15% physical attack) physical damage.
If no mirror image is present on the battlefield, one will be created for 2s, which dashes with her and replicates all of her actions except the Ultimate.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Reflective Assault

skill2.description:
Jing deals 160 (160 + 85% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and gains a 50% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 1s. Recovers 150 (150 + 2% extra Health) Health for the first enemy hit, and 25% of that value for each additional target hit.
If no mirror image is present on the battlefield, one will be created for 2s, which attacks with her and replicates all of her actions except the Ultimate.
—A skill practiced with Yao since they were children.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Shattered Illusions

skill3.description: Jing and her mirror image switch locations. Stocks 1 charge every 10s, up to 4 charges.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Dimensional Shift

skill4.description:
Jing flies forward, pulling enemies along her path with her. When she stops, she opens a Mirror Vortex and immobilizes the enemies at its center for 1s. She and her mirror image then move to either side of the vortex's central axis. While the vortex is present, she recovers 17 (10 + 4% physical attack) Health for every 0.05s spent dashing with Dimensional Shift. She gains 1 charge of shift if she deals damage to an enemy. The Mirror Vortex lasts 10s, during which Jing gains 10% damage reduction, but it will disappear if she leaves before then.
When the vortex is formed, 8 mirror fragments are generated along its border. When Jing or her mirror image deal damage to an enemy, the nearest mirror fragment will fly at the enemy, dealing 30 + 2% of the target's lost Health physical damage.
skill4.name: Skill 4: Mirror Domain

strategy.earlyGame: Jungle Jing is entirely about internalizing one system: every skill spawns a mirror image that mimics your actions, your body and the image each apply a different mark, and landing both triggers a slash for 8% of the target's missing HP while resetting Skill 1 and Skill 2. Drill that reset rhythm into your hands on jungle camps first and hit level 4 as fast as possible. For early ganks, Skill 1's dash and slow to stop their feet plus the mirror's overlapping damage to complete marks is plenty of chip. Prioritize practicing clean reset patterns over greedy invades.
strategy.midGame: From around 7 minutes, with your first physical core item finished, Jing's burst puts squishy targets inside one-combo range. Hunt lone enemies in their jungle or on side lanes: enter with Skill 1, complete marks with the mirror, take the reset, re-dash with the refreshed Skill 1—chain that loop and they never get a turn. Skill 2 heals per enemy hit but also slows you, so only swing it once you're fully inside their space. Before the 4-minute Tyrant and 10-minute Shadow Tyrant, deleting the enemy support who comes for vision frees up your whole team.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Jing is the flanking blade aimed at the enemy marksman's throat. But with durability that folds in a few hits, diving the front of a 5v5 unplanned is suicide, so you spend long stretches waiting. Watch which target the enemy's point-and-click crowd control gets used on, then enter with Skill 1. The Ultimate's swap is your trump card for both extending kills and escaping, but it caps at 2 stacks—impose one rule on yourself: always keep one for the road home, and your deaths drop dramatically. Getting your swap read and answered with crowd control is the number one killer, so varying your swap timing every time is the expert's secret seasoning.
strategy.teamfight: Wait on the perimeter until your tank draws the enemy's crowd control, then slide in the moment the backline's feet are exposed. Skill 1 into empowered basic attack into Skill 2 completes the marks; once the slash and reset land, swap with your mirror through the Ultimate to make their counterattack whiff, then re-enter on the refreshed Skill 1—that in-and-out loop is the ideal form. Because the slash scales off missing HP, your execution speed climbs as the brawl wears on and health bars drop. Every second spent hitting a full-HP tank is wasted, so keep your eyes locked on the softest target alive.

combos.title: Reset Fundamentals
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Reflective Assault) → Empowered Basic Attack → Skill 2 (Shattered Illusions) → Skill 1 (after reset)
combos.description: Apply your body's mark with the dash and empowered basic attack while the mimicking mirror layers the second type. Both marks complete, the slash lands, Skill 1 and Skill 2 reset—and you re-dash without a beat of downtime.

combos.title: Swap Disengage
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 → Ultimate (Dimensional Shift)
combos.description: Cut into the enemy team for damage and healing, then trade places with the mirror you created to exit. From there you choose: turn back on your pursuers with Skill 1, or simply walk away—a two-layered escape.

strengths: Dual-mark cooldown resets multiply both tempo and burst
The missing-HP slash makes her a premier executioner of chipped targets
The Ultimate's swap covers re-engage and escape in a single motion
On-hit healing from Skill 2 lets her brawl longer than she looks
weaknesses: Damage falls off a cliff whenever marks fail to complete
Skill 2 slows her too—swing it in the wrong spot and it's a free window
Paper durability; a predicted swap into crowd control is a death sentence
Mirror management piles on the workload and stretches the learning curve

synergy.reason: His sustained healing greatly boosts combat endurance whether mounted or dismounted.
He provides a solid frontline and shields, peeling to ensure they can continue dealing damage from a safe distance.

counters.reason: His immense mobility allows him to easily invade the jungle and disrupt early-game farming.
He targets the vulnerable dismounted state, and his strong chase potential makes escape nearly impossible.

passive.description:
Agudo has an affinity with the monsters of the Gorge. When she's near a monster, Recovery will be replaced with Release (grants buffs).
Upon hitting enemies, Agudo's Basic Attacks will drop Seed Mines and absorb nearby mines: She can pick up mines to gain 3% Attack Speed and Movement Speed for 2.5s, for up to 6 stacks.
Enemies that come into contact with a mine will take 30 (30 + 10% extra physical attack) physical damage.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Mountain Encounter

skill1.description:
Agudo sows a field in the target area, creating an animal wonderland that provides Agudo and her animal companions with 15% Attack Speed and Movement Speed, while granting 40 (40 + 0.6% extra Health) Health. Her animal companions will come to the field and fight alongside Agudo. Animal companions' stats scale with Agudo's hero level, while the chance of summoning more companions scales with skill level.
Animal companions gain additional Attack, Attack Speed, and Critical Rate based on 50% of Agudo's stats.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Wild Growth

skill2.description:
Tumble, Furball!: Agudo rolls forward with Furball, gaining 40 Block and immunity to 1 hard crowd control while rolling. Also deals 240 (240 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage to any enemies she hits and stuns them for (1/2s). If they hit a wall before the end of the roll, they'll ricochet up to 3 times, resetting the rolling distance while increasing the skill's effect by 25%. Agudo also enhances her next Basic Attack to shoot 3 Seed Mines and deal 60 (60 + 20% extra physical attack) physical damage.
Tumble, Agudo!: Agudo rolls forward and enhances her next Basic Attack to shoot 3 Seed Mines and deal 60 (60 + 20% extra physical attack) physical damage.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Tumble, Furball!

skill3.description:
While riding Furball: Agudo commands Furball to leap to the target location, dealing 460 (460 + 150% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and stunning them for 2/3s. After that, Furball will battle independently while inheriting 50% of Agudo's stats and 100% of her on-hit effects.
While not riding Furball: When Furball is defeated, it will enter recovery mode. It can rejoin the battle after its Health is fully restored.
She can call Furball back before the skill duration ends.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Gorge Mobilization

strategy.earlyGame: Agudo is a jungle marksman whose Passive lets him vacuum camps at speed few junglers match. Take both buffs, race to level 4, and keep collecting the seed bombs your basic attacks drop to maintain the attack and movement speed stacks (max 6). Skill 2's roll negates one hard crowd control effect, so even a face-check against the enemy jungler leaves you one free escape. His early dueling is average, though—if an invade is coming, just call teammates. When you gank, pick lanes with walls where the bounce stun can actually land.
strategy.midGame: The 4-minute Tyrant is where Agudo shines brightest. Drop Skill 1's paradise to boost your own and your companion monsters' attack and movement speed by 15%, and the pack melts the objective before a contest can even form. Mid-game skirmishes also start with Skill 1: a zone of healing and speed turns even-numbered fights lopsided. The Ultimate throws Pom-Pom for a ranged area stun, but your body is fragile once the throw is out, so only light the fuse on a brawl when your frontline is actually there.
strategy.lateGame: In late-game teamfights, where you throw Pom-Pom decides the result. Toss the Ultimate at the enemy marksman's or mage's feet for the stun, let the detached Pom-Pom maul them, and run a second front with your own basic attacks from the very back. Recast to recall Pom-Pom when the damage piles up. After the throw, your body is a plucked bird—check your escape wall and your teammates' positions before committing it. If Pom-Pom dies, half your power is gone until it recovers, so skip the solo side-lane pushes and keep shooting from under your team's umbrella.
strategy.teamfight: Lay Skill 1's paradise under your team before the fight starts, building the floor with companion monsters and the healing and speed buff. When the enemy engages, roll with Skill 2 to eat one crowd control effect while repositioning, and bounce off a wall to answer with the empowered basic attack's triple seed-bomb burst. Hold the Ultimate as the finishing move for the moment an enemy backliner ends up isolated. Between your summons and your own attacks you cover a wide front, so the longer a face-to-face fight drags on, the further it tilts toward Agudo.

combos.title: Wall-Bounce Counter
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Tumble, Furball!, into a wall) → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Bouncing off a wall boosts the skill's effects by 25% and upgrades your next basic attack into a triple seed-bomb volley. With one hard crowd control negation built in, it doubles as the perfect answer to a gank.

combos.title: Paradise into Pom-Pom Toss
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Wild Growth) → Ultimate (Gorge Mobilization) → Basic Attacks → Ultimate (recast to recall)
combos.description: Build your board with the paradise buff and companion monsters, then throw Pom-Pom into the enemy backline for the stun. Keep firing from safety, and the moment things turn ugly, recast to recall and regroup.

strengths: Companion summons plus Skill 1's buffs create numbers and board pressure
Skill 2 negates one hard crowd control and stuns off walls—great in attack or defense
The Ultimate's Pom-Pom toss is a ranged area stun you can throw from safety
Seed-bomb stacks and the Passive make his jungle clear exceptionally fast
weaknesses: The body is an assassin magnet while Pom-Pom is detached
Losing Pom-Pom guts his power until it finishes recovering
Before summons and stacks come online, his early dueling is merely average

synergy.reason: Her sustained healing and peel drastically increase the survivability of immobile, high-DPS marksmen.
Her massive healing pushes the effective health of frontline tanks to the absolute limit.

counters.reason: His strong lockdown shuts down mobility, preventing them from using walls to escape.
His high burst damage carries the risk of being instantly deleted before recovery or escape skills can be used.

passive.description:
Sakeer's Basic Attack deals melee damage and summons a firefly that deals 100 (100 + 20% magical attack + 3% extra Health) magical damage to enemies and exposes them for 3s. Sakeer also periodically restores 60 (60 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health to the nearby teammate with the lowest Health.
When there are no enemies nearby, charging his Basic Attack recovers 60 (60 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health. He will stop restoring Health to teammates while charging.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Firefly Protection

skill1.description:
Sakeer channels Luminescence to the target area, dealing 500 (500 + 10% magical attack) magical damage to enemies and launching them for 1s. Luminescence is consumed on hit, dealing 100 (100 + 20% magical attack + 3% extra Health) magical damage per stack. If there are teammates nearby, Luminescence instead heals the teammate with the lowest Health, restoring 60 (60 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health per stack.
Luminescence: He gains 1 stack every 1.5s, for up to 9 stacks. The skill's range increases with the number of stacks.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Mulberry Power

skill2.description:
Sakeer flies to the target brush, gaining 1 stack of Luminescence and releasing a number of fireflies depending on how far he flies. After 1s, the fireflies fly to the nearby hero with the lowest Health. If the hero is an enemy, the fireflies deal 100 (100 + 20% magical attack + 3% extra Health) magical damage and expose them for 3s. If the hero is a teammate, they restore 60 (60 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health.
This skill stocks up to 3 charges. Tap it to fly to a brush in front of him without aiming.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Ride the Wind

skill3.description:
Sakeer summons an Illuminating Brush at the target location. He can use this skill again within 6s to fly to the brush and gain a stack of Luminescence.
Illuminating Brush: 1s after the brush has been summoned, it releases fireflies at up to 5 nearby heroes every second. Every firefly deals 100 (100 + 20% magical attack + 3% extra Health) magical damage to enemies, or restores 60 (60 + 10% magical attack + 1.5% extra Health) Health to teammates.
Enemies that step into this brush will have their location revealed. After a while, the Illuminating Brush will stop releasing fireflies and turn into a regular brush that lasts for 30s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Firefly Fields

strategy.earlyGame: Sakeer's early game starts with juggling two jobs: escorting your marksman and sweeping bushes for vision. The fireflies from your basic attacks reveal stealth, and the Passive automatically heals the lowest-HP ally near you, so standing in the right spot alone stabilizes the lane. Skill 2 holds 3 charges—assign roles up front (one for river scouting, one for escape, one for gank follow-up) and your death count drops. Firefly Power builds 1 stack every 1.5 seconds, and Skill 1's radius and healing scale with stacks, so the patience to sit on them until the moment you fire is itself a form of power.
strategy.midGame: Once you learn the Ultimate, plant the glowing bush at the entrance to the battlefield before the 4-minute Tyrant and mid-game skirmishes. Fireflies launch every second—damaging enemies, healing allies—and you gain vision of any enemy who steps inside, so the side that placed it fights on terrain that wins both numbers and information. For gank follow-up, fly ahead with Skill 2 to a bush along the enemy's escape route and place Skill 1's knock-up on their exit—a brutal trap. At 9 stacks, Skill 1's radius is a different animal, so burn its maximum size into your muscle memory to sharpen your interceptions.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Sakeer stands half a step behind the carry, focused on one thing: delivering the 1-second knock-up at the perfect moment. The instant an enemy assassin or fighter touches your backline, launch them with a fully stacked Skill 1 and cut the follow-up cold—that single play swings teamfights directly. Firefly healing flies to the lowest-HP ally automatically, so as long as your own position is right, the support never stops. Against stealth heroes, your fireflies' true sight is close to a unique answer—build the habit of pre-firing a basic attack into any suspicious bush.
strategy.teamfight: Whether the glowing bush is placed before a teamfight nearly doubles Sakeer's contribution. After setting it, fly with Skill 2 to a bush near your backline and bank Firefly Power while you wait for the engage. Answer enemy dives with Skill 1's knock-up, and let the automatic firefly healing raise your whole team's HP floor through the brawl. Your personal damage is low, so there's no need to chase or step forward. Accept that not dying converts directly into healing output, and keep moving bush to bush, always one step outside the enemy's reach.

combos.title: Interception Knock-Up
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Phantom Step) → Skill 1 (Whirling Blades)
combos.description: Fly to a bush for a safe angle, then spend your Firefly Power on Skill 1 to launch the diving enemy for a full second. Radius and healing scale with stacks, so holding them until the very last moment is the trick.

combos.title: Glowing Bush Fortress
combos.sequence: Ultimate (Blade Dance) → Ultimate (recast to fly in) → Skill 1
combos.description: Place the glowing bush on a key chokepoint, recast to fly in yourself, and bank stacks. With firefly healing and damage ticking every second on your terrain, hold the knock-up ready and deny the enemy's entry.

strengths: Healing, a knock-up, vision, and stealth detection packed into one support kit
Bush-hopping through Skill 2 and the Ultimate gives him rare mobility for the role
The glowing bush dominates space and scouts around objectives
Fireflies auto-target the lowest-HP ally, so the support never misses
weaknesses: Skill 1 stays thin until Firefly Power builds, so he cannot spam it
Open terrain without bushes cuts his mobility and scouting in half
Low personal damage and no answer to chained hard crowd control
Healing dies when separated from allies—solo play is not an option

synergy.reason: Her strong CC locks down enemies, making it easy to stack the passive and chain combos.
By clumping multiple enemies together, he maximizes both the AoE damage and healing effects.

counters.reason: His silence forcefully interrupts skill combos, preventing the passive from stacking.
Her high mobility and kiting make it impossible to close the gap, allowing her to deal one-sided damage from afar.

passive.name: Passive Skill: SPLASH GRADATION
passive.description:
All of Charlotte's skills are considered Initial Skills. When any of her skills hit, the next different skill she uses will be enhanced to a Follow-Up Skill and she will gain 1 mark for 4s, for up to 5 stacks.
Upon reaching 3 stacks, her next Basic Attack is enhanced into the Follow-Up Skill SPLASH GRADATION, where she dashes toward the target and strikes 7 times, each strike dealing 121 (80 + 25% physical attack) physical damage while also slowing the enemy by 10%. The final strike deals extra physical damage equal to 12% of the target's lost Health. While launching an enhanced Basic Attack, she gains 21%-35% damage reduction.
Follow-Up Skills place 1 stack of Maim on enemies hit, reducing the enemy's Attack Speed by 10%-20% for 4s, for up to 2 stacks. Enemies lose 1 stack of Maim every time they use a Basic Attack.

skill1.name: Skill 1: TRI-SLASH

forms.description: Initial Skill: Charlotte unleashes TRI-SLASH in the target direction, and after a short delay, deals 366 (200 + 100% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. If TRI-SLASH hits an enemy, she gains a 80% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 2s.

Follow-up Skill: Charlotte quickly unleashes TRI-SLASH in the target direction, and after a delay that's shorter than that of the Initial Skill, deals 475 (260 + 130% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. If TRI-SLASH hits an enemy, she gains a 80% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 2s.

skill1.description: Initial Skill: Charlotte unleashes TRI-SLASH in the target direction, and after a short delay, deals 366 (200 + 100% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. If TRI-SLASH hits an enemy, she gains a 80% Movement Speed boost that diminishes over 2s.

skill2.name: Skill 2: SPLASH FOUNT

forms.description: Initial Skill: Charlotte dashes in the target direction and quickly strikes 6 times, each strike dealing 69 (45 + 15% physical attack) physical damage and restoring 70 (70 + 1% extra Health) Health.

Follow-up Skill: Charlotte dashes in the target direction and quickly strikes 6 times, each strike dealing 69 (45 + 15% physical attack) physical damage and restoring 70 (70 + 1% extra Health) Health. Cooldown is shorter than that of the Initial Skill.

skill2.description: Initial Skill: Charlotte dashes in the target direction and quickly strikes 6 times, each strike dealing 69 (45 + 15% physical attack) physical damage and restoring 70 (70 + 1% extra Health) Health.

skill3.name: Skill 3: POWER GRADATION

forms.description:
Initial Skill: Charlotte carves a seven-pointed star where she stands, dealing damage to nearby enemies up to 3 times, each dealing 320 (320 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1s. While the skill is active, she gains crowd control immunity and damage reduction.
When the same target is hit multiple times, subsequent hits only deal 30% damage.

Follow-Up Skill: Charlotte swiftly carves a seven-pointed star where she stands, faster than the Initial Skill. She strikes nearby enemies up to 3 times, each hit dealing 320 (320 + 75% physical attack) physical damage and slowing them by 25% for 1s.
Subsequent hits on the same target deal only 30% damage.
When the star forms, she unleashes POWER GRADATION, striking enemies at the center for equal damage and launching them for 0.75s. While active, she gains crowd control immunity and damage reduction.

skill3.description:
Initial Skill: Charlotte carves a seven-pointed star where she stands, dealing damage to nearby enemies up to 3 times, each dealing 320 (320 + 75% extra physical attack) physical damage and reducing their Movement Speed by 25% for 1s. While the skill is active, she gains crowd control immunity and damage reduction.
When the same target is hit multiple times, subsequent hits only deal 30% damage.

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Charlotte commits fully to touch-and-go trading until level 4. Skill 1 grants 80% movement speed on hit, so pre-cast it like a trap, close the gap the moment it connects, shave them down with Skill 2's six-stab heal, and leave. That one round trip is your winning trade pattern. The Passive's marks expire after 4 seconds, so resist any half-hearted engage that won't reach the third stack. Impose one condition on yourself—only step in deep right after your opponent whiffs a skill—and your early-game deaths plummet.
strategy.midGame: From around 8 minutes, as cooldown reduction items come online, Charlotte enters her unbeatable-in-a-1v1 window. Shove side waves to bait out the enemy fighter, then run them over from the front with the 3-mark empowered basic attack: seven dashing strikes, a final hit dealing missing-HP percentage damage, and damage reduction while it runs. The follow-up strikes' attack speed slow hurts basic-attack-reliant heroes most, so any side lane holding a retreating enemy marksman is prime hunting ground. Arrive at Tyrant fights slightly late from a flank, cycling skills on the perimeter to pre-build marks before you touch anyone.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Charlotte dives second, aiming for the enemy backline's head. Open by waiting: once your team's engage soaks the enemy's attention and crowd control, enter with Skill 2, layer the Ultimate's super armor, complete your marks, and unload the seven-hit flurry. Missing a single skill severs the whole chain—her greatest weakness—so the composure to wait for a guaranteed-hit distance converts directly into damage. Anti-heal items thin out Skill 2's sustain considerably, so check the enemy's item builds every single fight.
strategy.teamfight: The teamfight ideal is carving sword scars in the middle of the brawl while the Ultimate's super armor makes enemy crowd control whiff. Timing is everything: casting it on reaction, right as you see the enemy's stun animation start, is exactly fast enough. Fire it early and you're just a statue. The empowered basic attack carries damage reduction while it runs, so you survive the center of a scrum better than you'd expect. Even without kills, continually smearing the attack speed slow onto the enemy marksman visibly cuts the damage your frontline takes—there's always work to do.

combos.title: Full-Mark Standard
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Tri-Slash) → Skill 2 (Splash Sword) → Ultimate (Seven-Star Sword) → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Land three skills to complete the marks, then close with the seven-hit empowered flurry. The final strike deals missing-HP percentage damage, so the more chipped the target, the closer it gets to an execution.

combos.title: Speed-Boost Hit-and-Run
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 → Disengage
combos.description: Use Skill 1's 80% on-hit speed boost to erase the gap instantly, bank healing off Skill 2's six stabs, and leave. Marks linger 4 seconds, so re-touching quickly gets you to the empowered basic attack by the shortest route.

strengths: The 3-mark seven-hit flurry carries missing-HP damage that shreds even frontliners
Follow-up attack speed slows cripple basic-attack-reliant enemies
Skill 2's healing and the Ultimate's super armor win extended brawls
The 80% on-hit speed boost from Skill 1 dictates every engagement
weaknesses: Whiffed skills sever the chain and the marks, and the damage evaporates
No real answer to long-range poke or disciplined kiting
The wound debuff is stripped by enemy basic attacks, so it fades against heavy single hits
Silence locks her out of ever reaching the empowered basic attack

best_synergy.reason: Synergizes team firepower with Kongming's frontline engage to guarantee teamfight victories.
Synergizes team firepower with Li Bai's frontline engage to guarantee teamfight victories.

strong_against.reason: Can exploit Luban No. 7's skill windows to close the gap and overwhelm him with point-blank combos.
Can exploit Xiao Qiao's skill windows to close the gap and overwhelm her with point-blank combos.

weak_against.reason: Gets poked down before engaging by Ganjiang & Moye's long-range kiting and true damage.
Gets poked down before engaging by Arli's long-range kiting and true damage.

synergy.reason: Synergizes team firepower with Kongming's frontline engage to guarantee teamfight victories.
Synergizes team firepower with Li Bai's frontline engage to guarantee teamfight victories.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: Wish of the Living
passive.description:
At close range, Devara's Basic Attacks become melee attacks that have shorter attack intervals and grant 1 stack of Thunder Resolve, for up to 6 stacks. Upon reaching max stacks, Devara calls upon the power of thunder, gaining one extra basic skill use.
After using a basic skill, Devara gains an enhanced Basic Attack that deals an extra 85 (85 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and recovers 75 (75 + 1.2% extra Health) Health.
Ranged enhanced Basic Attacks deal 75% damage to non-target units and do not trigger on-hit effects.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Wish of the Living

skill1.description: Devara charges forward like lightning, dealing 240 (240 + 50% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in his path and gaining a shield that negates 360 (360 + 5.5% extra Health) damage for 2.5s.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Thunderblaze

skill2.description:
Devara unleashes a ball of lightning forward. Upon reaching its max range or colliding with an enemy, the lightning explodes after a short delay, knocking back enemies and dealing 240 (240 + 50% magical attack) magical damage.
The closer the unit is to Devara, the farther they are knocked back.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Divine Judgment

skill3.description:
Devara responds to an echo across millennia, rising into the air as he enters the Legacy Manifest state.
The transformation takes 1.5s, during which he ignores terrain and gains crowd control immunity and 30% [icon]. The golden staff at his back strikes nearby enemies in succession, prioritizing heroes. Each strike deals 100 (100 + 22% magical attack) magical damage, while also granting him 1 Thunder Resolve and a shield that negates 160 (160 + 2.5% extra Health) damage for 2s. Upon landing, he deals 200 (200 + 45% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies.
He remains transformed for 8s, during which the range of his enhanced Basic Attacks is increased, Basic Attacks grant 2 Thunder Resolve, and ranged Basic Attacks create chain lightning that bounces between multiple enemies, dealing 86 (50% physical attack) physical damage.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Millennium Echo

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, everything about Devara flows from one rhythm: one skill, one empowered basic attack. Every skill cast empowers your next basic attack with area magic damage and healing attached, so simply keeping that weave going wins the lane's war of attrition. Until level 4, treat Skill 1's shielded dash as your answer to being jumped, not as an engage tool. Basic attacks bank Passive stacks, and hitting the cap of 6 triggers thunder that lets you cast one bonus basic skill—so the iron rule is to only take trades from a full gauge.
strategy.midGame: From around 8 minutes, with one or two magic core items finished, Devara's skirmish power transforms. The Ultimate grants super armor and terrain-ignoring movement during its 1.5-second levitation, letting you drop into river scraps from over a wall. The transformed state lasts 8 seconds after landing: your empowered basic attacks grow in area and each basic attack banks 2 Passive stacks, raising both your damage and your healing a full tier. Cast it from behind a wall rather than in the enemy's face—floating in the open invites focus fire.
strategy.lateGame: In teamfights past 15 minutes, Devara is a semi-carry whose frontline rank jumps a tier for the transformation's 8 seconds. Float with the Ultimate as the fight opens, collect the lightning strikes and shields on the way down, and land near the enemy's squishiest members. Your transformed ranged basic attacks carry chain bolts that ricochet between clustered enemies, spiking your damage into grouped teams. The danger is post-landing isolation: drop deeper than your support can reach and the focus fire ends you. Cap your landing depth at a spot allies can reach within 3 seconds.
strategy.teamfight: In the brawl, your job is cycling in and out with Skill 1's shielded dash while keeping the empowered basic attacks' area damage and healing rolling. Against enemies glued to you, the answer is Skill 2 point-blank: the closer the target, the farther the knockback sends them, so the more suffocating the pressure, the calmer you should be about firing it in their chest. The Ultimate's super armor also answers enemy engage crowd control, so decide from their composition whether it's your sword or your shield. Whatever happens, never break the basic attack rhythm—it carries both your damage and your survival.

combos.title: The Core Weave
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Thunderblaze) → Empowered Basic Attack → Skill 2 (Divine Judgment) → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Slot one basic attack after every skill and collect the area magic damage plus healing every single time. This pattern is Devara's heartbeat—once it's second nature, you stop losing lane brawls outright.

combos.title: Transformation Dive
combos.sequence: Ultimate (Millennium Echo) → Skill 1 → Empowered Basic Attack → Skill 2
combos.description: Cross terrain under the levitation's super armor, land, and chain the shielded dash into repeated empowered basic attacks. Anyone who sticks to you gets peeled off with Skill 2's point-blank knockback.

combos.title: Thunder Follow-Up
combos.sequence: Basic Attacks (max Passive stacks) → Skill 1 → Bonus basic skill → Empowered Basic Attack
combos.description: Engage with the gauge capped at 6 and the thunder grants one bonus basic skill cast. That means an extra empowered basic attack too, jumping your short-trade damage up a full tier.

strengths: Empowered basic attacks after every skill deliver area magic damage and healing at once
The Ultimate's levitation pairs super armor with terrain-free entry angles
Max Passive stacks grant a bonus basic skill cast for extra tempo
Thick shields and sustain let a magic build brawl toe to toe
weaknesses: Break the attack-weave rhythm and damage and healing dry up together
Engaging on an empty gauge means no empowered hits and lost trades
Mobility lives entirely in Skill 1—spend it engaging and the exit is gone
A melee-centric core that suffers under sustained long-range poke

synergy.reason: She controls enemies to create a guaranteed opening, setting up the perfect situation to dive and start combos.
Her shields and peel greatly increase survivability when diving deep into the enemy team.

counters.reason: With his own cleanse and stun, he can easily turn the fight and punish any dives.
Her high mobility allows her to kite away, dealing high burst damage to poke them down before they can even engage.

passive.name: Passive Skill: Spear Will - Sweeping Fire
passive.description: Ying is mentally linked with her spear, Sweeping Fire. Using skills grants 1 stack of Spear Will. Basic Attacks expend all Spear Will, use the corresponding Spear Will skill (Stalwart - Peacemaker, Zealous - Devastation, or Zenith - Wildfire), and reduce Moonslash and Cloudchaser Cooldown by 1.5s. Spear Will skills can crit and benefit from 50% of Attack Speed.
passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: Spear Will - Sweeping Fire

skill1.name: Skill 1: Moonslash / Stalwart - Peacemaker

forms.description: Ying swings her spear upward, then slashes downward, executing 2 strikes that each deal 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage. The upward strike launches enemies for 0.5s.

Ying flourishes her spear and attacks repeatedly, gaining 25 Movement Speed for 1s, dealing 124 (55 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies over 4 strikes, and gaining a shield that negates damage equal to 260 (260 + 4.5% extra Health) for 2s.
This skill is cast by using an enhanced Basic Attack at 1 stack of Spear Will.

skill1.description: Ying swings her spear upward, then slashes downward, executing 2 strikes that each deal 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage. The upward strike launches enemies for 0.5s.

skill2.name: Skill 2: Cloudchaser / Zealous - Devastation

forms.description: Ying raises her spear and charges up, gaining up to 25% Movement Speed. After charging, she dashes forward and executes a horizontal sweep, dealing 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack)-360 (360 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 15% for 1s.

Ying strikes 3 times, dealing 129 (60 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage with each of the first two strikes and restoring 90 (90 + 1.3% extra Health) Health. The final strike deals 258 (120 + 80% extra physical attack) physical damage and restores 180 (180 + 2.5% extra Health) Health.
This skill is cast by using an enhanced Basic Attack at 2 stacks of Spear Will. The lower her Health, the greater the recovery effect (up to 2×).

skill2.description: Ying raises her spear and charges up, gaining up to 25% Movement Speed. After charging, she dashes forward and executes a horizontal sweep, dealing 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack)-360 (360 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 15% for 1s.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Starburn / Zenith - Wildfire

Ying ignites Sweeping Fire's tip and dashes back and forth through the area before her. Each dash deals 180 (180 + 60% extra physical attack) physical damage and launches enemies. Upon dashing to maximum range, she launches a flurry of stabs. Each stab deals 90 (90 + 30% extra physical attack) physical damage, for a total of 4 stabs.

This skill is cast by using an enhanced Basic Attack at 3 stacks of Spear Will. While airborne, Ying ignores terrain, gains 200% Movement Speed, and gains 10% damage reduction.
