combos.sequence: Skill 2 (apply curse) → Passive Enhanced Basic Attack (knockback + backward hop) → Skill 2 recast (root)
combos.description: Bounce the clinging assassin away, and if they keep coming, pin them in place for your team to delete. Managing the empowered basic's cooldown is the real skill check here.

strengths: Taxes gold off enemies — staying in motion converts into an economy lead
Two roots plus the knockback basic add up to serious lockdown and peel
The curse's stealth shutdown exposes ambushes and invisible heroes
Recast dashes stretch her healing and catch range surprisingly far
weaknesses: Dying refunds every coin she taxed back to the enemy
The recast-centric kit makes split-second reactions awkward
Near-zero personal damage — roots go to waste if allies don't respond
The bond system takes real time to internalize

581.name: Flowborn (Tank)

synergy.reason: Acts as a frontline meatshield to peel for low-mobility marksmen against enemy dives.
Locks down multiple enemies with strong CC, allowing the mage to safely unleash massive AoE damage.

counters.reason: Can completely ignore the tank's high survivability with armor penetration and percentage-based damage.
Possesses true damage that ignores shields and physical defense, making it impossible to tank.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: Flow of the World
passive.description:
Flowborn can draw the Flow into their body at the Base to enhance stats.
Vitality: Increases max Health by 300 and Physical and Magical Defense by 50.
Piercing Heart: Increases max Health by 300 and Physical Attack by 30.
Haste: Increases max Health by 300 and Movement Speed by 3.5%.
Focus: Increases max Health by 300 and Cooldown Reduction by 5%.
Spend 1 stack of Flow to perform an enhanced Basic Attack that deals 408 (220 + 100% physical attack + 4% extra Health) physical damage and recover 125 (125 + 2.5% extra Health) Health.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Flow of the World

skill1.description:
Flowborn channels the Flow, reducing the cooldown of other skills by 50% while gaining 5 stacks of Flow and recovering 150 (150 + 4% extra Health) Health. Gains 1 extra stack and recovers extra Health for every teammate and every 2 minions nearby, for up to 9 stacks and double the recovery.
Flowborn deals 100 (100 + 2% extra Health) physical damage to nearby enemies and knocks them back (without applying crowd control).
skill1.name: Skill 1: Convergence

skill2.description:
Flowborn charges toward the target, knocking back enemies in the path, then slashes forward to deal 600 (600 + 185% extra physical attack) physical damage and gain a 350 (350 + 7% extra Health) shield for 3s.
Using this skill continuously on the same target for 1.5s changes its effects in the following order.
Clearing Slash: Deals equal slash damage to enemies, launches them for 0.33s, and gains a shield of the same amount.
Rifting Slash: Deals equal slash damage to enemies, launches them for 0.66s, and gains a shield of the same amount.
If the skill is not on cooldown, spend 4 stacks of Flow to stop it from entering cooldown after this use.
All non-hero units within range of this skill are affected by the same crowd control effect.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Power From Within

skill3.description:
Flowborn leaps to the target location and attacks, dealing 400 (400 + 70% extra physical attack + 8% extra Health) physical damage and knocking back enemies for 0.75s. Deals an extra 50% damage at the center of the attack.
If the skill is not on cooldown, can spend 5 stacks of Flow to stop it from entering cooldown after this use.
skill3.name: Skill 3: All In

strategy.earlyGame: The game starts before the gates open: pick your Flow enhancement at base, and if you're frontlining, the dual-defense option is the safe default. The early rule that matters most: cast Skill 1 near allies or minions. Flow stacks scale with the bodies around you (up to 9) and the healing climbs with them, so the same button is a different skill depending on where you press it. Roam or clash lane both work. When the Ultimate unlocks at level 4, syncing its knock-up with your jungler's gank is your first highlight moment.
strategy.midGame: Through the 8-to-12-minute objective fights, your Flow bank is your voice in the game. Skill 2 recasts free of cooldown for 4 stacks and the Ultimate for 5, so at full stacks you're effectively a tank with double the spellbook. Engage with the Ultimate's center hit (50% bonus damage plus a 0.75-second knock-up), then chain Skill 2 into the same target: the second and third strikes add escalating knock-ups on top. Land the full chain and the average carry simply does not walk away.
strategy.lateGame: When the game settles into 5v5 set pieces, your edge is initiating twice by yourself: once with the normal rotation, once more with stack-funded recasts. The most lethal Ultimate of the night is the second one — cast right as the enemy steps forward believing you're out of cooldowns. Hold the frontline with Flow-empowered basic attacks: each one heals, so as long as you keep swinging you're genuinely hard to bring down. Just remember Skill 1's stack income depends on nearby bodies — never drift into isolated fights.
strategy.teamfight: You take the front, but top off with Skill 1 before committing — a full Flow bank changes how brave you're allowed to be. Enter on the Ultimate's center hit, then run Skill 2 three times into one target: the chained knock-ups juggle them while your team pours in damage. If the backline gets dived, Skill 2's charging knockback carves the assassin off your carry while the shield absorbs the exchange. A habit worth building: keep at least 4 stacks in reserve at all times, so a surprise engage can always be answered with an instant recast.

combos.title: Full-Bank Engage
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (refill Flow) → Ultimate (center-hit knock-up) → Skill 2 → Skill 2 (second strike) → Skill 2 (third strike)
combos.description: Stack up, then commit. Chaining Skill 2 into the same target within 1.5 seconds escalates the knock-up with each strike, holding one enemy functionally motionless while your team melts them.

combos.title: Stack Recast
combos.sequence: Ultimate (normal cast) → Ultimate recast via 5 Flow stacks
combos.description: A double knock-up with no cooldown in between breaks every assumption enemies make. Whiff the first and catch them with the second — only a stacked Flowborn gets to play that game.

combos.title: Interposing Peel
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (charge knockback + shield) → Empowered Basic Attack (heal) → Skill 1 (refill + push-back)
combos.description: Shove the diver off your backline, absorb the trade with the shield and healing, and rebuild stacks on the spot. Standing next to your carry, this answer covers most ambush attempts.

strengths: Flow stacks buy cooldown-free recasts of Skill 2 and the Ultimate
Chained, escalating knock-ups deliver exceptional lockdown
Empowered-basic healing and shields sustain a long frontline shift
The pre-game Flow choice tunes him against any enemy comp
weaknesses: With an empty Flow bank he's an ordinary tank with ordinary CC
Skill 1's income scales with nearby bodies, so isolated fights starve him
No mobility beyond the charge; long-range poke drains him for free
Stack accounting plus chained inputs make him busier than he looks

582.name: Flowborn (Mage)

synergy.reason: Locks down enemies with strong CC and shields, guaranteeing the mage can land their full skill combo.
Draws enemy aggro on the frontline, creating space to safely output sustained magic damage from a distance.

counters.reason: Closes the gap with overwhelming mobility and bursts them down before they can even cast a skill.
Possesses undodgeable point-and-click hard CC that completely neutralizes all mobility.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: Flow of the World
passive.description:
Flowborn can draw the Flow into their body at the Base to enhance stats (increases with level).
Vitality: Increases Magical Attack by 50 and max Health by 300.
Piercing Heart: Increases Magical Attack by 50 and Magical Pierce by 50.
Haste: Increases Magical Attack by 50 and Movement Speed by 3.5%.
Focus: Increases Magical Attack by 50 and Cooldown Reduction by 5%.
Can spend 1 stack of Flow to perform an enhanced Basic Attack that deals 60 (60 + 12% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Flow of the World

skill1.description:
Flowborn channels the Flow, reducing the cooldown of other skills by 50% while gaining 5 stacks of Flow and recovering 150 (150 + 4% extra Health) Health. Gains 1 extra stack and recovers extra Health for every teammate and every 2 minions nearby, for up to 9 stacks and double the recovery.
Flowborn deals 100 (100 + 20% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and knocks them back (without applying crowd control).
skill1.name: Skill 1: Convergence

skill2.description:
Flowborn controls the nearby Flow and conjures a magic circle, dealing 325 (325 + 65% magical attack) magical damage to enemies within range and slowing them by 30% for 1s. The magic circle deals 65 (65 + 13% magical attack) magical damage for 1.5s every 0.5s.
Can use this skill continuously over 1.5s, with new effects in the following order.
Launching Flow: Deals the same damage to enemies and launches them for 0.5s.
Stunning Flow: Deals the same damage to enemies and stuns them for 0.5s.
If used within the initial magic circle, both additional uses refresh the magic circle's duration and increase damage over time by 50%.
Can spend 4 stacks of Flow to use the skill without triggering cooldown.
The inner area of all circles inflicts an extra 50% crowd control effect.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Flow Formation

skill3.description:
Flowborn channels the Flow into a beam, dealing 700 (700 + 140% magical attack) magical damage to enemies in its path.
The beam will link with an enemy hero within range and continuously unleash Energy Bombs, dealing 350 (350 + 70% magical attack) magical damage to the area around the target.
Can spend 5 stacks of Flow to stop the skill from entering cooldown after this use.
Other skills can be used during this skill.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Arcane Arts

strategy.earlyGame: Your game starts before you leave the fountain: pick your Flow boon at base. The cooldown option (5% CDR) is the default for combo uptime, while the magic-pierce boon punishes opponents who stack magic defense. In mid lane, clear waves with Skill 2's formation and place its far edge so it clips your lane opponent — waveclear and harass in a single cast. Treat Skill 1 less as a weapon and more as fuel: it cuts your other cooldowns by 50% and restocks Flow stacks, so fire it during safe windows while the wave sits on your side and you will never run dry at the 4-minute Tyrant fight. Until your Ultimate arrives at Level 4, winning the chip war is the whole job — don't force kills.
strategy.midGame: Around eight minutes, once cooldown boots and a magic-pierce staff are finished, a single formation starts taking frightening chunks out of people. Your job now is placement in tight spaces. Lay Skill 2 across river entrances and the corridors around the Tyrant pit, then stack the second cast's knock-up onto anyone who steps in — landing it on the first formation also raises its damage over time by 50%, holding enemies inside a zone that hurts more every tick. Flow caps at nine stacks, so the iron rule is topping off with Skill 1 before every fight. Walk in empty and your bonus casts vanish, along with half your output.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, holding your full combo in reserve becomes the win condition. With your magic attack scaled through your final core items, the third cast's stun into the Ultimate's beam melts anyone with marksman-grade durability. Since Arcane Arts lets you cast other skills mid-channel, the ideal picture is sweeping the beam while laying fresh formations at your feet. Your only self-peel, though, is Skill 1's small knockback — the moment you stand ahead of your frontline is the moment you die. When setting up before Overlord, always keep a wall and your teammates at your back.
strategy.teamfight: Open every fight from the absolute backline. Skip the enemy tank; drop Skill 2 under the fighter pushing into your carries, then chain the second cast's knock-up into the third cast's stun to freeze their front. Once you see an enemy blink go down, commit the Ultimate — its homing energy bolts chase runners down without your help. A Flow Formation paid for with four Flow stacks never touches its cooldown, so you can keep re-laying zones as long as stacks remain; that loop is the whole point of this hero. When you're spent, don't chase — fall back and let Skill 1's healing patch you up.

combos.title: Triple Formation Lockdown
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Skill 2 (2nd Cast: Knock-up) → Skill 2 (3rd Cast: Stun)
combos.description: Recasting within 1.5 seconds upgrades the formation from damage to knock-up to stun. Casts paid for with four Flow stacks skip the cooldown entirely, so topping up to nine stacks with Skill 1 first lets you lay three zones back to back. Stacking a cast onto the first formation also raises its damage over time by 50%.

combos.title: Beam-Weave Full Combo
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 → Ultimate → Skill 2 (2nd Cast: Knock-up)
combos.description: Skill 1 handles the setup — a Flow restock plus the 50% cooldown cut — then Skill 2's slow pins your target for the beam. Because the Ultimate allows other casts mid-channel, layering a second formation for the knock-up while the beam burns leaves the target no room to run and no window to fight back.

strengths: Spending Flow stacks lets Skill 2 and the Ultimate ignore cooldowns entirely
Skill 2's consecutive casts supply knock-up and stun with no outside help
Casting other skills during the Ultimate's beam packs absurd damage density
Skill 1's healing and cooldown cut give far more staying power than expected
weaknesses: No mobility skill — once Skill 1's small knockback is baited, nothing else peels
Damage ceiling depends heavily on precise nine-stack Flow management
Skill 1's stack income and healing shrink without teammates nearby
Ground-placed formations let blink users simply step out of the damage

584.name: Flowborn (Marksman)

synergy.reason: Boosts backline survivability with shields, keeping them safe until their late-game damage scaling kicks in.
Stabilizes the laning phase with high sustain and protection, allowing the marksman to scale and shine.

counters.reason: Instantly deletes squishy marksmen with stealth engages and high burst damage.
Dives the backline with overwhelming mobility, bursting them down before there's any time to react.

passive.skill_name: Passive Skill: Flow of the World
passive.description:
Flowborn can draw the Flow into their body at the Base, increasing Attack Speed by 10%-20% (increases with hero level) and enhancing one of four other stats.
Vitality: Increases max Health by 300.
Piercing Heart: Increases Physical Attack by 30.
Haste: Increases Movement Speed by 3.5%.
Focus: Increases Cooldown Reduction by 5%.
Enhanced Basic Attack: Fires a piercing projectile, dealing 80 (80 + 20% extra physical attack) physical damage to enemies in its path. Hitting an enemy extends its travel distance while reducing damage by 30%.
Each enhanced Basic Attack consumes 1 stack of Flow.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Flow of the World

skill1.description:
Flowborn channels the Flow, dealing 100 (100 + 25% extra physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies and knocking them back (without applying crowd control). Also recovers 150 (150 + 4% extra Health) Health, gains 5 stacks of Flow, and reduces the cooldown of Arrow of No Retreat and Arrowstorm by 50%.
Nearby teammates and minions increase the recovery (up to 100%) and stacks of Flow (up to 9 stacks).
skill1.name: Skill 1: Convergence

skill2.description:
Flowborn shoots an enormous projectile at the target (can be blocked by enemy heroes), dealing 450 (450 + 120% extra physical attack) physical damage and knocking back non-hero units.
Flowborn can dash a short distance upon use (use it again within 1.5s to become enhanced).
Second Use: Enhances projectile damage by 25%.
Third Use: Levitates and enhances projectile damage by 50%.
Can spend 4 stacks of Flow to use this skill again.
Casting speed increases with Attack Speed.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Arrow of No Retreat

skill3.description:
Flowborn shoots 7 volleys of light projectiles at the target location (casting speed increases with Attack Speed), dealing 90 (50 + 24% physical attack) physical damage (every 3 projectiles counts as 1 Basic Attack). Projectiles lock on to targets within range. Also gains a 10% Movement Speed increase. Use this skill again to levitate.
Can spend 5 stacks of Flow to use this skill again.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Arrowstorm

strategy.earlyGame: Pick your Flow boon at base, then head for the farm lane. Take the max-HP option (300 HP) into aggressive matchups, and borrow damage with the physical attack boon when the lane looks safe. Until Level 4 your base damage is genuinely poor, so this is not a trading window — quietly collect last hits and experience and nothing else. If an enemy closes the gap, Skill 1's knockback and healing reset the exchange more often than not. It also halves the cooldowns of Skill 2 and the Ultimate, so spending it defensively never feels like a waste.
strategy.midGame: From 8 to 10 minutes, once attack-speed boots and your first damage item are online, Flowborn's signature mechanic starts spinning: attack speed accelerates your skill animations too. You're still not the main character of teamfights, so shove the lane, sweep open jungle camps, and rush your second core item. When called to Tyrant, join from the very back — planting Skill 2's giant arrow into the closest enemy is a full shift on its own. Each cast tacks on a short move afterward, so build the habit of stepping back half a pace every time you fire. It quietly prevents most deaths.
strategy.lateGame: Past 15 minutes, at four items and up, the lead role changes hands. Weaving bonus casts of Skill 2 and the Ultimate between basic attacks — paid for with Flow stacks — creates the damage spikes that define this hero's endgame. Fire Skill 2 three times within 1.5 seconds and the third becomes an aerial attack at 50% bonus damage, so the moment your frontline pins someone is the moment to unload the triple. Skill 1 restocks five stacks, more with allies or minions nearby; never let the tank run empty between fights. And never walk anywhere alone — stay close enough to see a teammate's back at all times.
strategy.teamfight: Your position is locked to the very back, and your target is whoever stands closest. When chased, Skill 1's knockback peels them off while the heal and the 50% cooldown refund on Skill 2 and the Ultimate set up your next burst. Arrowstorm's volley also grants 10% move speed, tailor-made for kiting backward. Once the enemy front cracks, spend your saved Flow stacks on the Skill 2 triple volley into whatever remains of their backline. You are softest right after dumping everything — at zero stacks, sit at max range and refuse to get greedy. That's how this hero grows old.

combos.title: No-Retreat Triple Volley
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Skill 2 → Skill 2 (Aerial Attack)
combos.description: Chaining casts within 1.5 seconds ramps the damage by 25% and then 50%, with the third shot becoming an aerial attack. The triple comes together by weaving the four-Flow-stack bonus cast between cooldown casts. The short move after each shot lets you kite while the arrows fly.

combos.title: Reset and Punish
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Enhanced Basic Attack → Skill 2
combos.description: When someone reaches you, Skill 1 buys the knockback and heal while restocking five Flow stacks and halving the cooldowns of Skill 2 and the Ultimate. Answer immediately with the piercing enhanced basic and Skill 2 — defense flowing straight into a counterattack. This is Flowborn's core self-peel pattern.

combos.title: Arrowstorm Pursuit
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Ultimate (Aerial Attack) → Basic Attack
combos.description: The lock-on volley comes with a 10% move speed boost, and recasting turns it into an aerial attack. Drop it across a fleeing enemy's escape path and you accelerate back into basic attack range while the arrows handle the chip work — the cleanest chase tool in the kit.

strengths: Attack speed uniquely accelerates skill animations, double-dipping every point
Skill 1's knockback, healing, and cooldown refund make elite self-peel
Flow-stack bonus casts create burst windows that ignore cooldowns
Post-cast movement and aerial attacks on Skill 2 and the Ultimate make kiting exceptional
weaknesses: Weak base damage before Level 4 — early trades are nearly always losses
The piercing arrow loses 30% damage after passing through a target, so long-range poke rarely finishes anyone
Sloppy stack management removes the bonus casts and flattens the damage spikes
Targeted CC is lethal once Skill 1 is down, with no second escape

synergy.reason: His AoE cleanse and CC immunity allow Florentino to continuously output damage and pick up flowers without his combos being interrupted.
By clumping enemies up, he massively increases the hit rate of Florentino's flower toss (Skill 1), letting him wipe out multiple targets at once.

counters.reason: His uncleansable suppression ultimate completely stops Florentino's fancy footwork and combos, leaving him vulnerable to getting burst down by the team.
His long-duration suppression ultimate forcefully interrupts Florentino's combo mechanics, completely neutralizing him.

passive.name: Passive: Sword Steps
passive.description:
When leaving combat or touching a bouquet, Florentino empowers his next Basic Attack (the effect lasts 5s after touching a bouquet). He dashes forward, dealing 160 (160 + 50% extra physical attack) physical damage, and recovers 140 (140 + 2% extra max Health) Health when hitting a hero (recovery is halved against non-hero units).
After the dash ends, he can quickly move a short distance.

skill1.name: Skill 1: Bloom
skill1.description:
Florentino throws a bouquet, dealing 300 (300 + 95% extra physical attack) physical damage to the first enemy hit and stunning them for 0.75s, then creates 3 bouquets around the target for 3.5s.
Touching a bouquet empowers his Basic Attack and resets the cooldown of Triple Slash.

skill2.name: Skill 2: Triple Slash
skill2.description:
Florentino strikes the target 3 times with his sword.
1st hit: deals 130 (130 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage and greatly reduces the target's Movement Speed for 1s.
2nd hit: deals 130 (130 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage.
3rd hit: deals 130 (130 + 40% extra physical attack) physical damage (in 2 stages).
Each strike deals an additional 130 (130 + 40% extra physical attack) true damage to the target and reduces the cooldown of Bloom by 1s.
The first 2 strikes have a 1.5s cooldown. The skill goes on cooldown after the 3rd strike. After the attack ends, he can quickly move a short distance.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Gentleman's Duel
skill3.description:
Florentino dashes in the target direction, marking the first enemy hero hit and increasing the damage they take by 10% for 5s, then creates 3 bouquets nearby.
While the skill lasts, the Health recovery of Sword Steps' empowered Basic Attack is doubled and he gains crowd control immunity (extended by 1s each time he touches a bouquet, lasts 3s).
Touching a bouquet empowers his Basic Attack and resets the cooldown of Triple Slash.
After the dash ends, he can quickly move a short distance.

strategy.earlyGame: In the clash lane, Level 1 starts with Skill 1. The 0.75-second stun sprouts three flowers around your target, so collect them mid-stun, then chain enhanced basic attack into Skill 2 for a trade loaded with true damage that your opponent simply cannot match. The enhanced basic heals 140 HP when it strikes a hero, which means the longer the slugfest runs, the wider the HP gap grows — that's the Florentino experience. Once the Ultimate arrives at Level 4, the mark's 10% bonus damage taken plus super armor makes your duels nearly unloseable. Just pick flower routes on the side ganks can't reach.
strategy.midGame: Around nine minutes, with your first two core items finished, it's time to move. Chip the enemy tower down, then show up mid: the Ultimate's dash into the flower loop makes you a one-man gank engine. In the standoffs before Tyrant or Overlord, one Bloom threaded from a river bush deletes somebody. When nothing is happening, splitting side towers is genuinely one of your best uses of time. One warning — the enhanced basic's healing is halved against minions, so don't loiter in a lane at low HP expecting to sustain it back.
strategy.lateGame: With a frost gauntlet and a sustain piece rounding out your build, the late game rewards duels over head-on 5v5s. Pressure a side lane, then catch whoever comes to answer with Gentleman's Duel and remove them — that's the golden pattern. Against a target taking 10% extra damage from your mark, cycling Skill 2's true damage through flower pickups kills even tanks on a timer. The only real threat is getting surrounded. Super armor extends when you touch flowers, but it has a hard limit — CC timed at its final second will still drop you.
strategy.teamfight: You are not the frontal engage. Wait in a side bush, let the enemy's CC land on your frontline, then commit the Ultimate onto their backline. The dash blooms three flowers on arrival, so once you land, dance the loop — flower, Skill 2, flower, Skill 2 — and your damage never pauses. While the Ultimate runs, enhanced basic healing doubles, letting you shrug off a surprising amount of focus mid-combo. Your one losing script is getting burst before the first flower pickup. In the instant before you dive, check what skills the enemy still has up — every time.

combos.title: Core Flower Loop
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Flower Pickup → Enhanced Basic Attack → Skill 2 → Flower Pickup → Skill 2
combos.description: Run to a flower during Skill 1's stun — every pickup empowers your next basic and resets Triple Slash's cooldown. Since each of Skill 2's three strikes carries bonus true damage, an ordinary fighter simply cannot out-sustain the loop once it starts spinning.

combos.title: Duelist's Full Combo
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Flower Pickup → Skill 2 → Skill 1 → Enhanced Basic Attack
combos.description: Apply the mark (10% bonus damage taken) and super armor before you start swinging — this is your maximum 1v1 output. Weave double-healing enhanced basics, and let each Skill 2 hit shave one second off Bloom's cooldown to reach the second stun. Most opponents are dead before it lands.

combos.title: The Parting Step
combos.sequence: Enhanced Basic Attack (Dash) → Skill 2 (First Two Hits) → Disengage
combos.description: The Passive also empowers your next basic when you leave combat, so short lane trades work: land the dash hit and Skill 2's opening strikes, then leave through Skill 2's follow-up move and the dash's extra step. You exit outside their range having healed — pure profit every time.

strengths: Flower pickups reset Skill 2 endlessly, cycling true damage nonstop
Enhanced-basic healing — doubled during the Ultimate — wins any slugfest
The super armor dash forces 1v1s on his terms
Constant dashes and bonus moves make roams and split pushes fast
weaknesses: Miss Skill 1 and no flowers bloom — the combo loses its front door
Flower spots are predictable; CC placed on the pickup path shreds him
Few answers to long-range poke and disciplined kiting
Flower tracking and micro-movement demand real practice time

synergy.reason: While Lorion's massive AoE knockup ultimate locks down multiple enemies, Marco Polo can safely unleash his full ultimate.
Chaining Lian Po's strong engage into Lorion's orb placement and ultimate creates a CC chain that devastates the enemy backline.

counters.reason: Zhuangzi's ultimate (team-wide CC immunity) completely negates Lorion's biggest strength: his massive AoE knockup ultimate.
With high mobility and i-frames, she easily dodges Lorion's Skill 1 orb placement and his ultimate's AoE.

skill_order.linked_note: Note: Leveling up Skill 2 also upgrades Skill 3.

passive.name: Passive: Eternity
passive.description:
Skill Activation: Deals damage on hit and activates the orb.
While the orb is outside his body, the activated orb deals 59 (59 + 12% magical attack) magical damage every 0.75s for 4s to the unit with the lowest Health in range.
While the orb is inside his body, the activated orb damages all units in range, its attack frequency is doubled, and it recovers 25 (25 + 0.4% extra Health) Health (halved for non-hero units).

skill1.name: Skill 1: Where My Will Reaches
skill1.description:
Lorion moves the orb to the target position, dealing 220 (220 + 44% magical attack) magical damage to units along its path. On hit at the destination, the orb activates and deals an additional 150 (150 + 30% magical attack) magical damage. While the orb is outside his body, casting this skill deals 250 (250 + 50% magical attack) magical damage to units between the orb's starting point and destination and reduces their Movement Speed by 20% for 1.5s.
Moving a certain distance away from the orb recalls it into his body.

skill2.name: Skill 2: Abyssal Pact
skill2.description:
While the orb is outside his body, Lorion recalls it into his body and activates it, dealing 150 (150 + 30% magical attack) magical damage and increasing his Movement Speed by 20% for 2s.
While the orb is inside his body, the cooldown is reduced by 30%.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Advent of the Dark God
skill3.description:
While the orb is outside his body, Lorion flies toward the orb and activates it, dealing 150 (150 + 30% magical attack) magical damage. While casting, he takes 25% reduced damage (lasts 2s after the flight ends) and gains crowd control immunity.
While the orb is inside his body, the cooldown is reduced by 30%.

skill4.name: Skill 4: Star of the Dark Night
skill4.description:
Lorion detonates the orb after 2s, dealing 600 (600 + 120% magical attack) magical damage to nearby enemies and knocking them up for 1.25s.
Casting the ultimate grants 1 stack of Skill 1.
If the ultimate does not hit a hero, its cooldown is reduced by 50%.

strategy.earlyGame: In mid lane, clear waves with the orb held inside your body. Activated there, it strikes everything around you at double frequency and even heals you, which makes Lorion shockingly durable in lane scraps. When you want to harass, send the orb out with Skill 1 — and the moment it connects, don't leave it lying there. Recall it with Skill 2 and collect the 20% move speed. Repeat that send-and-recall rhythm patiently until Level 4 and you'll walk into the 4-minute Tyrant contest with a visible HP lead over your lane opponent.
strategy.midGame: From about eight minutes, once cooldown boots and a magic-pierce staff are complete, orb placement starts deciding fights. In the standoffs before Tyrant, your job is shipping the orb into enemy escape routes and narrow corridors with Skill 1, booking the Ultimate's detonation in advance. After a 2-second charge it erupts for heavy damage and a 1.25-second knock-up, so enemies simply cannot stand in that zone. Time the blast with your team's engage — detonating early is just an expensive scare. And since the activated orb auto-targets the lowest-HP enemy in range, parking it near someone chipped forces a recall all by itself.
strategy.lateGame: Your late-game role is zone control from the backline. With your magic attack fully built, a single detonation removes over half the health bar of anything squishy. The discipline that matters here: never spend the Ultimate's flight offensively. Flying to your orb with 25% damage reduction and super armor is, in practice, your last lifeline. When the enemy assassin is missing from vision, pre-place the orb toward your escape side before stepping up — if they jump you, you fly straight out of their reach. Let the orb project the threat while your body stays safe. That's the iron rule of late-game Lorion.
strategy.teamfight: Teamfight prep starts 30 seconds before the fight. At Overlord or Shadow Tyrant, set the orb at the pit entrance, then rake Skill 1's start-to-end line damage and slow through their formation. The moment they clump, detonate for the knock-up and let your team's follow-up turn it into a numbers win. If the brawl swallows you, recalling the orb into your body with Skill 2 is a real option — the double-frequency damage around you plus the self-healing makes you far harder to kill than you look. Lorion's teamfight is one continuous choice: which do you show the enemy, the orb or yourself?

combos.title: Plant-and-Detonate Zoning
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Ultimate (Detonate) → Skill 2
combos.description: Ship the orb to the enemy's feet or escape path with Skill 1, then book the detonation. Two seconds later the blast lands with a 1.25-second knock-up, and because it's a placed zone, it warps enemy movement brutally. Recall with Skill 2 afterward and ride the speed boost to your next position.

combos.title: Inner-Orb Brawling
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 (Recall) → Basic Attack
combos.description: When someone dives you, pull the orb back inside. The recall's hit activates it, ticking double-frequency damage into everyone around you while restoring your HP. That un-mage-like melee sustain has ruined the math of many an enemy assassin.

combos.title: Lifeline Flight
combos.sequence: Skill 1 (Toward Escape Route) → Ultimate (Fly to Orb) → Skill 2
combos.description: Before you're caught, place the orb in the direction you want to leave, then fly to it. The flight carries 25% damage reduction and super armor, so crowd control cannot interrupt the trip. Land, recall for the speed boost, and walk away clean.

strengths: The orb swaps whole playstyles inside versus outside his body, covering any range
Planted detonation knock-ups own every chokepoint on the map
Damage-reduced, super-armor flight is elite escape for a mage
The outside orb hunts the lowest-HP enemy, projecting free closing pressure
weaknesses: Everything hinges on orb placement — one bad spot stalls the entire kit
The 2-second detonation delay gives mobile enemies time to dodge
Spending the flight offensively leaves him with no way out afterward
Straying too far force-recalls the orb and erases its zone threat

synergy.reason: Annette's ultimate (wind wall) completely shuts out enemy assassin dives, allowing the marksman to attack freely from the safety of the backline.
The wind wall keeps melee heroes at bay, allowing her to safely output damage from out of range.

counters.reason: They dish out heavy poke damage from far beyond the wind wall's range, easily overwhelming Annette's squishy health pool.
His high burst damage can potentially delete Annette before she even has time to deploy her ultimate.

passive.name: Passive: Whisper of the Wind
passive.description: Moving reduces skill cooldowns and restores Mana. When an ally is nearby, Movement Speed is increased by 25.

skill1.name: Skill 1: Premonition of Storm
skill1.description:
Annette summons a magic circle at the target position (triggers every 0.5s, lasts 4s). The magic circle deals 160 (160 + 28% magical attack) magical damage to enemy units and reduces their Movement Speed by 5% (up to 5 stacks, lasts 1s).
The magic circle increases allied units' Movement Speed by 5% (up to 5 stacks, lasts 1s).

skill2.name: Skill 2: Wind Guard
skill2.description:
Annette launches an orb in the target direction (bouncing herself in the opposite direction), gaining a 400 (400 + 6% extra magical attack) shield for 3s and 75 bonus Movement Speed for 2s.
The orb deals 300 (300 + 50% magical attack) magical damage to enemies it hits and grants allies it hits a 400 (400 + 6% extra magical attack) shield.
If the orb touches a magic circle from Premonition of Storm, it carries the magic circle to its destination.

skill3.name: Skill 3: Veil of the Spring Breeze
skill3.description:
Annette summons a barrier around herself (lasts 4s, can move), knocking back enemies in range and dealing 300 (300 + 50% magical attack) magical damage. Enemies touching the barrier take the same damage and are stunned for 1.25s, while allies inside the barrier gain crowd control immunity.
While casting, Annette becomes untargetable and her Movement Speed is reduced by 50%.

strategy.earlyGame: Shadow your marksman from the start and support the farm-lane scraps with Skill 2's orb. Hit an ally and it shields; hit an enemy and it damages; and you bounce backward on every cast — one aiming decision covers offense and defense at once. Before the 4-minute Tyrant, your job is tagging along on ganks: Skill 1's formation stacks slows on enemies who cross it and speeds up allies who do, a ready-made chase engine. Since the Passive refunds cooldowns and restores mana as you move, walking the river beats standing still in lane — Annette performs best in motion.
strategy.midGame: Once your support item upgrade and cooldown boots are in, skirmishes start brewing around mid. Annette's spot is half a step ahead of her carry. The instant an enemy fighter telegraphs a dive, open the Ultimate: anyone touching the barrier gets knocked back and stunned for 1.25 seconds, while allies inside gain super armor that shrugs off CC. The generous part is that it's fast enough to open on reaction — you can wait to see their engage first. The trick of pushing your formation forward with the orb is also worth practicing for chipping enemies who hide under tower.
strategy.lateGame: The late game is an exercise in patience: hold the Ultimate for the one enemy who decides fights. With your defensive capes stacked, you won't fall over even standing forward. The ideal sequence at a fight's entrance is Skill 1 first to control the ground, then catching the enemy assassin mid-leap with the barrier as they jump your marksman. While it's active you become untargetable but your move speed is halved, so opening in the wrong spot strands you away from your team while the fight is decided. Open it right beside the person you're protecting — no exceptions.
strategy.teamfight: Stand next to your carry. The job is three tasks: lay Skill 1 across the enemy frontline's path to blunt the charge; thread Skill 2's orb through your most-focused teammate to keep shields flowing; and when the real dive arrives, meet it with the Ultimate — knockback, stun, and super armor for everyone inside. Keep that order and you'll tilt teamfights while dealing almost no damage yourself. The one hazard is the orb's recoil: bounce backward into a flanker and the story ends badly. Glance behind you before every cast — make it a reflex.

combos.title: Counter-Peel
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Skill 1 → Skill 2
combos.description: Open the barrier against their dive: contact means a knockback and a 1.25-second stun. Follow with Skill 1 to slow the attackers and speed your allies, then stabilize your chunked carry with Skill 2's shield. This sequence is Annette's entire reason for existing, condensed.

combos.title: Formation Push
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2
combos.description: Strike your placed formation with the orb and it shoves the whole zone to the orb's endpoint. That delivers the slow field to enemies hiding under tower or kiting at max range — one of the few ways a low-damage hero like Annette projects pressure from a distance.

combos.title: Recoil Backstep
combos.sequence: Skill 2 (Fired at the Chaser) → Skill 1 (At Your Feet)
combos.description: When ganked, shoot the orb straight at your pursuer: the recoil bounces you away with a shield and 75 bonus move speed. Drop the slowing formation on your landing spot and most chases die right there. An escape with a counterattack sewn in — learn it early.

strengths: The Ultimate's knockback, stun, and super armor erase entire dives
Skill 2 is damage, shielding, and a reposition in a single button
Movement refunds her cooldowns, so skills keep cycling as long as she moves
Layered speed-ups and slows control the tempo of chases and retreats
weaknesses: Minimal personal damage — she can't convert her setups into kills alone
No healing, so teammates who are already chunked stay chunked
The barrier halves her move speed; a bad opening spot means instant separation
Forget the orb's recoil and it bounces you straight into trouble

synergy.reason: He grants CC immunity and damage reduction, allowing her to chain resets and secure kills uninterrupted.
His long-range stun can lock down enemies, creating a safe opening for Butterfly to dive.

counters.reason: His AoE CC and high sustain can easily break the chain of Butterfly's skill resets.
Her i-frames and healing allow her to dodge Butterfly's burst and easily turn the fight.

passive.description: Butterfly gains 2 marks from defeating heroes and 1 mark from assists and from killing monsters/minions. At 3 stacks, the next skill used will not enter cooldown.
passive.name: Passive Skill: Assassination

skill1.description: Butterfly deals 362 (240 + 70% physical attack) physical damage to nearby enemies. Each extra enemy hit increases damage by 25%. Also gains a shield that negates 381 (250 + 75% physical attack) damage lasting 2s, and gains 50% Movement Speed that diminishes over time.
skill1.name: Skill 1: Whirlwind

skill2.description:
Butterfly deals 333 (220 + 65% physical attack) physical damage to enemies in her path. The first enemy hit takes 1.5 times this damage and is slowed by 50% for 1.5s.
Hitting an enemy increases her Attack Speed by 25% and Critical Rate by 10% for 4s, for up to 2 stacks.
skill2.name: Skill 2: Sword Propel

skill3.description:
Butterfly jumps to a target enemy, dealing 557 (400 + 90% physical attack) physical damage (if the target is marked, deals extra true damage equal to 12% lost Health) and marking them for 4s. For 4s after hitting the target, she takes 50% less damage from all Basic Attacks.
While the mark is active, she recovers Health equal to 35% of damage dealt to the target. If the target is defeated, it will immediately reset her Ultimate's Cooldown.
Hitting marked targets with Basic Attacks will also reduce the Cooldown of Skills 1 and 2 by 1s.
skill3.name: Skill 3: Death Dealer

strategy.earlyGame: You're the jungler. Skill 1 gains 25% bonus damage for every additional enemy it hits, so casting from the center of each camp is free clear speed. The opening route is both buffs plus the river camps, aiming for Level 4 around the 3-minute mark. Passive stacks build from monster kills too, and at three stacks your next skill costs no cooldown — bank them before a gank and you walk in with an extra cast. As for the 4-minute Tyrant: touch it only when you've reached Level 4 before the enemy jungler has. Otherwise it's bait.
strategy.midGame: Once your jungle item and first damage item are finished, the real work begins: erasing chipped enemies. The ideal prey is a backliner under half HP. Death Dealer's leap applies the mark, converts 35% of your damage into healing, and — the headline — resets its own cooldown instantly on a takedown. Open ganks with Skill 2: the first enemy hit takes 1.5x damage and a 50% slow, and the attack speed and crit buffs it grants let your basics finish the job. The one rule that never changes, even in this window: do not walk into a healthy enemy team from the front.
strategy.lateGame: Late-game Butterfly is the cleanup crew, not the opening act. Even when the 5v5 starts, hold your side bush until the enemy's CC and attention are committed to your frontline. The Ultimate adds true damage equal to 12% of a marked target's lost HP, so anyone already chipped dies — armor stacked or not. One kill refunds the Ultimate on the spot, a hero takedown banks two passive stacks, and the chain reaction begins. The flip side: without that first kill, nothing starts. Whatever else you compromise on, never compromise on your entry timing.
strategy.teamfight: Your brawl loop is enter, kill, reset, next. Lead with Skill 2 before committing — the slow keeps them in reach, the attack speed buff quickens your swings, and each basic on a marked target shaves a second off both Skill 1 and Skill 2. When focus piles up, Skill 1's shield and decaying 50% speed boost carry you back to the edge of the fight. While your mark is active you take half damage from basic attacks, so a chasing marksman often can't actually finish you. One nuance: enemy support shields can rob your takedown reset, so start with the softest unshielded target — that's the correct kill order.

combos.title: Standard Gank
combos.sequence: Skill 2 → Ultimate → Basic Attack → Skill 1
combos.description: Skill 2's 1.5x damage and slow stop the target while its attack speed and crit buffs load your basics, then Death Dealer closes the gap. Basics on the marked target refund Skill 1 and Skill 2 cooldowns as you swing, and Skill 1's shield and speed boost cover either the chase or the exit.

combos.title: Takedown Reset Chain
combos.sequence: Ultimate → Basic Attack (Takedown) → Ultimate (Reset) → Skill 2 → Skill 1
combos.description: A takedown resets Death Dealer instantly, and a hero takedown banks two passive stacks — at three, your next skill has no cooldown. The jump from first kill to second target is effectively free, and that chain is the entire Butterfly experience.

combos.title: Speed-Clear Rotation
combos.sequence: Skill 1 → Skill 2 → Basic Attack
combos.description: Whirlwind scales with the number of targets caught, so always cast it from a camp's center. Grab the attack speed buff from Skill 2 and finish with basics. Every monster kill banks a passive stack, meaning clearing the jungle is literally gank preparation.

strengths: Takedown-triggered Ultimate resets give unmatched chain-kill power in brawls
35% damage-to-healing plus halved basic-attack damage while the mark runs
Lost-HP true damage finishes chipped targets through any amount of armor
Skill 1's shield and speed burst keep her entries and exits cheap
weaknesses: Without a first kill the resets never spin up and she fades hard
No CC of her own to start fights — she depends on teammates' lockdown
Hard CC exposes pure assassin fragility the moment it lands
Lacks a decisive answer to full-HP targets and healthy frontlines
